8. **A CHANDLER'S NOTE SAID OUT LOUD FOR THE THIRD TIME IN SEVEN MONTHS AND NOT RE-WRITTEN, and the yard is not going to say it a fourth time.**
9. **A WORKING HARBOR POORER ON THE FIFTH OF DECEMBER THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTIETH OF OCTOBER, AND NOTHING THIS YARD PUBLISHED IN THREE WEEKS HAS MADE IT BETTER, AND THE CISTERN WALKED ON NONE OF SIX CHARGES.**

### 9. Proposed canon changes

**None applied to any file outside the four state files. Eleven author-level decisions taken on the page, and no prompt figure corrected by the chapters.**

1. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE PROVISIONAL PUBLIC COPY RECORD EXISTS AND IS IN THIS YARD'S HANDS, AND IT IS A COPY OF A RECORD AND NOT THE OBJECT AND NOT A FRAGMENT.** Made at the counter of the copying room of the Morrow circuit office on Tuesday the twenty-fourth of November 2026, in six heads and about a page and a half, on an application made in the party's own left hand on Monday the sixteenth at a cost of a penny in the ordinary post. **IT CARRIES ON ITS FACE THE LIMITS THE RECORD ITSELF CARRIES, PRINTED IN THE RECORD'S OWN WORDS AND NOT A CLERK'S; IT SHOWS THAT A MANIFEST WAS ALTERED; AND IT SAYS ON ITS OWN FACE THAT IT DOES NOT SHOW BY WHOSE HAND, AT WHOSE INSTANCE OR WITH WHAT INTENT, AND NAMES NO PERSON. NO CHAPTER MAY STATE WHO ALTERED IT, OR WHY, OR ON WHOSE INSTANCE, OR MAY ADD A GROUND THAT IDENTIFIES A PERSON. THE COPY IS DATED THE TWENTY-FOURTH, WHICH IS THE DATE OF THE COUNTER AND NOT OF THE RECORD.**
2. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE SITTING WAS HELD IN THE HEARING ROOM OVER THE TIDE-GANG STORE ON THURSDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH AND FRIDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF NOVEMBER 2026, ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE IN THE ROOM ON THE FIRST DAY AND ABOUT NINE ON THE SECOND, AND THE STORE WAS SHUT BEHIND THEM AND THE MEN WHO COUNT THE CATCH IN IT WERE IN ANOTHER BUILDING.** The copy was read out whole by the ship's hand of the party and not by the holder, and the clerk entered that the answer came from her and not from him, which is the second time that has been entered in that room. **THE HOLDER WAS ASKED IN THAT ROOM, BY A CLERK WHO HAD WRITTEN THE QUESTION IN HIS OWN PAGE FIRST, WHETHER HE COULD SAY WHAT WAS IN THE WATER OFF THE SOUTH END OF THAT MOLE ON ANY DAY THAT YEAR, AND HE ANSWERED THAT HE CANNOT VOUCH FOR THE WATER WITH HIS OWN EARS, AND SAID THE THING HE SAID IN A MARKET ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF JULY AND THAT IT WAS WRONG IN THREE PARTS OUT OF FOUR AND HAS NOT BEEN TAKEN BACK, AND THE CLERK ENTERED ALL OF IT, AND NOBODY IN THE ROOM SAID ANYTHING.**
3. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE ITEM OF RECOVERED TRANSPARENT MINERAL STAYS IN THE CUSTODY OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE AND THIS PARTY DID NOT APPLY FOR IT, AND THE HOLDER ACCEPTED THAT IN A ROOM AND SAID IN THE SAME ROOM THAT HE WANTED IT.** No hand in this harbor has held it since the fourteenth of October two years past. **THE REASON FOR NOT APPLYING IS NOT A REASON ABOUT THE ITEM: IT IS THAT THE ONLY ROAD TO THAT ITEM ON THIS COAST RUNS THROUGH A COURT THAT HAS NOT SAT, AND EVERY OFFICE THAT COULD PUT A PERSON IN FRONT OF IT WOULD HAVE TO ASK THIS PARTY SOMETHING IT ENTERED ON THE SIXTEENTH INSTANT, WHICH IS THAT IT DOES NOT PUT A NAME ON A THING IT CANNOT CHECK. THE SHAPE OF SENTENCE WAS SAID ONCE, IN THAT ROOM, AND IMPROVED ON BY NOBODY, AND NO CHARACTER REMARKED ON HOW OFTEN IT HAS BEEN SAID.**
4. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE CIRCUIT OFFICE ACKNOWLEDGED THE DISCREPANCY IN A FORM OF HALF A SHEET DATED THE TWENTY-NINTH OF NOVEMBER, WITH NO SIGNATURE AND THE NAME OF AN OFFICE AT THE FOOT, AND THE REASON IS ON THE FACE OF IT AND IS THAT A COPY WHICH HAS BEEN MADE CANNOT BE UNMADE AND AN OFFICE WHICH HAS RELEASED A TRANSCRIPT CONTAINING A DISCREPANCY AND HAS NOT ACKNOWLEDGED IT WILL BE READ IN FOUR YEARS AS AN OFFICE WHICH RELEASED IT.** It finds against nobody, it is not a finding of the inquiry, and it does not alter the record. **THE PHRASE *RISK MANAGEMENT* IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH AND THE PAGE GONE OUT OF A FILE IS NOT PRODUCED, DESCRIBED OR SUMMARISED IN IT.**
5. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — PERNEL SAYE, FIFTY-EIGHT, A COPYIST, TOOK THE SAID FORM UP IN THE MARKET ON MONDAY THE THIRTIETH OF NOVEMBER OF HER OWN ACCOUNT AND UNASKED, MADE TWENTY-ONE COPIES AT A PENNY A SHEET, AND READ THE WHOLE OF IT OUT AT THE HEAD OF THE FISH DOCK ON TUESDAY THE FIRST OF DECEMBER IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING IN ABOUT NINE MINUTES.** She was not paid by this yard, this yard did not ask her, did not send anybody and did not stand near her while she did it, and she said she would rather they did not come and stand by her. **A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY BOUGHT FOUR COPIES AT FOUR PENCE. TWO MEN OF THE THIRD LAY READ THE WHOLE OF IT STANDING UP AND GAVE IT BACK WITHOUT BUYING A SHEET.**
6. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE HOLDER ASKED MARA VENN WHETHER THIS PARTY MIGHT OFFER HER PART PAYMENT ON THE FORTY MARKS OUT OF A DAY OF WORK AND TAKE THE REST WHEN THERE IS ANY, IN A LETTER OF THE SIXTEENTH OF NOVEMBER IN HIS OWN LEFT HAND, AND SHE ANSWERED IT IN WRITING ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH, PRICE FIRST, AND THE ANSWER IS NO.** **HER PRICE IS THAT THE LETTER BE KEPT AND WHAT SHE HAS WRITTEN GO IN THE SECOND COLUMN WITH A REASON AGAINST THE LINE AND NOT ONE WORD OF IT GO IN A MARKET, AND HER REASON IS THE ONE GIVEN IN HER OWN HAND, WHICH IS THAT IN ABOUT FOUR YEARS A MAN IN A CITY IS GOING TO READ THAT A YARD WENT TO A WOMAN IT OWED FORTY MARKS TO AND ASKED WHETHER IT MIGHT PAY HER PART OF IT AND WAS REFUSED, AND THAT THE SAID READING IS GOING TO BE TRUE OF A MAN LIKE HIM AND IS NOT GOING TO BE TRUE OF HIM. THE SIX MARKS AND TWO DAYS HAS NOT MOVED AND IS NOT GOING TO BE REDUCED BY ANYBODY INCLUDING BY HER, BECAUSE IT IS HER PRICE AND NOT A DEBT.** The forty marks stands first after food, unpaid, not reduced. **The not-telling of the seventh of August is a sixth occasion not to, entered on a line of its own, with the reason of the fourth of October given again and the undertaking not to invent a second one, and it is not on the same line as the answer and is not paid.**
7. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — A QUESTION WAS ASKED IN A MARKET IN THIS HARBOR ON WEDNESDAY THE SECOND OF DECEMBER 2026, IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING, BY WIL TRANTER, FIFTY-ONE, OF THE FIRST LAY, AND IT WAS NOT ANSWERED, AND THE REFUSAL IS IN THE YARD'S OWN HAND WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE, AND THE REASON IS ABOUT A PERSON OF NO OFFICE AND NOT ABOUT THE OFFICE.** The first question was which office agreed to an alteration; the second was what an office that has kept records for three hundred years thought it was guarding against when it decided what it was allowed to lose. **THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION IS THE SECOND OF THOSE AND IT IS OPENED AND NOT ANSWERED, AND THE PARTY'S ANSWER IS THAT IT DOES NOT KNOW, GIVEN WITH THE REASON OF THE THIRTEENTH OF AUGUST AND WITH A BARE SECOND-COLUMN FACT OF THE FIFTEENTH OF AUGUST, WHICH IS A LINE OF PLACES KEPT BY MORE THAN ONE COMMUNITY FOR LONGER THAN ANY BOOK IN THAT OFFICE GOES BACK AND WHICH NAMES NOBODY AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHAT ANYBODY THOUGHT THEY WERE PROTECTING. NO OFFICE IN VEYR IS SHOWN A DOCUMENT THAT WOULD ANSWER IT.**
8. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE CASE OF FIVE BELLS IS AT ABOUT FIVE AND A HALF FATHOMS INSIDE FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF THE OUTER MARKS AND IS NOT ON THE SCHEDULE OF THIS HARBOR AUTHORITY, NOR OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE, NOR OF ANYBODY'S, AND THE HOLDER SAID OUT LOUD IN A MARKET ON THE SECOND OF DECEMBER THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO BE A MAN WHO PUTS IT ON ONE IN DECEMBER TO LOOK BUSY.** The four people it belongs to are alive with no boat and no wages and about nine marks between them; their limit stands; the holder has not asked twice to have it lifted and did not ask in twenty-one days.
9. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE ELIGIBILITY OF THE HOLDER OF THE WRIT FOR THE FULL SECOND BELL EXAMINMENT IS GONE BY A FORM OF THE COURT OF WRECK CLAIMS IN A CITY, DATED THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER, WITH NO SIGNATURE AND THE NAME OF A COURT AT THE HEAD AND AT THE FOOT.** It is not a suspension, not a penalty and not a finding against anybody, and it says that a person who is not examined is not a person who has been refused. **IT IS NOT THE WRIT, AND THE HOLDER ENTERED THAT IN THE FIRST COLUMN IN HIS OWN LEFT HAND AND BEFORE ANY FIGURE: that he was put to the examination in the September of two years back and did not satisfy it, that the writ was granted eight months afterwards, and that this yard is not going to say in a street in January that the writ did this. A COPY OF THE SAID RECORD IS TO BE PRODUCED TO THAT COURT ON THE FOURTH DAY OF JANUARY, AND A PARTY WHICH DOES NOT PRODUCE IT IS NOT FINED.**
10. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE CHANDLER'S NOTE IS NOT RE-WRITTEN AND WAS SAID OUT LOUD AT THE HEAD OF THIS DOCK ON THURSDAY THE THIRD OF DECEMBER IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, FOR THE THIRD TIME IN SEVEN MONTHS, WITH THE THREE COUNTS OF WEEKS UNMOVED AT TWENTY-TWO, THIRTEEN AND ELEVEN, AND THE YARD SAID IT IS NOT GOING TO SAY IT A FOURTH TIME.** The mark figure is thirty-one and has not moved.
11. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — ALDEN MARR IS AT THE FAR BENCH ON FOUR DAYS OF THIS BATCH AND ON NO OTHER: THE SIXTEENTH AND THE NINETEENTH OF NOVEMBER, THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF NOVEMBER, AND THE THIRD OF DECEMBER. THE FIGURE OF FOUR IS COUNTED FROM THE PROSE AND WRITTEN FROM THE COUNT.**

### 10. The duplication audit for Batch 0005, run on the ten chapters as written, with the method stated

**THE METHOD IS THE THREE-PASS ONE THE BATCH 0003 REVIEW LEFT AND THE BATCH 0004 REVIEW RE-RAN, AND ALL THREE PASSES WERE RUN TWICE, BEFORE AND AFTER THE REPAIRS BELOW.**

1. **Pass one — byte comparison.** Every paragraph of twelve words or more, emphasis marks stripped, across `chapter-0191.md` … `chapter-0200.md`: **332 paragraphs compared, ONE byte-identical duplicate found, and it is now zero.** The duplicate was a single line — *Alden Marr was at the far bench on the Thursday from about ten until about four, and was not asked for anything and asked nothing* — which stood in `chapter-0192.md` and again in `chapter-0199.md`, because the nineteenth of November and the third of December are both Thursdays in this book's calendar and the same phrase came out of the same mouth twice. **The first instance is left exactly as it is and stands as the device. The second is varied in the yard's own idiom, with no fact added and no fact removed, and it now reads *And the far bench was occupied on the Thursday from about ten until about four*, which is also the form Chapter 200's read-out uses for all four days.**
2. **Pass two — fingerprint and containment.** Every paragraph of twelve words or more, keyed on its **first forty words**, which catches a truncated copy because the copy and its original share an opening. Then the same set run pairwise for **proper containment**, one paragraph's whole token sequence being a prefix of another's. **ZERO forty-word opening matches and ZERO cross-chapter containment pairs at the final pass, against one of each at the first.** The fingerprint pair was the cistern paragraph: `chapter-0191.md` and `chapter-0198.md` both opened *And at about ten on the Monday morning the cistern behind the engine house was charged at no figure by four men this yard does not know and this party did not walk it, and the rota is a Monday and a Thursday, and this party has walked none of them…* **The first instance is left exactly as it is. The second is varied to *And on the Monday morning the cistern behind the engine house was charged at no figure…*, with no figure added, no figure removed and no date moved, and the day's charge and the entry of the ninth of November and the refusal to add them together all stand in it.**
3. **Pass three — sentences.** Every exact sentence of eight words or more: **777 sentences compared, 47 repeated across the ten chapters, and every one of the 47 is this yard's standing inventory, the figure of the bag at the head of a chapter, or the printed text of a form being read out twice.** The highest frequencies are a form of *the fire party's hose is dead until the spring* (ten); *the Sea Wren is at the pile and this yard has not thanked him* (ten); a form of *the coast road is in type in a city beside a pilot's figure and neither is withdrawn, and this volume does not decide which of them is right* (nine); a form of *the notice of the thirty-first of October has its four clauses and has not been lifted, narrowed, re-served or altered* (eight); *nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April* (eight); a form of *the writ runs to midnight on the first of March next, four names and no fifth, and the second season is a named absence* (seven); and thirty-eight further forms at two to six each, every one of them an inventory line or a figure. **TWO OF THE FORTY-SEVEN ARE THE COPY RECORD'S OWN PRINTED HEADS AND ARE SUPPOSED TO BE IDENTICAL, BECAUSE A FORM READ OUT IN A ROOM READS THE SAME AS IT READ ON A BENCH, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF A FORM.**
4. **NONE OF THE REMAINING FORTY-FIVE IS REPAIRED, AND THE REASON IS THE ONE THE VOLUME 03 AUDIT GAVE AT ITS § 21d AND THAT `outline/volume-04.md` LOCK L23 GIVES AGAIN: the two-column read-out and the standing inventory are how this book states a position, and a harbor that improves on its own phrasing is a different book. THE DEVICE IS ONCE PER BATCH WHERE IT IS A DEVICE — THE READ-OUT, WHICH A MAN USES ON OTHER PEOPLE — AND IT WAS USED ONCE, AT THE HEAD OF THIS DOCK ON THE EVENING OF THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER. THE COPYIST'S READING OF AN OFFICE'S FORM IN A MARKET ON THE FIRST OF DECEMBER IS NOT THIS DEVICE AND THE ENTRY OF THAT CHAPTER SAYS SO ON ITS FACE, so that a later phase cannot count one as the other. **and because the fifteenth of August 2026 being a Tuesday and the first of September 2026 being a Friday are facts this volume opens on and neither is a fact the almanac gives, so the earlier half cannot be brought onto the second grid either.** The amendment then binds every chapter from 191 forward: take the days from Chapter 190 and from the chapters after it, the Mondays are the sixteenth, twenty-third and thirtieth of November, the wage Tuesdays the seventeenth and twenty-fourth of November and the first of December, the rota is a Monday and a Thursday, and the counter is the chapters' counter and does not restart. **A BOOK WITH TWO CALENDARS FOR TWENTY CHAPTERS IS A FAULT AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE, IN THE LOCK, AGAINST THE PARTY, IN THE HOUSE'S OWN FORM.** § 1 above is corrected to it and the withdrawn sentence is named as withdrawn.

### F. One conflict found, spanning three batches, and flagged for the close rather than settled

**THREE CHAPTERS IN THREE DIFFERENT BATCHES GIVE THREE STATES OF THE MARKET WALL, AND THE REVIEWER'S OWN MINOR FINDING AT ITEM 9 IS A SYMPTOM OF IT.** `chapters/volume-03/chapter-0150.md:37,39,41` stages the sheet of the fifteenth of August going up **on the outside** of the naval paper of the fourth of August, and has the ship's hand say so in about forty people's hearing — *it went up on the outside of it, and a sheet that goes up goes up on the outside* — and refuse to pretend that a sheet under a naval paper is a sheet on its own. `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0174.md:43`, in Movement 3, has a man say the yard's sheet is *under the naval paper that came down in August*, which is a third arrangement again. `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0192.md:19`, in this batch, says the yard *put a sheet on that wall on the fifteenth of August and had a naval paper nailed over it*. **THE THREE CANNOT ALL BE TRUE OF THE SAME SHEET.** Item 9 above was repaired **without** choosing between them, because Chapter 199 now repeats Chapter 192's own statement to the man in the market and does not say which paper is on top of which, **so this phase has added a voice to a contradiction that was already on the page rather than settled it.**

**NONE OF THE THREE CHAPTERS IS IN THIS PHASE.** Chapter 150 is Volume 03, which is closed and audited, and Chapter 174 is Batch 0003 of this volume, which was written and reviewed in an earlier phase. The precedent is the one at § E of the Batch 0004 review repairs above and at the foot of the Batch 0003 review repairs: **a missed instance outside the phase is flagged for the volume close and not edited.** It is flagged here, and it is flagged **because the review found a symptom of it inside this batch and a reader can now check all three against each other in an afternoon**, and because the Volume 04 close is already instructed to rule on the two-calendar fault in lock L1 and to rule on the market wall, and this belongs in the same ruling. **THE CLOSE SHOULD RULE ON WHICH ARRANGEMENT IS CANON, AND THE RULE SHOULD BE ENTERED ON THE FACE OF BOTH CHAPTERS, NOT LEFT AS THREE PASSING REFERENCES.** `outline/series.md` and `outline/ending.md` are untouched and neither bears on it.

### 3. The two-calendar fault, and its ruling

**CHAPTERS 151 TO 170 RUN ON ONE GRID AND CHAPTERS 171 TO 200 RUN ON ANOTHER, THREE DAYS OUT FROM IT, AND THE CHANGE FALLS BETWEEN CHAPTER 170'S SATURDAY THE THIRTIETH OF SEPTEMBER AND CHAPTER 171'S THURSDAY THE FIRST OF OCTOBER 2026. THE AMENDMENT AT THE FOOT OF `outline/volume-04.md`'s LOCK L1 STANDS, IS BINDING ON EVERY LATER VOLUME, AND IS NOT RE-OPENED.**

**IT IS NOT REPAIRABLE INSIDE THE TEXT OF VOLUME 04. The only textual repair is a re-staging of twenty chapters costing one sitting of two days, six wage Tuesdays, six slate-wall wipes, a rota on six days, a cistern run on six days, forty days of standing inventory and a fortnight of read-out, and it would be a different book. THE CHOSEN REMEDY IS THE HOUSE RULE: THE ALMANAC IS NOT THE RULE OF THIS BOOK, THE CHAPTERS DECIDE EVERY DATE, SIX SINGLE-CHAPTER DATE FAULTS ARE REPAIRED, AND A PLANNING FILE MAY NOT PRINT A DAY TABLE A CHAPTER CAN CONTRADICT. `outline/volume-05.md` LOCK L1 THEREFORE FIXES THE GRID BY RULE AND BY ANCHOR AND PRINTS NO TABLE, AND LOCK L1a STATES THE FAULT FOR THE VOLUME THAT INHERITS IT.**

**THE SLATE WALL'S COUNTER SURVIVES THE FAULT INTACT AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE REPAIR QUESTION: sixteen wipes, one running number, no gap, no repeat, from the fourteenth of August (the fifteenth) to the thirtieth of November (the thirtieth). The batch's last line is a fact, is checkable by any man who can get off a mole, and nobody in the shed improves on it.**

THE COUNT OF ENVELOPES ON THE BENCH IN THAT CHEST STANDS AT TWENTY THROUGHOUT, AND IT ADVANCES ONLY WITH THE COLUMN AND ONLY WITH A PAID WAGE. ### 4. The documents of this batch, one at a time, and what each of them is

1. **THE FORM WITH NO DATE ON IT, Wednesday the ninth of December, brought up the hill on foot by a man in a coat, left on a bench in the shed.** A sheet and a half. **No signature anywhere and no date at the head, none in the body and none at the foot, and at the foot, where a signature would be, the name of an office. THE NAME OF THAT OFFICE IS NOT ON ANY PAGE OF THIS YARD'S BOOK AND IS NOT PRINTED IN THIS FILE, AND THE REASON IS ON THE PAGE AND IS NOT A DEFECT: it is the form of an office in a city of the same kind as the form that put its name at the foot of the acknowledgment of the twenty-ninth of November 2026 and signed nothing, and this yard has entered that it does not know what office it is and is not going to guess in a book a man in a city is going to read. IT IS NOT THE CIRCUIT OFFICE, NOT THE COURT OF WRECK CLAIMS, NOT THE HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND NOT THE COAST OFFICE, AND THE COAST OFFICE WAS GIVEN NO THIRD SENTENCE IN THIS BATCH AND SAYS NOTHING AT ALL IN IT.** It proposes that one copy of a record be held in this place for the use of this coast, that the holder of it be named in the entry as the person who holds it, and that the entry be made now and not on any later day; that the party is not asked to be examined, licensed, enrolled, paid, or to find anything, and is asked one question, which is whether it will hold a copy of a record for the coast, and that the answer is to be entered with the name of the party, the place and the date of the answer, **and that the date of the answer is the only date on the sheet**; **that the office does not say what follows an answer of no, does not say what an address is used for, and does not say what an office in a city is going to do with the name of a party in a working harbor, and that if a man asks it in a room the answer will be that the office does not decide that and does not direct it either.** And it says on its own face that a party which holds a copy of a record becomes the address of that copy, that a copy which has been made cannot be unmade, and that an address, once it is an address, can be found.
2. **THE MAN IN A COAT OF AN OFFICE IN A CITY, the ninth of December. HE IS NOT NAMED ON ANY PAGE AND THE REASON IS ON THE PAGE: a man's name at the foot of a thing is a thing a man in a city can hold for four years, which is the reason a clerk of the circuit office gave at this bench on the twenty-third of November and which the yard has in its first column in two hands. He said he is not the man who directs it. HE SAID THE CROWN'S POSITION IN ONE SENTENCE AND IN ONE SENTENCE ONLY: *testimony is safe in one place and nowhere else, and this harbor is not that one, and that is not an opinion, it is what three hundred years of an office is.* NOBODY IN THAT SHED SAID IT WAS A LIE, NOBODY SAID THE MAN WAS ANYTHING AT ALL, AND NO VILLAIN, ANTAGONIST, OFFICE, MINISTRY OR PERSON WAS INVENTED FOR IT. He said he did not know what picking up a sheet off a bench is, and that the office that made the sheet does not say, and that he had asked and had been told the office does not decide that. He went down the mole at about half past eleven and nobody followed him, which is a thing this party does not do with a man who has come up a hill.**
3. **THE ANSWER TO THE FORM. IT WAS NOT WRITTEN IN THIS BATCH.** The sheet is still on the bench in the shed at the close of the twenty days, with a pump under it, and has not been answered and has not been put in the stove. **A DECISION NOT TO WRITE A SENTENCE IS ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN IN CHAPTER 205 AND IT IS A DECISION, NOT A REFUSAL TO THE OFFICE.**
4. **THE LETTER OF A PRINTER, Wednesday the twenty-third of December, one sheet, dated the twentieth, arriving in the ordinary post.** Jonas Peake, forty-four, a printer in a town of about two thousand up this coast, **who gives his trade and says the trade is not an office.** **IT IS NOT A THREAT AND NOT A FAVOR AND HE SAYS SO HIMSELF.** Its content: a man who sells ice up this coast bought a sheet at a counter off the fish market in this harbor on the sixth of December, paid a penny for it, put it in a box of fish and sent it up the coast, and the sheet is a half sheet with the name of an office at the foot of it and no man's name anywhere on it; the printer keeps a list of everything that comes into his shop that anybody means to keep, and the sheet is on that list with the day, the price and the name of the man who brought it; on the ninth of December **a man came to his counter and bought type, and nothing else, and asked whether he could say where a copy of a record was**; the printer said he could not say, the man did not argue and did not press him, wrote down the name of the town the sheet came from and the day, said thank you, and went out and bought his type; the printer has a line in his own book with a town on it and no address, and a man in a city has a line in his own book with his shop on it, and one of those lines is going into a letter inside a fortnight. **HIS ONE QUESTION IS WHERE THE COPY OF THE RECORD IS.** He is not asking for the sheet, is not asking for the record to be sent, is not asking this party to be examined about it or licensed or enrolled or paid, and is not asking on behalf of anybody; he is not going to write again until this party writes to him; and he is not going to put the letter in anybody's book but his own. **THIS PARTY DID NOT ANSWER IT, AND THE REASON IS IN THE FIRST COLUMN AND NOT THE SECOND, AND IT IS THAT A REPLY IS A DOCUMENT WITH THIS YARD'S NAME AT THE FOOT OF IT.**
5. **THE SHEET OF PAPER BOUGHT AT THE COUNTER, Friday the eighteenth of December, one sheet, a penny, paid into a copyist's own hand.** **It was for this yard's own use and not for a copy of anything, and the reason against the line is that this party cannot put a price in a record out of a person's mouth.**

No Volume 05 chapter may name the call, and none does.**

NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN THESE TWENTY DAYS HAS MADE ANYTHING BETTER AND NO FIGURE IN THIS HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT.**

### 6. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr, thirty-two.** He writes four sheets of his own in three weeks: the two dates, the non-answering of the printer, the reason the form is not answered, and the turn. **He said one sentence in a street on the sixteenth of December that was read as an intention to keep and he did not take it back and did not correct it, and the reason he could not correct it is in the second column of Chapter 206 and is that a correction is the reason and the reason is the four of the Sill's line and it does not go into a street. THE SAME TWO MEN OF THE FIRST LAY WERE SAYING A THING ABOUT THIS YARD AT THE HEAD OF THIS DOCK AGAIN ON SATURDAY THE NINETEENTH, AND HE DID NOT GO UP ON THAT DAY EITHER, AND THE ENTRY SAYS THAT HE DID NOT.** He refused a day of about three marks on the twenty-fifth and put the figure of three marks against that day.
- **Nessa Pike, twenty-seven, a party of one and a half until the first of March.** She wrote the eleven-line list of the twenty-second of November past out again beside a form, read the limit of the four of the Sill out once in the shed on the fourteenth and said she was not going to read it again, told the truth about the two prices at a copyist's counter, took a price from a man of fifty-five at the boards and entered it before anybody asked, said the party cannot be helped out of a sentence said in a street, and said that both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other, once, in Chapter 209, about a copy of a record and about this yard's name. **SHE HAS NOT BEEN THANKED AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK, AND HE HAS NOT THANKED HER AND IS NOT GOING TO AND DID NOT.**
- **Ors Kest, forty-four.** One scene, in the open air at the foot of the mole's steps on Thursday the tenth, in about eleven people's hearing. He said his office's view is that a thing kept in Morrow Quay is a thing kept in Morrow Quay, and gave the reason, which is that a record in a city can be asked for and got at by a man with a carriage and a record in Morrow Quay can be got at by about four people, and that a man in a city who wants a thing in a fortnight will not send a carriage and will write to this harbor authority first. **He named what his office cannot do — it cannot certify a copy of a record, cannot hold a record for the coast, cannot enter this in his ledger because the ledger is spent and the ninth acknowledgement is spent and a tenth may not be entered and will not be, cannot renew the writ of the first of May and is the only office that can, cannot overrule a seizure and cannot certify a glass witness — and said he was not going to do the rest of it and pretend afterwards that it was part of it. He entered the whole thing on a page of his own and NOT in the ledger, and gave the reason, which is that a page of his own is not a record and cannot be produced on demand by anybody. THE PRICE WAS NAMED BEFORE HE SAID YES AND IT IS NOT A MORNING OF THE TIDE GANG AND NOT A DAY OF THE THIRD LAY AND NOT ANYBODY'S BODY: it is that his office becomes a name in this business, and that after he has said it once every party who comes up that hill about anything at all is going to be told at the foot of those steps that this office has an opinion about a copy of a record, for years, including the ones who have nothing to do with this party. HE IS STILL NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY, SAID IT AGAIN IN A STREET, AND THE YARD AGREES WITH HIM AND DID NOT IMPROVE ON THE ENTRY OF THE NINETEENTH OF NOVEMBER. NO TENTH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT WAS ENTERED AND NONE WAS ASKED FOR TWICE.**
- **Pernel Saye, fifty-eight, a copyist with a counter in a room off the fish market, open to anybody from eight until the market is off the boards, where a sheet is a penny and forty sheets a shilling.** She priced two things in her own trade's words on Friday the eighteenth: a page that anybody in nine places could check is nine people who each went and got it, and nine men's time, and a man's time in a working port in December is a day at about three marks, so the price of a checkable page is the whole of a day's work at a seam; and a page that nobody can check is a sheet and a shed and no money at all and is the one that cannot be shown to anybody. She said a paragraph is a trade and a trade travels, and that the moment a reason goes on a page it is a paragraph and a reason cannot be kept in a paragraph. **AND SHE SAID, ABOUT SHEETS IN GENERAL AND NOT ABOUT THIS YARD'S, THAT A SHEET WITH AN OFFICE'S NAME AT THE FOOT OF IT AND NO MAN'S NAME ON IT ANYWHERE IS THE EASIEST THING IN THE WORLD FOR HER TO SELL BECAUSE THERE IS NOBODY ON IT FOR HER TO ASK WHERE IT CAME FROM, AND THAT THOSE GO OUT OF A SHOP AND INTO SOMEBODY'S BUYER'S BOOK AND NOBODY EVER KNOWS WHERE THEY HAVE BEEN, AND SHE ASKED IT TO BE NOTICED THAT SHE HAD SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE SHEET ON THE COUNTER. THAT SENTENCE IS THE SEED OF CHAPTER 209'S TURN AND IS PLANTED FIVE CHAPTERS BEFORE IT IS HARVESTED. SHE WAS PAID A PENNY AND IT WAS FOR A SHEET OF HER PAPER AND NOT FOR A COPY OF ANYTHING, AND NO PAGE OF THE COPY OF THE RECORD WAS READ ALOUD IN THAT ROOM AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM HEARD ONE LINE OF IT.**
- **Jonas Peake, forty-four, a printer in a town of about two thousand up this coast.** An ordinary person with a trade and no office and no title, who is not a villain and is not on a ladder. He asks one question, in good faith, and he is not answered.
- **Denzil Hare, of the third lay, about fifty, a boat of his own and no crew of his own since the spring.** Asked one question at the head of this dock on the sixteenth and was not answered, and the yard's answer to him is what produced the misreading.
- **A man of the second lay, about fifty-five, with a lighter, who lightered alongside that mole on the sixth of November 2026.** He told the ship's hand a thing at the boards on the twentieth of December and told her and not the holder, and gave the whole of it, and refused to give the name of the hired man and said that if this party went down to that quay he would be the man who told it.

She was not written to in three weeks and no letter of hers came up this hill.**
- **Bevin Rook is in no chapter of this batch as a person. The three nots stand. Forty marks stands whole. The head of the third column keeps his hand. THE THIRD COLUMN WAS NOT FILLED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH AND NOBODY WAS APPOINTED TO IT, AND A COLUMN NOBODY FILLS IS A COLUMN SOMEBODY ELSE FILLS.**
- **Alden Marr, sixty-one, at the far bench on four days and no other — the seventh, the eleventh, the eighteenth and the twenty-first — not asked, asking nothing, and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the four.**
- **Captain Veyra Holt is not in this harbor, is not in a room, and is a hand on a list in a city with this yard's four returns in her hands, and her name is on no page of this batch. Halven Rook is not in a room and is not in this batch. Magister Ilya Serr is on no page of this batch at all and the seal line is referred to, where it is referred to, as the seal line. - **THE FOUR WHO MAY NOT APPEAR IN A ROOM, AND DID NOT: MARA VENN, BEVIN ROOK, ALDEN MARR AS A PERSON RATHER THAN A BENCH, AND THE MAN IN A COAT. NO NEW ANTAGONIST, NO NEW INSTITUTION, NO NEW FINAL ENEMY, NO NAMED OFFICE THAT DID NOT EXIST IN VOLUME 04, AND NO NEW CHARACTER WITH A TITLE, UNIFORM, COMMISSION OR MOTIVE OUTSIDE HER OWN TRADE'S WORDS.**

**THE WAGE COLUMN STANDS AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS FROM THE FIRST PAGE OF THIS BATCH TO THE LAST, THE FIFTH OF MARCH THE OLDEST THROUGHOUT, AND THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE ON ANY OF ITS THREE TUESDAYS BECAUSE THE WAGE WAS NOT PAID ON ANY OF THEM. THE COUNT OF ENVELOPES ON THE BENCH IN THAT CHEST STANDS AT TWENTY THROUGHOUT, AND IT ADVANCES ONLY WITH THE COLUMN AND ONLY WITH A PAID WAGE. THE NUMBER OF WEEKS FALLEN DUE THIS YEAR WITH NO ENVELOPE STANDING AGAINST THEM IS NINE AT THE OPEN, TEN AFTER THE TWENTY-NINTH OF DECEMBER, ELEVEN AFTER THE FIFTH OF JANUARY AND TWELVE AFTER THE TWELFTH OF JANUARY, AND ALL TWELVE ARE GIVEN IN THE SAME BREATH WHEREVER THE FIGURE APPEARS AND NOT ONE AFTER THE OTHER: the fifteenth of August, the fifth of September, the sixth of October, the third of November, the seventeenth of November, the first of December, the eighth, the fifteenth and the twenty-second of December, the twenty-ninth of December, the fifth of January and the twelfth of January.**

**THE REASON THE WAGE IS NOT PAID WAS ENTERED ONCE, IN THE FIRST COLUMN, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN LEFT HAND, ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-NINTH OF DECEMBER PAST, AND IT WAS NOT RE-ENTERED, NOT IMPROVED ON AND NOT SAID AGAIN ON THE FIFTH OR THE TWELFTH OF JANUARY; CHAPTERS 216 AND 219 EACH SAY IN THEIR OWN WORDS THAT THE REASON IS THE REASON OF THE TWENTY-NINTH AND IS NOT BEING IMPROVED ON.** The reason, whole: **that a wage is a week and not a payment, and that paying one week out of ten weeks leaves a bag that pays one week and no other, and that a man who is paid a week in the last week of December and is paid nothing in the second week of January has been given a figure and not a wage, and that this yard has a page for a figure and does not want one; and that the column would stand at twenty-seven lines and one hundred and eight marks with the fifth of March still the oldest, and that a column with the fifth of March still the oldest and the twenty-ninth of December newest is a column that is nine weeks out of order, and that this yard is not going to begin it.** **THIS REASON IS AN AUTHOR-LEVEL DECISION OF THIS BATCH AND IT IS AT § 12 item 1. IT IS NOT A FIGURE, IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, IT IS NOT ANYBODY ELSE'S REASON, AND IT MAY NOT BE IMPROVED ON BY A LATER CHAPTER.**

**NO ITEM ON THIS HARBOR'S LIST OF WHAT A YARD OWES WAS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED IN THIS BATCH, AND THE WAGE IS ON THAT LIST.** Thirty-one on the chandler's note, not re-written, its three counts of weeks unmoved at twenty-two, thirteen and eleven, **and the yard did not say that note out loud in the five weeks ended on the fourteenth of January and did not say it once in these twenty days.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks owing to a man of Ashtide for the eighth of August, unmoved, **and he is not named in that book in any of these ten chapters and nobody has been sent for him and nobody in this batch said a word about him.** Seven pence owing to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid, and **not paid out of a sheet of paper at a penny, and that is now said in three of the ten chapters.** Eight marks and a day of a boat owing to this harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, **and he was not asked anything in these twenty days, he is not in a room in any of them, no digit of anything he said on the second of July is printed, the chest was not opened and was not brought down the hill.** Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots of the eighth of June standing, **the head of the third column keeping the boy's hand, the column not filled on any day of this batch, and nobody appointed to it.** Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, unpaid since the fifteenth of October, not one mark paid and not one shilling offered, **and she has told this yard not to ask her again this winter and this yard has not asked her once in these twenty days.**

### 4. The documents of this batch, one at a time, and what each of them is

1. **NINETEEN LINES, WRITTEN BY THE SHIPWRIGHT ON WEDNESDAY THE THIRTIETH OF DECEMBER PAST IN HER OWN HAND ON THE BOARDS, READ OUT ONCE IN THE SHED, AND NOT ADDED TO.** It is a list of what a thing that has to float and be found in this harbor is made of, in a shipwright's words, and it is a list and not a plan, and a plan is what you do when somebody is going to pay for it. **Every item on it is a figure this yard cannot pay or gear it does not own, and the seventh is a hand, and a hand is a person, and this yard has not got a person.** The name that is not on it is the only other name this yard has. **NO BUOY WENT INTO ANY WATER, NO LIST BECAME A PLAN, AND NO STAGE OF ANY KIND WAS TAKEN OR NAMED IN CONNECTION WITH IT.**
2. **A PAGE OFF A PRINTED SHEET OUT OF A PRESS IN A CITY, LYING ON THE BOARDS IN THIS HARBOR SINCE SATURDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF DECEMBER PAST WITH A STONE ON IT, AND SEEN ON WEDNESDAY THE SIXTH OF JANUARY, **AND THE CHAPTER'S OWN WORDING IS *THE SATURDAY BEFORE LAST*, WHICH FROM A WEDNESDAY IS THE TWENTY-SIXTH AND NOT THE SECOND, BECAUSE THE SECOND OF JANUARY IS THE SATURDAY LAST**.** It is folded twice and there is a thumb's width of dirt in the second fold. On it, in a column of five figures about what a boat of a given tonnage costs to be moved, are two figures about a bar of gravel off the mouth of this harbor, side by side in the same weight of type: **two and three-quarters, which is this yard's, and two and a half, which is a pilot's.** **NEITHER IS WITHDRAWN. BOTH ARE IN TYPE. THE KETTLE WAS NOT LOOKED AT AND IS NOT GOING TO BE LOOKED AT BY THIS YARD. THE REFUSED LICENCE STANDS UNREVERSED, THE THIRTY MARKS WERE NOT PAID, ARE NOT OWED TO ANYBODY, AND CANNOT BE APPLIED TO ANYTHING. THE WORD *NETWORK* IS IN NO MOUTH IN THIS BATCH.**
3. **A MAN'S OWN FIGURE FOR THE BAR OF GRAVEL, OFFERED AND REFUSED, AND NOT IN THIS BOOK.** A man of fifty-eight of the first lay, with a boat of about two hundred and thirty tons of his own, who has taken that printed sheet out of a city every three weeks for nineteen years, had a mark and a half in his own book since he was thirty-four and took it up this hill on a folded sheet with a year and a month on it and the name of a man who had been in his boat. **The holder refused it in the street and said he was not asking for the figure and was refusing one, and gave item eleven as the reason. THE FIGURE IS NOT IN THIS YARD'S BOOK, WAS NOT ASKED FOR, AND WILL NOT BE ASKED FOR.**
4. **A FOLDED SHEET WITH A FIGURE ON IT IN A MAN'S OWN HAND, LAID ON THE BOARDS ON THE SIXTH OF JANUARY AND TAKEN OFF THEM BY THE MAN WHO PUT IT THERE.** It is not in this yard's book. **THE OBJECT WAS ITEM ELEVEN OF THE LIST OF THE TWENTY-SECOND OF NOVEMBER PAST, AND THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THAT LINE IS A REFUSAL OF A MAN'S OWN FIGURE AND NOT A REQUEST FOR ONE, AND THE LINE IS NOT OFF THE LIST AND IS NOT GOING TO BE.**
5. **NOTHING ANSWERED.** The sheet and a half with no signature and no date on it is still on the bench in that shed and is not answered and is not in the stove, **and on Thursday the fourteenth of January a corner of it about the width of two fingers had gone soft**, and the yard did not lift it off the bench and gave the reason on the page: there is nowhere in this harbor for her to lift it on to.

### 5. The dated positions at the end of Chapter 220

- **The slate wall behind the reeve's bench came down bare three times in this batch, all Mondays, all with the clerk keeping his own page and not mentioning it, and no sitting was held on any of them: Monday the twenty-eighth of December being the thirty-fourth Monday since the first of May, Monday the fourth of January the thirty-fifth, Monday the eleventh the thirty-sixth. THE COUNTER DID NOT RESTART AND IS THIRTY-FOUR, THIRTY-FIVE AND THIRTY-SIX.**
- **The cistern behind the engine house was charged at no figure by four men this yard does not know on six rota days in twenty days — the twenty-eighth and thirty-first days of December instant and the fourth, seventh, eleventh and fourteenth days of January instant — and this party walked none of them. THE WALK IS NIL AND IT STAYS NIL. The charge of the ninth day of November 2026 stands entered with no figure against it, and this party is not going to say in a street what those six and that one make between them.**
- **The far bench is entered in six of the ten chapters of this batch, covering twelve of the twenty days, and is not claimed on the other eight. IT WAS NOT OCCUPIED AT ANY HOUR ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH, TWENTY-SEVENTH, THIRTIETH AND THIRTY-FIRST DAYS OF DECEMBER INSTANT, NOR ON THE FIRST, SECOND, THIRD, FOURTH, THIRTEENTH OR FOURTEENTH DAYS OF JANUARY INSTANT, AND EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS ENTERED WITH NO FIGURE OF WHAT CAME BEFORE IT: there are days of these twenty this party has not entered and is not going up that hill again to enter, and a man who comes up and sees that bench empty and asks what it was on the day before will be told that they do not know. IT WAS OCCUPIED ON THE ELEVENTH OF JANUARY INSTANT FROM ABOUT TEN UNTIL ABOUT FOUR, AND WAS NOT OCCUPIED ON THE TENTH AT ANY HOUR. NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING ON ANY DAY, ASKING NOTHING ON ANY DAY, NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, AND CALDER MARR DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM ON ANY DAY OF THE TWENTY.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about a hundred and ninety-seven days up the crown of that mole at the end of Chapter 211 and about two hundred and fifteen days up it at the end of Chapter 220, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved. The sequence across the ten chapters is 197, 199, 201, 203, 205, 207, 209, 211, 213 and 215, one day a day, each chapter keying its figure to its last day. **THE FIGURE IS STATED ONCE IN EACH OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND NOT TWICE IN ANY OF THEM, AND CHAPTER 213, WHICH HAD NOT STATED IT AT ALL, NOW DOES, IN ITS FIRST COLUMN AGAINST THE WALK UP THE CROWN, AND CHAPTER 220'S FIRST COLUMN NO LONGER GIVES IT TWICE AND SAYS INSTEAD THAT THE FIGURE IS IN THE CLOSING POSITION BELOW AND IS NOT GIVEN TWICE, ON CHAPTER 210'S OWN PRECEDENT.** The party went past both of them twice in these twenty days, on the Wednesday the thirtieth of December past and on the Wednesday the thirteenth of January instant, and touched neither time.**
- **The notice of the thirty-first of October has its four clauses and has not been lifted, narrowed, re-served or altered, and no person, no boat and no lead of this yard went inside its first clause on any day of the twenty. The plate at the fifth seam is in eleven feet in this mole's own foundation stone, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT STANDS OPEN, and no better letter was written about it in three weeks. The custody room was not asked for, nothing came out of it, no digit of any of the three numbers is in this yard's book, and the question that no paper in this harbor or in that office's copying room answers was not put to anybody. The lead plug is not asked about, not printed, not opened and not brought down the hill. The glass storm is not referred to. The run under this town is not referred to. The compartment is not named and no step of its finding is restated. The custody-log re-entry of the twentieth of December gave no reason and is not referred to.**
- **The delayed note stands at eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them, nothing was entered in these twenty days and nothing was measured, the delay is a hand's width of a second and has not moved, and nobody in this harbor has ever said why. No Volume 05 chapter may name the call, and none of these ten does.**
- **There are four returns up this coast and there is no fifth, and no day of this batch produced a finding of worked glass and no return of any kind was made. The plate, the boy, the third column, the five bells, the delay, the custody items, the lead plug, the coast road, the harbor's poverty, the case of five bells and the third of the four Gannet documents are all exactly where Batch 0001 left them.**
- **The harbor is poorer at the close of this batch than at its open. One herring berth of two is out, the north berth is out, the mole-head light is not on because a light costs oil, the fire party's hose is dead until the spring, the tide gang is four men short, the hard at Ashtide is unanswered, the cistern is charged at no figure on six rota days and walked on none, the compressor's gland is unpaid and useless and the thing after the gland is the hose and this harbor has no hose and no figure has been put on the hose and none is going to be, nineteen winters are in a list being made up in a city by a woman at a table who has this yard's four returns in her hands, the *Sea Wren* is at the pile and this yard has not thanked him, a man of fifty-eight's mark and a half is in his own book and nowhere else, a boat of forty tons is a hand short since the middle of July, and a name came off a list in a book in the next town down this coast on Friday the eighth of January. NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN THESE TWENTY DAYS HAS MADE ANYTHING BETTER AND NO FIGURE IN THIS HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT.**

### 6. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr, thirty-two.** He went up that mole's steps on the first of January and sat down on the third of them for about a minute and a half, and he said no to a man's key in a street with about eleven people in it, and he refused a man's own figure in a street, and he did not go over to the far bench on the eleventh of January, and he did not go up to either of the two men of the first lay on any of the three days they said a thing at the head of that dock. **He wrote five sheets of his own in three weeks: the decision to take the next day, the wage, the reason a refusal is not correctable in a street, the turn, and the turn's cost.** **THE ONE NAMING OF THE CONDITION IS NOT IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE.**
- **Nessa Pike, twenty-seven, a party of one and a half until the first of March.** She wrote nineteen lines on a board with her back to the wind and read them out once, and she said the seventh line is a person and a person is not a figure and is not going on that page; she put the figure of a day that was offered and not taken on the page against no day at all; she did not put a man's name in this yard's book on the day the name came off another man's book and gave the reason; she said the shape of sentence once in this batch, in Chapter 218, about a room above a chandler's and the man in it, and no character remarked on how often it has been said and none said it belonged to a Volume 02 room and no fisher claimed to have invented it. **SHE HAS NOT BEEN THANKED AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK, AND HE HAS NOT THANKED HER AND IS NOT GOING TO AND DID NOT.**
- **Pernel Saye, fifty-eight, a copyist with a counter in a room off the fish market.** One scene, on Thursday the seventh of January instant, at about eleven. She priced what she could price and refused to price the rest and gave the reason, that a guess in a list is worse than a blank, because a blank can be filled in by a man who knows and a guess cannot be got out. **Three things, two of them in her trade and one not, and she said which was which: that a yard of one and a half with about three marks in it cannot build anything, and that that is a thing about three marks and not a thing about anybody; that a thing on the water is not a building but a bill, made once against built for ever, and that nobody can produce the number of times anybody is going to look at it; and that in thirty-one years no man who ever came to that counter with a list has asked her what it will cost to BE the thing afterwards.** She was asked what a man has got to know to keep a thing on the water and answered it in her trade, and was asked whether there is anybody in this harbor the holder would go to and said she did not know a man of fifty-eight who does not already have three men he goes to and did not know one man in this harbor she would send a boat out in in February. **She was not told what a second column is, she did not ask, and the chapter says why: because she had been shown things for about an hour and had not been sold one, and she did not ask about a thing she had not been given. SHE CHARGED NOTHING, SHE BOUGHT NOTHING, AND NO MONEY OF THIS WARD WENT INTO THAT ROOM ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH. She is not a villain and she is not on a ladder and nothing in her mouth knows anything.**
- **A man of sixty-eight, who keeps a dry room with a firebox, a lock and a shelf above a chandler's on the north side of this town, and has kept it since he was thirty-one.** An ordinary person in his own trade's words. He offered a shelf, said he was asking for nothing, said he would give a second key this yard will not need, said he was not asking this yard to sign anything and did not know what being examined about it meant and did not want to know, said the room goes to a man who buys chandlers in the spring and that man will put a paper in a sack, and said he would tell people what happened and would not say this yard is keeping it because he did not see it keeping it. **THE ANSWER WAS NO, AND THE REASON WAS GIVEN IN THE STREET IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, AND THE PRICE OF GIVING IT WAS NAMED BEFORE IT WAS GIVEN: that about eleven people were hearing the reason.** He has not been asked again and is not going to be.
- **Two men of the first lay, unnamed, unasked.** They said a thing about this yard at the head of that dock on **three** days inside five weeks — the seventeenth and nineteenth of December past, and now Saturday the ninth of January instant, when one of them said that a dry room was turned down in this town in this weather and the other said that they will have somewhere and that a man does not turn down a man's key unless he has a better one. **NEITHER MAN IS NAMED, THIS PARTY HAS NOT GOT EITHER NAME, NOBODY HAS ASKED EITHER OF THEM ANYTHING, AND THIS YARD DID NOT GO UP ON ANY OF THE THREE DAYS. THE THIRD OF THE THREE WAS NOT OUT OF NOTHING AND THE ENTRY SAYS SO: a man asked a question in front of about eleven people on that dock and this yard said no in front of about eleven people and the two of them were standing there.**
- **A man of fifty-eight of the first lay with a boat of about two hundred and thirty tons**, who took a page off a printed sheet up a hill, and who said that there is not one man on this coast who has ever wanted his figure, and that he has told it to two people in thirty years and one of them is dead. He went down the hill and is not coming back about a figure.
- **A man of about forty of the third lay, one of three part owners in a boat of about forty tons of his own**, who told the ship's hand at the boards on Friday the first of January instant that his boat has been short a hand since the fifteenth of May past, that is seven months and seventeen days, the man he took in March having gone into a second trade in October, and that it has been one hand short since the middle of July past, which is the week the boy came off his boat, and that the three part owners have been making it up out of the shares, and that four marks, one shilling and eightpence has come out of his own share since then and is not coming back. **He asked this yard for nothing, said he was not going to ask in a month either, and he said the thing he expected her not to ask about, which is that there are four men in that crew now and not one of them has gone to see the boy who was in that boat in June, and that he is one of the four and has not gone.**
- **A man of the second lay with a boat of about seventy tons of his own, who came up that hill on the twenty-eighth of December and was told yes, and on the first of January and was told that the day could not be taken, and on the eighth and the eleventh of January with a pump and a man.** **HE HAS COME UP THAT HILL FOUR TIMES IN THE TWENTY DAYS AND NOT ON THE SATURDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF DECEMBER, WHICH IS CORRECTED IN PLACE: CHAPTER 212 SAID HE CAME BACK UP THE HILL THE MORNING AFTER HE WAS REFUSED, AND CHAPTER 211, WHICH IS THE CHAPTER THAT OWNS THE SATURDAY, NEITHER STAGES NOR RECORDS IT, SO THE VISIT IS OUT AND THE TWO PASSAGES THAT ASSERTED IT ARE CORRECTED. THE FIGURE ON THE PAGE IS NOW: HE CAME UP ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF DECEMBER AND WAS TOLD YES; HE CAME UP ON THE FIRST OF JANUARY AND WAS TOLD THE DAY COULD NOT BE TAKEN; HE CAME UP ON THE EIGHTH AND THE ELEVENTH OF JANUARY WITH A PUMP AND A MAN AND WORKED BOTH DAYS. FOUR TIMES ON THE PAGE, THREE ASKS AND THREE ANSWERS, AND *THE SECOND TIME IN FOUR DAYS* AND *A THIRD TIME IN A WEEK* BOTH STAND.**
- **A man of thirty-one, in that crew, with a mother in the next town down this coast, who put his own name down at a yard in that town on the Wednesday and took it off on Friday the eighth of January instant in about four seconds with a pen.** He is named once in the prose, by the man of the second lay, and **HE IS NOT IN THIS YARD'S BOOK, AND THAT IS THE CHAPTER'S WHOLE MECHANISM: the name is in the speaker's mouth and not in the page, and the reason is entered against the line, and a man in this harbor can go up that road and ask that yard and be told that a name came off a list on that day.**
- **Ors Kest is in no chapter of this batch and in no room in it.** His page of his own went in on the tenth of December past and he said he was not going to do that twice inside a month without saying so out loud first, and it is inside a month, and so he was not asked and he is not in it. **HE IS STILL NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY.**
- **Mara Venn is in no chapter of this batch as a person, is not in a room, is not cited, quoted, produced or asked again, and no letter of hers came up that hill in these twenty days. Her forty marks stand first after food and her six marks and two days stands as a price and not a debt.**
- **Bevin Rook is in no chapter of this batch as a person.** The three nots stand. Forty marks stands whole. The head of the third column keeps his hand. **THE THIRD COLUMN WAS NOT FILLED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH AND NOBODY WAS APPOINTED TO IT, AND A COLUMN NOBODY FILLS IS A COLUMN SOMEBODY ELSE FILLS — AND THIS BATCH SHOWED WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE, IN A LIST IN A BOOK IN ANOTHER TOWN, WITH A PEN, IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS.**
- **Alden Marr, sixty-one, at the far bench on one day of this batch, the eleventh of January instant, and entered as not occupied on six others, and on neither brother going over on any of them.**
- **Captain Veyra Holt is not in this harbor, is not in a room, and her name is on no page of this batch. Halven Rook is not in a room and is not in this batch. Magister Ilya Serr is on no page of this batch at all. The man in a coat of an office in a city stays unnamed, did not come up that hill a second time in these twenty days, and the reason is on the page and is not a defect. The Court of Wreck Claims does not speak and sent nothing up that hill. The coast office said no sentence in these twenty days and was not given a third one. Ambrose Sell has not been up that hill since the twenty-eighth of October 2026 and is in no room in this batch. The four people of the Sill are not named as persons in this batch, their limit is quoted in the yard's own first column in Chapter 213, it stands, and the holder did not ask to have it lifted once in twenty days.**
- **THE FOUR WHO MAY NOT APPEAR IN A ROOM, AND DID NOT: MARA VENN, BEVIN ROOK, ALDEN MARR AS A PERSON RATHER THAN A BENCH, AND THE MAN IN A COAT. NO NEW ANTAGONIST, NO NEW INSTITUTION, NO NEW FINAL ENEMY, NO NAMED OFFICE THAT DID NOT EXIST IN VOLUME 04, AND NO NEW CHARACTER WITH A TITLE, A UNIFORM, A COMMISSION OR A MOTIVE OUTSIDE HER OWN TRADE'S WORDS. NO PERSON IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS HAS A TITLE.**

### 7. The batch's ten cards, delivered, and the two devices it spent and the two it did not

1. **211 — the days after a turn. PAID.** No working day booked on either day, and the reason against the line that a day on which nothing happens still happened. The compressor looked at for the first time since the twentieth of October, the gland, and **the answer to what useless means: the part is on the machine and it holds and there is no hose.** **The yard declines to price a foot of hose and gives the reason, that the answer is not a figure.** The working question — a day at a seam is a pump, a line, a man on the pump and a slack water, and this yard has the line and two of them and a writ and has not got a pump, and the harbor's gear has no boat of its own. **The decision: the yard will take the next day that comes up the hill, and the reason is that being findable and being quiet about it are not a choice anybody gets to make.** The read-back runs.
2. **212 — the last Tuesday of the year and a wall that comes down bare. PAID.** The thirty-fourth Monday since the first of May, bare, the clerk keeping his own page. The cistern charged on the rota day and walked on none. **A man who was refused on the twenty-fifth comes back on the twenty-eighth and is told yes, in a doorway at the foot of the mole's steps, and the reason is given out loud: on the Friday he could not say what he was doing on the Saturday morning and on the Monday he could say, and that this is the whole of the change and it is not humility.** The working day on the Tuesday, three marks in. **The wage of four marks did not go in and the number of weeks fallen due is TEN, all ten in the same breath. THE REASON THE WAGE IS NOT PAID IS ENTERED HERE, ONCE, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN LEFT HAND, AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON FOR THE REST OF THE BATCH.** The board's own device runs at about half past one in the daylight.
3. **213 — the last two days of the year, and a thing that has to be built out of nothing. PAID.** **Nineteen lines in a shipwright's hand, and every one of them a figure this yard cannot pay or gear it does not own, and the seventh a hand.** **The day's cost is entered against that day before the day is spent, and the day is spent, and the thing at the end of the day is a list and a pencil and no agreement.** The cistern charged on the Thursday and walked on none. **On the Thursday afternoon a man says out loud at the head of that dock that this was the last day of the year and that a man ought to be able to say what he had done in it, and neither of them answers him, and neither of them says the day of the month, and that is entered because a day on which a thing is said in a street is a day on which a thing was said in a street. THE BATCH CROSSES A YEAR BOUNDARY IN CHAPTER 215 AND NOT ONE CHARACTER NOTICES.** **Item eleven is said out loud in this yard's own book as a thing this yard cannot put in front of anybody, and it is not off the list and is not going to be.** No buoy went into any water. No stage was taken or named.
4. **214 — the boy in a June berth that nobody in that crew has gone to see. PAID, AND NOT ONE DAY OF IT IS A SCENE IN THE BERTH.** The yard does not go, does not write, does not send anybody, does not ask anybody who has seen him what he said, and enters that and the reason, which is the reason of the fourth of October past and is not a new one and is not invented again. **The three nots stand and forty marks stands whole.** The berth is carried by a man of the third lay at the boards: the boat is a hand short since the middle of July, three part owners, the shares have been making it up, **four marks, one shilling and eightpence out of his own share since the middle of July, being six hundred and sixty pence, and it is not coming back and nobody is going to ask for it.** **THE COST FALLS ON SOMEBODY WHO IS NOT IN THIS YARD AND IS NOT THE THIRD LAY'S FOUR DAYS, NOT A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY'S MONDAY, NOT THE TIDE GANG'S THURSDAY MORNING AND NOT A HIRED MAN'S DAY ON A LIGHTER, AND ITS SHAPE IS A MAN WHO CAME OFF THE STONE AND WAS NOT REPLACED.** And the same chapter pays the body: **a day of about three marks was offered on the first of January and could not be taken, the figure is entered against that day and against no day at all, and the reason is in the second column with no name in it and is not going to have one.** The read-back is deliberately absent and the chapter says why.
5. **215 — the fourth of January. PAID, AND THE CHAPTER IS THE NOTHING.** The thirty-fifth Monday since the first of May, bare. The cistern charged and walked on none. On the Sunday the month's being out is said out loud in a shed and answered with a sentence about the length of a month, and entered, and that is the only thing anybody in this batch says about a month or a year. **On the fourth the date on the half sheet arrived and nothing happened: no court in this harbor and none sat, no clerk came up that hill, nobody was charged with anything, nobody was fined, nobody was refused anything and nobody was examined.** The reason is the reason of the seventh of December past, said out loud in a shed once, with the hour on it, and not said a second way. **And the half of it that is in the shed and not in a market: the copy could be produced tomorrow, and a letter would be in a man's hand in nine days and in a court in ten, and nothing whatever would happen to anybody, and a clerk would have a piece of paper with this yard's name at the head of it.** The writ and the fifty-five days. The read-back runs.
6. **216 — the coast road's own figures, the refused licence, and item eleven. PAID.** **The wage does not go in and the number of weeks fallen due is ELEVEN, all eleven in the same breath.** A page off a press in a city, lying on the boards in this harbor under a stone for a week and a half, with two figures for a bar of gravel in the same weight of type and neither withdrawn, and the Kettle not looked at, and the refused licence unreversed and the thirty marks not paid and not owed to anybody and applicable to nothing. **THE OBJECT IS THE ELEVENTH LINE OF THE LIST OF WHAT IS NOT GOING INTO A ROOM. A MAN'S OWN FIGURE IS OFFERED AND REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS A REFUSAL AND NOT A REQUEST, AND THE LINE IS NOT OFF THE LIST AND IS NOT GOING TO BE.** **THE COST OF THIS CHAPTER IS THAT THIS YARD'S OWN METHOD WENT OUT LOUD IN A STREET IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FOUR VOLUMES, and what went out loud was the method and not a figure.**
7. **217 — a hand at a counter, and the trade priced again. PAID.** The cistern charged on the Thursday and walked on none. **The question put to the trade is not about paper: what a yard of one and a half with about three marks in it can actually build, what a man has to know to keep a thing on the water, and how many days a year a thing on the water takes out of a working harbor.** A copyist prices what she can price and says plainly what she cannot price, and is not a villain and is not on a ladder and **does not know what a second column is and is not told and does not ask.** **A second-column fact with a reason against it and no name in it: that no man on this coast had ever asked that trade what it costs to be a thing rather than to make it.** And the compressor's gland, and the hose, and **the working day that comes on a pump a man brought up a hill, so that the three marks is for the hands and the line and the tide and not one penny of it is for a machine.**
8. **218 — what a refusal to hold is read as. PAID AND IT IS THE BATCH'S CLIMAX.** **The party is asked, reasonably and in good faith, to hand its one true record to a place that will keep it safe. THE ANSWER IS NO, IN THE OPEN, WITH THE REASON GIVEN IN THE OPEN.** **And the no is read as an intention to keep, by two men of the first lay who were standing there, and the yard cannot correct it without putting a name on something, and this time the thing it would have to name is not four people on a weir and not a reason: it is that the only way to be read correctly is to have somewhere to put it that is not a hold, and this yard has not got one and is not going to build one in a fortnight.** **The three sentences a man can say in a street are given and every one of them is shown to be wrong. The gap is not closed and the chapter says on the page that it is not closed and that the answer is a hole and a hole in a street fills itself.** The shape of sentence is said once. **No chain of custody, no page in a drawer in five towns and no agreement about who may read a page is described anywhere in this chapter or in this batch.**
9. **219 — the cost of a day, again, and a different shape. PAID.** The thirty-sixth Monday, bare. The cistern charged and walked on none. **The far bench is occupied from about ten until about four and neither brother goes over.** A working day. **THE COST HAS A SHAPE OF ITS OWN AND IT IS NOT ANY OF THE FIVE THE BATCH WAS FORBIDDEN: a man of thirty-one took his own name off a list in a book in the next town down this coast on Friday the eighth, and a woman in an office wrote it off with a pen in about four seconds, and a man is not asked at that place again, and that is not a day and it is not a wage and it cannot be put back by anybody, and the figure of it is about six marks and the figure is the least of it. THE NAME IS IN THE SPEAKER'S MOUTH AND IS NOT IN THIS YARD'S BOOK, AND THE REASON IS ENTERED AGAINST THE LINE.** The wage does not go in and the number of weeks fallen due is TWELVE, all twelve in the same breath, and the reason is the reason of the twenty-ninth of December and is not improved on.
10. **220 — the turn. PAID.** The cistern charged on the Thursday and walked on none, and that is the sixth. The far bench entered as not occupied on both days with no figure of what came before it. **A corner of the sheet and a half gone soft on a bench about the width of two fingers, and the sheet came up that hill on foot on the ninth of December and is going, and the yard did not lift it off the bench and gave the reason on the page.** **THE COST OF THE BATCH IS READ OUT IN ONE BREATH AND EVERY ITEM IN IT IS A FIGURE ON THE PAGE: a day of about three marks refused by this yard, a day of about three marks not taken, four marks one shilling and eightpence out of a man's share, this yard's own method in a street, a name off a list, and about six marks a man will not get back — and the last of those six items is a sheet of paper.** The read-back runs, and then the turn goes in the first column in the holder's own left hand with the date and the hour on it: **a refusal to hold is read as an intention to keep; the only way to be read correctly is to have somewhere to put it that is not a hold; this yard has not got one, knows what one would cost, and is not going to pretend it knows the cost of a thing it has not built.** **A question is left standing that this batch does not answer — what a place that is not a hold is, and who would keep it, and what it costs, and where the money comes from in a harbor where the mole-head light is not on because a light costs oil — and the entry says this party is not going to answer it in a market, is not going to answer it in a room, and is not going to answer it in this book.** **The batch's last line is a fact, is checkable by any man who can get off a mole, and nobody in that shed improved on it.**

**THE READ-BACK — the day's entries read back from the top of the bench by the ship's hand and read back after her by the holder, nobody else in the shed — RAN IN FOUR OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND THE HOUSE'S OWN PLAIN-STRING TEST FOR *read it back* OR *read back after her* RETURNS THE SAME FOUR: 211, 212, 215 AND 220.** 211, 215 and 220 are the shed-evening form and 212 is **the board's own device and not the shed's** — the board written in the ship's hand on the boards at about half past one, the slate into the book, and the holder reading it back after her at half past one in the daylight, which is what Chapter 204 did and which is the working day's device. **THE CHART IS: 211 1 · 212 2 · 213 0 · 214 0 · 215 1 · 216 0 · 217 0 · 218 0 · 219 0 · 220 1. FOUR CHAPTERS, FOUR, AND THE STRING TEST AND THE COUNT AGREE.** 214's is deliberately absent and the chapter gives the reason, that a thing which four men in a boat have not done is not a thing two people in a shed are going to do for them. 217's is absent and the chapter gives its own reason. **216, 218 AND 219 ARE SILENT ON IT.**

**THE READ-OUT DID NOT RUN IN THIS BATCH AND ITS ALLOWANCE WAS NOT USED, AND THE REASON IS GIVEN AT § 1 AND IS A CHOICE.**

1. **THREE WAGES OF FOUR MARKS NOT PAID, on Tuesday the twenty-ninth of December, Tuesday the fifth of January and Tuesday the twelfth of January, and no envelope made on any of them, and the number of weeks fallen due with no envelope standing against them is TWELVE, all twelve given in the same breath wherever the figure appears.** **The reason was entered once, on the twenty-ninth of December, and was not improved on and was not said again.**
2. **A DAY OF ABOUT THREE MARKS OFFERED ON FRIDAY THE FIRST OF JANUARY AND NOT TAKEN, and the figure entered against that day and against no day at all, and the man of the second lay not told that a figure was put against it.** The reason is in the second column and has no name in it.
3. **A BOAT OF ABOUT FORTY TONS ONE HAND SHORT SINCE THE MIDDLE OF JULY, AND FOUR MARKS, ONE SHILLING AND EIGHTPENCE, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE, OUT OF A MAN'S SHARE IN IT SINCE THEN, and it is not coming back and nobody is going to ask this yard for it.** A boy of twenty-two is off the stone since the fifteenth of May past and is not replaced, and this yard did not go and did not write and did not send anybody and did not ask anybody who has seen him what he said.
4. **THIS YARD'S OWN METHOD SAID OUT LOUD IN A STREET IN THIS HARBOR ON WEDNESDAY THE SIXTH OF JANUARY IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FOUR VOLUMES, and what went out loud was the method and not a figure: that a list of what does not go into a room is the instrument this yard has and that no line of it comes off.** A method anybody in about nine people can use, and whether that is a good trade is not checkable from a mole.
5. **A NAME OFF A LIST IN A BOOK IN THE NEXT TOWN DOWN THIS COAST ON FRIDAY THE EIGHTH OF JANUARY, written off with a pen in about four seconds by a woman in an office who did not know what she was writing off and could not be asked about it, and about six marks that the man will not get back, and the name is in a speaker's mouth and is not in this yard's book.**
6. **A DRY ROOM WITH A FIREBOX, A LOCK AND A SHELF, KEPT ABOVE A CHANDLER'S ON THE NORTH SIDE OF THIS TOWN SINCE A MAN OF THIRTY-ONE WAS ITS KEEPER, OFFERED TO THIS YARD IN THE OPEN ON SATURDAY THE NINTH OF JANUARY AND REFUSED IN THE OPEN WITH THE REASON GIVEN IN THE OPEN TO ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE, and the price of giving the reason was named before it was given.** The room goes to a man who buys chandlers in the spring.
7. **THE THIRD OF THREE DAYS IN FIVE WEEKS ON WHICH TWO MEN OF THE FIRST LAY SAID A THING ABOUT THIS YARD AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK, and this yard went up on none of the three, has not got either name, has not asked either of them anything, and is not going up the hill for it.**
8. **A CORNER OF THE SHEET AND A HALF WITH NO SIGNATURE AND NO DATE ON IT, GONE SOFT ON A BENCH IN THAT SHED ABOUT THE WIDTH OF TWO FINGERS, on a sheet that came up that hill on foot on the ninth of December and is worth a penny and cannot be bought and is not lifted off the bench, and the reason it is not lifted off the bench is that there is nowhere in this harbor to lift it on to.**
9. **A MAN OF FIFTY-EIGHT'S MARK AND A HALF, IN HIS OWN BOOK SINCE HE WAS THIRTY-FOUR, offered to this yard and refused, and the figure is not in this yard's book and is not going to be, and the refusal is a refusal and not a request.**
10. **THE FORTY MARKS TWICE, neither reduced and neither paid, and the third column unfilled and unappointed, and the forty marks first after food untouched and unoffered, and the man of Ashtide's three marks unmoved and unasked about, and the bellwright's eight marks and a day of a boat unargued and his chest unopened.**
11. **A WORKING HARBOR POORER ON THE FOURTEENTH OF JANUARY THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF DECEMBER, AND THE CISTERN WALKED ON NONE OF SIX CHARGES, AND NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN THREE WEEKS HAS MADE ANYTHING BETTER, AND NO FIGURE IN THIS HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT.**

### 11. The shape of the batch, stated on the batch's own face

**THIS BATCH IS A WORKING MOVEMENT AND IT IS THE SECOND MOVEMENT OF VOLUME 05, AND IT HAS NO ACTION CHAPTER, NO FIGHT, NO UNDERWATER SCENE, NO DIVE, NO FINDING, NO BUOY IN THE WATER AND NO POWER STAGE. FOUR DAYS AT A SEAM WERE WORKED AND EVERY ONE OF THEM CAME UP THE HILL ON A MAN'S OWN ACCOUNT BECAUSE A MAN BROUGHT A PUMP UP THE HILL, AND THREE THINGS CAME OUT OF THE TWENTY DAYS: NINETEEN LINES, A CORNER GONE SOFT, AND A FINDING.** The alternation of pressure types is deliberate and is in the order a working question, a working day and an institution, a working day and a discovery, political and emotional, institutional and emotional, political and a cost, working and character conflict, political and a refusal, a working day and a cost, and a turn. **The batch's discovery is in Chapter 217 and it came out of another trade's mouth: that a thing on the water is not a building, and that a building is made once and a thing on the water is a bill, and that in thirty-one years no man on this coast had ever asked a trade what it costs to BE a thing rather than to make it. The batch's climax is Chapter 218, where a man with a firebox and a key is refused in a street and the refusal is read as an intention to keep. And the batch's turn is Chapter 220's third entry, in the first column, in the holder's own left hand.**

**THE BATCH'S ONE WORKING RULE, WHICH IS THE MOVEMENT'S AND IS NOT INVENTED IN IT: ordinary harbor work does not stop because a letter has come up a hill, and a day at a seam in this harbor is a day with somebody else's pump on it, and the whole of the difference between what this yard knows how to do and what it has is a length of hose and a second pair of hands, and neither of those is a figure.**
