**THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT ON EVERY PAGE AND A LATER PHASE MAY RECHECK IT IN ONE LINE: 7,890 + (8 × 480) − 4 − 489 = 11,237.** The eight working days are the twenty-fifth and the twenty-sixth of February past and the first, the fifth, the seventh, the tenth, the twelfth and the fourteenth of March instant, **all on hirers' own accounts, with nobody in the water, and the man of the second lay brought the pump and the man on every one of the eight, and NO TWO OF THE EIGHT WERE WORKED BY THE SAME TWO PEOPLE, WHICH IS ENTERED AS A FACT IN FOUR CHAPTERS AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S COST IN ONE CLAUSE.**

**THE WHOLE OF WHAT CAME INTO THIS YARD IN THE TWENTY DAYS IS THREE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, BEING EIGHT DAYS AT THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM. THE WHOLE OF WHAT WENT OUT IN THE TWENTY DAYS IS FOUR HUNDRED AND NINETY-THREE PENCE, BEING THREE MARKS, ONE SHILLING AND ONE PENNY, BEING FOURPENCE AT THE POST ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH AND THREE MARKS AND NINE PENCE TO THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY ON THE TWELFTH OF MARCH. THE WHOLE OF WHAT HAS GONE OUT OF THIS YARD SINCE THE SIXTH OF DECEMBER PAST IS FIVE HUNDRED AND TWENTY PENCE, BEING THREE MARKS, THREE SHILLINGS AND FOUR PENCE, IN SIX TRANSACTIONS AT FOUR COUNTERS, BEING A PENNY ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF DECEMBER PAST, A PENNY ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JANUARY INSTANT, A PENNY ON THE THIRTEENTH OF FEBRUARY INSTANT, TWO SHILLINGS TO A BONESETTER ON THE TWENTIETH OF FEBRUARY, FOURPENCE AT THE POST ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH, AND THREE MARKS AND NINE PENCE TO THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY ON THE TWELFTH OF MARCH. NO OFFICE IN THIS HARBOR PAID THIS YARD A MARK AND NONE IS GOING TO, AND THE FIGURES OF *TWO COUNTERS* AND *TWO SHILLINGS AND THREE PENCE* AND *FOUR TRANSACTIONS* ARE WITHDRAWN.**

**AND THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE WENT UP BY THREE THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-SEVEN PENCE ACROSS THE TWENTY DAYS, FROM SEVEN THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY TO TEN THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SEVEN PENCE ON THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH, AND THAT IS EIGHT WORKING DAYS AT FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHTY PENCE LESS FOUR HUNDRED AND NINETY-THREE PENCE GONE OUT.** **THE PHRASE *THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE* IS THE HOUSE'S OWN AND HAS MEANT THE BAG LESS ONE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS SINCE CHAPTER 201, AND EVERY CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH GIVES IT THAT WAY, AND A LATER CHAPTER MAY NOT RE-DERIVE IT AS A SUM OF UNPAID WAGES AND MAY NOT CALL IT A SUM.**

**THE WAGE COLUMN STANDS AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS FROM THE FIRST PAGE OF THIS BATCH TO THE LAST, THE FIFTH OF MARCH THE OLDEST THROUGHOUT, AND THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE ON EITHER OF ITS TWO TUESDAYS BECAUSE THE WAGE WAS NOT PAID ON EITHER. THE COUNT OF ENVELOPES ON THE BENCH IN THAT CHEST STANDS AT TWENTY THROUGHOUT, AND IT ADVANCES ONLY WITH THE COLUMN AND ONLY WITH A PAID WAGE. THE NUMBER OF WEEKS FALLEN DUE THIS YEAR WITH NO ENVELOPE STANDING AGAINST THEM IS EIGHTEEN AT THE OPEN, NINETEEN AFTER THE SECOND OF MARCH, AND TWENTY AFTER THE NINTH, AND ALL TWENTY ARE GIVEN IN THE SAME BREATH WHEREVER THE FIGURE APPEARS AND NOT ONE AFTER THE OTHER: the fifteenth of August, the fifth of September, the sixth of October, the third of November, the seventeenth of November, the first of December, the eighth, the fifteenth, the twenty-second and the twenty-ninth of December, the fifth, the twelfth, the nineteenth and the twenty-sixth of January, the second, the ninth, the sixteenth and the twenty-third of February instant, and the second and ninth of March instant.**

**THE REASON THE WAGE IS NOT PAID WAS ENTERED ONCE, IN THE FIRST COLUMN, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN LEFT HAND, ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-NINTH OF DECEMBER PAST, AND IT WAS NOT RE-ENTERED, NOT IMPROVED ON AND NOT SAID A SECOND WAY. CHAPTERS 244 AND 247 EACH SAY IN THEIR OWN WORDS THAT THE REASON IS THE REASON OF THE TWENTY-NINTH OF DECEMBER AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON, AND CHAPTER 250 SAYS IT IN A STANDING ENTRY AND DOES NOT RESTATE IT.**

**NO ITEM ON THIS HARBOR'S LIST OF WHAT A YARD OWES WAS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED IN THIS BATCH, AND THE WAGE IS ON THAT LIST. Thirty-one on the chandler's note, not re-written, its three counts of weeks unmoved at twenty-two, thirteen and eleven, AND IT WAS SAID OUT LOUD FOR THE FOURTH TIME IN SEVEN MONTHS ON THURSDAY THE FOURTH OF MARCH INSTANT AT ABOUT SEVEN IN THE MORNING, AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK, IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, BY THE SHIP'S HAND, STANDING WHERE SHE COULD BE SEEN AND NOT ON THE BOARDS, WITH THE THREE COUNTS GIVEN IN ONE BREATH AND NOT ONE AFTER THE OTHER, THE REFUSAL OF THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH STANDING UNREVERSED, NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL, AND THE YARD SAYING OUT LOUD IN THE SAME BREATH THAT IT WILL NOT SAY IT A FIFTH TIME.** It had not been said once in the thirteen weeks before it. Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks owing to a man of Ashtide for the eighth of August, unmoved, **and he is not named in that book in any of these ten chapters, nobody has been sent for him, nobody has asked him a question, no letter has gone to him, and nobody in this batch said a word about him.** Seven pence owing to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat owing to this harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, **and he was not asked anything in these twenty days, he is not in a room in any of them, no digit of anything he said on the second of July is printed, and the chest was not opened and was not brought down the hill.** Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots of the eighth of June standing, **the head of the third column keeping the boy's hand, the column not filled on any day of this batch, and nobody appointed to it.** Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, unpaid since the fifteenth of October, not one mark paid and not one shilling offered, **and she has told this yard not to ask her again this winter and this yard has not asked her once in these twenty days.**

### 4. Every document created, quoted or discovered in this batch, one at a time

1. **A CROWN FORM, A SINGLE SHEET FOLDED TWICE, DELIVERED IN A SEALED ENVELOPE WITH A NAME ON THE OUTSIDE OF IT ON THURSDAY THE FOURTH OF MARCH INSTANT.** At the head of it, in the office's own type, is **Halven Rook**, and the office he holds is written out under it, **and that name is in this yard's first column in full because a name on a piece of paper is a thing a man can check, and he is in no room and on no mole and has said no word.** The form requires a party holding a crew's charter in a port of that coast to produce that charter at the vessel of a patrol of that Crown lying in that port within one day of the day of its delivery; **the charter so produced is entered on the schedule of that patrol and is not returned, and a party producing it may enter in writing once any particular of it that the party wishes to be recorded.** It says it is not a writ, and is not a licence, and is not a finding, and does not touch any matter before any court, and that nothing in it is a suspension and nothing in it is a penalty, and **that a party which does not produce the thing on the day is not fined, because a court does not fine a poor man, and the matter simply goes on.** Beneath that, in the same hand as the name, a line that is not the office's type: **that the party may not be required to produce any book of its own in any column, and that nothing in this form requires a party to say who altered anything or at whose instance or with what intent, and that the party is not asked to say it and is not going to be asked to say it.** **A CROWN PATROL ENTERED THIS BATCH AS A BOAT LYING OFF THE NORTH SIDE AND A HAND CARRYING AN ENVELOPE UP A MOLE. NO OFFICER OF THE NAVY IS A FACE IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND NONE MAY BE, AND NO NAVY OFFICER IS NAMED ANYWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** The envelope went into the drawer in place of the charter and is one of the five pieces of paper in that drawer on the fourth of March, being the four that were in it and itself; **the six at the close of Chapter 250 are the four, this form and the page about that harbor, and the count and the method are at item 12 of this section and at § 17 item 7.** **THE RESERVED SENTENCE OF THE VOLUME IS NOT ON THIS FORM AND WAS CUT FROM IT AT THE VERIFICATION PASS, BECAUSE A FORM CARRYING IT WOULD HAVE SPENT THE VOLUME'S LAST LINE FOUR CHAPTERS EARLY.**
2. **THE ONE-SEASON PROVISIONAL WORKING CHARTER OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF NOVEMBER PAST, TAKEN.** It came out of the drawer at about two on the afternoon of Thursday the fourth of March instant and went down that mole in a hand, **and the hand is the whole of what this book has to say about who took it.** It ran to the last day of March. It was granted in the hearing room over the tide-gang store by a reeve of this harbor, is on that harbor's ground inside that harbor line, is bounded by the outer marks and by four hundred yards off them, has the freed shoal iron as its bond at a clerk's thirteen which has not been sold, and may be suspended by that office after an inspection for cause, of which that office has none and has not looked. **THE HARBOR AUTHORITY IS NOT THE OFFICE THAT CAN GIVE IT BACK AND NEVER WAS, AND ITS OWN CLERK SAID SO OUT LOUD ON FRIDAY THE FIFTH AND IT IS IN A BOOK.**
3. **A PAGE ABOUT MORROW QUAY, MADE IN MORROW QUAY, IN THE SHIP'S HAND, PUT IN THE DRAWER ON THOSE BENCHES ON SATURDAY THE SIXTH OF MARCH INSTANT AT ABOUT TWO IN THE AFTERNOON.** It says on its face, in the first line and in the last, that it is not a document and not a record and not evidence and not a return and not a copy of anything. It is on the mole, the second seam's own face, the ninth seam's mooring with an end of it entered for the first of September and found in service, the weir called the Sill with its stone under four feet of stone and a foot and four inches above the third of six joints, the point with the light and the two households' accounts of one night, the cistern on its rota, the fire party's hose, the mole-head light, one herring berth of two out, the north berth out, the tide gang four men short, the hard at Ashtide, and the four days in the middle of July in about sixty boats. At its head, in the ship's hand, is a line that is the whole of it and is not a heading: **that a page about a place is in that place's hand on that place's paper and is not to be carried out of that place; that any person the page is about may come and read it or not; that the person who keeps it may say yes or no at any time and cannot be made to say yes; that nobody may be asked for it and nobody may be told it exists; and that there is no office to ask and no form and no penalty on anybody for not producing it, and that that is not an accident and is the whole of the design.** **THE HAND THAT PUT IT IN IS THE SHIP'S HAND AND SHE IS THE PERSON WHO KEEPS IT, AND THE HOLDER OF THE WRIT HAS NOT BEEN ASKED AND IS NOT GOING TO BE, AND A PERSON WHO KEEPS A PAGE HAS TO BE SOMEBODY AND NOT AN OFFICE.**
4. **FOUR SHEETS IN FOUR ENVELOPES, ADDRESSED TO FOUR PLACES AND NOT ONE NAME, POSTED ON SATURDAY THE SIXTH OF MARCH INSTANT AT ABOUT HALF PAST FOUR.** One to a place two days down that coast, one to a place four days up that coast, one to a chain of reed islands and floating markets, and one to the next town down that coast. The receipt is for fourpence and does not say what is in them. **THIS YARD SENT NOBODY TO ANY OF THE FOUR PLACES. THE PRICE OF A GOING WAS NAMED BEFORE THE GOING, BEING FOUR DAYS THERE AND FOUR DAYS BACK, TWO MEN AND A PASSAGE AND ABOUT TWENTY-FOUR MARKS, AND THE PARTY HAS NOT GOT TWENTY-FOUR MARKS AND HAS NOT GOT THE FOUR DAYS AND A SHEET IN A POST IS NOT A MAN IN A ROOM AND IS NOT GOING TO BE IMPROVED ON BY ANYBODY.**
5. **AN AGREEMENT OF FIVE LINES AND NO NAME, IN FIVE HANDS, IN FIVE TOWNS, MADE AT ABOUT HALF PAST SEVEN ON MONDAY THE EIGHTH OF MARCH INSTANT IN A SHED ON THAT MOLE.** The sheet has nothing at the top of it, the lines are not numbered, and they are: that a page about a place is in that place's hand on that place's paper and is kept by a person and is not a copy of a record; that any person the page is about may read it, and nobody else may be told it exists, and the person who keeps it may say yes or no at any time to any one of them and cannot be made to say yes; that nobody may be asked for it, in a shed, in a market, in a room, or to a man with a seal, and that a party which does not produce it is not fined, because a court does not fine a poor man, and the matter simply goes on; that a person may be asked to take a page out of a drawer, in their own town, in their own words, and may say no, and that nobody may be asked to take it out twice; and that these five towns are parties and that there are five pages and one page to a drawer, and that nobody has to add a name to the thing for it to be a thing. **The five hands are the ship's hand, a man of about thirty-four who sells lime and chalk who wrote his in this harbor on the Wednesday before he went four days down that coast and is in the country and not on this coast, a man of about sixty of this town who keeps a day-book of his own that his father began, a woman of about thirty-one of this town who has kept a page of her own since she was nineteen and was not asked a question about it, and the copyist of fifty-eight, who came up that hill for nothing and was not paid and did not ask. THE HOLDER OF THE WRIT'S HAND IS NOT ON IT AND HIS NAME IS NOT ON IT AND HE IS UP THAT COAST ROAD AND IS NOT GOING TO BE ASKED TO SIGN IT WHEN HE COMES BACK.**
6. **THE REASON THE AGREEMENT HAS NO NAME, IN A PERSON'S MOUTH AND NOT IN A NARRATION.** A copyist of fifty-eight, of a counter in a room off that fish market, who has kept that counter for thirty-one years and has no office above it and is not of this party and is not on a ladder: **that she has put a name on about nine things in thirty-one years and every one of them had a name somebody had already given it; that a name is the last thing a thing gets and the first thing it can be asked for; and that she does not know a single thing in that country that is called anything by anybody that cannot be asked about by somebody with a form; and that a name is a thing an office can be asked for, and that there is no office to ask, and that that is the whole reason and there is not a second reason behind it; and that if it is named then in about four years some clerk in some city will write it on the back of a sheet, and then there will be a file, and then a question about whether it still stands, and then somebody will want to know who holds up its end.** And she said that she answered because she was asked the other question first, and that she would have told them to go if they had been asked the name first, and she wanted that in that yard's book and not in hers.
7. **THE PART ABOUT THE LIMIT, IN THE SAME PERSON'S MOUTH, BECAUSE THE LIMIT IS FOUR PEOPLE'S AND NOT THIS YARD'S.** Four people on a mole in the month of August wrote down in their own words that they will not say what a bell-archive is to a man with a seal, and signed it, and that is the only reason anything this yard has done in five volumes has a floor under it, and it is not this yard's. **A wall with no door in it is the only kind of wall four people of that coast can stand behind, because there is no office on that coast that can put a door in it. They gave it for nothing in August without knowing what it was worth, and that is the only thing in this business nobody in it had to be paid for.** And the price, in her own words and not improved on: that a page in a drawer in five towns is a page nobody can check; that a record a man can check is worth what the man who checks it is worth and a record nobody can check is worth what the person who keeps it is worth; that there is no figure for either and there never has been; that she has met about nine people in thirty-one years she would trust with a page and about four hundred she would not and the nine are not better than the four hundred; and that she is not going to tell that yard it is a contradiction and is not going to tell it it is a good trade.
8. **FOUR LINES FROM FOUR TOWNS, IN FOUR HANDS, NONE OF THEM THIS YARD'S, AND NONE OF THEM A THING THIS YARD ASKED FOR.** A page in a drawer in a place two days down that coast was read out in a kitchen on a Sunday to about nine people and put back in the drawer and is not going to be read again. A page in a drawer in a place four days up that coast has been read by the person who keeps it and by nobody else and put back in the drawer, and the keeper of it has told nobody what is on it. A page in a drawer in a chain of reed islands and floating markets has not been opened since it came, and the keeper of it wrote that down so that whoever reads it knows it was not opened and not that it was not looked at. A page in a drawer in the next town down that coast has been copied out once in the keeper's own hand and the copy hung in a room people come into, and the page is in the drawer. **ALL FOUR ARE RIGHT, NONE IS THE ANSWER THIS YARD WOULD HAVE GIVEN, NONE IS WRONG, AND THIS YARD CANNOT GO AND LOOK IN ANY OF THE FOUR DRAWERS AND HAS NOT TRIED TO.**
9. **A COPY OF THIS YARD'S PRINTED SHEET OF THIRTY-EIGHT LINES, POSTED TO A TOWN FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST, ADDRESSED TO NO PERSON AND TO THE TOWN, AND NAILED ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE MARKET WALL OF THAT TOWN ON SUNDAY THE FOURTEENTH OF MARCH INSTANT AT ABOUT HALF PAST FOUR, WITH FOUR NAILS AND NO OTHER PAPER OVER IT.** The wall in that town has never had a paper on it. **The thirty-eighth line at the foot of that sheet is the only line in it this yard did not write for itself, and it says that there is a copy of that sheet in about sixty boats on that coast, and that if a man has one and that one has changed he is to say so to the yard that printed it, and that the yard that printed it is at the head of that dock, and that any man may go in there and read the said line and see where the other ones are.** A woman of about thirty-one of that town, who is the fourth of the five hands and who keeps a page in a drawer in that town, opened it in her own kitchen, read that line, and put it up. **The reason she gave was on the thirty-eighth line and is in her own mouth, was given to a neighbour, was written down by the neighbour, and came in the ordinary post on the fifteenth. THIS YARD DID NOT WRITE TO THE MAN OF FIFTY-EIGHT WHO SELLS TIMBER IN THAT TOWN, DID NOT ASK HIM, AND IS NOT GOING TO.**
10. **A NAME AT THE HEAD OF THE THIRD COLUMN, BESIDE THE BOY'S HAND AND NOT OVER IT, IN THE SHIP'S HAND, ON MONDAY THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH INSTANT.** See § 6 and § 12.
11. **THE DELAY, WRITTEN DOWN WITH A DATE AGAINST IT, ONCE, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, ON MONDAY THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH INSTANT.** The figure is a hand's width of a second and has not moved. **NO OCCASION WAS ENTERED, NEITHER OF ITS TWO COUNTS WAS ADVANCED, AND NOTHING WAS MEASURED. THE REASON IT WAS WRITTEN DOWN IS ON THE PAGE AND IS THAT A FIGURE NO MAN CAN CHECK IS A FIGURE NO MAN WILL BELIEVE, AND THAT A FIGURE IN A BOOK WITH A DAY AGAINST IT IS A FIGURE A MAN CAN GO AND LOOK AT AND SEE THAT IT IS THE SAME FIGURE IT WAS IN THE MONTH OF OCTOBER, AND THAT THIS YARD IS NOT GOING TO BE THE FIRST TO SAY WHY.**
12. **NOTHING FROM A CITY.** No office sent anything up that hill in these twenty days and this yard wrote to no office, and did not go to the counter of the circuit office, and sent nothing to a city, and did not write to any of the nine places, and sent nobody to any of them. **THE DRAWER ON THOSE BENCHES IS THE DRAWER AND NOT A NEW ONE, AND WHAT IS IN IT IS TAKEN FROM FOUR CHAPTERS AND NOT FROM THIS PARAGRAPH, AND THIS PARAGRAPH PREVIOUSLY GOT IT WRONG IN TWO PLACES AND BOTH ARE REPAIRED HERE.** Chapter 233 of the ninth of February past says the form is answered and is in the drawer with the other three; Chapter 243 of the first of March instant has the holder counting himself at midnight as a man with a charter, a bare bench, and a drawer with four pieces of paper in it; Chapter 245 of the fourth says the charter came out of that drawer at about two in the afternoon and the sheet with the name on it went into it in its place, and that the four pieces of paper that were in that drawer are in it now; and Chapter 246 of the sixth says the page about that harbor went into that drawer at about two in the afternoon and that the four pieces of paper that were in it are in it now and were in it before she came down the hill. **THE DRAWER THEREFORE HELD THE CHARTER AND FOUR PIECES OF PAPER UNTIL THE FOURTH OF MARCH AND HOLDS FIVE PIECES OF PAPER AFTER IT, BEING THE COPY OF A RECORD OF THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF NOVEMBER, THE ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF THE TWENTY-NINTH OF NOVEMBER, THE ANSWERED HALF SHEET OF A COURT IN A CITY OF THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER, THE CROWN FORM OF THE FOURTH OF MARCH, AND THE PAGE ABOUT THAT HARBOR OF THE SIXTH — SIX AT THE CLOSE OF CHAPTER 250, THE TWO ADDITIONS BEING THE FORM AND THE PAGE.** **THE PRINTER'S LETTER OF THE TWENTIETH OF DECEMBER, WITH ONE QUESTION IN IT THAT THIS YARD HAS THE ANSWER TO AND IS NOT GOING TO SEND, IS NOT ON A BENCH. CHAPTER 209 PUT IT IN THE SAME DRAWER AS THE FORM AND NOT IN THE SAME PLACE, IN THE SHIP'S OWN MOUTH AND AGAIN IN THAT CHAPTER'S FIRST COLUMN, AND IT HAS NOT BEEN MOVED SINCE; THE SENTENCE IN THIS PARAGRAPH THAT PUT IT ON A BENCH IS WITHDRAWN AS FALSE AND IS NAMED AS WITHDRAWN.** **AND THE SHEET AND A HALF WITH NO SIGNATURE AND NO DATE ON IT IS IN PIECES AND IS NOT IN THAT DRAWER AND CANNOT BE PUT BACK: IT CAME APART IN THE SHIP'S HAND ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF JANUARY PAST, AND CHAPTER 229'S COUNT OF FIVE PIECES OF PAPER IS A COUNT OF WHAT THAT YARD HAD ON THE FIRST OF FEBRUARY PAST AND NOT A COUNT OF THE DRAWER AT ANY LATER DATE, AND THE TWO FIGURES ARE NOT THE SAME FIGURE AND MUST NOT BE WELDED TO EACH OTHER.**
13. **NOTHING QUOTED IN FULL THAT IS NOT A FORM.** The copy record, the acknowledgment and the four records nine communities keep are not in this batch. **The name at the head of the fourth of the four is on no page of this batch, in no mouth in it and on no wall in it, and is called the name at the head of the fourth of the four wherever it is needed at all, and Chapter 250 enters that it is written once in the whole of the volume and was written once in a shed in the month of January.**

### 5. The chain of custody, as it was made, on the days it was made, and it is NEW

**A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND IT IS THE ONLY NEW ONE IN THIS SERIES SINCE THE WRIT. IT IS A PRACTICE. IT IS NOT A REGISTRY AND NOT A COURT AND NOT A HARBOR AUTHORITY. IT WAS MADE ON SATURDAY THE SIXTH OF MARCH INSTANT, AND NO ENTRY ABOUT IT APPEARS IN THIS YARD'S BOOK BEFORE THAT DAY AND NONE APPEARS AFTER IT THAT DATES IT EARLIER, AND NO LOCK IN `outline/volume-05.md` AGES IT AND NO LOCK MAY.**

**THE FIVE PAGES AND THE FIVE TOWNS AND THE FIVE HANDS, AS THEY STAND AT THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH.** Five towns are keeping five pages, one page to a drawer, and **no two of the five pages is the same page.** The five towns are **this harbor, a place two days down this coast, a place four days up this coast, a chain of reed islands and floating markets, and the next town down this coast.** The five hands are the ship's hand in this harbor, a man of about thirty-four who sells lime and chalk two days down, a woman of about thirty-one four days up, a person in the floating markets, and a person in the next town down. **A LATER PHASE MAY NOT RE-DERIVE THESE FIVE, MAY NOT ADD A SIXTH, MAY NOT CALL ANY OF THEM A REGISTRY, AND MAY NOT SAY THAT THE NINE COMMUNITIES AND THESE FIVE ARE ONE THING; THEY ARE NOT, AND THE FOUR COMMUNITIES THAT READ THIS YARD'S COPY ARE NOT THE SAME LIST AS THE FIVE HOLDERS AND THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE TWO LISTS IS ENTERED AT CHAPTER 247 AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON.**

**WHOSE HAND PUT THE PAGE IN.** In this harbor, the ship's hand, on Saturday the sixth of March instant at about two in the afternoon, and she is the person who keeps it. In each of the four other towns, one hand in that town, and this yard does not know whose and is not going to ask and has not asked. **THE CHAPTER THAT SHOWS ONE OF THE FIVE DRAWERS HAS TO SAY WHOSE HAND PUT THE PAGE IN AND WHAT THE OTHER FOUR CAN DO ABOUT IT. CHAPTERS 246, 247 AND 249 EACH DO IT AND EACH SAYS THE SAME TWO SENTENCES, WHICH ARE THE WHOLE OF IT.**

**WHAT THE OTHER FOUR CAN DO ABOUT IT, WHOLE AND IN THOSE WORDS, AS ENTERED ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH INSTANT: they can come to that shed on that mole and ask. And that is all of it. There is no counter they can go to, no form, and nobody in any city they can write to, because there is no office that has heard of this and that yard has not told one. And if a man in a room four hundred miles away asks them whether the page is in the drawer, they can say no, and they can say no for forty years, and nobody can make them say anything else.**

**AND WHAT NOBODY CAN DO, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE THING: a person may be asked to take a page out of a drawer, in their own town, in their own words, and may say no, and nobody may be asked to take it out twice; and the person who keeps it may say yes or no to any one of the people the page is about at any time and cannot be made to say yes; and a party which does not produce a page on a day is not fined, because a court does not fine a poor man, and the matter simply goes on. THE WARD WITH NO DOOR IN IT IS THE FOUR LINES FOUR PEOPLE OF THAT COAST WROTE AND SIGNED IN THE MONTH OF AUGUST, AND THAT IS THE REASON IT WORKS AT ALL, AND THE REASON IS THEIRS AND NOT THIS YARD'S.**

**AND THE PRICE, PAID IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT IN A SPEECH, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE VOLUME'S ARGUMENT AGAINST ITS OWN SOLUTION: a page in a drawer in five towns is a page no man in that harbor can look at, and that yard has spent five volumes insisting that a page a man cannot check is worth less than a page a man can look at, and that yard knows it, and has entered it, and is not going to get out of it with a better sentence, and in about four years it will not know whether three of the four pages are in three drawers or on three fires.**

**AND THE PARTIES. Ten places are parties to the agreement about who may read a page: the four communities this yard wrote to, and this harbor, and the five other places on that coast that keep records of their own and that this yard has not been to. **THE YARD'S OWN LIST OF NINE PLACES CAN PUT A NAME TO FIVE OF THEM AND CANNOT PUT A NAME TO FOUR, AND CHAPTER 247 ENTERS THAT A PLACE IT CANNOT NAME CANNOT BE A PARTY TO ANYTHING AND IS NOT GOING TO BE ASKED TO BE, AND THAT IS ENTERED AS A LIMIT OF THE YARD'S OWN BOOK AND NOT AS A DEFECT.** No institution, no new body, no compact, no name, and no new antagonist. **THE THING IS NOT CALLED ANYTHING AND THE REASON IT IS NOT CALLED ANYTHING IS A COUNTER IN A ROOM OFF THAT FISH MARKET.**

### 6. The dated positions at the end of Chapter 250

- **The writ of the first of May past ended at ten minutes past midnight on Monday the first of March instant and nothing took its place.** The holder is on no page of this book for the writ after that hour. No court sat, no clerk came up that hill, nobody was charged, nobody was fined, nobody was refused anything, nobody was examined, and nobody was told that the holder has not got it. **THE INSTRUMENT IS GONE AND NOBODY IS GONE.**
- **The one-season provisional working charter of the twenty-eighth of November past went out of that drawer at about two on the afternoon of Thursday the fourth of March instant and down that mole in a hand, and is on a schedule four hundred miles away, and the harbor authority is not the office that can give it back and never was.** It had sixteen days left to run. The freed shoal iron is still on the stack at a clerk's thirteen and has not been sold, and with the charter gone the bond is a figure in a book and nothing has a hold on it.
- **The slate wall behind the reeve's bench came down three times in this batch, all Mondays, all bare, all with the clerk keeping his own page and not mentioning it, and no sitting was held in that room on any of them: Monday the first of March being the forty-third Monday since the first of May, Monday the eighth the forty-fourth, and Monday the fifteenth the forty-fifth. THE COUNTER DID NOT RESTART.**
- **The cistern behind the engine house was charged at no figure by four men this yard does not know on six rota days in twenty days — the twenty-fifth of February past and the first, fourth, eighth, eleventh and fifteenth days of March instant — and this party walked none of them. THE WALK IS NIL AND IT STAYS NIL, AND THAT IS THE TWENTY-NINTH OF THE CHARGES THIS PARTY HAS ENTERED WALKED ON NONE OF SINCE THE THIRD DAY OF AUGUST PAST.**
- **The far bench is entered in ALL TEN OF THE CHAPTERS OF THIS BATCH AND IT COVERS ALL TWENTY DAYS. IT WAS OCCUPIED ON SIX OF THEM, AND THE SIX ARE TAKEN FROM THE STANDING ENTRY AT THE HEAD OF EACH CHAPTER AND FROM THE CLOSING FIRST-COLUMN RESTATEMENT IN THE SAME CHAPTER, WHICH AGREE IN EVERY CASE: the twenty-sixth of February, being the said Friday of Chapter 242, from about ten until about one; the fourth of March, the said Thursday of 245, from about ten until about four; the sixth of March, the said Saturday of 246, from about ten until about two; the eighth of March, the said Monday of 247, from about ten until about four; the twelfth of March, the said Friday of 249, from about ten until about one; and the fourteenth of March, the said Sunday of 250, from about ten until about four. IT WAS NOT OCCUPIED AT ANY HOUR ON THE OTHER FOURTEEN: the twenty-fourth, twenty-fifth, twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth of February, and the first, second, third, fifth, seventh, ninth, tenth, eleventh, thirteenth and fifteenth of March, and each of those fourteen is stated as not occupied in the chapter that carries it, at the head of the chapter and again in its closing first-column restatement. THE FIGURE OF NINE THAT THIS BULLET PREVIOUSLY CARRIED, AND THE WHOLE OF ITS LIST, ARE WITHDRAWN AND ARE NAMED AS WITHDRAWN HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY REPLACED: that list gave the twenty-seventh of February, the first, the seventh, the eighth, the twelfth and the fourteenth of March and then the eleventh, the thirteenth and the fifteenth, and it put the thirteenth of March in both halves of it, and **Chapters 242, 243, 248, 249 and 250 each state the contrary of what that list said of their own day, and the chapters govern.** The *quarter past two in the afternoon when the question was asked in that market*, which that list attached to the eleventh, IS ALSO WITHDRAWN TWICE OVER: the eleventh was not occupied at any hour, and the question was asked on that Thursday at about a quarter past eleven IN THE MORNING, as `chapters/volume-05/chapter-0248.md` gives it at its nineteenth and sixty-fifth lines and as § 2 of this section already states, and the boards came down at about two.** Not asked for anything on any day, asking nothing on any day, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, **and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any day of the twenty, and on fourteen of them he was up that coast road and not in that harbor, and both of those are entered and neither of them is a reason.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for forty-four nights as at the night of Monday the fifteenth of March, counting from the Sunday of the thirty-first of January instant on which a sheet and a half came apart in the ship's hand on that mole.** It is the only bare thing in that shed and the shape of that bench is the shape of a sheet and a half that came up that hill on foot on the ninth of December past and cannot be put back and cannot be bought. **IT WILL BE BARE FOR EVERY NIGHT AFTER THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH UNTIL SOMEBODY PUTS SOMETHING ON IT, AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED WAS ASKED AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED ASKED.**
- **A page went up on a market wall on Sunday the fourteenth of March instant in a town four days up that coast, on a wall in that town that has never had a paper on it.** Nothing went up on any wall in that harbor in these twenty days and nothing came off, and the two naval notices are not on that wall and were not taken down by that party, and the clerk kept his own page and has not mentioned it.
- **A mark is on the water at the face of the second seam, hired for a fortnight on Friday the twelfth of March instant at two marks, set from a boat of about forty tons a hand short, looked at on Sunday the fourteenth at a quarter past two, fouled on the weather side with about four inches of green, making a small noise in a flat calm that a man on a mole could not have heard, and nobody struck it and nobody is going to be told about it in this book. THE SEASON IS NINE MARKS AND IS NOT PAID AND IS NOT GOING TO BE PAID.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about two hundred and seventy-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June past and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the twenty days.** The notice of the thirty-first of October has its four clauses and has not been lifted, narrowed, re-served or altered, and no person, no boat and no lead of that yard went inside its first clause on any of the twenty. The plate at the fifth seam is in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, **THE NOTE AGAINST IT STANDS OPEN**, and no better letter was written about it in these twenty days and the only mechanism anybody has named for reaching it is a change of politics in an office.
- **The custody room was not asked for, nothing came out of it, no digit of any of the three numbers is in this yard's book, and the question that no paper in this harbor or in that office's copying room answers was not put to anybody. The lead plug is not asked about, not printed, not opened and not brought down the hill. The glass storm is not referred to. The run under this town is not referred to. The compartment is not named in this batch except in one standing entry of Chapter 250 which says that it is not named, and no step of its finding is restated. The custody-log re-entry of the twentieth of December gave no reason and is not referred to. The delayed note stands at eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them, nothing was entered in these twenty days, nothing was measured, the delay is a hand's width of a second and has not moved, nobody in this harbor has ever said why, and on the fifteenth of March the figure was written down with a date against it in the second column, which is not a measurement and is not an occasion.**
- **There are four returns up this coast and there is no fifth, and no day of this batch produced a finding of worked glass and no return of any kind was made. The case of five bells is at about five and a half fathoms inside the four hundred yards off the outer marks, on nobody's schedule, owned by four people alive in that town with no boat, no wages and about nine marks between them, and their limit is quoted in that yard's own first column in Chapter 249 and stands, and the holder did not ask them to take it off once in the twenty days.** The boy is off the stone and the third column is unfilled and unappointed and the boy's hand is at the head of it. The coast road is in type in a city beside a pilot's two and a half and neither is withdrawn and this volume did not decide which of them is right.
- **The harbor is poorer at the close of this batch than at its open.** One herring berth of two is out, the north berth is out, the mole-head light is not on because a light costs oil, the fire party's hose is dead until the spring, the tide gang is four men short, the hard at Ashtide is unanswered, the cistern is charged at no figure on six rota days and walked on none, the compressor's gland is unpaid and useless and the thing after the gland is the hose and this harbor has no hose, nineteen winters are in a list being made up in a city, a boat of about forty tons is a hand short, a reeve's office owes its own clerk two days, a harbor authority's office is not the office that can give back a charter, and a woman of twenty-seven has four stitches in her right hand and cannot hold a line. **NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN THESE TWENTY DAYS HAS MADE ANYTHING BETTER AND NO FIGURE IN THIS HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT. AND A YARD THAT HAS LEARNED ONE NEW TRADE IN TWENTY DAYS CANNOT YET PAY A MAN TO DO IT WITH.**

### 7. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr, thirty-two, the holder of the writ until ten minutes past midnight on the first of March and after that the holder of nothing this harbor can give him.** He went to a counter and was told what he would be on the first of March and put the clerk's words in the first column instead of his own sentence. He got on a cart at ten o'clock on the second of March and went up that coast road and was not in that harbor for the rest of the batch. He chose the living archive and let the lead go, and the lead does not come back, and nobody in that shed improved on that. He did not go over to the far bench on any of the twenty days, and on fourteen of them he was not in the town. **THE FIGURE THIS BULLET PREVIOUSLY GAVE, *NINE*, IS WITHDRAWN AND IS NAMED AS WITHDRAWN: CHAPTERS 244 TO 250 EACH ENTER HIM AS A MAN UP THAT COAST ROAD FOR BOTH OF THEIR TWO DAYS, AND THAT IS THE SECOND, THIRD, FOURTH, FIFTH, SIXTH, SEVENTH, EIGHTH, NINTH, TENTH, ELEVENTH, TWELFTH, THIRTEENTH, FOURTEENTH AND FIFTEENTH OF MARCH — FOURTEEN CONSECUTIVE DAYS, NOT NINE.** **He is on no page of Chapters 245 to 250 as a person and is in the first column of every one of them as a man up a coast road. THE ONE NAMING OF THE CONDITION IS NOT IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE.**
- **Nessa Pike, twenty-seven, a party of one and a half until the first of March, a party of two on paper after it, and in practice a party of one for fourteen days. **THE FIGURE THIS BULLET PREVIOUSLY GAVE, *NINE*, IS WITHDRAWN AND IS NAMED AS WITHDRAWN, ON THE SAME GROUND AS THE ONE ABOVE.**** She has four stitches in her right hand and wrote every day's book in this batch in her left hand, at about twice the time it takes her. She made a page about her own town and put it in a drawer and said out loud on a mole's steps that if a person who keeps a page has to be somebody then it is her. She asked a copyist the question about a name and got the answer and wrote the reason in the second column. She read four lines from four towns and said all four were right and that the yard was not going to do anything about them. She took a trade alone and paid two men out of the bag to do a day's work two of them would do between them. She said the shape of sentence once, in Chapter 249, about a mark on the water, and **no character remarked on how often it has been said and no fisher claimed to have invented it.** She wrote a name at the head of the third column beside the boy's hand and not over it on the fifteenth of March. **She has not been thanked and is not going to ask, and he has not thanked her and did not and could not, because he was up a coast road.**
- **Ors Kest, forty-four, a reeve with a spent ledger, in no room in this batch and asked for nothing.** His office is named in Chapter 245 only as the office that granted the charter, and it is said there, out of a clerk's mouth and not the reeve's, that his office is not the office that can give that charter back and never was and could not have given it back on the fourth of March if the man it was granted to had been standing at that counter with both hands on it. **HE IS STILL NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY AND THE VOLUME'S CLOSING POSITION SAYS SO IN THOSE WORDS IN CHAPTER 250, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, AND NO CHAPTER IMPROVES ON IT. A CHAPTER THAT SPENDS ANOTHER THING OF HIS MUST PAY FOR IT ON THE PAGE AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH SPENT ONE.**
- **Pernel Saye, fifty-eight, a copyist with a counter in a room off the fish market, in one scene on Monday the eighth of March at about a quarter to nine.** She was asked the name first or the other question first — **the other question** — and answered, and said that she would have told them to go if they had asked the name first. She gave the reason an agreement has no name, and the part about the limit, and the price, and she said that she was not going to be asked about the page in her own back room and was not going to ask about that party's four envelopes. She wrote the fifth of the five lines at about half past seven and came up that hill for nothing and was not paid and did not ask. **SHE IS NOT A VILLAIN, SHE IS NOT ON A LADDER, SHE HAS NO OFFICE ABOVE THAT COUNTER, SHE WAS NOT TOLD WHAT A COLUMN IS, AND THE MENTEE IS IN NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT USED AS A PROXY FOR HER.**
- **A man of about forty-five who sells lime and chalk, ten days up this coast and back on a cart, once, in Chapter 242.** He has a book of ground about a stretch of water about nine miles along that coast from his own door, in water no lead and no boat of this harbor has been in, kept by four people alive of whom two are women and one is seventy-one. He said a page about a place is the place's and does not come out of the place it is about, and that if it leaves it stops being the place's and starts being evidence, and that he has watched a man on that coast lose a thing exactly that way. **He was not asked one question about the book, was not asked to leave it, and was not told what a column is, and he did not ask. He is not a friend of this party and did not say he was and is not on a list.**
- **A man of about thirty-four who sells lime and chalk, who carried a sheet up that hill on nothing in January, in one scene in Chapter 242 and one in Chapter 244.** He brought a lead about the holder's own brother and said he had asked the man nothing and was not going to. He went four days down that coast on the Friday in his own cart on his own account and did not wait and was not asked to wait. **THE LEAD DOES NOT COME BACK. He wrote the second of the five lines in this harbor on the Wednesday before he went and is in the country and not on this coast and cannot be in that room.** He is owed nothing by this yard and is owed something by nobody he spoke to. He is not a villain and not on a ladder and was not cited as a witness.
- **A man of about sixty of the first lay, forty-one years on that water, who asked the volume's question in a market on the second of December past, in one scene in Chapter 248.** He asked it a second time, in about forty people, with the holder of the writ up a coast road, and said out loud that he wanted a fact or nothing. **He was given three facts and a reason and was told to his face that none of it is an answer, and he said that that is three numbers and a refusal, and she said that she would rather say that in about forty people than say a thing she has not got.** The question is not answered and is not going to be.
- **A herring skipper of fifty-one of that town, in one scene in Chapter 250, and it is nine words and a paragraph and it is the last thing anybody says in this volume.** He has nineteen winters disputed and unpaid in a list being made up in a city and has not been thanked for any of it and was not thanked in this chapter either. **The yard did not go to the hard at Ashtide on the fourth of March and nobody in this batch said the words Ashtide in a room, and that is entered and is not going to be improved on.** He did not say it twice.
- **A woman of about thirty-one of a town four days up that coast, who keeps a page in a drawer in that town, in one scene, described from another town, in Chapter 250.** She is the fourth of the five hands. She opened a copy of the printed sheet in her own kitchen, read the thirty-eighth line, and nailed it on the market wall of her town on a wall that has never had a paper on it. **She was not asked a question about her page and was not written to by this yard and this yard did not write to the man of fifty-eight who sells timber in that town and did not ask him and is not going to.**
- **A man of about thirty-one of that town, who is not named and is not in a room, whose copy is hung in a room people come into.** **THE YARD HAS NOT WRITTEN TO THAT TOWN AND WILL NOT, BECAUSE A PAGE THAT A TOWN PUTS ON A WALL BECAUSE A YARD TOLD IT TO IS A PAGE THE YARD IS HOLDING IN A DRAWER IN THAT TOWN. THAT IS ENTERED IN CHAPTER 249 AS A DECISION AND NOT AS A FAULT.**
- **THE FOUR WHO MAY NOT APPEAR IN A ROOM, AND DID NOT: MARA VENN, BEVIN ROOK, ALDEN MARR AS A PERSON RATHER THAN A BENCH, AND THE MAN IN A COAT.** A case-insensitive search of the ten chapters for *Mara*, *Venn*, *Bevin*, *Alden*, *Sell*, *Holt*, *Serr*, *Orison* and *Gannet* returns nothing. *Rook* returns one, in Chapter 245, on a form, in a first column, and he is in no room. **MARA VENN IS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING, IS NOT IN A ROOM, IS NOT CITED, QUOTED, PRODUCED OR ASKED AGAIN, AND NO LETTER OF HERS CAME UP THAT HILL IN THESE TWENTY DAYS; HER FORTY MARKS STAND FIRST AFTER FOOD AND HER SIX MARKS AND TWO DAYS STANDS AS A PRICE AND NOT A DEBT. BEVIN ROOK IS NOT A PERSON IN ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS, THE THREE NOTS STAND, FORTY MARKS STANDS WHOLE, THE HEAD OF THE THIRD COLUMN KEEPS HIS HAND, THE COLUMN WAS NOT FILLED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH, NOBODY WAS APPOINTED TO IT, AND NO BOY WAS HIRED TO READ A POSITION BACK. ALDEN MARR IS A BENCH AND NOT A MAN AND WAS OCCUPIED ON SIX OF THE TWENTY DAYS — THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF FEBRUARY AND THE FOURTH, SIXTH, EIGHTH, TWELFTH AND FOURTEENTH OF MARCH, THE LIST BEING TAKEN FROM THE CHAPTERS AT § 6 — AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING ON ANY OF THE TWENTY. **THE FIGURE THIS BULLET PREVIOUSLY GAVE, *NINE*, IS WITHDRAWN AND IS NAMED AS WITHDRAWN.** THE MAN IN A COAT CAME UP THAT HILL ONCE, ON THE NINTH OF DECEMBER PAST, WENT DOWN IT, AND DID NOT COME UP AGAIN.** **The condition is named nowhere in this batch and was not available to be. No new antagonist, no new institution, no new final enemy, no new named office, and NO NEW CHARACTER WITH A TITLE.**

### 8. The ten cards, delivered, and the two devices it spent and the one it did not

1. **241 — what the holder of the writ is on the first of March. PAID.** Wednesday the twenty-fourth, Thursday the twenty-fifth of February. **The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the first of six.** No work on the Wednesday. **THE CHAPTER'S WORK IS THE FINDING, AND THE FINDING IS A FACT AND NOT A CLIFFHANGER: the writ is a municipal instrument, it is inside the harbor line, it is bounded by the outer marks, it carries four names and no fifth, it is not the Second Bell license, it does not lead to one, it renews nothing, only the harbor authority may issue it, and that authority has said in its own instrument that it is not the office that can renew it, so on the first of March that instrument stops existing and nothing is renewed and nobody is charged with anything. THE CHARTER IS NAMED AND IT IS A DIFFERENT THING AND A CLERK'S MOUTH KEEPS THE TWO APART ON THE PAGE.** A working day on the Thursday. The read-back twice.
2. **242 — the thing that comes up the coast. PAID.** Friday the twenty-sixth, Saturday the twenty-seventh. No rota day. **A BOOK OF GROUND COMES UP THE COAST IN A CART AND DOES NOT COME DOWN IT, AND A LEAD ABOUT THE HOLDER'S OWN BROTHER COMES UP THE HILL IN THE RAIN, AND THE TWO ARRIVE INSIDE TWO DAYS AND THE CHAPTER DOES NOT RESOLVE EITHER.** No office's paper brings either of them. The lead is entered in the first column with the reason against the line and the price named before the day and not after it. The read-out did not run.
3. **243 — midnight on the first of March. PAID.** Sunday the twenty-eighth of February, Monday the first of March. **The forty-third wipe, the wall down bare. The cistern is charged on the Monday and walked on none, being the second of six. THE WRIT RUNS TO MIDNIGHT ON THIS DAY AND AT TEN MINUTES PAST MIDNIGHT IT IS OVER, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS IT IS OVER, AND NOBODY IS FINED AND NOBODY IS CHARGED WITH ANYTHING AND NO COURT SITS AND NO CLERK COMES UP THAT HILL. THE THING THAT HAPPENS IS NOT A DISASTER AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IT IS NOT.** A working day on the Monday. The read-back.
4. **244 — the choice, and it is the volume's climax. PAID.** Tuesday the second, Wednesday the third of March. **THE WAGE DOES NOT GO IN AND THE NUMBER OF WEEKS FALLEN DUE IS NINETEEN, all nineteen in the same breath, and the reason is the reason of the twenty-ninth of December and is not improved on. THE COST IS ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN BEFORE THE DAY AND NOT AFTER IT, BEING NAMED ON THE MONDAY NIGHT AT ABOUT ELEVEN.** The third of the three costs of a thing on the water — that it takes a crew, and a crew is people, and a party of two has no crew in it — is named and paid on the page here. The read-back.

THE PRICE IS PAID IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT IN A SPEECH, AND A PERSON WHO IS NOT OF THIS PARTY SAYS THE PART ABOUT THE LIMIT, BECAUSE THE LIMIT IS THEIRS.**

PAID.** Wednesday the tenth, Thursday the eleventh of March. **The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the fifth of six. THE YARD'S ANSWER THE SECOND TIME IS THREE FIGURES AND A REASON AGAINST THE LINE AND NO NAME IN IT, GIVEN IN THAT ORDER ON PURPOSE, AND THE YARD SAYS OUT LOAD BEFORE IT GIVES THEM THAT NONE OF THEM IS AN ANSWER. AND THE CROWN CANNOT MAKE THE YARD SAY IT ALTERED A MANIFEST AND CANNOT MAKE ANY OF THE FOUR COMMUNITIES HAND OVER A RECORD, AND THE YARD CANNOT MAKE ANY COMMUNITY TRUST IT AND DOES NOT TRY, AND BOTH OF THOSE ARE SAID IN A STREET AND NEITHER IS A VICTORY.** No institution speaks and no office answers.

## Volume 05 close — the audit's account, and the twenty-one author-level rulings that bind every later volume

**`reviews/volume-05/volume-05-close.md` is the authority for everything in this section. THE CHAPTERS ARE THE AUTHORITY ON WHAT HAPPENED; THE PLANNING FILES ARE THE AUTHORITY ON WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN; AND EVERY FIGURE BELOW WAS RE-DERIVED BY SEARCH AGAINST THE CHAPTERS AND NOT TAKEN OUT OF A STATE FILE.**

### 1. What the close is, and what it did not do

**VOLUME 05 IS CLOSED. CHAPTERS 201 TO 250 ARE AUDITED AGAINST `outline/volume-05.md` AND ALL THIRTY-FIVE OF ITS LOCKS, AGAINST `reviews/volume-04/volume-04-close.md`, AND AGAINST THE SIX BIBLE FILES. THE CLOSE ADDED NO CHAPTER, ADDED NO PASSAGE THAT A CHAPTER WAS SUPPOSED TO CARRY, DID NOT ROUND UP THE VOLUME'S FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE — WHICH IS PAID IN ALL FIVE OF ITS ELEMENTS IN CHAPTER 250 — QUEUED NO WRITING PHASE, WROTE NO MARKER, AND DID NOT EDIT `state/phase-ledger.json`.** One mechanical repair was made, in one chapter, in four instances, and it is a date. § 2.

### 2. The one repair, and the word counts

**AT `chapters/volume-05/chapter-0231.md` LINES 21, 87 AND 103, THE LAST CARRYING IT TWICE, THE DAY A LINE OF ONE OF THE FOUR RECORDS WAS SAID OUT LOUD IN THAT SHED AND WENT OUT OF THE DOOR OF THAT SHED INTO A STREET IS *THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF JANUARY* AND NOT *THE TWENTY-SIXTH*. ONE WORD IN EACH OF FOUR PLACES, LOCK L1, AND THE CHAPTER'S WORDCOUNT IS UNCHANGED AT 4,252.**

**THE DATE IS WRONG AND THE WEEKDAY IS RIGHT, ON FOUR INDEPENDENT GROUNDS: (a) CHAPTER 226 STAGES THE READING ON THE MONDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH — *the four of them were on that bench from about two until about four on the said Monday afternoon* and *at about ten past four on the Monday they stopped*. (b) CHAPTER 226'S OWN DAY LINE READS *Monday the twenty-fifth and Tuesday the twenty-sixth of January*, AND THE TWENTY-SIXTH IS CONFIRMED A TUESDAY BY TWENTY-NINE CHAPTERS' WORTH OF THE INHERITED WAGE LIST, WHICH MAKES IT A WAGE TUESDAY ON WHICH THE WAGE WAS NOT PAID. (c) THE SAME SECOND-COLUMN SENTENCE SAYS THE LINE *went out of the door of that shed into a street inside an hour*, WHICH IS ONLY TRUE ON THE MONDAY. (d) THE FIRST COLUMN OF THE SAME CHAPTER HAS THE HOLDER REFUSING TO SAY *what two people said in a shed to a man of the third lay on a Monday afternoon*.** The fifth mention of the twenty-sixth on that chapter, in the inherited wage list at line 107, is correct and was not touched. **After this repair, all 192 weekday-and-date pairs on the fifty pages are correct, and the two that disagree with the real 2026 almanac are the two inherited wage weeks of August and September, which agree with the chapters that staged them and which lock L1a item 2 expressly permits.**

**THE WORD COUNTS, MEASURED FILE BY FILE WITH `wc -w` INCLUDING HEADINGS: Batch 0001 40,408 · Batch 0002 35,356 · Batch 0003 44,543 · Batch 0004 46,740 · Batch 0005 41,196, WHICH SUM TO 208,243 WORDS ACROSS THE FIFTY CHAPTERS. THE FIGURES 41,194 AND 208,241 ARE WITHDRAWN AND ARE THE PRE-REPAIRER-PASS MEASUREMENTS, AND THE DERIVED FIGURE *5,546 WORDS UNDER THE BATCH BEFORE IT* IS 5,544 AND IS WITHDRAWN TOO. FIFTEEN OF THE FIFTY FILES CARRY NO TRAILING FINAL NEWLINE AND ACCOUNT FOR THE SIXTEEN WORDS BY WHICH A SINGLE CONCATENATION OF THE FIFTY FILES FALLS SHORT OF THE PER-FILE SUM; THOSE FIFTEEN ARE LEFT AS THEY ARE, BECAUSE A MISSING FINAL NEWLINE IS NOT A PROSE FAULT AND NO REPAIR IN THIS AUDIT TOUCHES ONE.**

### 3. The money, re-derived and closed twice

**THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 05 CLOSES IN ONE LINE: 717 + (23 × 480) − 520 = 11,237.** The volume opens on a bag of four marks and six shillings and five pence, being seven hundred and seventeen pence, and closes on seventy marks, three shillings and one penny, being eleven thousand two hundred and thirty-seven. **The whole of what came into that yard in a hundred days is twenty-three days at the face of the second seam at four hundred and eighty pence, on hirers' own accounts, with nobody in the water, and no two of the twenty-three were worked by the same two people. The whole of what went out is five hundred and twenty pence in six transactions at four counters, being a penny on the eighteenth of December, a penny on the twenty-eighth of January, a penny on the thirteenth of February, two shillings to a bonesetter on the twentieth of February, fourpence at the post on the sixth of March, and three marks and nine pence to the man of the second lay on the twelfth of March.** **THE LAST TWENTY DAYS CLOSE IN THEIR OWN LINE: 7,890 + (8 × 480) − 4 − 489 = 11,237.** **Every one of the twenty-eight readings of the bag in the fifty chapters is the correct rendering of the marks, shillings and pence given beside it, and not one is of the class this volume's own repair passes found and fixed six times in fifty chapters, being a shillings component wrong while the pence figure in the same sentence was right.** RULED.

### 4. The twenty-one rulings, each dated, and each in the state files

1. **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN VOLUME 05 AND MAY NOT BE NAMED IN IT.** The name returns **zero** occurrences across the fifty chapters. The Volume 04 audit's ruling is obeyed and is not re-opened. The body is charged and a day lost to it is a day and carries no figure because there is no figure for a day. **The four nameless lines above the named line of the twentieth of July past are still four, are still nameless, are not struck out, and are in about sixty boats on that coast, and a line does not come out of a column because it has been printed.**
2. **THERE WERE FOUR RETURNS AND NO FIFTH, AND NO FINDING OF WORKED GLASS WAS MADE AND NOTHING WAS RAISED ON ANY OF THE HUNDRED DAYS.** The four are carried in twenty-three chapters. The counting rule and the four dates are in a record in a city since the fourteenth of July and are not withdrawn.
3. **THE PLATE NOTE IS NOT PAID. IT IS PART. IT IS CARRIED OPEN, FOR THE THIRD VOLUME IN A ROW.** The plate is in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, in twenty-five chapters; the note stands open in the same twenty-five; no chapter reached it. The document that would have closed it is spent, and it is on no page of this volume. **And the volume said out loud in a character's mouth that the only mechanism anybody has named for ever reaching that plate is a change of politics in an office and not a better letter out of a shed, and that is on the page and cannot be improved on.**
4. **THE DELAYED NOTE STANDS AT ELEVEN LOGGED OCCASIONS AND TWO OF THEM WITH NO CALL IN THEM, NEITHER COUNT WAS ADVANCED, NOTHING WAS MEASURED, AND THE FIGURE OF A HAND'S WIDTH OF A SECOND WAS WRITTEN DOWN ONCE WITH A DATE AGAINST IT — WHICH IS NOT A MEASUREMENT AND NOT AN OCCASION AND DOES NOT ENTER EITHER COUNT.** The chapter says so on its own face and gives the reason: a figure no man can check is a figure no man will believe, and a figure in a book with a day against it is a figure a man can go and look at and see that it is the same figure it was in the month of October, and this yard is not going to be the first to say why.
5. **THE CUSTODY ITEMS ARE THREE, NO DIGIT OF ANY OF THE THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE, NONE RETURNS, NONE IS ASKED FOR, THE CUSTODY ROOM WAS NOT ASKED FOR ON ANY DAY OF THE HUNDRED, THE CORRIDOR OUTSIDE IT WAS NOT ENTERED, AND THE CIRCUIT OFFICE'S COPYING ROOM WAS NOT ENTERED AND THE PARTY HAS NOT BEEN TO THAT COUNTER SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF NOVEMBER PAST.** The question what a municipal claim does to a presumed Crown material was not put to a clerk or to anybody in any chapter, and the form of the court does not answer it. **THE DRAWER ON THOSE BENCHES HELD THE CHARTER AND FOUR PIECES OF PAPER UNTIL THE FOURTH OF MARCH AND HOLDS SIX AT THE CLOSE OF CHAPTER 250 — the copy of a record, the acknowledgment, the answered half sheet, the printer's letter, the Crown form that went in in place of the charter, and the page that is the first of the five pages in the five drawers. The sheet and a half that came apart in the ship's hand on the thirty-first of January is in pieces and is not in that drawer and cannot be put back.**
6. **THE BELL, THE BELLWRIGHT AND THE LEAD PLUG ARE ALL HELD.** The going out of the second of May is done and spent and was not repeated; the bell reads nothing, settles nothing and says no word. The bellwright was not asked in any of the fifty chapters, is in no room in any of them, no digit of anything he said on the second of July past is printed, and the chest was not opened and was not brought down the hill.
7. **THE BOY, THE THIRD COLUMN AND THE NAME THAT WENT IN. HE IS OFF THE STONE SINCE THE FIFTEENTH OF MAY 2026 AND IS NOT A PERSON IN ANY OF THE FIFTY; FORTY MARKS STANDS WHOLE; THE THREE NOTS STAND; THE COLUMN WAS NOT FILLED ON ANY DAY OF THE HUNDRED AND NOBODY WAS APPOINTED AND NOBODY WAS HIRED TO READ IT BACK; AND ON THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH A NAME WENT IN BESIDE THE BOY'S HAND AND NOT OVER IT, IN THE SHIP'S HAND, NEITHER THE BOY'S NOR THE HOLDER'S, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHICH OF THE TWO THINGS IS HAPPENING AND GIVES THE REASON.** Lock L21's three prohibitions and the outline's final chapter image are both satisfied. **The resolution was done in the prose and not in the author's head, and the prompt that dispatched Batch 0005 and lock L21 are in the same file, and the next audit will find the same fault in another volume if nobody says it here.**
8. **ALDEN MARR DOES NOT CONFESS AND THE HOLDER DOES NOT GO OVER TO HIM. THE FAR-BENCH FIGURE FOR THE WHOLE FIFTY CHAPTERS IS THIRTEEN DAYS, COUNTED FROM THE PROSE, in five batches of 3 / 1 / 1 / 2 / 6: the seventh, eighteenth and twenty-first of December, the eleventh of January, the first, sixteenth and twenty-second of February, and the twenty-sixth of February with the fourth, sixth, eighth, twelfth and fourteenth of March. The ninety-two instances of *was not occupied* are the same record from the other side and are not a second count.**

FIVE OF THE SIX ARE THE SHIP'S HAND'S AND ONE IS THE PARTY'S.** No character remarked on how often it has been said, none remarked that it belongs to a room in an earlier volume, and no fisher claimed to have invented it.

IT IS NOT STATED ON EVERY DAY OF THE HUNDRED AND THE TWO FIGURES THAT BRACKET THE UNSTATED STRETCH ARE CONSISTENT WITH ONE DAY A DAY ACROSS IT. NO FIGURE IS RE-BASED AND NO CHAPTER IS OPENED FOR IT.**

IT HAD NOT BEEN SAID ONCE IN THE THIRTEEN WEEKS BEFORE IT.** **AND THE OUTLINE'S STARTING STATE, WHICH GAVE A THIRD TIME AND A REFUSAL OF A FOURTH, IS RULED AS DELIVERED AGAINST THE CHAPTERS, BECAUSE THE OUTLINE'S OWN RESOLUTION CLAUSE ASKED FOR A FOURTH AND A REFUSAL OF A FIFTH.**
15. **THE SLATE WALL'S COUNTER IS FIFTEEN CONSECUTIVE WIPES, ONE UNBROKEN RUNNING NUMBER, NO GAP AND NO REPEAT, FROM THE THIRTY-FIRST ON THE SEVENTH OF DECEMBER TO THE FORTY-FIFTH ON THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH, AND ALL FIFTEEN CAME DOWN BARE. IT RUNS ONE LOWER THAN A STRICT COUNT FROM THE FIRST OF MAY 2026, THAT DISCREPANCY IS INHERITED FROM THE VOLUME 04 AUDIT'S ZEROTH, AND IT IS RULED AND CARRIED AND NOT RE-BASED, BECAUSE THE FIFTEEN FIGURES ARE UNBROKEN AND RE-BASING THEM WOULD MOVE THE VOLUME'S OWN CLOSING FIGURE OF FORTY-FIVE, WHICH IS ON THE PAGE IN CHAPTER 250.**
16. **THE PROTAGONIST IS ON NO PAGE AS A PERSON FROM THE FIFTH OF MARCH TO THE END OF THE VOLUME, AND THAT IS RULED FOR THE STRUCTURE AND AGAINST THE MEASUREMENT.** He speaks in Chapters 241 to 244 and not again and a case-insensitive search of Chapters 245 to 250 for his name returns nothing. **He is away for fourteen consecutive days, the second to the fifteenth of March inclusive, having gone, and his going is the volume's climax and his absence is the price of it.** The tie is broken by the outline's own clause that the change in this pair is a change of standing and not of feeling. **AND THE LIMIT OF THE RULING IS BINDING: a later chapter may not give him a closing monologue about the fourteen days, may not have anybody in that harbor explain the absence to a stranger, and may not have the absence reported twice as though it were news.**
17. **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION, IT IS THE ONLY NEW ONE IN THIS SERIES SINCE THE WRIT, IT IS A PRACTICE, IT IS NOT A REGISTRY, A COURT OR A HARBOR AUTHORITY, IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH INSTANT, AND IT IS NOT AGED IN ANY LOCK AND NO LOCK MAY AGE IT.** Five pages in five drawers in five towns in five hands, one page to a drawer, no two of them the same page. What the other four can do about this one is the whole of it: they can come to that shed on that mole and ask, and there is no counter, no form, and nobody in any city they can write to. ### 1. The grid, and the four things a writer must not re-derive

1. **THE ANCHOR IS THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH NEXT, A MONDAY, BEING THE LAST DAY OF VOLUME 05. The batch ran Tuesday the sixteenth of March to Sunday the fourth of April, twenty consecutive days, two days to a chapter, no day missing and no day in two chapters, and no chapter states a year.** The slate wall came down bare twice, being the forty-sixth on the twenty-second of March and the forty-seventh on the twenty-ninth; the next two are the forty-eighth on the fifth of April and the forty-ninth on the twelfth. The cistern was charged on five rota days, being the eighteenth and twenty-fifth of March and the twenty-second and twenty-ninth of March and the first of April, and walked on none of them, being the thirtieth, thirty-first, thirty-second, thirty-third and thirty-fourth of the charges walked on none since the third of August. The three wage Tuesdays are the sixteenth, the twenty-third and the thirtieth of March, and the next four are the sixth, thirteenth, twentieth and twenty-seventh of April.
2. **THE MONEY, IN ONE LINE: 11,237 − 168 − 169 − 168 − 328 − 1 = 10,403.** The bag opens at seventy marks, three shillings and one penny and closes at sixty-five marks and threepence. Short of the wage of four marks by nine thousand seven hundred and sixty-three pence. **The whole of what came into that yard in the twenty days is NOTHING, and this is the first twenty-day run in five volumes with no income at all, and the reason is a form and not a mood.** Out, in all: eight hundred and thirty-four pence. Running total since the sixth of December: **eight marks, six shillings and two pence in eleven transactions at five counters.** The hire rates are canon and were not re-priced: a boat with a man in her for a day is one mark and eightpence, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence, and a penny of line.
3. **THE WAGE COLUMN STANDS AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS, THE FIFTH OF MARCH THE OLDEST, TWENTY ENVELOPES ON A BENCH, AND DID NOT MOVE ON ANY OF THE TWENTY DAYS.** Weeks fallen due with no envelope went twenty, twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three, on the sixteenth, twenty-third and thirtieth of March. **Twenty-three is the whole of that year's list and it is entered in the book in the same breath and not one after the other.**
4. **THE TWO STANDING DAY-COUNTERS BOTH ADVANCED BY ONE A DAY AND BOTH CHECK OUT: the two objects of nobody's are at 279 / 281 / 283 / 285 / 287 / 289 / 291 / 293 / 295 / 297 days up the crown of the mole on the seventeenth, nineteenth, twenty-first, twenty-third, twenty-fifth, twenty-seventh, twenty-ninth and thirty-first of March and the second and fourth of April, being 277 at the fifteenth of March; and the bench under that pump is bare for a forty-sixth, forty-eighth, fiftieth, fifty-second, fifty-fourth, fifty-sixth, fifty-eighth, sixtieth, sixty-second and sixty-fourth night, being the forty-fourth at the fifteenth of March.** No state file may supply a figure for a day no chapter gives.

### 2. The new canon of this batch

1. **A PARTY WITH NO INSTRUMENT CANNOT BE HIRED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE FIRST MOVEMENT.** The one-season provisional working charter was what a hirer relied on when he sent a boat to ground inside the harbor line, and it went out of the drawer on the fourth of March in a hand, so from the sixteenth there is nothing to book on a working day. **The writ is not restored, the charter is not restored, the Second Bell eligibility is not restored and is not applied for, and a party which is not examined is not a party which has been refused.**
2. **A PRIVATE HIRE IS NOT A WAY OF GETTING PAST A LINE.** Hiring a boat to look at a mark is a service to a boat's owner, on his own account and for his own purpose; it is not salvage, not a claim, and not work under any instrument; and it is not a place to put a man in the water. **A Volume 06 chapter may not let a private hire become a passage past the harbor line, the outer marks or the four hundred yards, and none of the twenty days put a person, a boat or a lead of this yard inside the bar.**
3. **THE FORM OF THE FOURTH OF MARCH ASKED THIS YARD FOR NOTHING, AND THAT IS WHAT MADE IT A LEASH.** It is not a writ, not a licence, not a finding; it suspends nothing, fines nobody, and says that a party which does not produce a thing on the day is not fined because a court does not fine a poor man; it says the harbor authority is not the office that can give it back and never was; and it requires nobody to produce a book of its own in any column and nobody to say who altered anything or at whose instance or with what intent.
4. **A MARK ON THE WATER HAS BEEN HANDLED, AND THE FINDINGS ARE FOUR AND NOT ONE.** Fouling of about four inches on the weather side on the seventeenth, three bright places on the shackle by the twenty-third, a foot by the twenty-sixth, a foot and a half on the fourth of April; a shackle off the frame and back on the wrong way up; a wire cut and mended with three turns and a seizing wire, and the three turns on the water side of the frame where this yard turns on the landward side; a four-strand untarred line bent in a figure of eight and tied with a sheet bend; and a flat of about a quarter of an inch across the crown of the bow. **THE TWO BRIGHT PLACES OF THE SEVENTEENTH ARE NOT STRUCK OUT AND THE SEVENTEENTH IS WRITTEN AGAINST THEM. A SHACKLE THAT IS BRIGHT HAS BEEN HANDLED; A GREEN THAT COMES UP EIGHT INCHES IN THREE DAYS HAS BEEN PUT THERE, BEING FOUR INCHES ON THE SEVENTEENTH, THE SAME FOUR INCHES ON THE TWENTY-THIRD, AND A FOOT ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH; A SHACKLE OFF AND ON AGAIN IS TWO HANDS, A SPANNER AND A MORNING; AND NONE OF THOSE THREE KNOWS A NAME, WHICH A MAN OF NINETEEN YEARS' STANDING SAID OUT LOUD AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK IN ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING.**
5. **THE SHACKLE IS A SWAGED AND TRUED FINISH WITH A FLAT ON THE CROWN, AND THERE IS ONE SMITH ON THIS COAST WHO FINISHES THEM THAT WAY, AND HE IS SIXTY-EIGHT AND HAS A SHOP OFF THE YARD AT TERNWATCH, AND HE DOES IT FOR THE YARDS THERE AND FOR NOBODY ON THIS SIDE.** No name is in the yard's book. **THIS IS A FACT ABOUT A MAKE AND NOT ABOUT A MAN, AND IT IS THE OPENING OF MOVEMENT 2, AND NO CHAPTER MAY CARRY IT INTO A STATEMENT ABOUT WHO WAS ON THE MARK.**
6. **THE FOURTH LEAF IS NEW AND IS RULED ON SATURDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MARCH.** Four columns: what was there, who saw it, what was done, and what it is not. Ruled on the back of a sheet of chandler's paper in the ship's own left hand with a blunt nib. **It may not be dated earlier than the twenty-seventh of March, may not be filled for any date before it, is not a return and not a confession and not a publication, DOES NOT GO ON ANY WALL IN MORROW QUAY, and is a page no man can check, which this yard knows and has entered, because it has already built one thing it cannot check and has been paying for that since the sixth of March.** At the end of the batch it has one entry in its first column and one line in its fourth, being that the fourteenth of May is not a date on which the fouling will be a season's but a date on which anybody who goes and looks can see that it is not, and the fourteenth of May is nine weeks from the twelfth of March, which is the day the mark was set.
7. **TOBIAS WREN IS ON A PAGE AGAIN AND HAS NAMED HIS TERMS, AND THE BATCH DID NOT PAY HIM FOR THEM.** He came up the mole on the nineteenth of March because he heard on Saturday at a fish market that a mark was fouled, and said he did not come up to be asked. Six marks a day for the boat and the gear and the wear whatever the month, a hand of about forty called Ruad paid separate by the day with a family at Lowfen, and fuel at what fuel costs. **HE ASKED ONE QUESTION AND IT WAS WHO IS PAYING. HE SAID HE WOULD NOT BE A TEACHER, AND THAT IN THIRTYY-ONE YEARS BY ANOTHER MAN'S ACCOUNT HE WAS NEVER ASKED WHAT WAS IN A THING HE WENT INTO AND NEVER SAID, AND WHAT HE SAW THE LAST TIME WAS A WRECK TAKEN APART WITH A WIRE SAW AND A BAD WHEEL AND HIS OWN HANDS AND NOTHING IN THE FRAME HE COULD CARRY, AND A THING LEFT ON THE BOTTOM THAT WOULD HAVE FITTED IN HIS COAT.** No boat of his was hired and six marks a day was not paid in this batch.
8. **ORs KEST GAVE THREE THINGS AND SAID BEFORE GIVING THEM THAT A MAN WHO IS GIVEN THREE THINGS HAS NOT BEEN REFUSED THREE THINGS.** The harbor authority issues no instrument after the thirty-first of March, the ledger being spent and a clerk's page and a spent ledger being what a city reads an office back for four years; that office is not the office that can give the charter back and never was, said a third time; and the one thing it can do is **seat two people and take a finding as it is given, by an ordinary power needing no charter, no writ and no season, at eight on a Monday, at a cost of two clerks and himself, one afternoon a week, in a room he has to be warm for.** The other side of the mark is a man of about fifty of the second lay and a smith in Ternwatch who has never heard of the yard, and seating either as a party would be inventing a proceeding to get at a name, and he does not invent proceedings. **HE SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE IS NOT A FRIEND OF THAT PARTY AND THAT THIS IS NOT A RESCUE, AND THE REASON HE SAID IT IS SO THAT THE STORY WILL BE HARDER TO TELL IN A MONTH.** Nothing was written to the tide gang and nothing was written to the man of the second lay.
9. **GARROW FISK, THIRTY-FOUR, OF A PRESSURE HOUSE AT TERNWATCH, IS A WORKING MAN AND NOT AN OFFICER AND NOT A NEW INSTITUTION.** He came up the hill on the second of April with a copy of the yard's printed sheet of thirty-eight lines folded at the thirty-eighth line, because his brother sails in one of about sixty boats, and said he was not there about a job and wanted to know whether that line was true. **He can hire a compressor, a housing and a man who can run them off a Crown house book at a Crown house rate, and will not pretend in a shed that the figure is small and will not pretend that this party is a Crown hull. HIS CONDITION IS THAT HE WILL NOT GO UNDER ANYTHING THAT HAS NOT BEEN CUT, BEING A PLATE, A FRAME, A HULL, A BELL OR A DOOR, AND HE SAYS THAT IS NOT A RULE IN A BOOK BUT WHAT HAPPENED TO A MAN HE WORKED BESIDE FOR NINE YEARS AT A CROWN YARD ON THE WESTERN SHELF, WHO IS ALIVE AND DOES NOT GO DOWN AT ALL NOW. HIS OWN TIME IS TWO MARKS AND EIGHTPENCE A DAY, NAMED BEFORE HE WAS ASKED, AND HIS TRAVEL IS HIS OWN RATE AND HAS NOT BEEN GIVEN AND IS NOT YET OWED AND IS NOT TO BE TREATED AS A DEBT UNTIL HE NAMES IT.** Two marks and eightpence was paid on the second of April. He sat on the top step of the mole for about an hour and a half and was brought out a cup of water and no more.
10. **A LETTER FROM MARA VENN CAME UP THAT HILL IN THE ORDINARY POST ON FRIDAY THE SECOND OF APRIL AND WAS READ ON THE SATURDAY, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME SHE HAS BEEN ON A PAGE SINCE VOLUME 05 AND THE FIRST TIME ANYTHING OF HERS HAS COME UP THAT HILL IN FIVE MONTHS.** It is one page and it says one fact and it makes no request: **an office she worked in for nine years has a form for material that office calls unsettled, and a person who keeps unsettled material in a house is a keeper of it under that form, and whether that means a house or a drawer or a cupboard the form does not say, and she has not seen that form served on anybody and cannot say what it does when it is.** It also says that she is a person of no office and has been since the fourth of January past, and that she will come to this harbor if a person asks her and will not come if a yard asks her, and that she has thought for three days about the difference between those two things and has not got round to it. **NOTHING WAS ASKED OF HER AND NOTHING WAS WRITTEN BACK, AND NOT WRITING BACK IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST, BECAUSE THE FIRST COLUMN IS A RECORD OF WHAT A MAN DID AND NOT OF WHAT A MAN DID NOT DO.**
11. **A LETTER OF ONE PAGE, ASKING NOTHING, WENT INTO THE ORDINARY POST ON SATURDAY THE THIRD OF APRIL AT A PENNY, TO A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY WHO CANNOT READ IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST.** It says what was found on the mark on three named dates, and it keeps the three dates apart, being that on the seventeenth it was fouled on the weather side with about four inches of green and the shackle had two bright places on it, and that on the twenty-third it was fouled to the same depth and the shackle had three bright places, the third of them on the underside, and a wire on the frame that had been cut and mended, and that on the twenty-sixth it was fouled to about a foot, with a line upon it that was not this yard's and a quarter-inch flat on the crown of the bow of a shackle this yard does not fit, so that a person can come and look at the mark on any day of a week and see for himself that there is a shackle on it and a wire on it and a line upon it; it says that the copy of the thirty-eight-line sheet which went into a kitchen in that town was read out once to about nine people and has not been read out since and is not going to be; and it says that whoever put that sheet in that kitchen did a thing this yard did not ask for and cannot undo. **THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DID NOT SIGN IT.** The ship's hand gave two reasons, being that a name on a letter is a letter a clerk can produce in a room and say of, and that a name on a piece of paper about a mark that two parties have a claim to, going out of this yard to a town two days down that coast and near a town four days down it where four people keep a page in a drawer, is this yard's name in an office's file in about two years. **THE LETTER IS SIGNED AT THE FOOT IN THE HAND OF THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY AND IN NEITHER OF THE OTHER TWO, AND HE DOES NOT MIND HIS NAME BEING ON IT.** This is the first thing that yard has put in the ordinary post since the four pages went out on the sixth of March, and it cost a penny.
12. **THE VOLUME'S QUESTION WAS ASKED AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK ON SUNDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF MARCH IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING AND WAS NOT ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER WAS GIVEN BY THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT, IN PERSON, FOUR DAYS BACK IN THE HARBOR, AND HE ANSWERED IT BADLY AND KNEW HE WAS ANSWERING IT BADLY.** The asker is a man of about thirty-one of the third lay with a coaster out of Ashtide, and his reason is his own and small: he has been three years on that water, he has started the coaster on it, a Crown chart of the western approaches in a bag says the ground is the remains of a fleet lost in a sea catastrophe and a matter of record and not of dispute, and he has a mate who thinks the other of the two. **The three things given were that there is nobody in this harbor old enough and the record that would carry it is not a record anybody alive can hold; that the only thing that could answer it is at seventy fathoms, about four hundred miles west-southwest of the head of that mole, and its name is not going to be said in a market, the reason being that a name said in a market is a name that gets asked for by offices; and that this party holds no instrument of any kind.** The yard said out loud before giving them that none of them is an answer and that it will not call a fact an answer. The asker then asked one question, **being whether the thirty-eighth line will be there in four years**, and was told the honest thing, that it will be, because it is under four nails on a wall where there has never been a paper, and that if it does not go nobody in that party will find out for four years either. **NOTHING OF THAT ANSWER WAS WRITTEN DOWN, AND THE REASON IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN.**
13. **THE NAME OF THE PLACE AT SEVENTY FATHOMS WAS REFUSED IN A MARKET AND IS NOT ON A PAGE OF THAT YARD'S BOOK.** It was said once in a shed in the year before last by a man of sixty-one to four people and has not been said since. It is not on any wall and is not in the second column.
14. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY CAME UP THAT COAST ON FRIDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF MARCH AND LAY ALONGSIDE FROM THAT FRIDAY TO SUNDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH AND THERE WAS NO BERTH FOR HIM IN THE THIRD LAY ON THE SUNDAY BECAUSE HE WAS AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK BEING ANSWERED, AND THE BERTH WENT TO A BOAT OUT OF THE NORTH BASIN, AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED WAS ASKED ABOUT IT AND NOBODY HAS ASKED.** This is the batch's cost to a third party on the harbor's own ground and it is the smallest one this book has ever entered and it is entered because it is one.
15. **THE THIRD LAY FILLED ON THURSDAY THE FIRST OF APRIL AT ABOUT SEVEN IN THE MORNING AND THERE IS ONE HERRING BERTH SHORT OF TWO, AND IT HAS BEEN SINCE THE AUTUMN.**

### 3. What did not move, and may not be moved

THE DELAYED NOTE AT ELEVEN LOGGED OCCASIONS AND TWO OF THEM WITH NO CALL IN THEM, A HAND'S WIDTH OF A SECOND, NOTHING MEASURED, NO OCCASION ENTERED, AND THE FIGURE NOT WRITTEN DOWN AGAIN.
