### 1. The grid, the one departure from it, and the four things a writer must not re-derive

1. **THE BATCH RAN MONDAY THE FIFTH OF APRIL TO WEDNESDAY THE FOURTEENTH, TEN CONSECUTIVE DAYS, ONE DAY TO A CHAPTER, NO DAY MISSING AND NO DAY IN TWO CHAPTERS, AND NO CHAPTER STATES A YEAR.** The fifteenth of March next is a Monday, so the fifth of April is a Monday and the fourteenth is a Wednesday, and every weekday in the ten is checkable off that one anchor.
2. **ONE RULE OF `outline/volume-06.md` LOCK L1 IS DEPARTED FROM, AND IT IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY BROKEN.** Lock L1 item 5 says a volume's chapters run two days to a chapter. **The ten chapters of this batch are one day each, and each chapter states its single day on its own face in the date line under its title, which is what that item requires of a chapter that is one day, and no day is in two chapters and no day is missing.** The reason is a conflict in the prompt that dispatched the phase, resolved against the prompt's own computed figures and in favour of the ones a writer can check: the same sentence of that prompt said *twenty consecutive days, two days to a chapter* and also named **Wednesday the fourteenth of April** as the last day, and ten chapters cannot be twenty days and end on the fourteenth; and three of the prompt's own checkable statements are only true for a ten-day batch — it names **three** cistern rota days inside the batch, being the fifth, the eighth and the twelfth, and lists Thursday the fifteenth as a rota day that is **not** in the batch, and it names **the sixth and the thirteenth** as the wage Tuesdays not to move on, and it names the forty-eighth and the forty-ninth wall wipes as the *next two*. A batch running to the twenty-fourth of April would carry six rota days and four wage Tuesdays and three wall wipes, and would contradict all three. **The named end date and the three checkable counts govern; the boilerplate about twenty days does not; and the chapters are right about what happened and the prompt is thrown away where it disagrees with them, which is `outline/volume-06.md` lock L1 item 6's own rule.** A later writer takes the days from the chapters.
3. **THE FOUR FIGURES A WRITER MUST NOT RE-DERIVE: the bag, the wage column, the standing day-counters, and the running outgoings since the sixth of December.** The bag is **sixty-five marks and threepence, being ten thousand four hundred and three pence**, on the morning of the fifth of April, and it closes the batch at **twenty-four marks, seven shillings and sevenpence, being three thousand nine hundred and thirty-one pence**, on the fourteenth, and it was moved by one transaction in ten days, being eleven marks in on the sixth, and it is **forty marks and six shillings shorter** than it was on the morning of the fifth. The running outgoings since the sixth of December are **eight marks, six shillings and twopence in eleven transactions at five counters** when the batch opens, and **nine marks, seven shillings and twopence in twelve at five counters** after the seventh, **twenty-one marks, nine shillings and tenpence in thirteen at six** after the eighth, **thirty-three marks, twelve shillings and sixpence in fourteen at six** after the ninth, and **fifty-nine marks, twelve shillings and twopence in seventeen at six** from the tenth to the fourteenth, which is the figure every chapter after the seventh now carries. The whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December is **one thousand seven hundred and sixty pence** and the whole of what went out in the ten days is **fifty-one marks and six shillings, being eight thousand two hundred and thirty-two pence**, and 10,403 + 1,760 − 8,232 = 3,931. The wage column stands at **twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks with the fifth of March the oldest and twenty envelopes on a bench**, and **twenty-three weeks** had fallen due with no envelope when the batch opened, and **twenty-four on the sixth and twenty-five on the thirteenth**, and the column did not move on either Tuesday and the envelopes did not move. The two objects of nobody's are at **two hundred and ninety-eight days** on the fifth of April and **three hundred and seven** on the fourteenth, and the bench under that pump is bare for a **sixty-fifth** night on the fifth and a **seventy-fourth** on the fourteenth.
4. **THE ROTARY FIGURES: two wall wipes, being the forty-eighth on Monday the fifth of April and the forty-ninth on Monday the twelfth, the counter not restarting and the clerk keeping his own page; and three cistern charges, being the thirty-fifth, thirty-sixth and thirty-seventh of the charges this party has entered walked on none of since the third of August past, on the fifth, the eighth and the twelfth, which are the only rota days in the batch. NO FIGURE WAS ENTERED AGAINST ANY DAY THAT IS NOT A MONDAY OR A THURSDAY, and the seven days of the batch that are not rota days carry no charge at all.**

### 2. The new canon of this batch

1. **THE CROWN HOUSE RATE WAS GIVEN OUT LOUD ON THE FIFTH OF APRIL AND IT IS NINE MARKS A DAY, being one thousand four hundred and forty pence, for a compressor, a housing, the pipe, the gauges and one man off a Crown house book; two marks and eightpence a day, being three hundred and twenty-eight pence, for Garrow Fisk's own time; and a mark and two shillings a day, being one hundred and eighty-four pence, for a hand on the hose. THREE DAYS OF IT AT THE BASE RATE IS THIRTY-SIX MARKS AND EIGHT SHILLINGS, being a day at twelve marks, two shillings and eightpence, and the third day fourteen marks, three shillings and fourpence with a second man off that book on it. **THE HOUSE'S MONEY RUNS A MARK TO A HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE AND A SHILLING TO TWELVE, WHICH IS NOT THE BRITISH CONVENTION AND IS THE CONVENTION OF THIS BOOK, AND EVERY FIGURE ON EVERY PAGE OF THIS BATCH RESTS ON IT.** The yard's hand is a party of one and a half and there is no figure for the half, and that is in the second column.** A Crown hull has the figure in a harbour's book and takes it out without looking at it, and Fisk said on the mole steps in about nine people's hearing that this yard is going to look at it every day of it, and nobody in that hearing said it was small.
2. **HIS CONDITION IS NOT CAUTION AND IT IS NOT ABOUT WHAT IS UNDER A DIVER'S FEET.** It is about what is over his head: everything a pressure house sells is on the end of a line, and when there is nothing hung on the bottom the line is a rope, and when there is something hung on it the line is a thing a swell on the surface can put round a corner and take hold of, and everything on the surface is then pulling one end of it, and the man at the end of it in the dark does not get a vote. **The cut is therefore a cut in a line, made above the water, and not a cut in a hull: a bight of shot line rove through a shackle, the two ends on the crown in two men's hands, the bight cut on the surface when the pot is on the bottom and the gear is off, leaving a man and a pot and forty fathoms of slack and nothing anybody is holding.** The two ends were cut on the eighth of April at about eleven in the morning with a man at forty fathoms.
3. **THE CUT WAS MADE ON A BENCH ABOVE THE WATER BY THIS YARD'S OWN HAND, ON THE SEVENTH OF APRIL, AND THE THREE TURNS OF SEIZING WIRE ARE ON THE WATER SIDE, AGAINST THIS YARD'S OWN PRACTICE.** The shackle was swaged and closed cold with a drift and three blows of a sledge; the serving was put on half a turn out of true, which is a fault everybody makes and which is a fault you can see. **THE REASON IS ON THE PAGE AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S OWN ARGUMENT IN ONE SENTENCE: a shackle on the face of the second seam carries three turns on the water side and a quarter-inch flat on the crown of the bow that this yard does not fit, and a shackle of this yard's own making turned the way this yard turns would be the only one on that coast with three turns on the water side, and a man on a mole with a spanner in his hand would be two and two, and this yard does not want that man to be able to be two and two. The serving being half a turn out of true is entered in the fourth column and not the first, because a thing which is not is not a thing a man did.**
4. **THE DESCENT IS BOUGHT AND NOT FOUND, IT IS AT FORTY FATHOMS, AND IT IS A FREE DESCENT IN OPEN WATER IN A TRENCH OFF THE SOUTH END A MILE AND A HALF OUT, WITH NOTHING TO ENTER.** Forty fathoms is two hundred and forty feet. **THE GAUGE IS A PRESSURE GAUGE AND NOT A DEPTH GAUGE AND THE FIGURE ON IT IS POUNDS AND NOT FEET: the pot was charged to eighty-four pounds on a face of a hundred and fifty on the seventh at about four in the afternoon and on the eighth and on the ninth, the ninth reading unsteady, the man of the pressure house reading eighty-two and the ship's hand writing eighty-four, and both figures are in the book with the difference against them.** The pot was charged by the compressor's own gauge, the needle could be seen, and eighty-four is not near the end of a face of a hundred and fifty, and a pencil mark was left on the face where the needle stood, so that the reading is on a gauge in a shed at Ternwatch as well as in a book in this shed and a man in that shed can put a finger on the mark. **THE DEPTH OF THE FLOOR IS FORTY FATHOMS AND COMES OFF THE LINE, NOT OFF THE GAUGE, AND NO FIGURE OF THE DEPTH IS ENTERED ANYWHERE EXCEPT IN FATHOMS.**
5. **THE BOTTOM AT FORTY FATHOMS IS NOT THE FLOOR OF A QUARRY. IT IS A LAID FLOOR OF CUT STONE IN COURSES, running in straight lines for about a hundred and forty feet in one direction and rather less in the other, the stones squared and the joints tight, and there is a figure cut in the stone at the NEAR END OF EVERY COURSE, cut before the stone was set, to a depth of about an inch and a length of about two inches, and the figures ran from ONE TO FORTY-ONE without a break and then past a hundred on courses beyond a turn in the trench.** In a socket cut and chiselled in the dressed face of one stone in the top course there is a bar of square iron about two feet long with a cold eye in it, the eye about an inch and a half across the flats, and a chain is made to that bar, and Voke's net was bent round it in two turns and a half.
6. **THE BEARING OF THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE IS NORTH-WEST BY WEST, ABOUT TWO HUNDRED AND SEVENTY, AND IT IS THE SAME LINE AS THE COURSES ON THAT FLOOR.** It was taken four times off the outer end, four times along the south side and four times off the head, and once in a boat along the courses, and it did not move. **It is the same figure as the bearing of the crown of the mole on a sheet of paper rolled behind the tide table in that shed, which is not a Crown document and is not anybody's document, and a person in four years can take that sheet out and lay a compass on it. THE MOLE HAS A FOOT, AND THE FOOT IS AT FORTY FATHOOMS A MILE AND A HALF OFF THE SOUTH END, AND THE FOOT IS NOT RUBBLE ON A SLOPE.** A man of about fifty of the second lay said out loud that he has worked inside that line for nineteen years and has never once been told about it, and that never being told about a thing and not knowing a thing was there are two different facts.
7. **THE CHAIN AND THE BAR CAME UP ON THE NINTH AND ARE IN THAT SHED, AND NEITHER HAS BEEN MEASURED OR CLEANED.** The chain is nine feet; the links are not all the same; **every fourth link is longer than the others by about two inches and has a short piece of unseized seizing wire on it.** A long link is made every fourth one in the pressure trade so a chain may be bent round a thing without a smith, and a seizing is put on after a chain is made and is never cut, and it is there so a man counting the chain can tell at a glance which links are the long ones. It was hung on a nail in the shed wall on the eleventh and lay on the floor in a heap about the width of a dinner plate, and a man of about fifty of the second lay looked at it, did not touch it, said it was not chain that came off a boat, and said he would not take it if he could.
8. **THE PARTY THAT PAID IS A PERSON AND HE IS OF NO OFFICE: ELIAS VOKE, FIFTY-ONE, OF THE HERRING BOAT OF THE SECOND LAY CALLED THE *ANNA RAY*, WHO HAS NINETEEN WINTERS IN A LIST BEING MADE UP IN A CITY AND WHO IS ONE OF THE THREE ORDINARY MEN `outline/volume-06.md` LOCK L28 NAMES FOR THIS VOLUME.** His warp, his net and eleven cork floats went down on the night of the twenty-ninth of March past in the cut off the south end in about forty fathoms and are hung and not lost, and until they are cut off there is a mile and a half of ground that no boat in that harbor can drag a net through, and the ground is his by first refusal and he cannot use it, and the herring are off that ground at the end of the next month. **He named eleven marks before any price had been spoken of by anybody, on the mole, in about eleven people's hearing, and said he knew it was not the cost and would not be argued up, and said a man cannot pay out of a list. The yard took the job at a loss and put the why in the first column with the date on it: a man asked for his own net off his own ground, and a party that cannot be hired has one thing left it can sell, which is a day of itself, and it had not sold one in twenty-three days. Eleven marks is the whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December past.**
9. **THE RECOVERY IS A PARTIAL ONE AND IT IS NOT A GOOD ONE: two hundred and eight fathoms of net came up out of four hundred and eleven, being rather more than a half and not two fifths, with eleven of eleven cork floats and the head rope entire, and the belly of the net — which was the part that was holding, and which was the money — is still on a floor at forty fathoms with a chain round it, and the ground is shut, and the herring come off it at the end of next month.** Voke came up on the thirteenth with the figure he had got two ways and said out loud in a shed that he will not pay the difference, and why, and that if he had it he would not give it, and that he has never once been the man who was carried. He was not thanked and did not want to be, and said he would like that to be a fixed arrangement.
10. **THE INJURY IS THE BATCH'S, AND IT IS PAID ON THE PAGE IN EVERY ONE OF ITS THREE PARTS. AMOS SEARLE, TWENTY-EIGHT, A HOLDER FOUR YEARS, OFF A CROWN HOUSE BOOK, WENT OFF THAT HARBOR ON A BOAT ON THE NINTH OF APRIL WITH A LEFT SHOULDER THAT WILL NOT GO ABOVE HIS HEAD AND TWO RIBS BROKEN IN TWO PLACES.** A net that has been lying on a floor at forty fathoms for eleven days has been swinging its ends about the whole time; the belly came free on the ninth at about eleven in the morning and the net came up slow and wide and all at once and took him up about eleven feet and put him into the edge of a course of squared stone. He said one thing and asked for it in his own words: **a net that has been hung eleven days comes up slow, and if he had known that in the morning he would have gone under it and not beside it, and he knew it in the morning and did not think about it, and it is not anybody's fault and he is not going to say otherwise in a boat.** The three parts are: **a real bill** — a mile and a half by water to a hospital at Ashtide with a man in her at one mark and eightpence, the man's fee at four marks, and a week's keep of a bed at seven shillings, entered as three separate figures and paid out of this yard's own book on the tenth; **a real absence** — a Crown house book carries him as unfit for five weeks from the ninth of April, then as fit for light work only, then as fit on the fifth of June, and he was not asked one question about it; **a real consequence** — a holder's trade is a man's back and a man's arms and a man's hands, there is no light work in it, and somebody else will be carrying what he cannot carry on the same book at the same figure, and **a second man off that book, HESK OTTRIM, THIRTY-ONE, HAD TO BE SENT FOR ON THE FRIDAY NIGHT IN A COACH THAT TOOK FOURTEEN HOURS, at two marks and eightpence a day, which is the figure the book has all of them at, and the set does not get cheaper because the man is a stranger.** He came up on his own account too: he said in a boat that he asked for the job and that he was sent for and asked for, and it is in the first column in his words. **HE IS NOT A WITNESS, IS NOT CITED IN A ROOM, AND IS NOT ASKED ANYTHING. He is a man of twenty-eight in a bed, and the yard's own second column records that there is nobody to ask and that it is not because a man was hurt, it is because a man of twenty-eight was not there and has never been anywhere.**
11. **`outline/volume-06.md` LOCK L22 IS PAID AND NOT RENAMED. THE SIX CONDITIONS OF A FIRST ENTRY WERE READ ALOUD AT THE BOAT IN ORDER ON THE SEVENTH OF APRIL AND THERE WAS NO FIRST ENTRY AND NOTHING TO ENTER, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT THEN SAID OUT LOUD IN FRONT OF FIVE PEOPLE THAT THERE IS NO HARBOR AUTHORITY'S BOOK TO GO IN — the ledger is spent, the season of that office ended on the thirty-first of March, no instrument has been issued since, and the clerk keeps his own page — AND THE SHIP'S HAND ANSWERED THAT THAT YARD'S OWN BOOK IS NOT THAT OFFICE'S BOOK AND IS NOT THE SAME THING AND CANNOT BE THE SAME THING, AND THAT THAT YARD IS GOING INTO THE WATER WITHOUT A THING IT HELD FOR FOUR MONTHS. THIS YARD'S OWN BOOK WAS NOT SUBSTITUTED FOR THAT BOOK AND CALLED THE SAME THING. NO PRIVATE BOOK, NO TENDER'S STOP AND NO REQUEST ENTERED ANY WATER.** The three days on which a person of that yard was in the water are the eighth, ninth and tenth, and each is in the first column with the reason against the line and with the price named before it was agreed — the price was named on the fifth, in a shed, and then on the mole, and the man of the second lay is the only other man who heard it and is not owed anything.
12. **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS HAS CEASED TO EXIST, AND IT CEASED BECAUSE THERE IS NO LONGER ANY SUCH FIGURE AND NOT BECAUSE ANYTHING WAS PAID.** The bag stood at eleven thousand nine hundred and ninety-one pence on the seventh of April and the wage of four marks is six hundred and forty of those, and the sentence this book has carried since the third week of March has had no subject since. **Nobody in that shed said one word about it at the time, and a woman in a shed is the only person in this story who would have.**
13. **THE BATCH'S TURN IS PAID IN CHAPTERS 268, 269 AND 270 AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S OWN TURN AND NOT A NEARER ONE: THE VOLUME'S QUESTION IS FOUND TO BE ANSWERABLE AND THIS PARTY IS FOUND TO BE THE WRONG PARTY FOR IT, BECAUSE THE EVIDENCE THAT ANSWERS IT IS ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST UNDER SEVENTY FATHOMS AND THE PEOPLE WHO KEEP THE ANSWER ARE THE PEOPLE THIS YARD WILL NOT ASK.** The finding is the method and not a fleet: a man laid stone at forty fathoms off this quay and cut a figure at the end of every course so that the man setting it would know whether he had laid a whole course or part of one, and the order a made thing was done in is cut into the made thing and can be read by anybody with a pot and a reason to be in the water. **THE DESCENT WAS AT FORTY FATHOOMS AND NOT AT SEVENTY, AND NOTHING AT SEVENTY FATHOMS WAS TOUCHED, MEASURED, NAMED OR ASKED ABOUT.** The third part of the arithmetic is not a number: a descent to seventy fathoms is a hundred and eighty feet under where the needle stood, and every part of the business is multiplied, and a set is a pressure house's set on a book and goes where the book sends it, and there is no book on that coast that sends it four hundred miles west and there is no yard on that coast that rents one, and there has never once been a man on that coast with a reason deep enough and a book good enough to be allowed to ask. And the four people on that coast who go into deep water without a book, four days down it, **were not asked, and the reason is the reason of the second of April and is about a trade and a price and not about a family: a man asked on a mole whether he cuts answers it with a price, and a price answered to a man of about thirty-four of a pressure house is a thing this yard would then have to pay, and it has not got, and it is not going to ask a man of sixty-one what he will take.**
14. **NOTHING WAS DONE ABOUT THE FLOOR AFTER THE BEARING WAS TAKEN, AND THAT IS ENTERED.** Nobody was sent for, no letter was written, no figure went up on any wall in that harbor, and the reason given out loud is that a refusal is better than a sheet, and that the first worst thing that can happen to a made floor is a man going down and being wrong about it, and the second worst is a chart of it.
15. **THE FORM FOR UNSETTLED MATERIAL WAS NOT SERVED ON ANYBODY AND NOBODY KNOWS WHAT IT DOES, AND THE PRESSURE IT PUTS ON THIS YARD IS LEGAL AND IS THE WORST IN THE BOOK: THIS YARD BECAME AN ADDRESS IN THE ORDINARY POST ON THE THIRD OF APRIL, AND AN ADDRESS IS A THING THAT CAN BE GIVEN TO A MAN WHO IS GOING SOMEWHERE.** The ship's hand said out loud that she does not care what the form is and that she cares that this yard did that to itself in writing in a day for a good reason, and that a good reason is the reason people use when they have not thought about the fourth year. Nothing was asked of the woman of no office, nothing was written back, nobody went up that coast road to a doorstep, and all three of those are in the second column and not the first, because the first column is a record of what a man did.
16. **THE FOURTH LEAF HAS SIX LINES IN ITS FOURTH COLUMN AT THE END OF THE BATCH, BEING THE LINES OF THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY AND OF THE FIFTH, THE SEVENTH, THE ELEVENTH, THE THIRTEENTH AND THE FOURTEENTH OF APRIL, AND THREE ENTRIES IN ITS FIRST COLUMN AND SEVEN LINES IN ITS SECOND AND NONE IN ITS THIRD. THE FIRST IS THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY, THE SECOND IS THE THREE TURNS ON THE WATER SIDE, THE THIRD IS THE SERVING HALF A TURN OUT OF TRUE, THE FOURTH IS THE CHAIN AND THE BAR AND THE SOCKET, THE FIFTH IS THE WRONG PARTY, AND THE SIXTH IS THE LINE READ BACK ON THE FOURTEENTH.** The boy was not on the stone on any of the ten days, came down once on his own account on the eleventh, was put on nothing, was not asked one word about the omissions he has entered, and said one thing at a shed door, which was **that the second column is getting full, and that it was not getting full in the spring.** The leaf goes on no wall and never will.
17. **THE BOY OF TWENTY-TWO WAS NOT ON THE STONE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND THE THIRD COLUMN IS UNFILLED, UNAPPOINTED, AND HIS HAND IS AT THE HEAD OF IT, WITH THE FOUR LINES ABOVE HIS NAMED LINE STILL FOUR, STILL NAMELESS AND NOT STRUCK OUT, AND THEY ARE IN ABOUT SIXTY BOATS ON THAT COAST.**
18. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY WAS NOT ASKED ANYTHING IN THESE TEN DAYS AND ASKED NOTHING, AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT OF TWO AND HAS BEEN SINCE THE AUTUMN. He was not turned into a witness, was not cited in a room, and was not asked a second question about the fleet. The Crown chart of the western approaches is in a bag in a boat out of Ashtide and this yard has not asked for it and has not written to him.**

19. **THE FOUR-HUNDRED-YARD BAR WAS NAMED OUT LOUD AT THE BOAT ON THE SEVENTH OF APRIL AND WAS ENTERED WITH THE PRICE AND THE DAY ON IT, AND THE GROUND WAS FOUND TO BE OFF THE SOUTH END AND ROUND THE CORNER FROM IT.** Fisk named it before the man of the second lay had finished asking how far off the ground was: the outer marks are a mile and a quarter off the head of that mole, the bar is four hundred yards off the outer marks, the bar begins about a mile and a half out on the north-west line, and the cut is off the south end and round the corner from all of it. **NO PERSON, NO BOAT AND NO LEAD OF THAT YARD WAS INSIDE THAT BAR ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, THE BAR WAS NOT NARROWED BY ANYTHING, AND THIS PARTY DID NOT ASK TO HAVE IT NARROWED, DID NOT ASK FOR IT IN ADVANCE AND DID NOT ASK FOR IT IN A BOAT.** The line is in the first column of the seventh and of the eighth and of the fourteenth and is repeated in the ledger of the twelfth. **This is `outline/volume-06.md` lock L5 kept rather than merely respected, and no later chapter may put that party inside the bar or may move the ground off the south end to a bearing that would do it.**
20. **THE CROWN HOUSE BOOK WENT DOWN THE COAST ROAD ON THE THURSDAY NIGHT OF THE EIGHTH WITH THE NEWS OF THE SHOULDER IN IT AND CAME UP AGAIN ON THE FRIDAY NIGHT IN THE SAME COACH THAT BROUGHT THE SECOND MAN, AND THE ROAD IS A NIGHT'S ROAD EACH WAY AND A MAN WAS IN A COACH ON IT FOR FOURTEEN HOURS.** Fisk said on the Friday that he would read the entry out when the book came up the road and not one minute before, and he read it out in that shed on the Saturday morning at about seven, with the door open and about four people in the street and the market not up, and the ship's hand entered the four lines in the second column in his words and entered the figure in no column. **THE READING IS A SATURDAY MORNING BEAT IN CHAPTER 266 AND NOT A SUNDAY BEAT IN CHAPTER 267, BECAUSE FISK WENT IN THAT BOAT TO ASHTIDE ON THE SATURDAY EVENING AND WAS AWAY FROM THE ELEVENTH TO THE FIFTEENTH, SAYING SO OUT LOUD ON THE STEP.**

### 3. What did not move, and may not be moved

**THE CHANDLER'S NOTE AT THIRTY-ONE, NOT RE-WRITTEN, ITS THREE COUNTS OF WEEKS AT TWENTY-TWO AND THIRTEEN AND ELEVEN, UNMOVED BY ARITHMETIC, AND IT WILL NOT BE SAID A FIFTH TIME. THE DELAYED NOTE AT ELEVEN LOGGED OCCASIONS AND TWO OF THEM WITH NO CALL IN THEM, A HAND'S WIDTH OF A SECOND, NOTHING MEASURED, NO OCCASION ENTERED, AND THE ANSWER INSIDE IT NOT APPROACHED. THE NOTICE OF THE THIRTY-FIRST OF OCTOBER WITH ITS FOUR CLAUSES, NOT LIFTED, NARROWED, RE-SERVED OR ALTERED, AND NO PERSON, NO BOAT AND NO LEAD OF THAT YARD INSIDE ITS FIRST CLAUSE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS EXCEPT THE THREE DAYS THAT ARE ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN WITH THE REASON AND THE PRICE NAMED BEFOREHAND. FOUR RETURNS AND NO FIFTH, AND NO RETURN OF ANY KIND MADE OUT OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. THE PLATE IN ELEVEN FEET, NOT REACHED, NOT MEASURED, NOT TOUCHED, NOT ASKED ABOUT, NOTE OPEN FOR A THIRD VOLUME. THE CASE OF FIVE BELLS, NOT RAISED, NOT ASKED ABOUT, AND THE LIMIT FOUR PEOPLE OF THAT COAST WROTE AND SIGNED STANDS, AND THE HOLDER DID NOT ASK TO HAVE IT LIFTED ONCE IN TWENTY-ONE DAYS. THE LEAD PLUG AND THE CHEST AND THE UNDERTAKING OF THE SECOND OF JULY; THE BELLWRIGHT WAS NOT ASKED IN ANY OF THESE TEN DAYS AND NO DIGIT OF ANYTHING HE SAID IS PRINTED. THE THIRD COLUMN. THE FORTY MARKS TWICE, STANDING WHOLE AND FIRST AFTER FOOD, NEITHER REDUCED AND NEITHER PAID. THE COMPARTMENT SPENT, THE THREE GANNET DOCUMENTS STILL THREE, THE NINE-LINE MARK NOT RE-OPENED, THE COAST ROAD UNRESOLVED AND THE KETTLE NOT LOOKED AT, THE THREE FIGURES NOT SWAPPED, THE SIXTH OCCASION NOT TO TELL AND THE UNDERTAKING NOT TO INVENT A SECOND ONE. THE WRIT, THE CHARTER, THE SEASON THAT ENDED ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH WITH NOTHING ISSUED, THE FOUR-HUNDRED-YARD BAR, AND THE SECOND BELL ELIGIBILITY, WHICH IS NOT RESTORED, NOT APPLIED FOR AND NOT MOVED ONTO ANYTHING. THE FAR BENCH WAS OCCUPIED ON THREE OF THE TEN DAYS, BEING THE TENTH, THE TWELFTH AND THE FOURTEENTH OF APRIL, AND WAS NOT OCCUPIED AT ANY HOUR ON THE OTHER SEVEN; THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM ON ANY OF THE TEN, WAS IN THAT HARBOR ON ALL TEN, AND NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT. TOBIAS WREN IS NOT ON A PAGE IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT SENT FOR AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING, AND THE REASON IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN OF THE TWELFTH AND IS ABOUT A PRICE AND NOT ABOUT A FAMILY.**

**AND THE REVEALS: THE WORD *QUIETENING* APPEARS NOWHERE IN CHAPTERS 261 TO 270. THE WORDS *CROWN SEAL* APPEAR NOWHERE. THE OFFICE OF RETURNING MEMORY IS NOT NAMED. NO ONE OF THE NINE FINAL ROUTES IS NAMED IN THE PROSE. NO SENIOR EXAMINER, NO MAGISTRATE AND NO OFFICER OF THE NAVY IS A FACE ON ANY PAGE OF THIS BATCH; HALVEN ROOK IS NOT NAMED IN IT AND HIS FORM IS NOT YET SERVED ON ANYBODY IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS. NO ONE OF THE FOUR PEOPLE OF THAT COAST WAS ASKED FOR ANYTHING. THERE IS NO PANEL, STAT BLOCK, CHARACTER SHEET, STATUS MESSAGE, FLOATING TEXT, QUEST TEXT, SKILL TREE, LEVEL-UP OR SOFTWARE VOCABULARY, NO SECOND PERSON ADDRESSING THE READER, AND NOTHING ON ANY PAGE KNOWS ANYTHING. A MECHANICAL SCAN OF THE TEN CHAPTERS FOR *PANEL*, *QUIETENING*, *CROWN SEAL* AND *ORISON* RETURNS NOTHING.**

### 4. The power state, and the cost of the perception paid as a body and not as a stage

**NO STAGE IS TAKEN. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, IMPROVED OR RENAMED ON ANY PAGE. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED. THE VOLUME'S POWER CHANGE IS THE COST OF THE PERCEPTION IN ORDINARY WORK AND IT IS PAID IN THIS BATCH TWICE: ON THE EIGHTH OF APRIL THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT CAME UP OUT OF FORTY FATHOOMS WITH A FIGURE HE COULD NOT GET OUT OF HIS HAND, HE HAD IT IN HIS HAND TWICE AND COULD NOT SAY WHAT IT WAS, AND NOBODY IN THAT BOAT ASKED HIM WHAT HE MEANT; AND ON THE ELEVENTH HE LOST A DAY TO THE BODY AND SAID THE ONLY SENTENCE ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS EVER USED FOR IT, WHICH WAS THAT HE HAD TO GO AND STAND AT SOMETHING FOR A BIT. THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH AND THE DAY CARRIES NO FIGURE, BECAUSE THERE IS NO FIGURE FOR A DAY. AND ON THE TWELFTH HE COULD HOLD A COMPASS AND COULD NOT HOLD A SLATE, AND A COMPASS IS A NEEDLE AND A CARD AND A BIT OF LOOKING AND IS NOT A JOIN, AND THAT IS ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN AS A THING THAT WAS DONE AND THE REASON AGAINST THE OTHER INSTRUMENT IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN WITH A REASON AND NO NAME IN IT.**

**31,660 WORDS ACROSS TEN CHAPTERS, AN AVERAGE OF 3,166, AGAINST 2,200–3,200 A CHAPTER: Ch261 3,720 · Ch262 2,830 · Ch263 3,250 · Ch264 2,896 · Ch265 2,927 · Ch266 3,556 · Ch267 2,538 · Ch268 3,214 · Ch269 2,844 · Ch270 3,885, AS RE-MEASURED WITH `wc -w` AFTER THE REVIEW REPAIRS OF 28 SEPTEMBER 2026. FIVE INSIDE AND FIVE PAST, AND THE LARGEST IS CHAPTER 270 AT 3,885, WHICH IS THE BATCH'S CLOSE AND CARRIES THE WHOLE STANDING INVENTORY ONCE. Method as at the Volume 05 audit: every paragraph split at the markers *First column* and *Second column, not checkable from a mole*, the words in each class counted, the remainder counted as scene. THE APPARATUS IS 41.2% OF THIS BATCH'S WORDS AGAINST 40.9% FOR IT AS IT FIRST CLOSED, 41.5% FOR BATCH 0001 AND 41.0% FOR VOLUME 05. IT WENT UP BY THREE TENTHS OF A POINT BECAUSE THE REPAIRS ADDED FIGURES, A REASON AGAINST A LINE AND FOUR LEDGER SENTENCES AND TOOK ONE PARAGRAPH OF STANDING INVENTORY OUT OF CHAPTER 267, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN REPRESENTED AS A FIX. THE REAL CHANGE IS STILL A STRUCTURAL ONE AND IS NOT A PERCENTAGE: BATCH 0001 CARRIED THE WHOLE STANDING INVENTORY IN EVERY ONE OF ITS TEN CHAPTERS AND THIS ONE CARRIES IT WHOLE IN CHAPTER 270 AND NOWHERE ELSE, AND THE FIRST-COLUMN AND SECOND-COLUMN ENTRIES IN THE OTHER NINE CHAPTERS CARRY DATED FIGURES THAT THE SCENE ALSO CARRIES RATHER THAN RESTATING THE BOOK. NO SCENE WAS CUT AND NO COST WAS DROPPED TO BRING ANY CHAPTER INSIDE A NUMBER.**

## Batch 0002 (Volume 06) review repairs — the disposition of every finding in `logs/batch-0002.review.log`, applied 28 September 2026

**THE BATCH WAS NOT RESTARTED AND NO CHAPTER WAS REWRITTEN. `NOVEL_REVIEW_RESULT: FIX` WAS RETURNED ON TEN SERIOUS FINDINGS AND FOUR PROSE ITEMS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS AN ARITHMETIC ERROR, A CONFLATED DATE, AN ORPHANED SCENE, AN UNADDRESSED BOUNDARY, A META CONSTRUCTION OR A REPETITION, NOT A FAULT OF SHAPE, PRESSURE, PACE OR PLOT. NO STAGE WAS TAKEN, NO REVEAL WAS MOVED, NO COST WAS WAIVED, NO RELATIONSHIP WAS ADVANCED AND NO NEW ANTAGONIST, INSTITUTION OR FINAL ENEMY APPEARS IN A SINGLE REPAIRED LINE. THE PLANNED ENDING IS UNTOUCHED.**

### The ten serious findings, each disposed of in the chapter that carried it

1. **GARROW FISK WAS IN TWO PLACES AT ONCE, AND THE ROAD TIME WAS BROKEN IN TWO DIRECTIONS.** `chapter-0266.md` had him sail to Ashtide on the Saturday evening with a promise to be back on the Thursday, and `chapter-0267.md` then had him read the Crown house book out in the shed at ten on the Sunday morning; `chapter-0265.md` had the book going back on the Friday night over a road that takes two days, and `chapter-0267.md` had it back on the Saturday night over a night's road. **THE READING IS NOW A SATURDAY-MORNING BEAT IN `chapter-0266.md` AT ABOUT SEVEN, BEFORE THE BOAT WENT OUT AT HALF PAST EIGHT, AND THE BOOK GOES DOWN THE COAST ROAD ON THE THURSDAY NIGHT OF THE EIGHTH WITH THE NEWS OF THE SHOULDER IN IT AND COMES UP AGAIN ON THE FRIDAY NIGHT IN THE SAME COACH THAT BROUGHT THE SECOND MAN, AND THE ROAD IS A NIGHT'S ROAD EACH WAY.** The promise of Chapter 265 — *I will read it out when the book comes up the road and not one minute before* — is now kept on the page and its ledger line in Chapter 265 is true, and the second-column entry for the reading has moved with it out of Chapter 267 into Chapter 266. **The Sunday is now the shed, the chain, a man who asks for the figure in the bag, the lost day and the boy, and Fisk is in a boat off that harbor from the Saturday evening to the Thursday of the next week, as he said on the step.**
2. **CHAPTER 267'S PARAGRAPH ORDER WAS BROKEN AND ITS BOOK-READING SCENE WAS ORPHANED** — the reading narrated in the past tense at the top, the dialogue stranded after a rule with no antecedent, "He was up at eight" reading as the boy who had just gone, and one fourth-column line attributed in the scene to the holder of that writ and in the ledger to the ship's hand. **ALL FOUR ARE GONE WITH THE SCENE, AND THE CHAPTER NOW RUNS IN CLOCK ORDER: the chain on the nail at nine, the man of the second lay at half past ten, the day lost to the body from eight and the bench, the boy at eleven and the entry read back at half past eleven, and the fourth line of the fourth column dictated at the bench at about four in the afternoon and written by the ship's hand in her own left hand, which is entered in the first column as well as in the scene.**
3. **THE MONEY CHAIN DID NOT RECONCILE WITH THE RATES NAMED ON THE PAGE.** The rate sheet, the per-day figures, the three-day figure and every total down to the bag agreed with one another and all of them were wrong in the same place: the hand on the hose was named **a shilling and fourpence** and was valued at **one hundred and eighty-four pence** wherever a total was worked out. **THE HAND'S DAY RATE IS NOW A MARK AND TWO SHILLINGS, which is one hundred and eighty-four pence in this book's money, and the correction beat in Chapter 261 is now a correction of a mark and four shillings down to a mark and two. NO TOTAL IN THE BATCH CHANGED.** Thirty-six marks and eight shillings for three days, three marks and six shillings for the hand, twelve marks two shillings and eightpence a day and fourteen marks three shillings and fourpence on the third day, thirty-eight marks eight shillings and eightpence for the three days together, fifty-one marks and six shillings for the ten, and every bag figure are as they were and are now consistent with the rates printed beside them. **THE HOUSE'S CONVENTION IS NOW STATED IN THIS FILE AT § 2.1: A MARK IS A HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE AND A SHILLING IS TWELVE, WHICH IS NOT THE BRITISH CONVENTION.** A second instance of the same class was found while applying this and is repaired: a week's keep of a bed at Ashtide was entered as a shilling and fourpence a day and as seven shillings for the week, and the bed is **a shilling a day** in Chapter 265 and in the ledger of Chapter 266.

### What the review found that was itself wrong, and the arithmetic that settles it

**THREE FIGURES IN THE REVIEW DO NOT SURVIVE RE-DERIVATION AND THE CHAPTERS WERE RIGHT.**

1. **The restatement of the three days in `chapter-0270.md` — thirty-six marks and eight shillings at the base rate, plus a second man at two marks and eightpence, being thirty-eight marks, eight shillings and eightpence — IS CORRECT** and is left as it stood. Thirty-six marks and eight shillings is 5,856 pence, two marks and eightpence is 328, and 5,856 + 328 = 6,184 = thirty-eight marks, eight shillings and eightpence at this book's rates. The review made the addition as though eightpence were eight shillings.
2. **The itemized ten-day list in `chapter-0270.md` SUMS TO FIFTY-ONE MARKS AND SIX SHILLINGS, which is what the chapter says**, being 172 + 1,952 + 1,952 + 2,280 + 984 + 892 = 8,232. The whole of the ten days' outgoings was already right in the chapters, in `state/current.md` and in `state/chapter-summaries.md`, and is still right.
3. **The queued prompt's "FORTY MARKS AND SIX SHILLINGS SHORTER" THAN THE MORNING OF THE FIFTH OF APRIL IS CORRECT** and was not touched. Ten thousand four hundred and three minus three thousand nine hundred and thirty-one is six thousand four hundred and seventy-two pence, which is forty marks and six shillings. The review had set the cumulative outgoings against the bag instead of the ten days' outgoings against the bag.

**AND ONE FINDING WAS AIMED AT A FIGURE IN THIS FILE THAT IS NOT THE ONE THE REVIEW NAMED: the batch's own bag was never wrong.** 65m 3p − 172 − 1,952 − 1,952 − 4,156 + 1,760 = 3,931, and every bag figure printed in Chapters 262 to 270 was and is correct.

1. **THE BATCH RAN THURSDAY THE FIFTEENTH OF APRIL TO SATURDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH, TEN CONSECUTIVE DAYS, ONE DAY TO A CHAPTER, NO DAY MISSING AND NO DAY IN TWO CHAPTERS, AND NO CHAPTER STATES A YEAR.** The fifteenth of March next is a Monday, so the fifteenth of April is a Thursday and the twenty-fourth is a Saturday, and every weekday in the ten is checkable off that one anchor.

3. **THE THREE STANDING FIGURES, COUNTED AND NOT TAKEN FROM A STATE FILE. THREE cistern rota days fall in the batch, being THURSDAY THE FIFTEENTH, MONDAY THE NINETEENTH AND THURSDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND OF APRIL, and all three were walked on none of them, being THE THIRTY-EIGHTH, THIRTY-NINTH AND FORTIETH of the charges this party has entered walked on none of since the third of August past; no figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday. ONE wall wipe falls in it, being THE FIFTIETH on Monday the nineteenth at eight in the morning, the counter not restarting, the clerk keeping his own page and no sitting being held in that room on any day of this book; the fifty-first is on Monday the twenty-sixth and is outside the batch. ONE wage Tuesday falls in it, being the TWENTIETH, on which the twenty-sixth week fell due with no envelope and THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE; the twenty-seventh is outside the batch and the column will not move on it either.**
4. **THE MONEY, IN ONE LINE: 3,931 + 0 − 834 = 3,097.** The bag opens at **twenty-four marks, seven shillings and sevenpence, being three thousand nine hundred and thirty-one pence**, and closes at **nineteen marks, four shillings and ninepence, being three thousand and ninety-seven pence**. **NOTHING CAME INTO THAT YARD ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, so the whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December past is still one thousand seven hundred and sixty pence, being the eleven marks of Elias Voke on the sixth of April, and there is nothing else and there is not going to be.** Out, in the ten days, and it is four things: one penny at a box on the corner of that mole on the fifteenth; four hundred and eighty pence on the seventeenth for a day at the face of the second seam on the hirers' own account with nobody in the water; one penny at the same box on the eighteenth; and three hundred and fifty-two pence on the twenty-first, being the boat of the man of the second lay for a day at a mark and eightpence and a man of twenty-six hired by the day at a mark and two shillings, **the price named on the Tuesday evening and not on the Wednesday morning.** That is **eight hundred and thirty-four pence, being five marks, two shillings and tenpence.** The running outgoings since the sixth of December are **fifty-nine marks, twelve shillings and threepence in eighteen transactions at seven counters** on the fifteenth and the sixteenth, **sixty-two marks, twelve shillings and threepence in nineteen at seven** on the seventeenth, **sixty-two marks, twelve shillings and fourpence in twenty at seven** from the eighteenth, and **sixty-five marks, one shilling and eightpence in twenty-one at seven, being ten thousand four hundred and twenty pence**, from the twenty-first onward. A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve. **A DAY OF A HIRED HAND IS THREE MARKS AND THAT FIGURE IS NOW ON THE PAGE IN A LETTER.** **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS DOES NOT EXIST AND DID NOT EXIST ON ANY OF THESE TEN DAYS, and will not come back while that bag is above six hundred and forty pence, and nobody in that shed said one word about it at any hour of any of them.**

No state file may supply a figure for a day no chapter gives.**

Chapter 275, which falls on the nineteenth, enters only the days up to and including the nineteenth and says that the count of the ten is not entered until the ten are done.**

### 2. The new canon of this batch

1. **THE FORM EXISTS AND HAS BEEN SEEN AND HAS NOT BEEN SERVED, AND IT IS AN INSTRUMENT AND NOT A PERSON, AND ITS TEXT IS ON THE PAGE.** A single printed sheet, headed in type as **particulars of material held as unsettled**, with five ruled lines under the head, of which the first is filled in with a name and a place and the other four are blank; **the place is a house in a town two days down that coast**; at the foot, under a rule, a line which says **served** and has nothing after the word; and below that **a seal line with a name on it, and the name is Halven Rook, entered in the first column on the sixteenth of April because a name on a piece of paper is a thing a man can go and look at.** HE IS A NAME ON A SHEET. He is in no room, on no mole, and in no market, and no office answers anything in a room in this batch, and **no clerk in a copying room explains what the form does to anything.**
2. **THE FORM IS SERVED BY BEING PUT IN THE ORDINARY POST, AT AN ADDRESS, ON A DAY, AND IT WAS SERVED ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF APRIL PAST AT HALF PAST FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON AT A BOX ON THE CORNER OF THAT MOLE AT A PENNY.** The address is **the man of about thirty who cannot read in the town two days down that coast**, being the address this yard wrote to on the third of April past. **HE IS NOT BEING SERVED IT BECAUSE HE IS A KEEPER, AND THE YARD SAID SO OUT LOUD: a form cannot tell the difference and neither can the holder of that writ, and the reason it went to that address is that it is the only address in that book which is not that yard's.**
3. **MARA VENN IS A PERSON OF NO OFFICE, THIRTY, OF THIS HARBOR, AND HAS BEEN OF THIS HARBOR SINCE THE FOURTH OF JANUARY PAST, AND SHE CAME DOWN THAT COAST IN THE AUTUMN.** **THE GEOGRAPHY CONFLICT RECORDED AT `state/open-threads.md` § *Volume 06, Batch 0001 — review repairs*, item 6, AND CARRIED AT § *Volume 06, Batch 0002*, author-level decision 5, IS RESOLVED ON THE FACE OF THE PAGE AND NOT BY INVENTION. The second column's line of the fourth of April past which said that her letter came from a person of no office FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST IS WRONG; IT WAS NOT STRUCK OUT; the correction is written against it in the second column with the said Friday's date on it, in the first column's reading, and **the reason she gives for not striking it out is that a yard which strikes out its own line because it was wrong is a yard which has decided that a wrong line is not a record.** `chapter-0175.md:105` AND `chapter-0176.md:83` STAND, AND `chapter-0260.md`'s SECOND-COLUMN LINE OF THE FOURTH OF APRIL STANDS WITH THE CORRECTION AGAINST IT, AND NEITHER FILE WAS EDITED.**
4. **SHE CAME UP THE HILL BECAUSE A PERSON ASKED HER AND NOT A YARD, AND THE ASKING BROKE THE UNDERTAKING OF THE FOURTEENTH OF APRIL, WHICH WAS BROKEN OUT LOUD IN THE SHED BEFORE NINE ON THE FIFTEENTH, WITH ONE REASON, WHICH WAS THAT A FORM EXISTS AND THAT A YARD WHICH DOES NOT ANSWER A LETTER IS AN ADDRESS THAT ANSWES NOTHING.** The four lines are unsigned — the reason of the third of April, not improved on — and **the fourth line is five words, and it is *I am asking you. Not the yard***, and she reads that line eleven times and the three above it not once. **NOTHING WAS ASKED OF HER FOR ANYTHING AND NOTHING WAS PAID TO HER AND HER FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD WERE NOT MENTIONED ONCE IN ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, and she stood in that shed on six of the ten days.**
5. **SHE HAD THE SHEET ELEVEN WEEKS, SINCE THE FOURTH OF JANUARY PAST, AND COULD NOT PUT IT IN A DRAWER AND COULD NOT BURN IT AND COULD NOT TAKE IT TO A POST OFFICE AND COULD NOT HAND IT TO A YARD, AND THOSE WERE FOUR THINGS AND SHE HAD TRIED THREE.** She rules out her own name as an address herself, in these words: **a form that can be left on a shed can be left on a room and then on a county and then there is no end to it, and she will not be the wrong place.**
6. **THE BURNING IS THE KEEPING, AND IT IS THE CLAIM OF THAT OFFICE STATED IN A SENTENCE SHE HAS SPOKEN TWICE.** A person who burns a paper with unsettled material on it has handled it; a person who has handled it has kept it; a person who has kept it is the thing the paper is about. **THE BATCH'S DESIGN IS THAT THIS CLAIM IS TRUE ENOUGH TO BE DANGEROUS AND IT IS TRUE, AND THE VOLUME HAS NOT ONCE MADE IT FALSE, AND THE YARD'S OWN ARGUMENT IS BUILT ON IT AND IS ALSO GUILT BY IT.**
7. **FOUR DOORS SHUT ON THE SHEET INSIDE TWO HOURS ON THE EIGHTEENTH, IN THIS ORDER, AND THE FIFTH IS A BOX ON A CORNER. NOT THE DRAWER, because a drawer is a drawer and that drawer holds a page five people in five towns agreed to keep. NOT THE TIN, because a tin shuts. NOT A WALL, because a sheet on a wall in that harbor is a sheet that goes out of that harbor and this yard has put four copies of its own sheet out of it already. NOT A FIRE, for the reason above.** And the two addresses that are not that yard's were ruled out as well: this shed, and the boy of twenty-two, and **no name of the boy is in any column of that book and none has ever been.**
8. **THE BATCH'S DISCOVERY, MADE ON THE SEVENTEENTH OUT OF A SHEET THIS YARD ALREADY HAD, AND NOBODY WAS ASKED FOR IT: THE FOUR LINES OF THE SIXTH OF MARCH PAST ARE ABOUT A *RECORD* AND ARE NOT ABOUT A *HOUSE*.** There is not one address in those four lines and the word house is not in them at all. A record may be asked who has read it, which is the reason the second line is written the way it is written — a no can be asked about, so a no is not written, so nobody has to say one. **A HOUSE MAY BE ASKED NOTHING. A form cannot be served on a record because a record has no address, and a record is given one by writing down where the drawer is, and a house is the only kind of thing in this country you cannot refuse anybody anything about.** The four lines as read out in full on the seventeenth, in four hands and four people's English: *One. Nobody comes for this. Two. Nobody copies this, and nobody is asked to say no to copying it, because a no is a thing that can be asked about. Three. It does not move, and it does not go anywhere, and it does not go with anybody, and nobody is to be told where it is by us. Four. If anybody comes, they are told there is a drawer and the drawer is a drawer, and they are not told what is in it, and they are not told it is not in it either.*
9. **AND THE TURN, SAID ONCE IN CHAPTER 273 AND ONCE IN CHAPTER 280 AND NOT IMPROVED ON EITHER TIME: THIS YARD DID IT ON THE THIRD OF APRIL PAST AND DID IT IN A GOOD CAUSE, AND A PAGE IN A DRAWER IN A HOUSE IS CUSTODY THAT AN OFFICE CAN REACH, AND THE ONLY REASON A FORM HAS NOT BEEN AT SOMEBODY'S DOOR ON THIS COAST IN ELEVEN DAYS IS THAT NOBODY ON THIS COAST HAS HELD ONE, AND THAT IS NOT A PROTECTION AND IS A FORTNIGHT OF LUCK.** And: **a house is not a place a thing is safe in; it is a place a person cannot refuse anybody anything about, and it is a door with no handle on the inside, and a drawer is a house, and a yard is a house, and this shed is a house.**
10. **MARA VENN SAID A THING OUT LOUD IN A FISH MARKET IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING ON THE TWENTY-SECOND OF APRIL PAST, AND IT COST HER THE STANDING OF A CERTIFICATE OF METHOD, AND THE CERTIFICATE ITSELF IS NOT WITHDRAWN AND CANNOT BE.** A woman of about fifty-eight who has sold fish off that quay for thirty-one years, the end stall in the second row, four boxes of the small sort, a son in a city, asked one question in about forty people's hearing and it was **is a person allowed to burn a thing like that.** She was answered in the words of a method, about a thing that is not glass, in a place with no glass and no bench and no oath in it. **A certificate of method in the reading of worked glass and its faults, held by a woman of thirty of no office, issued in the ninth year of her time in that office: the standing of such a certificate is that a person may repeat what she has said under that method in a room where a thing is on a table, and every person in that room may act on it, because a method is behind it and a method can be checked by anybody who holds the same method. A method's words said in a market, about a thing that is not glass, in about forty people's hearing, are a story told by a woman who used to be certified. THE CERTIFICATE IS NOT WITHDRAWN AND NO OFFICE IN THIS COUNTRY CAN WITHDRAW IT FROM HER, BECAUSE SHE IS OF NO OFFICE AND THE OFFICE THAT KEEPS THE COPY IS A BUILDING WITH A DOOR ON IT AND NO PERSON BEHIND THE COUNTER, AND THE SHEET SHE WAS ISSUED IS IN A DRAWER IN A TOWN FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S KEEPING, AND THIS YARD IS NOT GOING TO WRITE TO THAT TOWN. AND WHAT SHE SAID WAS TRUE, AND NOBODY IN THAT MARKET WAS ABLE TO TELL WHETHER IT WAS TRUE OR NOT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE PRICE.** **No person of that yard was in that market and nobody was sent.**
11. **THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT HAS A SHEET OF PAPER WITH A SEAL ON IT IN A DRAWER UNDER HER BED WITH HER WILL AND HER MARRIAGE LINES, AND SHE GOT IT FROM HER SON IN THE AUTUMN, AND A MAN WHO BUYS FISH FROM HER TOLD HER IN FEBRUARY THAT HE HAD HEARD OF A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE WHO WOULD KNOW WHAT A PAPER WAS.** **NOTHING HAS BEEN SERVED ON HER AND NOBODY HAS EVER SAID ONE WORD TO HER ABOUT IT AND SHE IS AFRAID, AND THIS YARD IS NOT GOING TO WRITE TO HER, and the reason against the line is that this yard has made itself one address in this country and is not going to make a second.** **THE PRICE OF THE VOLUME'S OWN ANSWER IS A DRAWER IN A TOWN WHERE THIS YARD HAS NEVER PUT A QUESTION TO ANYBODY, and it is not four hundred miles from the coast the yard swore about on the fourteenth of April, and that is the point.**
12. **A LETTER OF ONE PAGE CAME UP THAT HILL ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF APRIL PAST, IN A YOUNG HAND, SIGNED WITH TWO NAMES, BEING WEND BRACE, THIRTY, AND ILSE BRACE, NINETEEN, AT THE ADDRESS THIS YARD WROTE TO ON THE THIRD OF APRIL PAST. IT COST THIS YARD NOTHING AND IT ASKED FOR NOTHING, AND ITS THREE DATES ARE ENTERED AS THREE DATES AND ARE NOT MADE INTO ONE.** A sheet was on a step in that town on **Tuesday the twentieth** in the afternoon and was not there in the morning; a man came in from the water at about half past five on **Wednesday the twenty-first** and found it where it had lain since the Tuesday, wet and dried, and stood in his own doorway and did not pick it up for about ten minutes, and was by that out of a day's work, being **a hand hired by the day at three marks**, and the boat's man is not in the letter and does not know there is a letter; and on **Thursday the twenty-second** his daughter read it out to him and he had it read twice and he cannot read and the letter says so in those words. **THE THREE MARKS IS A FIGURE THE BOAT'S MAN PAYS AND NOT THAT YARD, THE BOAT'S MAN IS NOT NAMED, AND IT IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST, BECAUSE THE DAY AFTER THAT SOMEBODY IS GOING TO SAY TO AN OFFICE THAT THIS YARD HAS TAKEN A MAN'S WAGE OFF HIM.** And: **a girl of nineteen read a page of that yard's own printed sheet out in that kitchen in the autumn to about nine people and has not read one out since and is not going to, and a form of an office that yard does not belong to is on her father's step, and those two are entered as two and are not made into one, and that sentence is the reason against the line of sending anybody.**
13. **THE YARD SENT NOBODY, WROTE NOBODY AND PAID NOTHING, AND THE THREE MARKS ARE NOT GOING TO BE PAID, AND THE REASON IS NOT THAT THE YARD HAS NOT GOT THEM.** The reason is that **the day this yard pays that man three marks he is a man this yard has paid, and a man this yard has paid is a man this yard can be asked about, and this yard put a page in his daughter's mouth in the autumn without asking him and has an arrangement with nothing.** The not-sending and the not-paying are in the second column and not the first, because refusing is not a thing that was done.
14. **THE CHAIN AND THE BAR WERE OFFERED AT THREE DOORS ON THE TWENTIETH AND REFUSED AT THREE, AND A SHILLING WAS OFFERED FOR THE CHAIN AND REFUSED.** A chandler would not take it at nothing and would not take it at four shillings; a boat's owner of about fifty-five asked whose it was, was told it came up out of a cut off the south end on the ninth of April past at forty fathoms and is not that yard's, and said out loud on his own step that **the next man who comes down that street with a thing off a wreck will be able to say that this yard asks, and a cat is not even the next worst thing**; and a man of about sixty-one behind a counter in a shed off the back of that market **offered a shilling for it and was refused, and asked for the reason and was told that a shilling is money, and that the day that thing is a transaction this yard is trading in a thing it does not own and cannot say whose it is, and that a nail is a thing that cannot be a sale.** **What the afternoon cost is not a money figure and has no conversion: about nine people on a front street now know that this yard has nine feet of chain it is trying to get rid of.**
15. **THE OUTER MARKS AND THE BAR WERE LOOKED AT FROM A BOAT ON THE TWENTY-FIRST, AND THE FINDING IS CHECKABLE AND IT IS THAT NOTHING HAS CHANGED.** The outer marks are two baulks of green timber a fathom and a half long and about fourteen inches square with a ring of stone and a can of sheet iron on a stake, in about six feet at low water, a mile and a quarter off the head of that mole on the north-west line; three bearings agree with a chart of about thirty years standing in a boat's locker to within a cable's length. **THE BAR OF FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF THE OUTER MARKS IS NOT A FENCE AND THERE IS NO POST IN IT: it is a line of about a mile and a half running north-north-west about four hundred yards beyond the outer marks, on which the water darkens and stands up in a low sea, and any man in a boat can see it and any man on a mole cannot, and the man of fifty-one of the second lay says it has been there all day on both sides of a spring tide and that you do not want to be on the inside of it in a bad blow off a south-west.** **NO PERSON, NO BOAT AND NO LEAD OF THAT YARD WAS INSIDE THAT BAR ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, THE BAR WAS NOT NARROWED BY ANYTHING, THIS PARTY DID NOT ASK TO HAVE IT NARROWED IN ADVANCE OR IN A BOAT, AND THE PRICE WAS NAMED ON THE TUESDAY EVENING AND NOT ON THE WEDNESDAY MORNING.** **The ground of the twentieth's three doors is the front street of that harbor and of the twenty-first's boat day is off the south end and round the corner, and both are where the earlier batches said the ground was.**
16. **THE WAGE, THE ROTARY FIGURES AND THE DAY-COUNTERS ARE CARRIED IN § 1 ABOVE AND ARE NOT TO BE RE-DERIVED.**
17. **THE BOY OF TWENTY-TWO WAS NOT ON THE STONE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND CAME DOWN ON NONE OF THEM, WAS PUT ON NOTHING, WAS NOT ASKED ONE WORD ABOUT THE OMISSIONS HE HAS ENTERED, AND THE THIRD COLUMN IS UNFILLED AND UNAPPOINTED WITH HIS HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT AND THE FOUR LINES ABOVE HIS NAMED LINE STILL FOUR, STILL NAMELESS AND NOT STRUCK OUT.** **He is not on a page of this batch in any other way, and no name of his is in any column of that book and none has ever been.**
18. **THE FAR BENCH, ALDEN MARR, TOBIAS WREN, ORS KEST, THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY, AMOS SEARLE, GARROW FISK, HESK OTTRIM, CORVIN SARN AND THE BELLWRIGHT'S CHEST ARE ALL EXACTLY WHERE BATCH 0002 LEFT THEM, AND NOBODY WAS ASKED ANYTHING OF ANY OF THEM.** **Tobias Wren is not on a page in this batch and was not sent for, and nothing in these ten days made him a teacher and nothing made him a door.** **Garrow Fisk was away at Ashtide from the eleventh to the fifteenth and is not on a page in this batch.** **The man of about thirty-one of the third lay was not asked anything in these ten days and asked nothing, and is on the page twice, and on both of those occasions only to say that he is not going to be found, and the second column says why.**
