The inherited list of unpaid wage weeks is not carried forward in this batch as a list; the batch advances it by one figure, from twenty-nine to thirty, and that is the whole of the carriage.** See `outline/volume-07.md` lock L1a.

### 2. The money, and it closes in one line

2.1 **THE BAG WAS TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE PENCE, BEING ONE MARK, EIGHTEEN SHILLINGS AND FIVEPENCE, ON FRIDAY THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY. IT IS NINETY-TWO PENCE, BEING SEVEN SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, AT THE CLOSE OF MONDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH. A MARK IS A HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE AND A SHILLING IS TWELVE.**

2.2 **THE WHOLE OF WHAT CAME INTO THAT YARD IN THE TEN DAYS IS NOTHING. THE WHOLE OF WHAT WENT OUT IS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE FOR A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS WITH A MAN IN HER FOR A DAY AND ONE PENNY OF LINE, BOTH ON WEDNESDAY THE NINETEENTH.** **261 − 169 = 92, and 261 − 169 is the whole of it: NOT ONE PENNY LEFT THAT BAG ON ANY OTHER DAY OF THE TEN. **AS FIRST WRITTEN `chapter-0305.md` ALSO PAID THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF THE SECOND LAY THREE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, BEING FORTY-TWO PENCE, OUT OF THE SAME BAG, WHICH PUTS THE CLOSE AT FIFTY PENCE AND BREAKS LOCK L7; THAT PAYMENT IS WITHDRAWN AND THE MAN CAME OUT IN THE HIRE AND COST THAT BAG NOTHING BEYOND THE HIRE. The figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks was three hundred and seventy-nine pence, being two marks, four shillings and eleven pence, and is now five hundred and forty-eight pence, being three marks, five shillings and eightpence.** Nothing else moves in the batch and no later figure may be moved without saying why on the page. This is `outline/volume-07.md` lock L7 and the chapters obey it.

2.3 **THE WAGE COLUMN STANDS AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS AND TWENTY ENVELOPES ON A BENCH AND DID NOT MOVE ON THE ONE WAGE TUESDAY IN THE TEN DAYS, AND THIRTY WEEKS HAVE FALLEN DUE.** The thirty-first week falls due on Tuesday the twenty-fifth of May and the column will not move on it, and the next writer takes the figure from that sentence and not from an almanac.

2.4a **EVERY COUNTED FIGURE IN THIS BATCH NOW COUNTS. **THE CHANDLER'S ANSWER IS *I sell candles and rope, not other men's water* — NINE WORDS — AND THE TENDER'S ANSWER TO THE BOAT'S MAN IS *Then you'll want it again from who wrote it* — NINE WORDS. As first written they were sixteen and fourteen. The eighth clause's courtesy, *nothing in this notice is a judgment upon any vessel or any master*, is **THIRTEEN** WORDS and not eight. The boy's message, *Two of us need a berth or a stove*, is **NINE** words and not six, and the man of about thirty-four of the first lay named **FOUR** of the notice's lines he could not read, being four, five, seven and the last half of two. **THE SLATE IN CHAPTER 306 IS HEADED *FEBRUARY. THE NINETEENTH.* and every one of its nine figures is written in pence first, per lock L5: three hundred and seventy-eight, fifty-seven, fifteen, thirty, twenty-three, fourteen, one hundred and eight, sixty-four, fourteen.**

2.4 **THE HIRE RATES ARE CANON AND WERE NOT RE-PRICED.** A boat with a man in her for a day, one mark and eightpence, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence. A penny of line. A sailor's day, four marks. A slip, three shillings a week. A candle, fourpence. A sack of flour at a chandler's or a baker's, four shillings and ninepence in February. A barrel of lamp oil, thirty-one shillings and sixpence in February. A small bottle of physic, one shilling and twopence in February. A sheet of paper, one penny, and forty sheets one shilling, and that last figure has not moved in nine years. A man's hand split and working is not a figure and is not on any list. **A FIGURE RIGHT AND IN THE WRONG PLACE IS A LIE, and every market figure in this batch is a figure the yard did not set and is entered as what it is.**

### 3. The four-column leaf, and its four columns at the close of Chapter 310

3.0a **A FIGURE A LATER WRITER MUST NOT RE-DERIVE BY COUNTING PARAGRAPHS. The second column's figure of one hundred and forty-three is the ledger's own and is not a count of paragraphs: Chapter 310's second column is two paragraphs and its own ledger says *four this afternoon*. THE REPAIRS OF 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 ADDED ONE SECOND-COLUMN LINE TO CHAPTER 303, being the line distinguishing the clerk of the harbor authority from the clerk of the circuit office, and left the ledger's figures of 139 at the read-back and 143 at the close where they were, because they are not paragraph counts and no other definition of the word line is stated on any page of this batch. A later writer who counts lines MUST SAY ON THE FACE OF THEIR OWN LEDGER WHICH DEFINITION THEY COUNTED, and the same applies to the first column's forty-three and the fourth column's thirty-five, which ARE paragraph counts and ARE checkable.**

3.1 **THE LEAF RULED ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MARCH PAST HOLDS, AT THE CLOSE OF MONDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF MAY: FORTY-THREE ENTRIES IN THE FIRST COLUMN, being thirty-three on the fourteenth of May, nine from the fifteenth to the twenty-third, one for every day and not one day in two of them, and one this evening; ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE LINES IN THE SECOND, being one hundred and fifteen, twenty-four, and four this afternoon; NONE IN THE THIRD; AND THIRTY-FIVE IN THE FOURTH, being twenty-five on the fourteenth of May, nine from the fifteenth to the twenty-third, and one this evening, which is the last thing in that book.** The read-back figures are forty-two, one hundred and thirty-nine, none, and thirty-four, and the read-back was at about four in the afternoon with three people in that shed.

3.2 **THE THIRD COLUMN HAS NOT BEEN FILLED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NOBODY HAS BEEN APPOINTED TO IT. The hand of a boy of twenty-two is at the head of it. A name sits beside that hand and is neither the boy's nor the holder's and WAS SAID OUT LOUD ONCE ON THE THIRTEENTH OF MAY IN A BOAT AND IS NOT SAID AGAIN IN THIS BATCH AND IS NOT TO BE SAID AGAIN IN VOLUME 07. The four lines above his named line are four and nameless and are not struck out and are in about sixty boats on that coast. He was not on the stone on any of the ten days and was put on nothing and no name of his is in any column of that book and none has ever been.** See `outline/volume-07.md` locks L6 and L27.

3.3 **THE FOURTH COLUMN TOOK ONE LINE A DAY FOR NINE DAYS AND THE TENTH LINE GOES IN THIS CHAPTER, and the tenth line is about eleven people on this coast who cannot read a notice on a market wall.** The fourth column is a page no man can check and this yard knows it and has entered that it knows, and the line about a figure that is not proof and not a stage is now the fourth day running on a mark that fouls faster in some months than in others, and no chapter has said why and no chapter is going to.

### 4. The money and the standing positions that did not move

4.1 **NOTHING IN A TIN IN THAT SHED SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL PAST. Three marks to a man of Ashtide for the eighth of August, unmoved, and nobody was sent for him. Seven pence to that yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May past, unargued, the chest not opened, the bellwright not asked on any of the ten days and no digit of anything he said is printed. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid and not reduced by a crate. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots of the eighth of June standing. Nine feet of chain on a nail in that shed wall and a bar of square iron in the drawer, neither sold nor given away, and nobody has asked whose either is.** No item of that list was paid, advanced, reduced or improved in these ten days and no later chapter may say one of them was.

4.2 **THE TWO OBJECTS OF NOBODY'S ARE ABOUT THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-SEVEN DAYS UP THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE, ABOUT NINE FEET APART, UNDER TWO TARPAULINS, ONE WITH A CORNER OFF IT SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF JUNE PAST AND NOT LASHED BACK, AND NEITHER HAS MOVED. THE BENCH UNDER THAT PUMP IS BARE FOR THE HUNDRED AND THIRTEENTH NIGHT.** **They were looked at on the nineteenth of May by TWO people — the holder of that writ and the man of about thirty-four of the second lay — after that boat came in under the steps, standing on the crown itself in a flat calm with the water nowhere near the stone, and they were not touched and were not measured.** As first written they were four people standing in about four inches of water on the crown of that mole on the same afternoon three men had sounded to thirty-one feet off the south end, which is a fourth-person error and a tide that cannot happen in one afternoon.

4.3 **THE PLATE IN ELEVEN FEET IN THE MOLE'S OWN FOUNDATION STONE IS CARRIED OPEN FOR A FOURTH VOLUME.** It was not reached, not measured, not touched, not asked about on any of the ten days, and the note against it stands open, and the mechanism by which it is ever reached is a change of politics in an office and not a better letter out of a shed, and that sentence is on the page in Volume 05 and has not been improved on.

4.4 **THE CASE OF FIVE BELLS IS NOT RAISED. The four people of that coast, four days down it, who go into deep water without a book, were not asked anything on any of the ten days, the complaint was not raised, and the limit four of them wrote and signed stands, and the holder did not ask them to take it off once in ten days. The lead plug, the chest, and the undertaking of the second of July are not touched.**

4.5 **THE DELAYED NOTE STANDS AT ELEVEN LOGGED OCCASIONS AND TWO OF THEM WITH NO CALL IN THEM AND NOTHING WAS MEASURED AND NO OCCASION WAS ENTERED AND THE ANSWER INSIDE IT IS NOT APPROACHED.** The chandler's note is at thirty-one, not re-written, its three counts of weeks at twenty-two, thirteen and eleven, and was not said out loud a fifth time. The notice of the thirty-first of October stands with its four clauses and no tenth acknowledgement was asked for. Four returns stand and there is no fifth and no finding of worked glass was made in these ten days. The chain of custody is a practice and not an office, was made on the sixth of March past, and is not aged by this batch.

4.6 **THE MANIFEST IS THE PUBLIC MANIFEST OF THE *ASTER GANNET* AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH PROVES, SUGGESTS BY ACCUMULATION, OR NAMES WHO ALTERED IT, AT WHOSE INSTANCE, OR WITH WHAT INTENT. THE COMPARTMENT IS STILL NOT NAMED AND THE THREE GANNET DOCUMENTS ARE STILL THREE. THE ITEM IS NOT A FOURTH ITEM. No chapter of this batch uses even the discrepancy.**

### 5. The notice of the seventeenth of May, which is the volume's instrument and is a new canon object

5.1 **THE NOTICE IS EIGHT CLAUSES, IS POSTED ON THE OUTSIDE OF WHATEVER IS ON THE MARKET WALL OF MORROW QUAY AT ABOUT A QUARTER PAST NINE ON MONDAY THE SEVENTEENTH, ON A STRETCH OF THAT WALL WHICH HAD BEEN TAKEN DOWN AT ABOUT FOUR THE PREVIOUS AFTERNOON AND WAS THE YARD'S OWN FOURTH RETURN, SO THAT THE WALL WAS BARE AT EIGHT, AND IS SIGNED WITH A NAME AND A RANK AND NO TITLE.** Its clauses: **1.** no vessel shall leave the port or pass the line described in clause five without a master's declaration in the form of the second schedule, made in writing before two witnesses, and lodged with the harbor authority at Morrow Quay before noon. **2.** the declaration shall state the vessel and her master, her cargo in general terms, and whether she carries material which is the subject of an unsettled claim. **3.** a master who declares truly is not detained and his vessel is not held. **4.** a master who does not carry a declaration may be detained and his vessel held to the outer marks. **5.** the line runs from the mole-head of Morrow Quay to a can upon a stake at the outer marks and thence to the point named in the first schedule. **6.** this notice is not a closure of the port and vessels may enter without a declaration. **7.** it continues until a notice says that it does not. **8.** nothing in it is a judgment upon any vessel or any master and no master is accused of anything by it.

5.2 **THE NAME ON THE EIGHTH LINE IS *SOREN VEY*, CLOSED-SEA SQUADRON, AND IT IS A NAME AND A RANK ON A LINE AND HE IS IN NO ROOM, ON NO MOLE, IN NO MARKET AND NOT IN THIS HARBOR IN THIS BATCH.** He is the antagonist of Volumes 7 to 9 in `outline/series.md` and is fifty-two in `bible/characters.md`, and **no later chapter may put him in a room before Volume 07 is written further, and no Volume 07 chapter in Movement 1 may make a face of the squadron an officer: the three people of that kind in this batch are a man in a blue coat of about fifty with a book at a slip, on a tender, and in a shop, and a man on a tender with a form, and neither is named and neither is a rank.** His argument is not made false on any page of this batch and no chapter of this volume may say it is a lie or that it is obviously right.

5.3 **THE CATCH, AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S SECOND TURN AND IT IS FOUND BY A PERSON AND NOT BY AN OFFICE: THE NOTICE REQUIRES A FORM TO BE LODGED WITH THE HARBOR AUTHORITY AT MORROW QUAY, AND THAT AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH WITH NOTHING ISSUED, ITS CLERK IS A REAL CLERK OF ABOUT SIXTY WHO HAS BEEN ONE FOR TWENTY-TWO YEARS, DID NOT GIVE HIS NAME ON THE SEVENTEENTH AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR IT, IS OWED HIS OWN QUARTER AND HAS BEEN FOR TWO MONTHS, HAS NO BOOK INTO WHICH A PAPER CAN BE PUT AND HAS HAD NO POWER TO RECEIVE ANYTHING SINCE THE FIRST OF APRIL, AND SAID THE WORDS *I DO NOT KNOW* OUT LOUD IN A ROOM WITH ONE MAN IN IT ON THE MONDAY AND THE TUESDAY. THE FORM ITSELF IS AT A DESK IN TERNWATCH AND IS PROPERLY MADE AND TWO WITNESSES SIGNED IT. **HE IS UNNAMED AND HE STAYS UNNAMED, AND HE IS NOT AMBROSE SELL: Sell is the clerk of the CIRCUIT office, a different man in a different building, and locks L15 of Volumes 03 to 06 read that Ambrose Sell AND the harbor authority's clerk are the mouths of clauses. THE TWO ARE NOT ONE MAN AND MAY NOT BE MADE ONE.**

5.4 **NO PERSON IN THAT YARD SAID OUT LOUD THAT THE SAID NOTICE WAS DRAFTED IN ORDER THAT IT COULD NOT BE COMPLIED WITH, AND THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE OF THE SAYING IS THE REASON OF THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF APRIL PAST, being that a person who says *they did it on purpose* has stopped being the party that says what a thing is not, and there is no evidence either way and there may never be any and this yard has entered that it does not know. THE SAME HOLD IS PLACED ON THE INVERSE: the holder of that writ said out loud in a market in about forty people's hearing on the twenty-fourth of May that he is not going to say anybody wrote the two true sentences four lines apart on purpose, and is not going to say nobody did, and that he has been getting that wrong in his own head for seven days.** Both halves stand and neither is a concession.

5.5 **THE FIRST VESSEL OUT OF MORROW QUAY AFTER THE NOTICE WAS A COASTER OF ABOUT SEVENTY TONS WITH A MASTER OF FIFTY AND TWO MEN, WHICH WENT OUT AT ABOUT ELEVEN ON TUESDAY THE EIGHTEENTH WITH NO DECLARATION, WAS NOT ASKED FOR ONE, NOT STOPPED, NOT SPOKEN TO AND NOT FOLLOWED, LAY OFF THE SOUTH END OF THAT MOLE UNTIL ABOUT THREE IN THE AFTERNOON, AND CAME BACK IN AT ABOUT SIX AND TOOK HER BERTH.** Nobody in that harbor knows what happened to her outside that line and nobody went out to see, and both of those are entered.

5.6 **THE NOTICE WAS NOT TAKEN DOWN BY ANYBODY IN THIS HARBOR AND THE TWO NAVAL NOTICES THAT WERE ON THAT WALL BEFORE IT, OF THE SECOND OF DECEMBER PAST AND THE TWENTY-SECOND OF JUNE PAST, WERE NEITHER TAKEN DOWN BY THIS YARD NOR BY ANYBODY ELSE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. THE CLERK DID NOT MENTION THE PUTTING UP OF IT AND KEPT HIS OWN PAGE.** **AND THE THREE PAPERS ARE NOT STACKED. The wall held three things before the eighth: the yard's own fourth return, on the stretch that came off at four the previous afternoon, and two naval notices FURTHER ALONG THE SAME WALL AND NOT ON THE SAME SQUARE OF IT. The notice of the seventeenth did not go over the top of anything and is not under the other two. No Volume 07 chapter may put this yard's own figures, its fourth column, or any part of the volume's method on that wall.**

### 6. The can upon a stake, and the chart that does not carry it

6.1 **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY, OF A COASTER OUT OF ASHTIDE, SAID OUT LOUD IN A FISH MARKET IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING ON SUNDAY THE TWENTY-THIRD OF MAY THAT THE CAN UPON A STAKE AT THE OUTER MARKS IS NOT UPON A CROWN CHART OF ABOUT NINE YEARS STANDING THAT HE CARRIES, NOT ON THE OUTER MARKS, NOT ON THE MOLE-HEAD APPROACH, AND NOT IN THE APPROACHES TABLE AT THE BACK; THAT IT WAS THERE IN THE LAST WEEK OF MARCH PAST; AND THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO SAY WHERE HE GOT THE CHART AND NOBODY IN THAT MARKET IS GOING TO ASK HIM.**

6.2 **THE CHART WAS NOT OPENED IN THAT MARKET AND WAS NOT SHOWN TO ANY PERSON AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR BY ANY PERSON, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT STOOD IN THAT MARKET FOR ABOUT FOUR MINUTES AND ASKED HIM NO QUESTION, AND SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE USED THE FOUR MINUTES ON THE NOT-ASKING AND THAT THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IN ONE MONTH HE HAS WRITTEN THE PRICE OF IT DOWN AFTERWARDS INSTEAD OF BEFORE AND THAT BOTH OF THEM WERE THE SAME MISTAKE.**

6.3 **THIS IS A FACT WITH A REASON AND IT IS NOT A ROUTE, AND IT IS NOT THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT, WHICH IS THE BRAMBLE STRAIT STORM ROUTE AND WHICH THIS BATCH DOES NOT TOUCH. No Volume 07 chapter may call the can a route, may put it on a chart, may follow it, and may say what it is for.** The man is a person of no office, was refused a question by this yard in the middle of March past, has asked nothing since, **is not a witness, has not been made one, and may not be cited in a room in this volume or any other.**

### 7. The copyist's counter, and the leak, and the two hundred and eleven

7.1 **THE COUNTER IS IN A ROOM OFF THE FISH MARKET OF THIS HARBOR, A SHEET IS A PENNY AND FORTY SHEETS ARE A SHILLING, AND IT IS THE ONLY OFFICE IN THIS BOOK THAT WILL TAKE ANYBODY'S MONEY FOR A COPY OF ANYTHING WITHOUT ASKING WHAT IT IS FOR. A COPYIST OF ABOUT FIFTY-NINE HAS BEEN IN THAT ROOM FOR TWENTY-TWO YEARS.**

7.2 **THE TWO HUNDRED AND ELEVEN ARE OF ONE NINE-LINE SHEET ABOUT A CHAMBER OF A DROWNED CITY AND NOT OF THE NAVAL NOTICE, AND THE TWO SHEETS ARE NOT ONE SHEET.** The naval notice was issued on Monday the seventeenth of May; there cannot have been two hundred and eleven copies of it by the twenty-second, and the first draft of the chapter said there were, and also gave the copyist's reason for not stopping as *eight clauses went on a wall on Monday*. **SHE STATED OUT LOUD, IN A ROOM WITH TWO PEOPLE IN IT, ON SATURDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND OF MAY, THAT SHE HAS MADE TWO HUNDRED AND ELEVEN COPIES OF ONE NINE-LINE SHEET ABOUT A CHAMBER IN A DROWNED CITY SINCE THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF APRIL PAST, said out loud that not one word of the eight clauses she had just been paid to copy is in it, and gave the reason for not stopping as a copyist who stops copying is a copyist who has admitted she copied something, and that a trade can be put in a schedule and a confession cannot, and that the difference between those two is her living and her name.** The nine lines are the nine lines of the copy of a copy of a municipal sheet of a chamber of a drowned city that this yard bought for a penny on the twenty-seventh of April past, **being a third of the SEVEN pieces of paper in that yard's drawer and not of six, per Chapter 310's closing inventory.** **THE NAVAL NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH IS A SECOND SHEET AND HAS BEEN COPIED FOUR TIMES SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH, OF WHICH THIS ONE IS THE FOURTH; THE FIRST THREE WERE NOT MADE BY THIS YARD AND THIS YARD HAS NOT ASKED WHO MADE THEM. THIS YARD IS NOW THE ONLY PARTY IN THIS HARBOR THAT HAS BOUGHT ONE OF EACH FROM THE SAME COUNTER, AND THAT IS ENTERED AS A FACT ABOUT THIS YARD AND NOT AS WHAT CAUSED ANYTHING.**

7.3 **SHE KEEPS A RULED BOOK OF WHAT SHE HAS COPIED IN HER OWN HAND AND SAID OUT LOUD WHY, being that a copyist who does not keep a book of what she copied is a copyist who cannot be asked anything, and that this is not a defensive act and is the oldest caution in her trade. THE BOOK WAS NOT OPENED ON THE COUNTER AND WAS NOT HANDED OVER AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR BY ANY PERSON, AND THIS YARD DID NOT ASK TO SEE IT AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK TO SEE IT.** The figure is in that yard's second column **as a figure said out loud by a person and not as a page**, and that distinction is the reason and is on the page.

7.4 **SHE NAMED FOUR BUYERS AND SAID THEY ARE ALL FOUR AND THAT THERE ARE TWO HUNDRED AND SEVEN MORE. The first is a yard: the twenty-seventh of April past at about half past two in the afternoon, a man of about thirty-two with split hands who did not sit down and was in a hurry, on better paper than the rest, who paid for one and did not ask for a second, and whom nobody has asked her about. The second is a man who pays cash, takes his own paper away, and is a stranger, of whom she has not had him twice. The third is a woman who came in on the ninth of May past and bought nine at a penny each, carried them out in a cloth against her chest with both arms, and did not look at one of them in that room, and had not one folded and had not one creased, and about whom the said copyist has thought for a fortnight and does not know what a person does with nine.**

7.5 **THE THIRD BUYER WAS NOT FOLLOWED, WAS NOT WRITTEN AGAINST, AND WILL NOT BE FOLLOWED BY ANY CHAPTER OF THIS YARD'S LIFE, AND THE REASON IS ON THE PAGE, being that following it would make this yard the party that looks, and that a woman with a cloth is a drawer that has not been given a number yet. THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT SAID OUT LOUD ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF MAY, IN THE READ-BACK, THAT HE WANTED TO PUT THE WOMAN WITH THE CLOTH IN FRONT OF A PERSON WITH A PEN, AND DID NOT, AND IS NOT GOING TO, AND THAT THE ONLY REASON HE WOULD BE ABLE TO DO IT IS THAT HE IS GOOD AT FINDING THINGS OUT, AND THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO BE THE OTHER THING AS WELL.** No later chapter may pay that off, resolve it, identify the woman, or make it a clue.

7.6 **A COPY OF THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH WAS MADE AT THAT COUNTER AT A PENNY, AND THE PENNY WAS THE SHIP'S OWN AND DID NOT GO OUT OF THAT YARD'S BOOK, and she said so out loud when the copyist asked, and the copyist said it was the first time in twenty-two years anybody had told her which pocket a penny came out of.** No further money left that yard's book after the nineteenth of May.

### 8. The standing cost of the batch, and it is the yard's, and it is nobody else's

8.1 **THIS BATCH'S FIRST STANDING COST IS THE YARD'S OWN, AND IT IS UNUSUAL, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE MOVEMENT: A PARTY THAT HAS SPENT SIX VOLUMES REFUSING TO BE FINDABLE HAS BEEN MADE FINDABLE IN TEN DAYS BY A SHEET IT PRINTED IN ITS FIRST YEAR WITH A PLACE FOR EVERY COPY OF ITSELF ON THE FACE OF IT, AND BY A COMMUNITY THAT PUT THAT SHEET ON A MARKET WALL IN A TOWN FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST ON THE FOURTH OF APRIL PAST, WHICH THIS YARD DID NOT PUT THERE AND HAS NOT WRITTEN TO AND IS NOT GOING TO WRITE TO.**

8.2 **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF A SCREW-STEAM PACKET OUT OF BRAMBLE STRAIT CAME ASHORE IN A DINGHY AT ABOUT FIVE ON MONDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH, DID NOT GO UP THE HILL, STOOD ON THE STONE AT THE TOP OF THE MOLE STEPS, AND READ OUT LOUD IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING THE LINE OFF A SHEET FOLDED IN FOUR, being: *a page in a shed on the mole at Morrow Quay, in a drawer, fourth of five*. HE SAID HE HAD BEEN FOUR DAYS ON THE WATER TO READ IT OFF A WALL; THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO SAY WHO HE WORKS FOR; THAT HE DOES NOT WORK FOR ANYBODY; THAT THE MARKET FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST WOULD NOT TAKE THE SHEET DOWN; THAT HE CAME TO SAY IT OUT LOUD IN FRONT OF PEOPLE RATHER THAN HAVE IT FOUND QUIETLY; AND, WITHOUT BEING ASKED, THAT THE LINE IS ON THAT WALL AND IN A DRAWER IN THIS SHED AND ON ABOUT SIXTY BOATS, AND THAT IT IS ON THOSE BOATS BECAUSE A YARD PRINTED IT, IN ITS FIRST YEAR, WITH A PLACE FOR EVERY COPY OF ITSELF ON THE FACE OF IT, AND THAT HE HAS NOT GOT ANYTHING AGAINST THAT.** He went down the steps at about a quarter to six and went off on the tide at about seven and was not thanked and is not on the page.

8.3 **HE IS NOT AN OFFICER, NOT A SERVANT, NOT A CROWN MAN, NOT A COURIER, NOT A WITNESS AND NOT A FACE OF AN INSTITUTION, AND NO LATER CHAPTER MAY MAKE HIM ONE. NO PERSON OF THAT YARD SENT FOR HIM, KNEW HE WAS COMING, ASKED HIM ONE QUESTION, WROTE TO HIM, SENT ANYBODY OR THANKED HIM.**

8.4 **THE YARD'S RESPONSE, GIVEN OUT LOUD ON THE STEPS AND ENTERED IN THE SECOND COLUMN: the standing reason of the ninth of April past, being that this yard has one address in this country and is not going to make a second, and that it has kept nine people off that hill since the first of May, and that it has not been improved on in three weeks and is not going to be improved on for this man.** And the same reason was held a second time in sixteen days, on the twentieth of May, about the woman of about fifty-eight with a drawer under her bed, **and the second time the reason was given as WORSE than the first and not better, being that in April the yard did not know her and on the twentieth of May the yard knows she is frightened, and both times it cost somebody else and not this yard. A RULE WHICH IS NEVER WRONG IS NOT A RULE, and that sentence is in the fourth column and is not improved on.** The woman of about fifty-eight has not been written to and may not be.

8.5 **A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY OF THE FIRST LAY, FORTY-ONE YEARS ON THAT WATER, WHO ASKED A QUESTION IN A MARKET IN THIS HARBOR ON THE SECOND OF DECEMBER PAST AND AGAIN ON THE ELEVENTH OF MARCH PAST AND WAS ANSWERED NEITHER TIME, NAMED THREE HONEST TARGETS FOR A COMING ANGER IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING IN A CHANDLER'S ON FRIDAY THE TWENTY-FIRST OF MAY, BEING A MAN WITH A BOOK, A CHANDLER, AND THE HARBOR AUTHORITY OF THIS HARBOR, AND SAID ALL THREE ARE WRONG — AND THEN STOPPED ON PURPOSE, AND SAID WHY OUT LOUD, being that a sentence said in a chandler's on a Friday morning is in eleven markets by Sunday and comes back with a man's name on it that the man did not put there, and that he had watched that happen to a man on this coast twice and once it was fair and once it was murder and he could not tell afterwards which was which. HE TOOK TWO CANDLES AT FOURPENCE AND WENT DOWN TO THE WATER AND SAID HE WOULD COME BACK INTO THAT SHOP ON MONDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH.** He was asked for a name and had not got one and is not going to go and look for one, and said he has asked this harbor two questions already and that the correct number of times to ask a question is three and not four and is not spending the third one in a fortnight.

8.5a **THE VOLUME'S GOVERNING SENTENCE IS NOT PAID IN MOVEMENT 1 AND IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT STATE OF THE MANUSCRIPT.** Neither half of it is said: not *a restriction that comes in a sentence and not in a boat is a thing a man cannot be angry at, and a man who cannot be angry at it will be angry at something else by Friday*, and not the captain. `outline/volume-07.md` § *Escalation sequence* MOVEMENT 2 places both, and the first draft of Chapter 307 spent them; **they are withdrawn from Chapter 307 and restored to Movement 2, and the three honest targets and *all three are wrong* stand in Chapter 307 because they are the pressure and not the sentence.** **CONSEQUENCE FOR CHAPTER 311 ONWARD: THE VOLUME'S NEW-VOLUME QUESTION HAS NOT BEEN ASKED. CHAPTER 319 PRINTED FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT AGAINST THE NINETEENTH OF MAY IN TWO PLACES, ITS APPARATUS AND ITS CLOSING PARAGRAPH, AND BOTH WERE CORRECTED ON 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 AGAINST `logs/batch-0002.review.log` ITEM 1; THE ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE IS ALSO GIVEN AT `chapters/volume-07/chapter-0305.md` LINE 7 AND THE NINETY-TWO PENCE LEFT IN THE BAG AFTER IT IS GIVEN AT LINES 61 AND 107 OF THAT CHAPTER, AND TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE IN THE BAG BEFORE IT AT `chapters/volume-06/chapter-0300.md` LINE 89, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE FIGURE CHECKABLE TWICE OVER.** Note for any later writer on that chapter: `chapter-0305.md` line 61 spells the same outgoings as *one mark, eight shillings and a penny*, being two hundred and fifty-seven, where the figure is one hundred and sixty-nine, being *one mark and eightpence and a penny of line*; the narration, the apparatus and the closing paragraph of that chapter all carry the right figure and one line does not, and the line was NOT EDITED BY THIS PASS because that chapter belongs to Batch 0001 and is out of this phase's scope. **IT IS FLAGGED HERE SO THAT IT IS NOT INHERITED AS CANON AND IS REPAIRED BY THE PHASE THAT OWNS IT, NOT BY A LATER ONE.**

### 4. The declarations, the fourth line, and the notice, which did not move

4.1 **THE FOURTH LINE OF A MASTER'S DECLARATION IS, IN THE WORDS OF THE FORM, *whether she carries material which is the subject of an unsettled claim*, AND A MASTER OF ABOUT FIFTY OF THE SECOND LAY READ IT OUT OF HIS OWN FORM TWICE IN A FISH MARKET ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF MAY AND SAID OUT LOUD, IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, *a yes is a handing over and a no is a lie*, AND GAVE TWO REASONS, AND SAID HE WAS GOING OUT ON THE FRIDAY WITH THE BOX EMPTY AND THAT THAT IS THE ABSENCE OF A PLAN AND NOT A PLAN. HIS BOAT OF ABOUT SEVENTY TONS WENT OUT AND CAME BACK ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF MAY WITH NOTHING HAPPENING AND HE SAID ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH THAT A TUESDAY ON WHICH NOTHING HAPPENS IS A TUESDAY AND DOES NOT GO ROUND AGAIN.**

4.2 **NO PERSON OF THAT YARD DRAFTED, COPYED, WITNESSED, COUNTERSIGNED OR ADVISED ON ANY DECLARATION FOR ANY VESSEL ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, AND THE REFUSAL WAS GIVEN OUT LOUD IN A MARKET IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING IN FIVE PARTS, BEING THAT THIS YARD DOES NOT DRAFT AND DOES NOT COPY AND DOES NOT WITNESS AND DOES NOT COUNTERSIGN AND DOES NOT ADVISE, AND THAT A PARTY WITH NO PAPER IN THIS COUNTRY HAS ONE ADVANTAGE, WHICH IS THAT NOTHING ANYBODY DOES FOR IT IS A PARTY TO ANYTHING, AND THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO GIVE THAT UP FOR A BOX IN A MARKET.**

4.3 **THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY IS EIGHT CLAUSES, IS ON THE MARKET WALL OF THAT HARBOR, AND WAS NOT TOUCHED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT WALL AND NOTHING CAME OFF IT, AND THE TWO OLDER NAVAL NOTICES FURTHER ALONG THE SAME WALL ARE STILL ON IT. THE HEARING ROOM AND THE MARKET WALL WERE NOT IN ANY ONE CHAPTER, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH PUTS ANY PART OF THAT YARD'S OWN METHOD, ITS FIGURES OR ITS FOURTH COLUMN ON THAT WALL IN THAT HARBOR.**

4.4 **THE CLERK OF THAT HARBOR AUTHORITY IS A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY AND TWENTY-TWO YEARS IN THAT OFFICE AND IS UNNAMED. HE DID NOT GIVE HIS NAME ON THE SEVENTEENTH AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR IT, AND NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 07 MAY GIVE IT TO HIM. HE IS NOT AMBROSE SELL, WHO IS THE CLERK OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE, A DIFFERENT MAN IN A DIFFERENT BUILDING WHO HAS NOT BEEN UP THAT HILL SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF OCTOBER PAST. ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MAY HE WAS USED AGAIN AND THE USE WAS WORSE, AND the four things he said that day are: the same three true things in the same order, that the season of that office ended on the thirty-first of March past with nothing issued, that there is no book of that authority a paper can be put into, and that he has had no power to receive anything since the first of April; a refusal to unsay or improve on the four words he spoke on the eighteenth of May; a fourth thing that is not one of the three, being that he is not going to hold the form put on his table, because in about four years somebody will want to know where that sheet was on the twenty-seventh of May and there is one answer to that; and the fact, said unprompted, that he has been owed a quarter by his own office since the first of April and has not mentioned it to a living soul. HE IS NOT A VILLAIN AND IS NOT A HERO, HE IS A MOUTH OF CLAUSES, HE IS OWED MONEY BY HIS OWN OFFICE, AND *I DO NOT KNOW* IS NOT SAID A SECOND TIME ON ANY PAGE.**

4.5 **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SIX OF THE THIRD LAY, UNNAMED, WENT INTO THAT ROOM AT ABOUT HALF PAST ELEVEN ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MAY WITH A FORM AND WAS REFUSED, AND SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE HAD ELEVEN WEEKS OF A SEASON ON A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS, THAT HE HAD NOT BEEN OUT SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY, THAT HE WAS NOT GOING OUT ON THE FRIDAY, AND THAT THAT IS A DAY, AND SAID IT TO THE ROOM AND NOT TO THE CLERK. HE IS THE MAN WHO NAMES THE CHANDLER ON THE TWENTY-NINTH AND HIRES THE BOAT ON THE THIRTY-FIRST AND GOES OUT ON THE SECOND OF JUNE. HE IS A PERSON OF NO OFFICE, HE IS NOT OF THAT YARD, HE GAVE HIS NAME TO NOBODY, AND HE IS NOT A WITNESS AND HAS NOT BEEN MADE ONE.**

### 5. The two private hires inside the line, and the whole price of them, which is the batch's spine

5.1 **THE FIRST MONEY INTO THAT YARD SINCE THE FIFTH OF MAY PAST CAME IN ON FRIDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF MAY AND IS A PRIVATE HIRE INSIDE THE LINE, ON A PRIVATE PERSON'S ACCOUNT AND FOR A PRIVATE PERSON'S PURPOSE: a boat of about thirty tons with a man in her for a day, at one mark and eightpence, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence, hired at a box on the corner of that mole by a boat's owner of about fifty-five, who has a boat of about thirty tons lying inside that harbor on the west quay on soft ground with a green length of copper under her housing and a slip at three shillings a week, and who wanted his own hook and chain out of about nine feet of mud off that west quay. THE NOTICE GOVERNS LEAVING THE PORT AND PASSING A LINE NAMED IN THE FIFTH CLAUSE AND DOES NOT GOVERN ONE SHACKLE OF CHAIN IN NINE FEET OF MUD INSIDE THAT HARBOR'S OWN WATER. IT WAS NOT SALVAGE, NOT A CLAIM, NOT A CLAIM WINDOW, NOT A CHARTER AND NOT A WAY OF GETTING PAST ANYTHING, AND ALL FIVE OF THOSE THINGS WERE SAID OUT LOUD TO EVERY PERSON IN THAT BOAT BY THE BOAT'S OWNER AND NOT BY THAT YARD, BEFORE THE PAINTER WENT AND NOT AFTER.**

5.2 **THE MAN IN THAT BOAT IS COBB TERRELL, ABOUT FORTY-ONE, OF THAT HARBOR'S OWN SECOND LAY, A HIRED HAND WHO HAS DONE THAT WORK FOR NINETEEN YEARS, AND HE GAVE HIS NAME OUT LOUD IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING AND IT WENT IN. HE IS HEEL, IS NAMED, AND IS THE FIRST PERSON IN THIS HARBOR WHOSE NAME THIS YARD HAS ENTERED AT A HIRER'S INSISTENCE SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY. AT ABOUT HALF PAST THREE IN THE AFTERNOON OF THE SAID FRIDAY A BROKEN STUD ON THE END OF THAT CHAIN CAME THROUGH THE MUD AND TOOK HIM ACROSS THE TOP OF THE LEFT FOOT. HE DID NOT GO IN THE WATER. NOBODY FROM THAT YARD WAS IN THAT BOAT OR ON THE WATER AT ANY HOUR OF THAT DAY. HE WENT TO A BONESETTER ON THE SATURDAY MORNING ON A CRUTCH ON HIS OWN AND PAID NOTHING, AND THE BONESETTER SAID HE IS NOT TO PUT WEIGHT ON THAT FOOT FOR TEN DAYS AND NOT TO BE ON THE WATER FOR FOURTEEN, AND SAID THE FIGURE OUT LOUD TWICE OF HIS OWN ACCORD.**

5.3 **THE SECOND HIRE IS ON MONDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MAY, THE SAME BOAT, THE SAME FIGURE, FROM THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SIX OF THE THIRD LAY, TO SHIFT ABOUT NINE TONS OF SALT OFF A LIGHTER INSIDE THAT HARBOR'S OWN LINE, AND THE MAN IN HER IS ABOUT TWENTY-SIX AND GAVE HIS NAME AND IT WENT IN, AND THE FIVE THINGS WERE SAID TO HIM BY THE HIRER AND NOT BY THAT YARD. NOTHING WAS LANDED FROM OUTSIDE THAT HARBOR AND NOTHING WAS TAKEN OUT OF IT ON EITHER DAY.**

5.4 **THE MOMENT SOMEBODY ASKED A MAN IN A BOAT THAT YARD HAD PAID A QUESTION IS ON THE PAGE, AND IT IS ON THE SUNDAY THE THIRTIETH OF MAY AT THE HEAD OF A SLIP IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, AND THE ASKER IS A MAN IN A BLUE COAT, ABOUT FIFTY, WITH A BOOK, WHO IS NOT AN OFFICER AND HAS NO RANK AND IS NOT NAMED AND IS A WORKING MAN OF A CLOSED-SEA SQUADRON AND NOT A FACE OF ANYTHING. THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT GAVE THE STANDING REASON OUT LOUD BEFORE THE MAN ANSWERED, BEING THE RULE OF THE FIRST OF MAY, THAT A MAN IN A BOAT THAT YARD HAS PAID IS A MAN THAT YARD CAN BE ASKED ABOUT, AND HE GAVE IT TO THE ASKER AND NOT TO THE MAN ASKED. THE ANSWER WAS: *I am not going to tell you what you should have said*. NOBODY IMPROVED ON IT AND NOBODY ARGUED WITH IT. AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT GAVE OUT LOUD ON THAT MOLE, IN NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, THE REASON IT IS SAID A SECOND TIME, BEING THAT A MAN WHO HAS A SENTENCE FOR A THING WHEN IT IS EASY AND A BETTER SENTENCE FOR IT WHEN IT IS NOT HAS A CHOSEN SENTENCE, AND THAT A CHOSEN SENTENCE IS ONE PICKED THAT DAY ABOUT A PERSON HE DOES NOT LIKE BEING ASKED ABOUT, AND THAT THIS IS WHAT THE FIRST OF MAY IS FOR. THE SENTENCE WAS SAID ON THE SIXTEENTH OF MAY PAST TO A BOAT'S MAN OF ABOUT FORTY AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON AND IS NOT GIVEN A THIRD OCCASION WITHOUT THE REASON BEING GIVEN AGAIN ON THE PAGE.**

5.5 **THE THREE THINGS THE MAN IN THE BLUE COAT SAID OUT LOUD ARE ON THE PAGE AND NONE OF THEM IS A THREAT AND NONE IS A LIE. THE CROWN'S POSITION IS NOT MADE FALSE AND IS NOT ANSWERED BY A FACT. HE SAID THAT HE HAS NOT GOT A ROOM WITH MEN IN IT DECIDING THIS AND HAS GOT A NOTICE, A FORM, A DESK AT TERNWATCH, A LINE DRAWN FROM A MOLE-HEAD TO A CAN UPON A STAKE, A MASTER WHO WILL NOT TICK A BOX AND A MAN IN AN OFFICE WHO CANNOT WRITE ANYTHING DOWN, AND THAT HE HAS BEEN GIVEN ONE PAGE AND A BOAT AND HAS USED THEM; THAT HE DOES NOT KNOW WHETHER THAT IS RIGHT AND WOULD LIKE TO GO ON NOT KNOWING; AND THAT A RESTRICTION THAT GETS A MAN'S PAPER INTO A ROOM HE CANNOT REACH IS A BAD INSTRUMENT, WHICH HE DOES NOT SAY IS A FALSE ONE, AND THAT HE HAS BEEN USING IT FOR NINE DAYS AND HAS WATCHED A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS LIE OFF THAT MOLE WITH A STOVE OUT OF HER WHEELHOUSE WHILE IT WAS BAD. ADMIRAL SOREN VEY IS A NAME AND A RANK ON A LINE AND IS IN NO ROOM, ON NO MOLE AND IN NO MARKET.**

5.6 **THE PRICE OF THE FORTNIGHT, SAID OUT LOUD BY THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT IN THAT SHED ON WEDNESDAY THE SECOND OF JUNE AND NOT SOFTENED: a party with no instrument may be hired by a private person for a private purpose; that has been the rule since the first of May and is not a door; the price of it is one mark and eightpence; a yard that has three marks standing to a man of Ashtide since the eighth of August past, and seven pence standing to its own shipwright, and eight marks and a day of a boat standing to that harbor's own bellwright, has gone and been the thing that moves things inside a blockade, and the answer is that it is exactly like the other things and is not going to be made into anything else; and a man in a boat that yard has paid is a man that yard can be asked about, which was true before the money was taken and is exactly as true after a bonesetter and is four hundred and eight pence more expensive.**

### 6. The price that rose, and the two figures and two dates

6.1 **EXACTLY ONE FIGURE OF THE NINE ON THE SLATE AT THE END STALL CHANGED IN THESE TEN DAYS, AND IT WAS A RISE AND NOT A FALL, AND IT WAS QUOTED ON A STATED DAY AND ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN ON THAT DAY.** A sheet dated the twenty-ninth of May past, being a bill of a merchant's agent at Ternwatch and not a quotation, was read out loud at the end stall in the fish market at about ten in the morning of Tuesday the first of June, in about forty people's hearing, by a man of about forty-four of the second lay who said out loud that he had carried it in his coat since the Friday and had not opened it. **A BARREL OF LAMP OIL: THREE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT PENCE IN FEBRUARY, BEING THIRTY-ONE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE; FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE ON THE FIRST OF JUNE, BEING THIRTY-SEVEN SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE. A RISE OF SEVENTY-TWO PENCE, BEING SIX SHILLINGS EXACTLY.** The February figure was left visible above the new one on the same board with both dates against them, and the other eight of the nine figures did not move, and the small bottle of physic at fourteen pence with *none in this harbor* against it did not move, on purpose.

6.2 **THE FIGURE WAS NOT SET IN THAT MARKET AND THE PERSON WHO SET IT HAS NEVER BEEN TO THAT QUAY.** The woman of about fifty-eight with that end stall said out loud that nobody in that harbor put it up, that a man in an office in a city four hundred miles from that harbor wrote it on the twenty-ninth of May past and is not going to come to that quay and does not have to, and that she had said the same thing in that market on the twentieth of May past and was not going to say it better. She said out loud that she has said *I have none* to about two hundred people since the ninth of April past of whom about forty had money, and that from the first of June she can say a figure instead of a sentence, and that she called the loss of the sentence the only thing she had.

6.3 **THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE VOLUME'S OWN AND IT IS PAID HERE: a mole-head light with its lens out since the seventh of May was going to be out in October on the February figure, and a fifth more oil is not a fifth more light.** The holder of that writ said out loud in that shed that he is not going to go up to that stall and say the rise is the notice and is not going to go up and say it is not the notice, and gave the reason as the twenty-fourth of April past, being that a person who says *they did it on purpose* has stopped being the party that says what a thing is not, and that a price is a price and a figure is a figure and he has not got a figure for a market's anger and is not going to invent one so that a shed has something in it. **THE CHEAPEST THING IN THAT HARBOR WENT UP SIX SHILLINGS ON THE FIRST OF JUNE AND IS NOT COMING BACK DOWN.**

### 7. The harbor arranging itself wrongly, and the standing cost, and who paid it

7.1 **THE VOLUME'S GOVERNING SENTENCE WAS PAID ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF MAY, IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING IN A CHANDLER'S, BY A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY OF THE FIRST LAY, WHO SAID IT OUT LOUD, COUNTED IT, AND SAID HE DID IT ON PURPOSE AND NOTICED IN ABOUT THE FOURTH WORD THAT HE WAS DOING THE VERY THING HE HAD WARNED ABOUT ON THE TWENTY-FIRST. The sentence is twenty-one words and the second half of it is unnumbered, and neither is on any page of Batch 0001 and both are now on the page.**

NO CHARACTER NAMED A BODY AND NO CHARACTER PROPOSED ONE. A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHTEEN BEGAN TO SAY, IN NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, THAT THIS HARBOR WANTS SOMEBODY TO SPEAK FOR IT, AND WAS STOPPED BY THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT ABOUT FOUR WORDS FROM FINISHING, IN FRONT OF ALL OF THEM, SO THAT THE UNFINISHED THING WAS ON A MOLE AND NOT IN A DRAWER; AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO TELL THAT MAN WHAT SHOULD COME NEXT AND IS NOT GOING TO REFUSE IT EITHER, AND THAT HE IS GOING TO LEAVE A SPACE ON THAT MOLE WHERE IT WAS GOING TO GO, AND THAT NOT ANSWERING A QUESTION AND REFUSING IT ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE BOTH OF THEM ON THE SAME MORNING. NO CENTRAL BODY, NO COMMITTEE, NO ASSEMBLY, NO FLEET, NO WING AND NO GUARD IS NAMED ON ANY PAGE OF THIS BATCH.** He is asked for a name, has not got one, is not going to go and look for one, and says this is the third thing and the correct number of times to ask a question in a harbor is three and not four.

7.3 **AT LEAST ONE OF THE THREE HONEST TARGETS WAS ACTUALLY HIT, BY SOMEBODY WHO IS NOT OF THAT YARD AND WAS NOT ASKED BY IT, AND IT COST THAT PERSON SOMETHING A READER CAN COUNT. THE TARGET IS A CHANDLER, AND THE PERSON IS THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SIX OF THE THIRD LAY, AND THE COST IS FOURPENCE A CANDLE AT THAT COUNTER AND ABOUT SIXTY OF THEM BEFORE THE END OF JUNE, WHICH IS FOUR SHILLINGS.** A sentence of fifteen words, being *the chandler of the front street put a sentence into this harbor on Tuesday morning*, was said in a fish market in about nine people's hearing on the twenty-ninth of May, and the man's wife counted it out loud at fifteen words at her own counter the next morning and said that the first four of them are her trade and that she did not put them there. **THE YARD SENT NOBODY, ASKED NOBODY, TOLD NOBODY, BOUGHT NO CANDLE, AND SAID OUT LOAD THAT IT IS NOT GOING TO WRITE FOUR SHILLINGS AGAINST A MAN'S ANGER BECAUSE FOUR SHILLINGS IS THE PRICE OF CANDLES AND THE THING THAT HAPPENED IS NOT THE CANDLES.** A man of about fifty-one with a stove on an afterdeck stood at that counter for a quarter of an hour on the twenty-eighth and bought no candle at fourpence, and the chandler did not ask him what he had.

7.4 **THE OTHER TWO HONEST TARGETS WERE APPROACHED AND ONE OF THEM WAS USED. THE HARBOR AUTHORITY WAS USED AGAIN ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MAY AND THE USE WAS WORSE, AND A MAN LOST A DAY. THE MAN WITH A BOOK, BEING A MAN IN A BLUE COAT, CAME UP THAT MOLE ON THE THIRTIETH, WAS NOT AN OFFICER, ASKED ONE QUESTION AND WAS ANSWERED ONCE, AND WENT OFF IN A DINGHY.**

7.5 **THE OTHER STANDING COST OF THE BATCH, WHICH IS THIS YARD'S OWN AND NOT SOFTENED: two hundred and sixty pence came in and four hundred and eight pence went out, so that a bag which held ninety-two pence on the twenty-fourth of May holds twenty pence on the third of June, and a man of about forty-one is off the water for fourteen days, and a man of about thirty-six buys no candles, and a man of about thirty-six is not trusted with anything in a market, and a man of about thirty-four who was told the price of a boat on a quay and did not ask why has entered that he did not ask.**

7.6 **ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE ON THAT COAST CANNOT READ THE NOTICE, AND IT IS A COUNT OF PEOPLE AND NOT OF ANYTHING ELSE, AND IT WAS SAID AGAIN FROM THE FOOT OF THAT MOLE'S STEPS ON THE TWENTY-NINTH OF MAY BY THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR WHO CANNOT TELL WHAT FOUR LINES OF IT MEAN, AND NO PERSON IN THAT YARD HAS GONE AND TOLD ONE OF THOSE ELEVEN PEOPLE ANYTHING AND IS NOT GOING TO, AND NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 07 RESOLVES IT.**

See `outline/volume-07.md` locks L6 and L27.

3.4 **THE FOURTH COLUMN TOOK ONE LINE A DAY FOR THE NINE DAYS FROM THE FIFTH TO THE THIRTEENTH OF JUNE AND ONE LINE GOES IN ON THE CLOSE, MAKING TEN, AND THE FIFTY-FIFTH IS THE LAST THING IN THAT BOOK.**

### 4. The route itself, as it stands in each book, with its spellings and its dates — the full text this batch creates

4.1 **THE ROUTE IS A STORM ROUTE ACROSS BRAMBLE STRAIT AND NO CURRENT CHART INCLUDES IT. THE CHART THAT OMITS IT IS A CROWN CHART OF ABOUT NINE YEARS STANDING THAT THIS HARBOR HOLDS TWO COPIES OF, ONE FRAMED UNDER GLASS ON THE WALL OF THE REEVE'S OFFICE ON THE WEST BASIN AND ONE IN THAT OFFICE'S BACK ROOM IN A DRAWER, NEITHER EVER TAKEN OUT OF THAT BUILDING. THIS YARD LOOKED AT THE FRAMED COPY FROM THE DOORWAY FOR ABOUT A MINUTE ON THE SEVENTH OF JUNE WITHOUT ENTERING AND WITHOUT TOUCHING, AND HAS HELD NEITHER COPY AND IS NOT A PARTY TO ANY CUSTODY OF EITHER.** A man's own Crown chart, bought fair at Ternwatch six years past, omits it likewise. **NONE OF THE NINE FINAL ROUTES IS NAMED IN THE PROSE AND THIS IS NOT ONE OF NINE: IT IS ONE ROUTE ACROSS ONE STRAIT AND NOBODY CALLS IT A FINAL ROUTE.**

4.2 **THE SEQUENCE AS IT STANDS, BOOK BY BOOK, WITH EVERY SPELLING AND FIGURE AND DATE EXACTLY AS ON THE PAGE:**

- **Book of the *Morrow Lass*, in a round hand, dates at the head of every page: *Skur Deep, nine fathom, foule ground to the eastard*, eleven years past.**
- **Book of the *Gull's Rest*, first half in a tall hand: *Scurr Deepe, nyne fadom, foule grounde to the estwards*, seventeen years past; second half in a short hand: *Skere Depe, niene fathoms, foul bottom east*, twenty-three years past, three pages of four undated.**
- **Book of the lighter *Tern's Debt*, in pencil, half rubbed out and written over, in two hands: *Skower Deep, 9 faddom, foule E.*, and rubbed out and written over, *Skour Deap, nine fathoms, foul to eastward*, nineteen years past.**
- **Stitched book with no vessel's name on the cover, *Sella's boat* on the first page in a hand not Sella Brigg's, in three hands: *Skorr Depe, eyght fathoms and three quarters, foule to the easte*, twenty-seven years past; *Skor Deep, nine fadome, foul ground E.*, nine years past; *the depe off the Skore, nine fathoms, keep her full and by*, undated.**
- **Father's book of a man of about thirty-six of the third lay, in a square hand, dates at the foot of every page, carried by its owner: *Skar Deep*, eight and three quarters fathom, twenty-one years past; *Skarre Depe*, nine fathom, fifteen years past; *Skar Deap*, nine and a half fathom, eight years past.**

4.3 **ELEVEN SPELLINGS ACROSS FIVE BOOKS, SEVEN HANDS IN THE YARD'S FOUR, EIGHTEEN TO TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS OF DATES, ONE WATER, FIGURES EIGHT AND THREE QUARTERS TO NINE AND A HALF FATHOM. A LINE OF FIGURES IN FIVE BOOKS IDENTIFIES A DIFFERENCE IN FIVE BOOKS AND NOT A TRUTH ABOUT A SEA.** The yard's own four books hold eight of the eleven, being the *Morrow Lass* one, the *Gull's Rest* two, the *Tern's Debt* two and the stitched book three, and the father's book holds the other three. Nessa Pike entered every spelling, figure and date in the second column exactly as it stands, copied nothing out, and wrote the difference-line under each opening. A seam identifies difference and not truth. **THIS IS THE FIGURE THE CHAPTERS MAKE CHECKABLE, BECAUSE CHAPTER 328 HAS THE SHIP'S HAND READ ALL EIGHT OF THE YARD'S SPELLINGS OUT LOUD IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING AND A STRANGER MAY COUNT THEM, AND IT IS ELEVEN AND NOT TEN.**

4.4 **THE TWO PRICES, BOTH NAMED IN THE FIRST COLUMN BEFORE ANY USE AND BEFORE ANYBODY AGREED TO ANYTHING. First, entered the fifth of June: the soundings are of a coast that has moved, not a figure anybody may measure out, not a defect to be fixed, no figure for how far to be approached. Second, entered the sixth of June: the route can be used only if a crew gives up a safer supply crossing, being the Ternwatch road inside the line for flour and coal and oil, of about eleven tons to a lighter, for the season. NOBODY AGREED TO IT IN THIS BATCH AND NOBODY REFUSED IT IN A ROOM, AND NO STAGE WAS TAKEN.**

4.5 **FOUND IN A MARKET AND NOT IN A ROOM WITH A DOOR SHUT: read first in about nine people's hearing on Friday the eleventh (the father's book read by its owner), then in about forty people's hearing on Saturday the twelfth (the father's three soundings read again, this yard's eight further spellings said out loud by the ship's hand, the man's own chart laid open by himself with his hand on the empty middle water, boat named *Ashtide Rose*, coaster out of Ashtide, about forty tons, nine years his). NOBODY TOUCHED ANY BOOK BUT ITS OWN AND NOBODY TOUCHED THE CHART BUT ITS OWNER.**

4.6 **TOBIAS WREN WAS NOT IN THAT MARKET AT ANY HOUR OF THE TWELFTH, AND HE IS THE MAN THIS YARD MOST WANTS IN IT. ON SUNDAY THE THIRTEENTH, ON THE CROWN, ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE ROUND FIVE OPEN BOOKS ON TWO SAILCLOTHS, HE STEPPED FORWARD FROM HIS OWN WORK BENCH, LOOKED AT THE PAGES FOR ABOUT FOUR MINUTES, TOUCHED NONE, REFUSED TO SAY EITHER OF THE TWO THINGS HE COULD SAY — NEITHER OF THEM IS IN THIS YARD'S BOOK AND THIS YARD IS NOT PUTTING EITHER OF THEM IN — AND SAID INSTEAD ONE TRUE THING BECAUSE HE HAS SEEN IT BEFORE: *I have seen that water*, said of *Skorr Depe* twenty-seven years past, **five** words. **THE COUNT IS CORRECTED ON ITS FACE BY THE VOLUME 07 CLOSE: *I have seen that water* IS FIVE WORDS AND THIS BATCH SAID EIGHT IN THREE PLACES, AND THE THREE ARE REPAIRED IN CHAPTER 329; AND CHAPTER 339'S SEPARATE EIGHT WORDS, BEING *You should not have done that for us*, ARE EIGHT AND ARE RIGHT AND ARE NOT TOUCHED, AND THE TWO ARE TOLD APART SO THAT NO LATER PHASE REPORTS THE ONE AS THE OTHER.** HE MAY BE LOOKED AT AND MAY NOT BE ASKED; HE WAS LOOKED AT BY FORTY AND ASKED BY NONE. HE IS NOT A TEACHER, NOT A DOOR, NOT A SACRIFICE, AND NOBODY IN THAT RING WAS STANDING IN FOR HIM; LOCK L27a HOLDS. THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM, WAS IN THAT HARBOR ON ALL TEN DAYS AND UP NO COAST ROAD ON ANY OF THEM, AND NEITHER BROTHER HAS SAID WHY.** **HE IS NOT ALDEN MARR, AND THE TWO ARE NOT ONE MAN; see item 1.7 above and the divergence recorded on the face of `outline/volume-07.md`.**

5.1 **THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY IS EIGHT CLAUSES, ON THE MARKET WALL, NOT TOUCHED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS; NOTHING PUT ON, NOTHING TAKEN OFF; TWO OLDER NAVAL NOTICES STILL ON IT. THE HEARING ROOM AND THE MARKET WALL WERE NEVER THE SAME DAY IN THIS BATCH.** No part of the yard's method, figures or fourth column is on that wall.

This yard did not draft, copy, witness, countersign or advise on any declaration on any of the ten days.

### 6. The cost, and who paid it, and the bodies

6.1 **THE BATCH'S COST IS THE REVERSAL ITSELF, AND IT FELL ON NO BODY AND ON EVERY STANDING FIGURE: a party that has always said a record nobody can check is worth less than one a man can is handed the best record it has ever been offered, in five honest books that disagree by a quarter to three quarters of a fathom, and the offer is only good if it stops checking it. THE BATCH DID NOT REFUSE THE ROUTE FOR THE OLD REASON AND DID NOT ACCEPT IT FOR FREE AND DID NOT TAKE A STAGE AND DID NOT LET A MAN AT A FAR BENCH MAKE IT SAFE.**

6.2 **COBB TERRELL, ABOUT FORTY-ONE, CAME DOWN WITHOUT THE CRUTCH ON THE EIGHTH, HAVING PUT WEIGHT ON THE LEFT FOOT FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE SEVENTH, THE TEN DAYS WITHOUT WEIGHT BEING UP WITH THE SEVENTH, AND WALKED PLAINLY ON THE ELEVENTH WITH THE FOURTEEN DAYS OFF THE WATER UP, AND WENT BACK TO WARPS AND NOT IN A BOAT.** **THE ARITHMETIC IS THE BONESETTER'S AND IT IS CHECKABLE: hurt on the twenty-eighth of May, ten days without weight counted from the twenty-ninth puts the seventh of June as the first day he could stand, and fourteen off the water counted from the twenty-ninth puts the eleventh.** The mending is a mending and not a stage. He is named, of no office, not a witness, not a symbol.

6.3 **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH. NOTHING IS CHARGED AGAINST IT, NO DAY WAS LOST TO IT, AND NO LATER CHAPTER MAY ENTER A DAY OF THIS BATCH AGAINST IT AFTER THE FACT.**

6.4 **NO STAGE WAS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND NOT RE-TAKEN. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE IS TAKEN IN MOVEMENT 5 ONLY, IN SHARED WORK, WITH A CREW, AT A COST, AND NOT BEFORE, AND NOT AS A SOLUTION TO A PROBLEM OF POLICE OR PRICE — AND IT IS NOT TAKEN HERE AND IS NOT NAMED AS SOMETHING THIS YARD IS ABOUT TO DO.** A route somebody left does not command the sea.

6.5 **THE REVERSAL IS LANDED AND NOT ANNOUNCED. The yard's standing method — a route remembered across several vessels is checkable by going there, and a record nobody can check is worth less than one a man can — IS NOW STATED ON THE FACE OF THE CHAPTERS TWICE AND NO MORE: on the tenth of June, entered in the second column as having been said in that shed before any book was opened, and on the thirteenth of June, in the shed after the four minutes and the eight words, where the holder of that writ says the yard has not refused it for the old reason and has not accepted it for free. NOTHING IN CHAPTERS 321 TO 330 PREDICTS THE TURN, NAMES IT, OR PUTS A DAY-NUMBER ON IT, AND NO CHARACTER IS ASKED TO FORESEE IT.** A later batch may restate the method and may not announce that it is about to be turned round.

### 7. The people inherited and the ones brought in

7.1 **CALDER AND MARA: she is in that harbor on all ten days and goes nowhere, is of no office, thirty, not on the crew, not restored, not forgiven, forty marks first after food neither reduced nor paid; she mends cuffs on the bench, asks nothing about the books, and the concealment is spent and not told.** CALDER AND NESSA: she counts, reads all eight of the yard's spellings out loud in about forty people's hearing, writes left-handed at twice the time, enters the difference-line four times, reads the leaf back in full on the fourteenth; nothing romantic, everything expensive. CALDER AND ALDEN: do not move; the far bench occupied on all ten days ten until four and not approached on any, nothing on it read as a gift, neither brother said why, and **the minute looked at on the tenth and the four minutes among forty on the thirteenth belong to Tobias Wren and not to him.** CALDER AND BEVIN: unchanged, off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, three nots of the eighth standing unasked, third column unfilled. CALDER AND TOBIAS: looked at for a minute on the tenth and four minutes on the thirteenth, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice.

7.2 **KEPT APART, EACH WITH ONE TRADE AND ONE BOAT AND ONE THING HE IS NOT: Cobb Terrell, about forty-one, second lay, hired hand, hurt and mended, not a witness; a man of about thirty-six, third lay, coaster of about thirty tons, eleven weeks of a season, no candles at a counter, carries his father's book, not a witness; a chandler of about fifty and his wife who counts, counter shut to one man, not villains; a man of about fifty, second lay, form in his coat with a box not filled, not advised; a man of about thirty-one, third lay, coaster *Ashtide Rose* out of Ashtide, Crown chart in a bag bought fair at Ternwatch six years past, refused a question in March, asked nothing since, not a witness and not to be cited in any room this yard keeps, never touched by this yard; a second man of about thirty-one, no lay, rope-maker's hand, no boat and no bag, not that man; a man of about thirty-four, second lay, whole fouling ladder in his own book, name to nobody, not Garrow Fisk of a pressure house at Ternwatch; a man of about twenty-six with a hod of lime, who says the man of thirty-six is not to be trusted and is answered by nobody. **AND ALDEN MARR IS NOT TOBIAS WREN, AND THE PROSE NOW KEEPS THEM IN DIFFERENT SENTENCES.** NO CAPTAIN NAMED, NONE PROPOSED. NO NEW ANTAGONIST, INSTITUTION OR FINAL ENEMY: SOREN VEY A NAME AND RANK ON A LINE IN NO ROOM; ILYA SERR NOWHERE BUT WHERE A SEAL LINE PUTS HIM, AND NOT IN A ROOM, ON A MOLE, IN A MARKET OR IN THIS HARBOR.**

### 4. The mark's new use, and the book that stays its owner's — the full text this batch creates

4.1 **THE USE, STATED WHOLE: water is level, and a dated band of fouling on a fixed stone is a record of the height of the water at that stone on that day, and a figure and an hour and a clock give a man the height of the water over any ground inside that harbor without his standing on it. TAKEN ON FRIDAY THE EIGHTEENTH OF JUNE BETWEEN TWENTY TO SEVEN IN THE MORNING AND TWENTY PAST TWO IN THE AFTERNOON, BY TWO PERSONS OF THAT YARD IN A DINGHY THAT BELONGS TO NOBODY, WITH A LEAD AND A LINE, THREE READINGS OF THE FOULING AGAINST THE SAME INCH OF STONE AND THREE READINGS OF THE WATER AT THE SAME MOMENTS ON A MARKED PLANK, AGREEMENT INSIDE AN INCH. THIS USE HAS NEVER BEEN PUT TO THAT MARK ON ANY PAGE OF THIS YARD'S LIFE BEFORE THIS ONE: IT IS NOT A CHART, DOES NOT TELL A MAN WHERE ANYTHING IS OR HAS BEEN, DOES NOT SAY WHAT IS UNDER ANY WATER, SETTLES NOTHING, AND IS NOT A STAGE.**

4.2 **THE FOUR FIGURES READ ALOUD OFF ONE PAGE OF A MAN'S OWN BOOK AT TEN PAST SEVEN IN THE MORNING ON THE EIGHTEENTH, IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING AND NO MORE: the nineteenth of May past, the fourth of May past, the twenty-sixth of March past, and the twelfth of March past. NO PAGE WAS COPIED, NO PAGE WAS CARRIED AWAY, THE BOOK WENT BACK IN HIS COAT AND HE WENT UP THE HILL AND NOBODY FOLLOWED HIM. 4.3 **THE LIMITS, ENTERED BEFORE THE WORK AT ABOUT FIVE IN THE MORNING ON THE EIGHTEENTH WITH A WRITTEN REASON AND NO NAME AGAINST IT: that one morning, that one boat, that one day, and no further; this yard holds four figures and not the page they came off; a party of one is not a custody and there were three parties in it, two in the water and one on the steps. THE USE IS CLOSED, SAID OUT LOUD ON THE TWENTY-FIRST: FOUR FIGURES AND NO MORE, NO PAGE COPIED OR TO BE COPIED, AND NO FIFTH FIGURE AT ANY HOUR OF ANY DAY, NOT SOFTENED ON A DAY A BOAT IS IN TROUBLE.**

4.4 **THE LAUNCH BOOK OF THE SIX OWNERS OF THE *OSPREY*, READ ON THE STEPS ON THE TWENTY-FIRST AND IN THE MARKET ON THE TWENTY-THIRD BY ITS OWNERS, TOUCHED BY NOBODY ELSE.
