A sheet, written on the back of one of seven pieces of paper in the drawer in that shed with the place of the charter empty, opened in that shed at about half past four in the afternoon of Friday the twenty-fifth of June past and finished at about four o'clock in the morning of Sunday the twenty-seventh, in the ship's own left hand with four stitches in a right hand since the twentieth of February past. IT CARRIES FORTY LINES, EACH WITH A NAME AND AN HOUR, AND THIRTY-SEVEN OF THE FORTY WITH A PRICE AND A PAYER AS WELL. **THE COUNT OF FORTY-OF-FORTY WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED ON ITS FACE BY THE VOLUME 07 CLOSE: lines 2, 14 and 40 carry a name and an hour and no price and no payer, because the men on them said no price, and line 15 supplies the price of the first two periods in the man who did say one; and the four claims of forty of forty on the page, at Chapter 346's subtitle, at Chapter 346's closing paragraph, at Chapter 350's third statement and at Chapter 350's fourth column's seventy-fifth line, are repaired in the chapters and the repair went onto the claim and not onto the document, because the sheet's own second rule is that the price is the price he said he was paying. See `reviews/volume-07/volume-07-close.md` Part 1 § 12.1 and § 21a items 20 to 22.** IT WAS READ ALOUD IN FULL IN THAT SHED ON THE MORNING OF WEDNESDAY THE THIRTIETH OF JUNE PAST IN THE PRESENCE OF THE ELEVEN MEN WHO ARE ON IT. FOUR COPIES WERE WRITTEN OUT ON THE BACKS OF FOUR FURTHER SHEETS FROM THE SAME DRAWER, IN FOUR HANDS, AND THE FIVE PLACES ARE WRITTEN ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE FOLD AND AT THE FOOT OF THE SHEET. THE PROMPT REQUIRES THE FULL TEXT AND IT IS GIVEN HERE ENTIRE.**

4.2 **THE FIVE PLACES, AS THE SHEET ITSELF CARRIES THEM: one to a market wall in a town four days up that coast, put up by whoever puts it up and not by this yard, this yard not having written to that town and not going to — **IT LEFT THIS HARBOR ON MONDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JUNE IN THE COAL OF AN ORDINARY BOAT GOING UP FOR COAL, AND A WORD CAME DOWN A COAST ROAD ON FRIDAY THE SECOND OF JULY SAYING THAT IT WENT UP ON A WALL THERE ON THE EVENING OF THE SECOND OF JULY PAST AND THAT NOBODY PAID FOR IT AND THAT IT WAS NOT PUT UP BY THIS YARD**; one to the end stall in the fish market; one to a man of about thirty-one of the third lay who has a chart in a bag, in the bag with the chart in it; one to a man of about fifty-one of that harbor who owns five sixths of a boat on the foul off the south end of that mole; and one to this yard, in a drawer with the charter's place empty, where nobody is going to get at it, being the one that will be lost. **NOTHING WAS BOUGHT AND NOBODY WAS PAID. A SHEET OF PAPER IS A PENNY AND FORTY SHEETS ARE A SHILLING, AND THE MAN WHO TOOK THE COPY UP IN HIS COAL SAID HE WAS NOT GOING TO CHARGE ANYBODY FOR A BIT OF PAPER THAT CAME UP HIS OWN COAL.**

4.3 **THE HEAD OF THE SHEET, AND THE ONE CORRECTION TO IT. Three words of the head were changed on the twenty-fifth of June past at the asking of the holder of that writ, from *a man could have refused* to *a man could have refused it and said so*; the words as they stood at half past four in the afternoon of the twenty-fifth are not scratched out, are on the copy in the end stall and on the copy in the bag with the chart in it, and the sheet says that a sheet which shows a stranger what it said before it was corrected is worth more than one which does not. Three words were written in the margin by the holder of that writ and they are not a signature.**

4.4 **ONE CORRECTION WAS MADE ON THE SHEET AFTER IT STOPPED, AND IT IS ON LINE FIFTEEN AND NOT ON LINE ELEVEN.** The thirty-ninth line's own hour was NOT corrected and carries no correction, no second touching and no date; **this file claimed otherwise before the repair pass at item 12 and the claim was false, and the volume's document cannot carry a feature that is not on it.** The fifteenth line's price was corrected at the asking of the man whose name is on it, the correction was made at half past eleven in the morning of Wednesday the thirtieth of June past, being the day of the reading, and the wrong figure stands beside it: *nothing*, corrected to *the slip at the head of that mole for the three weeks from the fourth of June to the twenty-sixth, being three shillings a week, that is one hundred and eight pence, which I am not paying anybody, I am losing it*. The three weeks and the fourth of June are the same period and were not before. HIS REASON FOR THE CORRECTION IS ON THE SHEET'S OWN ACCOUNT IN CHAPTER 346 AND IS A MAN'S: *a man does not get to have a loss and call it nothing on a piece of paper*.

4.5 **THE SHEET STOPS AT LINE FORTY AT TWO MINUTES PAST FOUR IN THE MORNING AND SIX THINGS HAPPENED AFTERWARDS AND ARE NOT ON IT. The holder of that writ said so out loud in that shed and the sentence is the rule: *the third rule at the head of that sheet is that it stops when somebody says it stops and not one line after, and a rule bent the first time it is inconvenient is not a rule, and I would rather have a sheet of forty lines that ended at four o'clock than forty-four lines that somebody could say afterwards were put in after the man who wrote the fortieth had gone to bed.* What the six things were is in the first column of the yard's own book, which is a different book with a different rule in it, and the two books have never been the same and Chapter 346 is the first time anybody found that out.**

4.6 **THE FORTY LINES, IN FULL, AS THEY STAND, AND AS THEY STAND ON THE PAGE OF CHAPTER 346, WHICH IS THE AUTHORITY:**

> *The night of the twenty-sixth day of June next. Eleven men were asked and eleven answered, and ten of the eleven went out. Forty decisions are on this sheet and every one of them is one a man could have refused and said so, and the refusals are on it too and they are not smaller than the rest. The time is the time the man said it. The price is the price he said he was paying. Nobody was sent for. Nobody was asked twice by anybody but themselves. — N. P., ship's hand.*
>
> *And under the head of it, in the same hand and dated the twenty-ninth day of June past, one line, being that three words of that head were changed on the twenty-fifth day of June past at the asking of the holder of that writ, from *a man could have refused* to *a man could have refused it and said so*; and that the words as they stood at half past four in the afternoon of the twenty-fifth are not scratched out and are on the copy in the end stall and on the copy in the bag with the chart in it; and that a sheet which shows a stranger what it said before it was corrected is worth more than one which does not.*
>
> **1.** *The twenty-fifth, half past ten in the morning. JOSIAH MEAR, twenty-four tons: no. Entered on the twenty-sixth at ten in the morning because the sheet was not opened until half past four on the twenty-fifth and I said it before that, and it is first on here because I said it first and I said it in the open. Price: a season I do not get either way. Payer: me, by staying on the hard.*
>
> **2.** *The twenty-fifth, eleven o'clock in the morning. HAMO BIRT, twenty-two tons: yes.*
>
> **3.** *The twenty-fifth, four o'clock in the afternoon. HAMO BIRT, twenty-two tons: no. Price: a paper on a table in an office and whose hand was in it. Payer: me.*
>
> **4.** *The twenty-sixth, ten minutes past nine in the morning. ELIAS VOKE, Anna Ray: I will bring back flour and I will not bring back physic, there being physic at fourteen pence and none in this harbor and I have a lighter's room. Price: two days of a season and nineteen winters. Payer: me.*
>
> **5.** *The twenty-sixth, twenty-five minutes past nine. IVER SALLOW, Ashtide Rose: nobody is to touch the chart in my bag, being it is nine years old and it is mine and it has nothing in the middle of that water. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **6.** *The twenty-sixth, five past ten. ROY KETTLE, thirty tons: eleven weeks of a season are standing against me and I am going to be two nights further in, and I have no figure for a night and I am not going to make one. Price: two nights, unpriced. Payer: me.*
>
> **7.** *The twenty-sixth, half past ten. PEDER LUND, thirteen tons: I am the smallest thing going out and nobody in this harbor has a figure for what thirteen tons does in a strait, and I have said that out loud so that it is not said afterwards. Price: nothing to name. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **8.** *The twenty-sixth, ten past eleven. IVOR PRIDE, forty-five tons: I am two men short of a crew of five and I am going with a boy of seventeen and a man of sixty and I am saying that out loud now and not in the morning. Price: two men. Payer: me.*
>
> **9.** *The twenty-sixth, forty-five past eleven. ALBAN PREE, thirty tons: I will take the wheel for four hours, and four hours is not a figure anybody in this harbor has got, and I am not going to invent one at eleven o'clock in the morning. Price: four hours, unpriced. Payer: me.*
>
> **10.** *The twenty-sixth, half past twelve. TAM RUNDLE, Mary Rend: I want the name of my boat on this and I want it in your hand and not mine, being I cannot write. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **11.** *The twenty-sixth, twenty past one. JENS OWER, lighter, eleven tons: I am going to the north end of the bar and no further, and I am saying it now at one o'clock in the afternoon and not at midnight. Price: the outer two miles. Payer: me.*
>
> **12.** *The twenty-sixth, two o'clock in the afternoon. ADAM SLEE, twenty-six tons: I will not take flour. I am a shipwright and I have not looked at her bottom since the twenty-fourth of April past. Oil and physic go and flour stays. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **13.** *The twenty-sixth, ten past three. IVOR PRIDE, forty-five tons: The tide on the Monday is gone and it is gone because of last night and not because anybody took it off me, and I wanted the hour. Price: one tide. Payer: me.*
>
> **14.** *The twenty-sixth, four o'clock in the afternoon. HAMO BIRT, twenty-two tons: I have untied her at last and nobody asked me to and nobody is going to.*
>
> **15.** *The twenty-sixth, eight o'clock in the evening. HAMO BIRT, twenty-two tons: I said yes on the twenty-fifth at eleven and no at four and I am saying yes again, and both go on and the sheet does not choose between them. Price: the slip at the head of that mole for the three weeks from the fourth of June to the twenty-sixth, being three shillings a week, that is one hundred and eight pence, which I am not paying anybody, I am losing it. Payer: me. — The price on this line was entered first as *nothing* at eight o'clock on the twenty-sixth and was corrected at half past eleven in the morning of the thirtieth at the asking of the man whose name is on it, and the wrong figure is not scratched out.*
>
> **16.** *The twenty-sixth, twenty to ten at night. PEDER LUND, thirteen tons: If I find it different then it is mine and not yours, and you are not to come aboard and ask me about it in the morning. Price: a stranger with a lead would have to be here tonight. Payer: me.*
>
> **17.** *The twenty-sixth, fifty-one minutes past ten. ELIAS VOKE, Anna Ray: I will hold her to nine fathom on the line and I will not lift a foot of it for anybody on this coast. Price: two days of a season and nineteen winters. Payer: me.*
>
> **18.** *The twenty-sixth, twenty past eleven. TAM RUNDLE, Mary Rend: My light goes out here and it stays out until we are through, and a light in a strait is a thing somebody will come for. Price: a night's passage, about nine tons. Payer: me.*
>
> **19.** *The twenty-seventh, five minutes past midnight. ADAM SLEE, twenty-six tons: I will not take flour. Price: two days off my bench and my apprentice of fourteen goes without. Payer: me.*
>
> **20.** *The twenty-seventh, forty-eight minutes past midnight. JENS OWER, lighter, eleven tons: A lighter will not cross a bar at night. I am at the north end of the bar and I have not gone one mile past it, and I am saying it at this hour so that nobody can say in the morning that I said something else. Price: the outer two miles, said twice. Payer: me.*
>
> **21.** *The twenty-seventh, six minutes past one in the morning. COLL MABRY, forty-five, third lay, in the forty-five tons: two fingers of my left hand off the warp, and I am off the water for nine days, and I have a girl of eleven and it is her I am thinking about, and I am putting that on the sheet so that I cannot say in a week that I did not say it tonight. Price: nine days, and I have no figure for a day of my own and I am not going to make one up. Payer: me, and whatever the nine days cost, and nobody here.*
>
> **22.** *The twenty-seventh, nineteen minutes past one. IVER SALLOW: I have got my own hand on my own chart in the middle where the strait is, and I am saying so out loud so that if I am wrong afterwards there is somebody who heard me say I was holding it. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **23.** *The twenty-seventh, thirty-one minutes past one. ALBAN PREE: Sea by hand and not by instrument, being I have no instrument. First reading and second reading are not the same and I am going with the second. Price: my hands, at sixty. Payer: me.*
>
> **24.** *The twenty-seventh, forty-four minutes past one. ROY KETTLE: Half speed. I am not going to be hurried by anybody on this coast tonight. Price: an hour I have not got. Payer: me.*
>
> **25.** *The twenty-seventh, fifty-eight minutes past one. HAMO BIRT, twenty-two tons: I am going to hold her to the other nine and not to make my own, being ten boats is a figure and one boat of twenty-two tons is not a figure, and I have been one man saying one thing today and that is enough of it. Price: none given. Payer: me.*
>
> **26.** *The twenty-seventh, twelve minutes past two. PEDER LUND, thirteen tons: I was on the line off the twenty-seven-year page, the eight and three quarters, and by my own hand on my own lead she was carrying two foot more than that over it, and I went on, because a man of about thirty-two at my wheel said go. Price: nobody in this country can check this in a year. Payer: me.*
>
> **27.** *The twenty-seventh, twenty-four minutes past two. ELIAS VOKE, Anna Ray: I am going to take three people in on the way back, being there is room, and the three are a woman of about sixty-two and two of her sisters, and they have been on the other side eleven days going to a burial. Price: three places. Payer: me.*
>
> **28.** *The twenty-seventh, thirty-three minutes past two. TAM RUNDLE: Anchor down at the north end and I come back for it. It is mine and it cost me eleven shillings and I am not asking anybody for it. Price: eleven shillings. Payer: me.*
>
> **29.** *The twenty-seventh, forty-one minutes past two. ADAM SLEE: I am not looking at my bottom again until I am alongside, and anybody who wants to know why can come and hold a lamp for me at seven in the morning. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **30.** *The twenty-seventh, forty-eight minutes past two. JENS OWER: That is the second time I have said the north end of the bar tonight and I am not going to say it a third. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **31.** *The twenty-seventh, fifty-five minutes past two. ALBAN PREE: I am going to bring her in on the morning flood and I am not going to try the north end in the dark. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **32.** *The twenty-seventh, one minute past three. ROY KETTLE: I will not have anything lit on my boat. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **33.** *The twenty-seventh, seven minutes past three. IVER SALLOW: I have looked at my own chart in the dark on a moving boat and it told me nothing that I did not have, and I am not going to say any more about it tonight or after. Price: nine years of carrying it. Payer: me.*
>
> **34.** *The twenty-seventh, thirteen minutes past three. ELIAS VOKE, Anna Ray: I will not answer anybody who shouts at me, being there are nine other boats on that water tonight and I am answerable for one. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **35.** *The twenty-seventh, nineteen minutes past three. TAM RUNDLE: I am not putting my light on again until I am inside the harbour, being a light at the outer marks is a thing somebody writes down and I do not want a thing written down. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **36.** *The twenty-seventh, twenty-five minutes past three. HAMO BIRT, twenty-two tons: I am going in behind the Anna Ray and I am not going in first, being I have been the first one into everything all my life and I am not doing it tonight. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **37.** *The twenty-seventh, half past three. ADAM SLEE: The oil is short by four gallons and I am putting that on here and taking it, being I am the man in this harbor who would know and I would rather it was on a sheet than on my conscience. Price: four gallons. Payer: me.*
>
> **38.** *The twenty-seventh, thirty-five minutes past three. JENS OWER: I am a ton light and I said so at about three and I will say it again at ten, and nobody is to write it twice. Price: about a ton. Payer: me.*
>
> **39.** *The twenty-seventh, forty-seven minutes past three. PEDER LUND, thirteen tons: Nobody has come aboard and asked me about the two feet, and I said on a quay last night that nobody would, and I am saying at this hour that nobody has, and if anybody comes tomorrow I will say the same thing again. Price: nothing. Payer: nobody.*
>
> **40.** *The twenty-seventh, two minutes past four in the morning. ELIAS VOKE, Anna Ray: That is the sheet. Nobody writes on it after this. I have had two days of a season and I am not writing anything at four in the morning that I would have to read at ten.*
>
> *And under the fortieth line, in the ship's own left hand, the places of the copies: one to a market wall in a town four days up that coast, put up by whoever puts it up and not by this yard, this yard not having written to that town and not going to; one to the end stall in the fish market; one to a man of about thirty-one of the third lay who has a chart in a bag, in the bag with the chart in it; one to a man of about fifty-one of that harbor who owns five sixths of a boat on the foul off the south end of that mole; and one to this yard, in a drawer with the charter's place empty, where nobody is going to get at it, being the one that will be lost.*

**AND THE HEAD IS PRINTED HERE AS IT STANDS IN CHAPTER 346, AND NOT ONE WORD OF IT HAS BEEN ADDED BY THE VOLUME 07 CLOSE, because the sheet's own second rule is that the price is the price he said he was paying and a document may not be made to carry a figure no man said. THE COUNT THE CLOSE RULES IS THEREFORE A COUNT OF THIS ITEM AND NOT A CHANGE TO IT: all forty lines carry a name in capitals and an hour, and thirty-seven carry a price and a payer as well, and the three that carry neither are line 2, which is Hamo Birt's first yes at eleven o'clock in the morning on the twenty-fifth; line 14, which is his untieing at four o'clock in the afternoon on the twenty-sixth; and line 40, which is the line that stops the sheet. See `reviews/volume-07/volume-07-close.md` Part 1 § 12.1 and § 21c item 1.**
### 5. The stage, the route, the mark, and the prices — none moved except the figures named

5.1 **THE STORM-READER STAGE IS TAKEN, ONCE, ON THE NIGHT OF THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF JUNE PAST, IN SHARED WORK, WITH A CREW, AT A COST, AND AS A TRADE AND NOT AS A POWER, AND IT IS ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN ON THURSDAY THE FIRST OF JULY PAST, FIVE DAYS LATER, BECAUSE THE YARD MAY NOT ENTER ON THE DAY A THING A MAN DID WITH A CREW.** It is named on the face of Chapter 347 and again on the face of Chapter 350. **The cost, named whole: the soundings it works from are of a coast that has moved; there is no figure for how far a coast moves and none was invented; a line on a page is a thing a person left and the person is not on the water; a seam identifies a difference and not a truth; a power is a thing one man can do that other men cannot and this yard has never had one; a trade is a thing four people do together on a night and it stops when they stop and it stopped at four o'clock in the morning because a herring skipper of fifty-one said so. IT SETTLED NOTHING. IT DID NOT POLICE ANYTHING AND IT DID NOT PRICE ANYTHING.**

5.2 **THE ROUTE AND THE TWO PRICES, CARRIED UNCHANGED FROM BATCH 0003 AND PRICED AGAIN BEFORE ANYBODY WAS ASKED ANYTHING IN CHAPTER 341.** Eleven spellings of one water in five books under seven hands, being eight in this yard's four and three in the father's book OF ROY KETTLE, A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SIX, WHICH IS HIS AND NOT THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE'S, EIGHTEEN TO TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS, eight fathoms and three quarters to nine and a half, and no current chart includes it and the Crown chart of about nine years has nothing in the middle of that water and is not made to agree with a twenty-seven-year page. The two prices: the soundings are of a coast that has moved and there is no figure for how far to be approached; the Ternwatch road inside the line, of about eleven tons to a lighter for the season, given up on the twenty-fifth by a lighterman of about twenty-nine and not given back to anybody.

5.3 **THE USE OF THE MARK ON THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM WAS NOT LOOKED AT, NOT MEASURED, NOT TOUCHED AND NOT READ ON ANY DAY OF THE TEN DAYS. It remains closed at four figures with no fifth at any hour of any day. The whole fouling ladder is in another man's own book and nobody has seen one page of it and he is about thirty-four and gave his name to nobody and is not Garrow Fisk. THE SECOND SEAM'S SEASON IS NINE MARKS AND IS NOT PAID AND IS NOT GOING TO BE PAID, AND SO IS THE MARK FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF IT, AND NEITHER FIGURE IS IMPROVED ON IN ANY CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH.**

5.4 **THE NOTICE, THE BREACH, AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE. THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY IS EIGHT CLAUSES AND IS ON THE MARKET WALL AND WAS NOT TOUCHED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, NOTHING WAS PUT ON IT AND NOTHING CAME OFF IT, TWO OLDER NAVAL NOTICES ARE STILL ON IT, AND THE HEARING ROOM AND THE MARKET WALL WERE NEVER THE SAME DAY. The six clauses that bear on the batch are: the first, that no vessel shall leave the port or pass the line described in the fifth clause without a master's declaration lodged with the harbor authority before noon; the fourth, that a master who does not carry a declaration may be detained and his vessel held to the outer marks; the fifth, that the line runs from the mole-head of that mole to a can upon a stake at the outer marks and thence to a point named in the first schedule; and the sixth, that this notice is not a closure of the port and vessels may enter without a declaration. TEN BOATS OF THAT HARBOR WENT OUT PAST THE MOLE HEAD AND PAST THAT LINE ON THE FLOOD OF THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-SIXTH AT ABOUT HALF PAST SEVEN WITHOUT A DECLARATION, WHICH IS A BREACH OF THE FIRST, AND CAME IN PAST THE OUTER MARKS AT ABOUT HALF PAST FIVE THE NEXT MORNING UNDER THE SIXTH, AND **THE HARBOR IS OPEN ENOUGH AND THE NOTICE IS NOT LIFTED AND HAS NOT BEEN WITHDRAWN AND NOTHING IN THIS BATCH WITHDRAWS IT. NO CHAPTER SAYS IT IS A LIE AND NO CHAPTER SAYS IT IS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT.** This yard drafted, copied, witnessed, countersigned and advised nothing, and no vessel of this yard's was on that water, and the holder of that writ went in a boat of about thirteen tons belonging to a man of about thirty-eight of no lay, at that man's own asking and on his own account, and it is entered in the first column in those words.**

5.5 **A FACE OF THE CLOSED-SEA SQUADRON IS ON THE PAGE TWICE AND IS A WORKING MAN AND NOT AN OFFICER.** One man in one boat lying at the outer marks with a book open on the thwart. He did not hail the ten going out on the twenty-sixth and did not hail the ten coming in on the twenty-seventh, and nobody in that harbor spoke to him and he was not asked anything and was not thanked. **The second column carries, with a reason against the line and no name against it: that the holder of that writ was not hailed, and that this yard has no instrument and no power and has never had either, and that a man with a book who does not hail a boat is not the same thing as a man with a book who cannot, and that nobody in that yard knows which of those two it was and is not going to find out and did not ask him and is not going to. ADMIRAL SOREN VEY IS A NAME AND A RANK ON A LINE IN NO ROOM, ON NO MOLE AND IN NO MARKET, AND IS IN NONE OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS.**

5.6 **THE PRICE LIST DID NOT MOVE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND DID NOT MOVE BECAUSE SOMETHING CAME IN.** A barrel of lamp oil stands at four hundred and fifty pence quoted the first of June, the February figure of three hundred and seventy-eight pence left visible above it with both dates on the board, and on the February figure that mole-head light was out in October and it is out now and its lens has been out since the seventh of May. The other eight figures did not move. Physic at fourteen pence with *none in this harbor* did not move. **THERE IS NO FIGURE ANYWHERE IN THAT HARBOR FOR ELEVEN TONS OF OIL THAT CAME IN ON TEN BOATS AT NIGHT ON NO DECLARATION, AND THE WOMAN WITH THE SLATE SAYS SO OUT LOUD AND WILL NOT PUT ONE THERE, GIVING THE REASON THAT A WOMAN WHO PUTS A FIGURE ON A BOARD CANNOT TAKE IT OFF AGAIN, WHICH IS THE SAME REASON SHE HAS GIVEN SINCE THE TWENTY-NINTH OF APRIL PAST.** Two quarts at ten pence on the nineteenth of June past is the figure of the fifteenth batch and is not re-priced here. A slip is three shillings a week. A sheet of paper is a penny and forty sheets are a shilling. **THE PRICE OF THE CHEAPEST OIL IN THAT HARBOR WENT UP SIX SHILLINGS ON THE FIRST OF JUNE AND DID NOT COME BACK DOWN, AND THAT IS THE RESOLUTION AND IT IS NOT A VICTORY.**

5.7 **THE FOUR COLUMN FIGURES THAT MUST NOT BE SWAPPED STAND IN THIS ORDER IN CHAPTER 350: nine communities and the records one in each, six centuries of that practice, and three hundred years of the office that answers it; the office's three hundred years was not handed to the communities.**

### 6. The cost, and who paid it, and the bodies

6.1 **THE BATCH'S COST IS THE VOLUME'S COST AND IT IS PAID BY MEN WHO ARE NOT THIS YARD AND NOT BY ANYBODY IN IT. TEN BOATS AND TEN MEN GAVE TWO DAYS OF A SEASON AND THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-EIGHT OF ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTEEN PENCE OUT OF THREE WEEKS OF ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHT PENCE AND ONE TIDE AND TWO MEN AND FOUR HOURS AT A WHEEL AND FOUR GALLONS AND ABOUT A TON AND FOUR TONS OF FLOUR AND ELEVEN TONS OF OIL AND A ROAD OF ABOUT ELEVEN TONS AND THREE WEEKS OFF A SHIPWRIGHT'S BENCH AND AN APPRENTICE OF FOURTEEN AT HOME FOR TWO DAYS AND TWO FINGERS OF A WORKING MAN'S LEFT HAND AND NINE DAYS OFF THE WATER, AND NOT ONE PENNY OF IT CAME TO THAT YARD.**

6.2 **COLL MABRY, ABOUT FORTY-FIVE, OF THE THIRD LAY, twenty-six years on that water, LOST TWO FINGERS OF HIS LEFT HAND OFF A WARP AT ABOUT SIX MINUTES PAST ONE IN THE MORNING OF THE TWENTY-SEVENTH, IN THE BOAT OF ABOUT FORTY-FIVE TONS, AND BOUND IT WAS BY A SHIPWRIGHT OF ABOUT SIXTY IN ABOUT FOUR MINUTES WITH A STRIP CUT OFF THE LEECH OF A SAIL, BECAUSE THERE IS NO BONESETTER ON THAT COAST AT ONE IN THE MORNING OR AT FOUR OR AT SIX. HIS LINE ON THE SHEET CARRIES THE NINE DAYS AND THE FACT THAT HE HAS A GIRL OF ELEVEN, AND HE ASKED FOR THE HOUR TO BE PUT AGAINST IT SO THAT HE COULD NOT SAY IN A WEEK THAT HE HAD NOT SAID IT THAT NIGHT. He is ashore, alive, not asked one word, and has not been to a bonesetter of about sixty in that harbor on his own account, and nobody in that yard sent him. **This is an injury to a working person that costs a real bill and a real absence, and it is NOT Tobias Wren's injury of Volume 06 and is not discharged by it; Rowan Teel's right forearm, set on the twenty-first of June past for sixteen pence out of his own hand, is a second such injury and is carried at Batch 0004 § 6.2.**

6.3 **ROWAN TEEL, ABOUT FORTY, OF THAT HARBOR'S OWN WATER, HURT ON THE NINETEENTH OF JUNE PAST, RIGHT FOREARM SET BY A BONESETTER OF ABOUT SIXTY ON MONDAY THE TWENTY-FIRST FOR SIXTEEN PENCE SAID TWICE AND PAID BY THE MAN OUT OF HIS OWN HAND IN SMALL COIN, HIS OWN NAME ON THE SEVENTH LINE OF THE LAUNCH BOOK UNDER THE NINETEENTH. On the evening of the twenty-sixth a man asked him whether there was a place for him on any of the ten boats, and he said there was not a place he could fill with his arm, out loud, on the quay, in about nine people's hearing, and nobody comforted him, and that is the whole of it.**

6.4 **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH, AND A DAY WAS LOST TO IT, WHICH IS OWED AND PAID. On Thursday the first day of July next the holder of that writ set himself a day of ordinary work and did not do it. THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE IN THE SECOND COLUMN IS THAT HE WAS NOT ABLE TO, AND THERE IS NOTHING ELSE AGAINST IT AND NOTHING IS TO BE PUT AGAINST IT, HE HAS NOT SAID WHY AND WAS NOT ASKED WHY, NO NAME IS AGAINST THE LINE AND NO NAME IS TO BE PUT AGAINST IT, NO DAY OF ANY WEEK BEFORE THAT ONE MAY BE ENTERED AGAINST THE SAME LINE AFTERWARDS, AND A LOST DAY CARRIES NO FIGURE, BEING THAT THAT YARD HAS NO FIGURE FOR WHAT A DAY OF THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT IS WORTH AND HAS NOT INVENTED ONE. The ship's hand said out loud in that shed, unasked and in advance, that if a name is ever put against that line it will be put there by somebody who is not her and that she will not write it, and that it is not a stage and is not on the sheet of forty lines and is not going to be, and that a man of about sixty-one on the crown of that mole is not it, and that a man of about sixty-one on the far bench across that crown is not it, in two sentences and not in one, as `outline/volume-07.md` line 199 requires. **Batch 0004's own position was that the condition is named nowhere and that no day was lost to it, and that is why this cost falls to Movement 5 and to no other batch. NO NAME IS ANYWHERE. `reviews/volume-04/volume-04-close.md` § 3.24 stands and the one naming spent in Chapter 164 of Volume 04 is not available here or anywhere.**

6.5 **NO STAGE BUT ONE IS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH. The faultreader stage is spent and was not re-taken. The bellwright stage is not improved. ### 7. The people inherited and the ones brought in

7.1 **CALDER AND MARA: he told her in plain words on the twenty-fifth without softening a figure and without putting it in a book first, which is what he did on the sixteenth and was caught at for on the nineteenth, and she said four things, none of them kind, and asked for the second of them to be written down before she said the other three, being that it is not his and he is going anyway. She is not going, and gave the reason herself, being a man of about thirty-four two days down that coast who cannot read and a daughter of nineteen, and the fact that one more person in the town who knows is a thing she can do without. She asked for it to be heard out of a book a stranger can pick up and check, and said that that is the only difference between a man and a notice. SHE IS OF NO OFFICE, THIRTY, NOT ON THE CREW, NOT RESTORED, NOT FORGIVEN, FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD NEITHER REDUCED NOR PAID, IN THAT HARBOR ON ALL TEN DAYS AND GOING NOWHERE. IT IS NOT RESOLVED IN THIS VOLUME.** CALDER AND NESSA: she counts, writes the sheet left-handed on a thwart, enters the day lost with a reason and no name, says out loud that she will not write a name against it, reads the leaf back in full on the fourth, and states on the face of the reading which figure is a count of paragraphs and which is not; nothing romantic, everything expensive. CALDER AND ALDEN: do not move; the far bench occupied on all ten days ten until four and not approached on any; one shoe on that bench beside him that is not his and has been there since the third of May past; neither brother said why; the holder was out of that harbor for one night of the ten and went up no coast road on any of them; **the far-bench man is not in that yard's book at all.** CALDER AND BEVIN: unchanged, off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, three nots standing unasked on all ten days, third column unfilled. CALDER AND TOBIAS: looked at on all ten days, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice; the hook in the left hand on every one of the ten; about nine people round him on any afternoon of the ten and not one word said to him about a sheet, a stage or a night.

7.2 **THE ELEVEN MEN WHO WERE ASKED, OF WHOM TEN ARE MASTERS AND ONE IS A REFUSAL, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS SERIES, EACH WITH ONE TRADE, ONE BOAT AND ONE THING HE IS NOT, AND NONE OF THEM A WITNESS, A SYMBOL, AN OFFICER OR A MEMBER OF ANYTHING: ELIAS VOKE, fifty-one, herring skipper of the *Anna Ray*, nineteen winters disputed and unpaid, a hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November past, a season of nine marks not going to be paid, four lines on the sheet, and the man who said *that is the sheet* at two minutes past four in the morning. IVER SALLOW, about thirty-one, of the third lay, of the *Ashtide Rose* out of Ashtide, about forty tons, nine years his, a Crown chart of about nine years in a bag that nobody else has touched since the twelfth of June past, five lines, and the man who said aloud that a thing on the water has to be looked at by somebody who is not being paid by the person who wants it looked at. ROY KETTLE, about thirty-six, of the third lay, of a coaster of about thirty tons, eleven weeks of a season and no passage past that mole head since the seventeenth day of May past, four lines. PEDER LUND, about thirty-eight, of no lay and no standing whatever, of a boat of about thirteen tons that he keeps and pays for himself, five lines including the one about two foot, and the man who came close to finishing a sentence in a market in the month past and got four words out and was stopped. IVOR PRIDE, about forty-seven, of the third lay, of a boat of about forty-five tons, two men short of a crew of five, two lines, one of them a berth on the Monday. ALBAN PREE, about sixty, of the first lay, forty-one years on that water, the man who asked this volume's question at a mole head on the thirty-first day of May past in sixty-three words which he counted four times, four lines, none of them about the question. TAM RUNDLE, about thirty-four, of the screw-steam packet *Mary Rend* out of Bramble Strait, who works for nobody, five lines, the anchor of eleven shillings, and the light put out in the strait and not lit again until she was inside the harbour; **NOT AN OFFICER, NOT A SERVANT, NOT A CROWN MAN, NOT A COURIER AND NOT A FACE OF AN INSTITUTION, AND ON THE LAST PAGE OF THE VOLUME HE IS ON A MOLE STEP WITH A COPIED LINE IN HIS HAND THAT IS NOT HIS.** HAMO BIRT, about fifty, of the second lay, of a boat of about twenty-two tons, a form in his coat with a name and a date and a box not filled, a paper on a table in an office with no season, five lines and three hours and one correction; JENS OWER, about twenty-nine, of no lay, of a lighter of about eleven tons, four lines and two miles of work given up; ADAM SLEE, about sixty, a shipwright of about fifty, with a bench and an apprentice of fourteen, four lines and a refusal to carry flour; and JOSIAH MEAR, about fifty-five, of a boat of about twenty-four tons on a slip with a line about her moulds that is staying on, WHO SAID NO AND WHOSE REFUSAL IS THE FIRST LINE ON THE SHEET.**

7.3 **KEPT APART, EACH WITH ONE TRADE AND ONE BOAT AND ONE THING HE IS NOT: Cobb Terrell, about forty-one, second lay, back to warps and not in a boat, spliced a warp in nineteen minutes on the eleventh of June past and was spliced against in the ledger on the first of July past; a man of about thirty-six with a coaster of about thirty tons and his father's book in his house; a chandler of about fifty and his counting wife, counter shut to one man, and the eight marks and a day of a boat standing unargued with the chest shut and no digit printed; a man of about fifty with a paper on a table; a man of about thirty-one of no lay with a rope-maker's hand, no boat and no bag, not that man; a man of about thirty-four of that harbor's own second lay who keeps the whole fouling ladder in his own book, gave his name to nobody, is not Garrow Fisk, said eight words on the twenty-third of June and one sentence in that shed on the thirtieth, and was asked nothing on either occasion and his name is in no book; a boy of about seventeen who carried a copy up a quay for nothing, having been paid one penny for one word on the nineteenth of June past, and did not ask to read it and was not given one; a woman of about thirty-four of that harbor who put her hand on the arm of a woman of about sixty-two and walked her into the back of the end stall, of no office, not on a crew, not thanked; THE TRUE GRID FOR THE BATCH IS Monday the fifth, Tuesday the sixth, Wednesday the seventh, Thursday the eighth, Friday the ninth, Saturday the tenth, Sunday the eleventh, Monday the twelfth, Tuesday the thirteenth and Wednesday the fourteenth. A SWEEP OF THE TEN FILES GIVES TEN WEEKDAY-AND-DATE PAIRS, ONE PER FILE, AND ZERO MISMATCHES AGAINST THAT GRID. NO CHAPTER STATES A YEAR. THE NINETY, TAKEN ON THE FIFTEENTH OF JUNE, BEING THE DAY SIX MEN WERE TOLD TO STAND BY, RUNS DAYS TWENTY-ONE TO THIRTY INSIDE THIS BATCH, ON THE FACE OF CHAPTERS 351 TO 360.**

**THE TWO-CALENDAR FAULT IS INHERITED, NOT NOTICED, NOT REPAIRED, AND IS RULED ON IN THE HARD FORM THE FIVE EARLIER AUDITS SETTLED, AND IT IS RE-DERIVED AND REPORTED ONCE HERE. Against the almanac, the fifth of July in the year Chapter 350 names falls on a Sunday and not on a Monday, and every day of the batch is one out. The almanac is not the rule of this book. No character in these ten chapters says a word about it and none of them could.**

The three standing figures, counted in that shed and not taken out of any other book: **TWO wipes, being the sixty-first on Monday the fifth and the sixty-second on Monday the twelfth, the next being the sixty-third on Monday the nineteenth, which is outside this batch; THREE cistern rota days charged and walked on, being the sixty-first on the fifth, the sixty-second on Thursday the eighth and the sixty-third on Monday the twelfth, the rota being a Monday and a Thursday; and TWO wage Tuesdays, being Tuesday the sixth for the thirty-seventh week and Tuesday the thirteenth for the thirty-eighth, the column unmoved on both, so that THIRTY-EIGHT WEEKS STAND FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE AGAINST ANY OF THEM.** The two objects of nobody's run 388 to 398 one a calendar day across the ten, and the bench under that pump runs 154 to 164 one a night, and both run without a skip, the missing fourth of June being behind the last volume.

### 2. The money, and it closes in one line

**THE BAG IS NOTHING AT THE OPEN. One hundred and sixty-eight pence comes in on Wednesday the seventh, being a day's work with a boat and two men at the north berth, and ninety-two pence goes out the same day, being nine feet twelve inches of new stud chain. One hundred and sixty-eight pence comes in on Monday the twelfth, being a day's work off the foul, and forty pence goes out the same day, being a shackle and a fathom of line. Nothing else comes in or goes out on any day of the ten. NOTHING PLUS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PLUS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT MINUS NINETY-TWO MINUS FORTY IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, being one mark and three shillings and eightpence. THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS IS SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY MINUS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR, BEING FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, being two marks and nine shillings and eightpence, and it is not going to be paid and nobody is to write one word under it saying anybody is going to.** A boat with a man in her for a day is one hundred and sixty-eight pence, so that bag is a day and a piece of a day, and it is the most money in that bag since the eighteenth of May past.

**REPAIRED BEFORE THE BATCH WAS CLOSED, AND RECORDED AS A REPAIR AND NOT AS A FINDING, PER LOCK L1 ITEM 6: Chapters 358 and 359 as first written gave the man of about fifty-one of the six the day's wage of one hundred and sixty-eight pence AND gave the man of about forty-four a separate one hundred and sixty-eight pence, which would have made three hundred and thirty-six pence in on the Monday and broken the chain above. THE CHAPTERS ARE RIGHT AND THE COMPUTED FIGURE WAS THROWN AWAY. The man of about fifty-one takes the whole of the day's wage, being one mark and eightpence out of a tin, and the man of about forty-four, who is the second of the six, was in that boat ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT, was not paid, was not asked to pay, was told the terms before he went out and said he knew them, and worked the day for nothing and lost the top of two fingers of his left hand on it. The man of about thirty-four of the second lay, who asked to be in the boat, was in it on his own account and was not paid and was not asked to pay. The other four men of the six were not in the boat and were not asked and were not told there was work.**

**NINETY-THREE / THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE / NONE / EIGHTY-FIVE at the close of Wednesday the fourteenth of July; NINETY-TWO / THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN / NONE / EIGHTY-FOUR at the read-back at about four the same afternoon. The third column is none on ten consecutive days and nobody has been appointed to it and the boy's hand at the head of it, which has been there since the fourth of April past, was not scratched out on the eleventh of July, and the name beside it was said once on the thirteenth of May past and was not said again. The fourth column's eighty-fifth line is the last thing in that book and the column is not closed.**

### 4. The instrument of the seventh of July, and the eleven leaves, and the sheet of thirteen lines — the full text this batch creates

**THE INSTRUMENT. A single leaf. Two seals. One signature, *Magister Ilya Serr, senior Registry examiner*, which is the first time those words have appeared in that order with that name under them. The second seal carries *Admiral Soren Vey, fifty-two, of the closed-sea squadron*, printed small at the foot, ON THE FACE OF THAT ONE INSTRUMENT AND ON NO OTHER PAPER IN THAT HARBOR, and no meaning was read into it. The first line is the word AMNESTY, the second is the word PROTECTION, and both are spelled out at the bottom in a line of type no larger than the rest, and the four things are on the face of it. There is no schedule, no enclosure and nothing on the back. Read out in full in about four minutes by the ship's hand in her left hand, in the presence of five people who were told in advance that it was going to be read and were not asked to come and were not asked to stay.**

**THE FOUR PRICES, AND ELEVEN LEAVES IN SIX HANDS, AND THE FIGURES ARE FIXED HERE SO THAT NO LATER CHAPTER CAN MOVE THEM:**
1. **The public provenance record, being FIVE leaves**, made in the woman of no office's own hand when the two glass objects left that town's deck under one witnessed surrender, and there are two of those records and this is the one that is not in the circuit office.
2. **The sheet of forty lines, being ONE leaf**, with a name and an hour on all forty and a price and a payer on thirty-seven, the wrong figure standing beside its own correction and the wrong figure not scratched out, and the FIVE PLACES written on the outside of the fold.
3. **FOUR COPIES of that same sheet, being FOUR leaves in four hands**: a copyist of about fifty-nine in a room off the fish market, twenty-two years copying and never once having asked what; a herring skipper of fifty-one, on a thwart, in that harbor; a man of about thirty-six out of his father's book, in his father's house a day up that coast, in a coal locker there, and a locker is not a room anybody can be asked about; and a man of about thirty-eight of no standing whatever with a boat of about thirteen tons, in about two hours sitting on a coil of line.
4. **A leaf carrying ONE CORRECTION and ONE DATE and nothing else on it**, in the ship's own left hand, in that shed, in the drawer with the sheet in it, and it is the only one of the eleven in a building anybody can walk into for nothing.

**AND THE LAST PARAGRAPH, WHICH IS NOT A THING: that the parties subscribing confirm the account of the seizure of the ferry *Aster Gannet* as the same account set out in the salvage report and the seizure report, and no correction of that account is to be offered or held. IT DOES NOT SAY HOW MANY SUBSCRIBING PARTIES IT MEANS, AND THAT IS THE ELEVENTH THING ABOUT THAT LEAF WHICH IS NOT ON THE LEAF. The ship's hand priced it at eleven conversations and about forty days and one of them that cannot happen at all, and that eleven is HER OWN READING AND IS ENTERED AS HER READING AND NOT AS A FACT OF THE INSTRUMENT.**

**THE SHEET OF THIRTEEN LINES. One leaf, the back of a reeve's office docket, in the woman of no office's hand, about an hour and a half, on Saturday the tenth. Three rules at the head of it, being the same three rules as the sheet of forty lines and copied out and not improved on: a decision goes on at the moment a man says it; a man may take it back and both go on; it stops when somebody says it stops and not one line after. UNDER THE THIRD RULE AND ABOVE THE FIRST LINE, A FOURTH THING WHICH IS NOT A RULE: that the price against a line is what the man said he was paying, and the payer against a line is the man himself, and where nobody was asked there is a place and no price and no payer and the place is the price of not asking. THIRTEEN LINES. A NAME AND AN HOUR ON ALL THIRTEEN. A PRICE AND A PAYER ON ELEVEN, the price against all eleven being the word *nothing* and the payer against all eleven being the name of the man who gave it. THE TWO LINES CARRYING NEITHER ARE THE TWELFTH, a market wall in a town four days up that coast where a page of forty lines has been since the previous month and the name of whoever put it there, which nobody in that yard knows and did not ask; AND THE THIRTEENTH, a table in a corridor of the office of the Morrow circuit where two of the three things in that building are and where one of the two cannot read and who was not asked and no request was made and nobody has been sent. LINE ONE IS HIS OWN ANSWER IN HIS OWN HAND, four sentences, and the last of them is that a thing needing eleven men has ten and a hole. It went up that coast in the coal of an ordinary boat at about two in the afternoon, in the inside pocket of that boat's own boy of about seventeen, who was not paid and did not know what it was and did not ask. THIS YARD WROTE TO NONE OF THE FIVE TOWNS AND CHARGED NOBODY FOR ANY PART OF IT. The empty line of the man of about thirty-six was filled in on Monday the thirteenth at about six in the morning when his answer came down in the coal, NEITHER OF THE TWO BLANKS WAS TOUCHED, and the sheet was not recopied and none of its five places has a fresh copy on it because of anything that happened.**

### 5. The stage, the route, the mark, the notice, and the tender — none moved except the figures named

**NO STAGE WAS TAKEN IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND NONE WAS IMPROVED, RE-TAKEN OR RENAMED, PER LOCK L26. No chapter entered an echo, entered a vessel or surfaced a practice trace. The third channel on the borrowed pinger is an instrument reading and not a discovery, and the pinger's own rule is on the face of Chapter 358: a pinger puts down two channels on a thing that has been in the water a long while, it is not reading anything, it is counting what the iron on the other side of a hull is doing to a note, and a man with the instrument on the wrong side of a plate gets a figure and not a truth. Nothing was measured, nothing was timed, the instrument was not left in the water, and it went back up that coast on the Tuesday in the ordinary way, and the man it is borrowed from has not been asked about it and is not going to be.**

**THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY PAST: on its wall in a different street for fifty-eight days as at the fourteenth of July, not touched, not withdrawn, not compared with anything by anybody in that harbor, and NOT COMPARED WITH THE PAGE ON THE MOLE. The fifth clause is a breach and the sixth clause is free, and the sixth clause has been the reason that harbor is open since the seventeenth of May, and it was written by an office that did not write it for that harbor. The two older naval notices further along the same wall are still on it. This yard's own fourth return is on that wall under one sheet and is still the only paper on it that any office in any city is obliged to look at, and the man of about fifty's second paper went onto the table in the office off the west basin on Monday the fifth with the fourth box not filled, and the man already at that table is a man off the west quay and is not this man, and neither of them spoke, and the clerk of about sixty wrote both names in one register and neither looked at the other's line, and the yard does not know on which of the two papers the fourth box was not filled and did not ask.**

**THE TENDER. A small steam tender of about ninety tons, at the outer water of that harbor from about half past two on Saturday the tenth to the end of the fourteenth, OUTSIDE THE LINE, with two lines out. A young man of about twenty-three in her own wheelhouse with a telescope came out on the roof twice and looked at that harbor for about four minutes and came back in again, and he is not an officer of anything and was asked nothing and said nothing. A man of nineteen at the wheel of a vessel of perhaps eighteen tons was levering a boat's hook at a bight of line round a bollard, got it round twice, was not in a hurry, and the only thing anybody entered against him is that he was patient with a bight of line and did not cut it. A girl of about nineteen at the steps of the pilot's house said she had come round the point in thick weather off a coal boat, had not come in past the line, had not hailed anybody, and that she has had two steamers alongside her at Ternwatch for four days and came ninety miles on a tide. NO OFFICER CAME ASHORE, NO PAPER CAME ASHORE, NOBODY HAILED ANYBODY, NOBODY WENT ABOARD HER, AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE OF THE NOTICE WAS NOT READ ALOUD ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. A man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait, four days down that coast on his own account and not paid, said nine words on the third step from the bottom of that mole at about ten past five on the thirteenth, being that she asks at Ternwatch whether a boat has a man in her, and was asked nothing and was not thanked.**

### 6. The cost, and who paid it, and the bodies

**THE INJURY OF THIS BATCH IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S AND IT COSTS A REAL BILL AND A REAL ABSENCE, PER LOCK L27a, AND IT IS NOT TOBIAS WREN'S AND IT DOES NOT DISCHARGE VOLUME 06's. The top of two fingers of the left hand of a man of about forty-four, being the second of the six men of that harbor who are ashore with no boat, taken off by the shackle of an adrift mooring buoy at about half past two in the afternoon of Monday the twelfth, off the foul, and he was not in the water and did not go in, and he HAD WORKED THAT DAY FOR NOTHING and was not paid and was not asked to pay and was told the terms before he went out and said he knew them. NO BONESETTER ON THAT COAST ON A MONDAY AFTERNOON. A shipwright of about sixty set it at about four with a strip off a leech and a needle in about forty minutes; a bonesetter of about fifty came on the Saturday, said it was not a bonesetter's work, had not done it and would not touch it, and the first man to be seen by the second was a shipwright. The bill was five shillings and sixpence, being sixty-six pence, out of his own hand in coin, said twice and not a third time, and NO PART OF IT CAME OUT OF THAT YARD AND NONE OUT OF THE LIST OF THE HARBOR AUTHORITY AND NOTHING IN THAT OFFICE PUT IT ON ANYTHING. He is off the water nine days. The wife of that shipwright said at her door that he is one of about eleven people of that harbor who cannot read the notice, and two people heard it and one of them wrote it down, and he was not added to the count because nobody asked and the count is two people counting separately and adding.**

**AND THE OTHER BODIES, all of them unpaid and all of them on the page: forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid; forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two who is not on the stone; three marks to a man of Ashtide, unsent for; seven pence to that yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, chest shut, NOT ASKED IN SIXTY DAYS, no digit printed; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure; four days of a packet man's time on that coast, not paid, no figure entered because this yard does not know what a day of his is worth; and six men with no boat, of whom one took a day's wage and one of whom worked for nothing and was hurt, and a page on a mole that says a boat and says no figure.**

NONE OF THE ABOVE IS A WITNESS, A SYMBOL, AN OFFICER, A MEMBER OF ANYTHING OR A COURIER, and the woman of about fifty-eight would not accept the word symbol and was not asked to.**

### 2. The money, and it closes in one line

**THE BAG IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE AT THE OPEN. NOTHING CAME INTO THAT YARD ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NOTHING WENT OUT OF IT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PLUS NOTHING MINUS NOTHING IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, being one mark and three shillings and eightpence, and it is the same figure it was on the fourteenth of July and it did not move. THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY MINUS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR, BEING FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, being two marks and nine shillings and eightpence, and it is not going to be paid and nobody is to write one word under it saying anybody is going to. A boat with a man in her for a day is one hundred and sixty-eight pence, so that bag is a day and a piece of a day, and it is the most money in that bag since the eighteenth day of May past. NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL PAST.**

**THE ONE SUM THAT LEFT ANYBODY'S HAND IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS IS TWELVE PENCE AND IT IS NOT IN THAT BAG. A lodging behind the market in Veyr for one night, at six pence a night each, paid out of two people's own hands and out of nothing in that yard, entered so that nobody says afterwards that it was a figure in that yard's book, in a room that pays for nothing and in which nobody is paid by anybody. A man of about forty-four who lost the top of two fingers of his left hand on the twelfth of July paid five shillings and sixpence, being sixty-six pence, out of his own hand for it on the twelfth of July, and no part of that bill came out of this yard then or now. NOBODY IN THIS BATCH IS PAID BY THE PERSON WHO WANTS THE THING LOOKED AT, AND THAT IS ALSO THE SIXTH LINE OF THE SEVEN TERMS.**

### 4. The instruments this batch creates, and their full architecture

**NO CARD FILE EXISTS FOR THIS BATCH AND NONE WAS INVENTED. THE BATCH CREATED FIVE INSTRUMENTS AND TWO INSTANCES, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS FIXED HERE SO THAT NO LATER CHAPTER CAN MOVE IT.**

1. **THE PAPER OF THE FIFTEENTH OF JULY. Two leaves, folded twice, not sealed, carried down that coast in the coal in the inside pocket of an ordinary boat's own boy of about seventeen, who was not paid and did not know what it was and did not ask. Six words on the outside in a hand nobody in that shed knew: *for the holder of that writ*.** It says an inquiry will sit in Veyr in a room off a street behind the fish market there, on terms drawn by the Crown; the two people on that coast who can be shown the thing the terms are about are the holder of that writ and a woman of no office; both are asked to come; and a boat will wait at Ternwatch for three days and would not wait longer. **A paper carried down a coast in the coal is a paper carried down a coast in the coal, and it is not an order and it is not a summons, and this yard has no figure for three days of a boat waiting at Ternwatch and did not invent one. The boat that would wait was not taken, because it is a boat that waits and not a boat that is sent, and a man who is asked to a room does not get to send for a boat at a price he has not got.**
2. **THE SEVEN TERMS, being the second leaf of that paper, in a clerk's hand, and thereafter a sheet under glass on the wall of the room in Veyr, read out in full in about six minutes on the seventeenth of July, standing at the end of the table, read once and not twice, because twice is a conversation a man can join.** ONE — the room sits to look at how a harbor on that coast uses its own papers when it sends a boat out and brings one in. TWO — it may write down what it is shown and nothing else. THREE — nobody in the room has a title and nobody will be given one in it. FOUR — the clerk will write the hour and what was said and will read it back and give out nothing. FIVE — **the room requires a particular work to be ordered, being a foundation survey of that harbor's own mole where it stands in eleven feet, and the ordering is the whole of what the room does about it, and the work has not been done.** SIX — no person in that harbor is to be paid by the person who wants the thing looked at. SEVEN — the room convicts nobody and takes nothing and closes nothing. **THERE IS NO EIGHTH LINE, NO SCHEDULE, NO ENCLOSURE AND NOTHING ON THE BACK OF THEM, AND NO LINE IN THEM NAMES ANYBODY.**
3. **THE ROOM. Off a street behind the fish market in Veyr, up one flight of stairs, a window onto a yard where a pump stands, a table, six chairs round the table, a bench against the wall, and nothing on the walls but the seven lines under glass.** A man of about fifty keeps the room and not the inquiry, has no title in it and no seal in it, and sits at the end of the table and not at the head of it, with a leaf on the table in front of him with a day and an hour on it. **NOBODY ELSE IS IN THE ROOM ON ANY OF THE FIVE DAYS HE IS IN IT. NO TITLE IS SAID IN IT. NO SEAL LINE IS CARRIED IN IT BY ANYBODY AND NOBODY IN IT CARRIES A SEAL LINE THAT IS NOT ALREADY ON THE FACE OF A DOCUMENT IN THAT ROOM, AND THERE IS NO SEAL LINE ON ANY FACE IN THAT ROOM AT ALL EXCEPT THE TWO LEAVES IN HIS OWN COAT, WHICH HE DID NOT TAKE OUT.** A clerk of about sixty sits in a room off it with the door open, at a desk, with a book open and a pen in his hand, and writes the hour and the two names as they give them, and reads back, and asks nothing, and is asked nothing, and the pen goes on after they have stopped speaking. **THE ROOM CONVICTS NOBODY AND TAKES NOTHING AND CLOSES NOTHING AND IS NOT A COURT AND DOES NOT SPEAK IN ANYBODY'S MOUTH.**
4. **THE MUNICIPAL PAPER OF THE EIGHTEENTH OF JULY, from the office on the west basin, carried down in a coat by a man off the west quay who was given it to carry and not to read, who carried it to Veyr on the ordinary boat, asked for nothing and was thanked for nothing.** It names two boats and three men and a tide; the name at the foot of it is that of the clerk of that office, being the clerk of about sixty who has been twenty-two years in it and is owed a quarter and has no book and no power; it says the two boats may go out together under it and come in under it; and **it is a municipal document and not an instrument of anybody's.** **THE ROOM-KEEPER SAYS THAT ANY PERSON MAY PUT A PAPER IN FRONT OF THE ROOM, THAT THE QUESTION ON THE SECOND ONE WAS WHETHER IT MADE ANY DIFFERENCE TO THE FIRST, THAT THE ROOM WILL ANSWER ONLY WHAT THE LINES SAY, AND THAT THE MAN WHO LEFT THAT PAPER ON THAT TABLE WAS NOT IN THE ROOM AND HAD GIVEN NO NAME AND WOULD NOT BE ASKED FOR ONE IN IT.**
5. **THE COPY OF THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY PAST, in a clerk's hand, all eight lines of it, the fifth and the sixth marked at the side with a stroke of the pen, on the same table on the eighteenth of July, and nobody read it out loud. IT IS A COPY AND THE WALL IS THE WALL, AND THE WALL HAS NOT BEEN TOUCHED AND HAS NOT BEEN COMPARED WITH ANYTHING BY ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR.**

**AND THE TWO INSTANCES OF THE CLAUSE, WHICH ARE LEAVES IN AN OPEN DRAWER AND NOT INSTRUMENTS: the leaf of the twenty-second of July, in his own hand, saying what a room wants a paper for and asking a day before, which she read where she sat and did not have read out, and which he turned face down on the bench and she turned back up; and her answer of the twenty-third, in her own hand, not read out, saying that no paper using her hand will be shown in any room on the strength of it this week and that she will keep the five leaves where they are. THE ANSWER CAME INTO THE DRAWER WITH THE SHEET IN IT. NEITHER LEAF IS A SIGNATURE AND NEITHER IS AN ANSWER TO THE INSTRUMENT OF THE SEVENTH OF JULY, AND NEITHER REDUCES FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD BY ONE PENNY.**

**AND WHAT THE ROOM WROTE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE LEGAL THING AND NO MORE: that the door is open to such a convoy where the papers are in order; that where there are no papers there is no door; that a paper on a table is a paper on a table and nothing more; and that it binds nobody who does not use it. IT IS THE FIRST THING ANYBODY HAS COME OUT OF A ROOM WITH THAT IS A DOOR AND NOT A REFUSAL. IT IS A FOOT AND NOT A FLEET, IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT OF ANYBODY'S, IT BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT USE IT, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM SAID ANYBODY WAS IN THE WRONG FOR NOT USING IT, AND THAT LAST CLAUSE IS PROVED TWICE ON THE PAGE OF THIS BATCH BY TWO MEN WHO DID NOT USE IT.**

**NO STAGE WAS TAKEN IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND NONE WAS IMPROVED, RE-TAKEN OR RENAMED, PER LOCK L26. NO CHAPTER ENTERED AN ECHO, ENTERED A VESSEL, OR SURFACED A PRACTICE TRACE, AND NO PERSON OF THAT YARD WAS IN ANY WATER ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NONE IN ANY STONE. **THE PLATE AT THE FIFTH SEAM, PER LOCK L8, AND ITS ONE INSTRUMENT AND NO OTHER. THE PLATE IS NOT REACHED, NOT MEASURED, NOT TOUCHED, NOT ASKED ABOUT AND NOT CLOSED, IT IS NOT NAMED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, AND THE ONLY THING ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR SAID ABOUT IT WAS SAID BY A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE ON A STAIRWELL IN A CITY, TO THE STAIRWELL AND NOT TO HIM: *they have ordered it and they have not done it, and nobody in that harbor wants it done*. THE TERMS WERE CARRIED BY A MAN OFF THE WEST QUAY TO A ROOM FOUR DAYS' WATER AWAY, AND NOBODY WENT BACK FOR THE PLATE AND NOBODY ASKED.**

**THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY PAST: on its wall in a different street for fifty-eight days at the open of this batch and sixty-eight at the close, not touched, not withdrawn, not compared with anything by anybody in that harbor, and NOT COMPARED WITH THE PAGE ON THE MOLE. A clerk's-hand copy of it went onto a table in a room in a city on the eighteenth with its fifth and sixth lines marked, and this is the first time in this series that any of it has been off its wall in a copy, and the wall itself is unmoved and the two are told apart on the page. The fifth clause is a breach and the sixth clause is free, and the sixth clause has been the reason that harbor is open since the seventeenth of May, and it was written by an office that did not write it for that harbor. The two older naval notices further along the same wall are still on it. The chandler's note stands at thirty-one with its three counts at twenty-two, thirteen and eleven, unadvanced and not re-written. The delayed note stands at eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them, unmeasured, and nobody may name the call. Physic stands at fourteen pence with *none in this harbor*. The four returns stand and there is no fifth. The first echo's witness is where he is. The compartment is spent and the three Gannet documents stay three documents and the manifest's discrepancy was not restated in either form and no compartment was named.**

**THE TENDER. A small steam tender of about ninety tons at the outer water of that harbor from about half past two on Saturday the tenth to the close of the twenty-fourth, FIFTEEN DAYS, OUTSIDE THE LINE, with two lines out. NOBODY ENTERED HER, NOBODY SPOKE TO ANYBODY IN HER, NO OFFICER CAME ASHORE, NO PAPER CAME ASHORE, NOBODY HAILED ANYBODY, AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE OF THE NOTICE WAS NOT READ ALOUD ON ANY OF THE FIFTEEN DAYS. A young man of about twenty-three in her own wheelhouse with a telescope came out onto the roof twice in ten days and looked at that harbor and came back in. A man of nineteen at the wheel of a vessel of perhaps eighteen tons was patient with a bight of line round a bollard and did not cut it on any day the page gives him one. A man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait, whose nine words at a mole step on the thirteenth of July are the only thing anybody in that harbor knows about a vessel of ninety tons, SAYS NOTHING FURTHER IN THIS BATCH AND IS NOT ASKED. THE THIRD CHANNEL ON THE BORROWED INSTRUMENT IS CARRIED AND NOT MEASURED AND THE INSTRUMENT WENT BACK UP THAT COAST ON THE TUESDAY OF THE PREVIOUS BATCH AND HAS NOT COME BACK.**

### 6. The cost, and who paid it, and the bodies

**THE COST OF THIS MOVEMENT IS NOT A BILL AND IT IS NOT AN INJURY. IT IS A DAY AND A LEAF AND THE ASKING, AND A PAID NIGHT'S LODGING IN A CITY OUT OF TWO PEOPLE'S OWN HANDS, AND A WAGE TUESDAY THAT DID NOT MOVE.** A man of about forty-four is on the seventh, eighth and ninth days off the water of his nine and goes back on the tenth with the binding still on and as a boat's man and not a master, not paid and not asked to pay, told the terms before he went and saying he knew them; a shipwright of about sixty says the binding would hold for a boat's work and not for a buoy's; a bonesetter of about fifty looks at it from three paces off and says it is not a bonesetter's work, has not done it and will not touch it; and neither of them asked for anything and neither was asked. **HIS BILL OF FIVE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE WAS PAID ON THE TWELFTH OF JULY OUT OF HIS OWN HAND AND NO PART OF IT CAME OUT OF THAT YARD AND NONE OUT OF THE LIST OF THE HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT IS NOT PAID TWICE.**

**AND THE BODIES, all of them unpaid and all of them on the page: forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid, and she was in a city for five days and in this room on the twentieth of July and said she has no figure for what a refusal costs and will not invent one; forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two who is not on the stone; three marks to a man of Ashtide, unsent for; seven pence to that yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, chest shut, NOT ASKED IN SEVENTY DAYS, no digit printed; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure; six men with no boat and a page on the mole saying a boat and no figure, of whom one took a day's wage on the twelfth of July, one worked that day for nothing and lost two fingers, and four have had nothing and were not told there was anything; and a harbor poorer on the twenty-fourth of July than on the fourteenth of May, the cheapest oil at four hundred and fifty pence with February's three hundred and seventy-eight above it and both dates on the board, the mole-head light out, the hose dead until the spring, the tide gang four men short, the reeve's office's list not a schedule, and the cistern charged three times and walked on none.**

### 7. The people inherited and the ones brought in

Inherited and on the page this batch: a herring skipper of fifty-one with a boat of his own and municipal papers who will not use them for a convoy and about whom nobody said he was wrong; a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons who has no papers and wants none, and about whom nobody said he was wrong; a man of about fifty-one of the six with a page on the mole, who asked whether there was a day's work and was told there was not; a man of about forty-four of the six, ninth day off the water and then back on it; a man of the tide gang with a hod; a man of about thirty-two with the hose at the standpipe; a copyist of about fifty-nine in a room off that market, copying what she has never asked about, not asked in this batch and not to be; a chandler of about fifty with his counter shut to one man and his wife doing the counting, not asked a third time; a shipwright of about sixty and a bonesetter of about fifty; a man of about nineteen at a wheel with a boat's hook and a young man of about twenty-three in a wheelhouse with a telescope, both at the outer water; the clerk of about sixty of the office on the west basin, twenty-two years in it and owed a quarter, whose name is at the foot of the municipal paper and who is not in the room. **Brought in by this batch and available to later movements: a man of about fifty who keeps the room in Veyr, has no title in it and no seal in it, and sat at the end of the table; a clerk of about sixty in a room off that room who wrote the hour and the two names and asked nothing and was asked nothing; a man off the west quay who carried a paper in a coat and was thanked for nothing; a boy of about seventeen who carries messages for a penny and did not know the street and asked twice; a master of a coal boat at a tiller who asked them nothing; a boy of about seventeen who minds sheets and did not know what boat he was minding them for. ### 2. The money, and it closes in one line

**THE BAG IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE AT THE OPEN. One hundred and sixty-eight pence went out on Tuesday the twenty-seventh, being a boat of perhaps eighteen tons and a man in her for a day at one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, being the figure in chalk on the slate at the end stall of that market, paid in coin on the flat of the mole head stone at about a quarter to seven in the morning before she sailed. One hundred and sixty-eight pence came in on Saturday the thirty-first, being a day's work with a boat and two men at the third lay, being the same figure, paid in coin on the same bench stone at about four in the afternoon. NOTHING ELSE CAME IN OR WENT OUT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PLUS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT MINUS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, being one mark and three shillings and eightpence.**

**AND THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS RECOMPUTED FROM EACH DAY'S CLOSE AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD, PER LOCK L7 IN ITS SUCCESSOR FORM: FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, being two marks and nine shillings and eightpence, on the twenty-fifth, the twenty-sixth, the thirty-first, the first, the second and the third of August; and SIX HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, being three marks and ten shillings and fourpence, on the twenty-seventh, the twenty-eighth, the twenty-ninth and the thirtieth, being the four days on which the bag was thirty-six pence, being three shillings. NEITHER FIGURE IS GOING TO BE PAID AND NOBODY IS TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER EITHER SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO. A boat with a man in her for a day is one hundred and sixty-eight pence, so that bag is a day and a piece of a day, and it is the same figure it was on the twenty-fourth of July, and IT CAME BACK TO THAT FIGURE BY A HERRING SKIPPER OF FIFTY-ONE PAYING FOR A DAY'S CAULKING AND NOT BY ANYTHING THAT HAPPENED ON THE WATER, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF IT. NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL PAST.**

**THE ONE FIGURE THAT WAS PUT ON A PUBLIC OBJECT THIS BATCH, AND IT IS NOT THIS YARD'S: the price of a boat and a man for a day, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, put in chalk on a slate at the end stall of that market by a woman of about fifty-eight on Sunday the twenty-fifth, with the day of the month beside it, and given the reason herself, being that three men had asked her in one week and she was not saying it out loud a fourth time. A FIGURE PUT ON A BOARD CANNOT BE TAKEN OFF AGAIN AND THIS ONE IS NOT GOING TO BE. The said figure is also the figure of a day's work with a boat and two men at a berth in that harbor, and has been since the seventh of July past, and the two of them being the same number is a fact about that harbor and not about this yard. The said slate is in a market and is not on the market wall, and no part of this yard's figures, its fourth column or any part of its method is on any wall in that harbor, PER LOCK L24.**

**THE OTHER SUMS THAT LEFT ANYBODY'S HAND IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND NONE OF THEM IS IN THAT BAG: nothing. No lodging, no bill, no victuals bought, no toll, no fee. The herring skipper of fifty-one paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence to the yard and the yard charged him nothing over it and nothing under it. A man of about twenty-nine with a caulking iron brought his own bread and his own water out of his own hand and was not paid and was not asked to pay. A man of about forty-one in a boat of the line had a man in the water for two hours and twenty minutes and neither of them said a word about money and nothing was paid. A man of about fifty-three in a lighter was asked for nothing and given nothing and promised nothing. THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR'S BILL OF FIVE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, BEING SIXTY-SIX PENCE, WAS PAID OUT OF HIS OWN HAND ON THE TWELFTH OF JULY PAST AND IS NOT PAID TWICE.**

**THE TEN LINES ADDED TO THE FOURTH COLUMN IN THIS BATCH ARE THE NINETY-SIXTH THROUGH THE HUNDRED AND FIFTH, ONE A DAY, AND EACH IS ON THE FACE OF THE CHAPTER THAT CARRIES IT. 1. **THE BOARD, WHICH IS THE SHAPE OF THE FORM AND IS NOT THE FORM.** About a yard wide and a couple of feet long, of painted and ruled timber, lying on the after thwart of the third boat of a line of eight under a sloping piece of canvas where anybody in that boat can read it. Across the head, in block capitals filled in and not ruled, **one word: UNSEALED.** Under the head, two columns ruled the whole length, the left-hand one empty, and at the head of the right-hand one a date in May, and under that date **eleven marks at even spaces against dates beginning on the eighth of May and ending on the twenty-second of July.** At the foot, side by side and of the same age, **two impressions, the first round and about two inches across and the second smaller and struck close against it.** Above the head, on the bare timber where there is no ruling, **a date cut into the wood and gone white in the grain: THE FOURTEENTH OF FEBRUARY.** **NO DOCUMENT OF ANYBODY'S CHANGES HANDS ON THE WATER IN THIS BATCH, AND THE ONE THING THAT DOES CHANGE HANDS IS THE SLIP AT ITEM 2 BELOW, WHICH IS A PIECE CUT FROM THE BACK OF A TALLY MAN'S OWN PAD AND IS NOT A FORM AND IS NOT A COPY OF ONE. THE HOLDER DID NOT GO CLOSE ENOUGH TO EITHER IMPRESSION AND DID NOT ASK WHAT WAS ON EITHER AND IS NOT GOING TO. HE DID NOT GET THE FORM AND HE DID NOT GET A COPY OF IT AND NO CHAPTER MAY GIVE IT TO HIM.**
2. **THE SLIP OF PAPER.** About two inches by an inch, cut off a pad with a knife and not off a fold, in pencil sharpened with the blade of that knife in front of the holder, in a hand that is not the hand on the board. **Seven thousand on it and no name on it and nothing else on it and no mark against it, and no two columns and no column head and no unit of any kind.** It was put into the holder's hand in a boat on the twenty-seventh, at about noon, by a man of about twenty-six with a slate, who cut it off his own pad, wrote on it, held it out over the gunwale and said what it was not for — he said he was not going to put a number on the board, because a mark goes in that column when a hull comes alongside and he is not a hull — and said he did not know what it was a number of and could not ask anybody in a room. **HE DID NOT NAME IT, HE DID NOT EXPLAIN IT, HE WAS NOT ASKED WHY, AND HE ASKED FOR NOTHING AND WAS ASKED FOR NOTHING. THE HOLDER DID NOT LOOK AT IT IN THAT BOAT AND DID NOT LOOK AT IT IN HIS OWN BOAT AND LOOKED AT IT IN THAT SHED ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH, WHICH IS WHY `chapter-0374.md:25` SAYS IT HAD BEEN IN THE INSIDE POCKET OF HIS COAT SINCE THE MIDDLE OF THE DAY YESTERDAY, AND THAT IS NOW A FIGURE A READER CAN CHECK AGAINST `chapter-0373.md:65–79` AND COULD NOT BEFORE.** **NO MOUTH ON THE WATER EXPLAINED IT AND NO MOUTH IN THAT SHED EXPLAINED IT. It is entered in the second column as a slip of paper with a figure on it and no name on it, with the reason against the line that nobody said; it is not entered as a sum, because a figure not written out in pence and in marks and shillings and pence is not a sum of money to a shed that keeps a book; it has no column head and no name, because the day this yard gives a piece of paper a name is the day it has an opinion about it; it was not shown to any room, was not read out of that shed, and lies in a drawer with the sheet in it. IT IS NOT A WAGE, IT IS NOT A PRICE, IT IS NOT A BILL, IT IS NOT A FIGURE ANYBODY IS OWED, IT IS NOT A NUMBER THAT IS PAID OUT, IT CARRIES NO NAME, AND NO LATER CHAPTER MAY PUT A NAME ON IT OR A UNIT ON IT OR A HEAD ON IT.**

THE TOW TOOK HIS LINE AND NOT THE OTHER WAY ROUND. THE PAINTER OF A LIGHTER OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS PARTED. THE LIGHTER WAS HELD ELEVEN MINUTES, SAID TWICE BY A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-SIX AT A TELLER TO TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE, AND TOOK THE GROUND IN ABOUT SIX FOOT ON THE EDGE OF THE FAIRWAY.** A line is a thing a man may cut and a lighter is not. **ABOUT TWENTY-SIX TONS OF FLOUR IS IN SEVEN BOATS OF THAT TOW OF EIGHT, LYING OFF THE POINT AT ABOUT A MILE WITH TWO LIGHTS, WHICH WERE FIRST SEEN ON THE EVENING OF SUNDAY THE FIRST OF AUGUST AND WERE NOT THERE ON THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH, AND THEY HAVE NOT COME IN AND HAVE NOT BEEN HAILED AND HAVE NOT MOVED IN TWO DAYS, BEING THE INTERVAL RUNNING FROM THE HOUR THEY WERE FIRST SEEN AND NOT FROM THE HOUR THEY WERE FIRST MISSED.** THE LIGHTER ITSELF PUT IN ON THE NIGHT OF THE TWENTY-SEVENTH ON HER OWN ACCOUNT BECAUSE SHE WAS MAKING WATER AT HER SEAMS, WITH A FOOT AND FOUR INCHES OF WATER IN HER AND ABOUT TWO TONS OF FLOUR IN HER BOTTOM WET THROUGH THE BOARDS, AND NO SACK OF ANYTHING HAS COME ASHORE OUT OF HER AND NO FIGURE OF ANYTHING HAS BEEN WRITTEN AGAINST HER AND NO CLAIM HAS BEEN MADE ON HER AND THE CLERK OF THE OFFICE ON THE WEST BASIN WAS NOT SENT FOR. **AND THE SECOND COST, WHICH IS A MUNICIPAL RECORD AND WAS NOT EXPECTED AND IS THE SAME COST PAID A SECOND WAY: on the second of August a man of about fifty in the office on the west basin told the holder at about eleven in the morning that he was going to enter the twenty-seventh of July in the box on his table for days a boat of that harbor has gone out past the line without a declaration, a box which has been empty since the fifth of July. NOTHING ELSE CAME IN OR WENT OUT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. NEITHER FIGURE IS GOING TO BE PAID AND NOBODY IS TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER EITHER SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO. Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April past.**
