THE DERIVATION IS PRINTED HERE SO THAT IT IS CHECKABLE: BATCH 0001'S TEN DAYS, THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF AUGUST TO THE SECOND OF SEPTEMBER, WERE THE NINTH WEEK, AND THESE TEN DAYS ARE THE TENTH, AND NO FIGURE THAT WAS NOT ALREADY ON THE FACE OF BATCH 0001 HAS BEEN MOVED TO GET HERE.**
- **NOT ONE STANDING COUNT IS ON A DAY THAT IS NOT A DAY OF THIS BATCH, AND NO CHAPTER EXPLAINS A CALENDAR, AND NOTHING IN THE BOOK NOTICES THAT A CALENDAR IS A THING THAT CAN BE WRONG.**

### 2. The money, and it closes in one line

**THE WHOLE TEN DAYS OF MOVEMENT 2 IN MONEY, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF IT, NOT A SAMPLE. A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve pence, per lock L2, and the chain is re-derived off the face of the ten chapters and closed in one line, with the balance printed at the end of every entry so that a stranger can take it again without adding anything:**

**ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY AT THE OPEN, BEING ONE MARK, ON THURSDAY THE SECOND DAY OF SEPTEMBER, AND NOTHING CAME IN ON IT AND NOTHING WENT OUT OF IT, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON FRIDAY THE THIRD, LEAVING THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-EIGHT. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON SATURDAY THE FOURTH, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO. NOTHING ON SUNDAY THE FIFTH, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON MONDAY THE SIXTH, BEING A CAULKER'S DAY IN COIN ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON, LEAVING TWO HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FOUR. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON TUESDAY THE SEVENTH, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO. FORTY-FOUR OUT ON WEDNESDAY THE EIGHTH, BEING THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE FOR A LOAF AND A HALF, A CANDLE AND A POT AT ABOUT HALF PAST TEN IN THE MORNING, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT. NOTHING ON THURSDAY THE NINTH, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON FRIDAY THE TENTH, BEING A DAY'S WORK AT A BERTH AND A SECOND CAULKER'S DAY IN COIN ON THE SAME STONE AT THE SAME HOUR, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT. NOTHING ON SATURDAY THE ELEVENTH, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT. NOTHING ON SUNDAY THE TWELFTH, LEAVING FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT, BEING TWO MARKS SEVEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE.**

**AND THE TOTAL, WHICH IS THE CHAPTERS' OWN ARITHMETIC AND IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 420'S OWN OPENING BLOCK: FIVE HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE CAME IN ON THREE DAYS, BEING THE FOURTH, THE SEVENTH AND THE TENTH, AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT A DAY, AND THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY PENCE WENT OUT IN THREE PAYMENTS ON THREE DAYS, BEING ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT ON THE SIXTH, FORTY-FOUR ON THE EIGHTH AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT ON THE TENTH, AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY PLUS FIVE HUNDRED AND FOUR MINUS THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY IS FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT, WHICH IS THE BAG, AND THE TWO SUMS ARE NOT THE SAME FIGURE AND NEITHER OF THEM IS THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS.** **THE FIGURE OF SIX HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-TWO THAT STOOD IN CHAPTER 420 IN THE FIRST WRITING OF IT IS WRONG AND IS RULED OUT BY NAME, WITH ITS REASON AT § 12: FOUR DAYS WERE COUNTED WHERE THERE ARE THREE, AND THE ARITHMETIC WAS CARRIED ON THE WRONG FIGURE, AND THE FIGURE OF FIVE HUNDRED AND FOUR IS THE CHAPTERS' OWN, BEING THREE TIMES ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT.**

**AND THE FIGURE SHORT OF THAT WAGE, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-SIX PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS THREE SHILLINGS, ON THE THIRD; ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ONE MARK TWO SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, ON THE FOURTH, THE FIFTH AND THE SEVENTH; THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-SIX PENCE ON THE SIXTH; AND TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PENCE, BEING ONE MARK SIX SHILLINGS, ON THE EIGHTH, THE NINTH, THE TENTH, THE ELEVENTH AND THE TWELFTH. IT IS NEVER ZERO ON ANY DAY OF THE TEN AND NOBODY IS TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER IT SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO PAY IT. NOTHING HAS BEEN IN A TIN IN THAT SHED SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF APRIL PAST. THE ONLY OTHER SUMS THAT LEFT ANYBODY'S HAND IN TEN CHAPTERS ARE ONE PENNY FOR ONE SHEET OF GOOD PAPER, PAID OUT OF THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT'S OWN HAND AND NOT OUT OF THE BAG; FORTY PENCE INTO THE BOWL ON THE STEP OUT OF THE HAND OF A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE AND OUT OF HER OWN MONEY; AND NINEPENCE IN THAT BOWL ON SUNDAY THE FIFTH, WHICH IS THE LETTING MAN'S AND IS NOT A FIGURE OF ANYTHING. **

**AND EVERY FIGURE OF MONEY IN THE TEN CHAPTERS WAS RUN ONCE IN THIS PASS, IN THE HOUSE'S OWN ARITHMETIC, ON EVERY GLOSSED FIGURE OF THE FORM *<N> PENCE, BEING <MARKS, SHILLINGS AND PENCE>*. ELEVEN DISTINCT GLOSSES WERE EXTRACTED AND ELEVEN RESOLVE, AND THE COUNT IS ELEVEN AND NOT SIX: ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY AS ONE MARK; ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT AS ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE; TWO HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FOUR AS ONE MARK TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-SIX AS TWO MARKS THREE SHILLINGS; FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO AS TWO MARKS AND ELEVEN SHILLINGS; ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-EIGHT AS ONE MARK TWO SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT AS TWO MARKS SEVEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO AS ONE MARK SIX SHILLINGS; FORTY-FOUR AS THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE; SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE AS FOUR MARKS; AND ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY AS NINE MARKS. **THE TENTH OF THAT ELEVEN STOOD IN THE FIRST WRITING OF THIS PARAGRAPH AS *NINE HUNDRED AND SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE AS FOUR MARKS*, WHICH IS TWO FIGURES JOINED AND IS NOT A GLOSS OF ANYTHING ON ANY PAGE, AND IT IS REPAIRED HERE TO *SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE AS FOUR MARKS*, BEING THE WAGE, WHICH IS THE FIGURE THE HOUSE CALLS FOUR MARKS AND WHICH STANDS AS SUCH ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 418'S CLOSING BLOCK AND CHAPTER 420'S. THIS WAS FOUND IN THE SECOND REPAIR PASS AND IS THE SAME FAULT AS A LOCK CELL THAT REPORTS A COUNT OF ZERO IT HAS NOT GOT: A RECORD IS A PAGE AND A FIGURE ON A RECORD IS A FIGURE.** **FIVE OF THESE ELEVEN WERE WRONG IN THE FIRST WRITING AND ALL FIVE ARE REPAIRED, WITH THE FULL DISPOSITION AT § 12: FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO HAD BEEN GIVEN AS THREE MARKS TWELVE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, WHICH IS SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO; ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-EIGHT AS ONE MARK TWELVE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, WHICH IS THREE HUNDRED AND TWELVE; FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT AS TWO MARKS EIGHT SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, WHICH IS FOUR HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FOUR; AND TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO AS ONE MARK ELEVEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, WHICH IS TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX. THE FIGURES OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY FOR THE BARREL OF LAMP OIL, THREE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT FOR FEBRUARY, BEING THIRTY-SEVEN SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE AND THIRTY-ONE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, AND FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-PENCE LEAVES IN THE LAMP-OIL BOARD OF CHAPTER 418, ARE GLOSSED CORRECTLY WHERE THEY APPEAR.**

### 3. The four-column leaf, and its four columns at the close of Chapter 420

**AT THE HOUR OF THE READ-BACK ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT THAT MOLE HEAD AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING ON SUNDAY THE TWELFTH OF SEPTEMBER: ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO / SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE. AT THE CLOSE OF THAT DAY: ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-THREE / SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE.** Both sets of figures are on the face of Chapter 420's own reading and both definitions are printed there in the ship's own mouth, as they were on the face of Chapters 350, 360, 370, 380, 390, 400 and 410.

**THE WHOLE TWENTY-DAY RUN ACROSS THE TWO BATCHES, RE-DERIVED HERE OFF THE FACE OF TWENTY CHAPTERS AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANY OTHER BOOK: the first column's base is ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE at the close of Chapter 400 and takes one entry against each of the twenty days, no day in two of them, being ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-THREE at the close and ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO at the hour of the last read-back, the twentieth day's own entry going in after the reading. The second column's base is FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE at the close of Chapter 400, being four hundred and eighty-nine plus fifty and not three hundred and thirty-nine, and it takes five a day, three before the hour of that day's reading and two after it, being SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE at the close and SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN at the hour of the read-back, the arithmetic being five hundred and eighty-nine plus fifty.**

**AND THE FOURTH COLUMN IS RULED HERE AND PRINTED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 420'S OWN READING: IT STANDS AT ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE, IT HAS TAKEN NO LINE IN ANY OF THESE TEN DAYS NOR IN THE PREVIOUS TEN, THERE IS NO HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SIXTH LINE IN IT, IT IS NOT A CLOSURE AND IT IS NOT A STRIKE-OUT, AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD HAS CLOSED IT. THE COUNT OF THE ITALIC FOURTH-COLUMN LINE — THE LINE THAT BEGINS *What it is not* — ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT AND NOT A COINCIDENCE: A CHAPTER THAT ENTERS THAT LINE ENTERS A HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SIXTH LINE, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH DOES. THE REASON WAS ENTERED ONCE, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, IN THE YARD'S OWN MOUTH, AT ABOUT TEN PAST NINE IN THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF AUGUST, AND IS ENTERED AGAIN NOWHERE. EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DAILY BLOCKS CARRIES THE FACT THAT THE REASON HAS BEEN ENTERED AND NONE OF THEM ENTERS IT A SECOND TIME, AND THE FACT IS CARRIED IN ALL TEN AS ONE SENTENCE PER DAY, WRITTEN FOR THAT DAY.**

**THE THIRD COLUMN IS NONE ON TWENTY CONSECUTIVE DAYS AND NOBODY HAS BEEN APPOINTED TO IT, THE BOY'S HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT, WHICH HAS BEEN THERE SINCE THE FOURTH OF APRIL PAST, WAS NOT SCRATCHED OUT, THE NAME BESIDE IT WAS SAID ONCE ON THE THIRTEENTH OF MAY PAST AND NOT SAID AGAIN, AND HIS SURNAME IS ON NO PAGE OF THE TWENTY. THE THREE NOTS STANDING AGAINST THE EIGHTH OF JUNE PAST WERE NOT ASKED ABOUT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND ARE A TENTH WEEK UNASKED, AND THE FIFTH THING THAT IS A PERSON IS STILL NOT ON ANY SHEET.**

### 4. The public book, and the four figures a stranger with a pencil can take off it, and the omission

**THE PUBLIC BOOK OF WHAT THAT HARBOR HOLDS IS A BOUND VOLUME OF THIRTY HEADS ON THE FRIDAY THE THIRD DAY OF SEPTEMBER AND THIRTY-ONE ON THE SUNDAY THE TWELFTH, KEPT ON A LONG TABLE IN A ROOM OVER A JOINER'S SHOP AT THE TOP OF FISH STREET, BEGUN ON THE TWENTIETH OF APRIL PAST, AND IT IS A BOOK AND NOT AN OFFICE AND NOT A BUILDING AND NOT A COURT. IT DECIDES NO CONTESTED CLAIM, IT BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT SIGN IT, AND IT HAS NO LIST OF WHO CAME INTO THE ROOM. THE HEAD OF IT CARRIES FOUR LINES TO BE FILLED UNDER EVERY HEAD, BEING WHAT THE THING IS, WHERE IT CAME FROM, WHO STANDS WHERE IT IS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW, AND CARRIES IN ADDITION THAT THE REFUSALS ARE ON IT TOO AND ARE NOT SMALLER THAN THE REST, THAT NOTHING ENTERED IN IT IS A DECISION AND NOTHING ENTERED IN IT BINDS ANYBODY, THAT WHERE A MAN HAS SAID NO IT IS WRITTEN AS HE SAID IT WITH THE REASON AGAINST HIS NAME, AND THAT THE NAME OF A MAN WHO HAS SAID NO IS PUT IN AS PLAINLY AS THE NAME OF A MAN WHO HAS SAID YES. THE SECOND LINE OF THAT HEAD HAS BEEN RUBBED AT THE END FOR ABOUT FORTY YEARS OF AN ELBOW ON A TABLE.**

**AND THE PAGE BEARS THE RULE OUT, ON TWO ENTRIES AND IN THE OPEN. THE NINETEENTH HEAD, ENTERED ON THE NINTH OF JUNE PAST, IS OF TWO BOATS OF A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR OF THE SECOND LAY, OF NINE AND ELEVEN TONS, WHO CAME ON THE SEVENTH OF JUNE AND SAID NO TO HAVING THEM ENTERED, AND IT CARRIES FOUR LINES AND HIS NAME AND AN ELEVEN-WORD REASON, AND IT WAS READ OUT ALOUD IN THAT ROOM ON SUNDAY THE FIFTH OF SEPTEMBER FOR THE FIRST TIME. THE THIRTY-FIRST HEAD, ENTERED IN THAT ROOM ON THAT SAME SUNDAY AT TWENTY-SIX MINUTES PAST THREE IN THE AFTERNOON, IS THE FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE FOR A BARREL OF LAMP OIL, QUOTED THE FIRST OF JUNE, WITH FEBRUARY'S THREE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT PENCE STANDING VISIBLE ABOVE IT AND BOTH DATES ON THE BOARD, AND IT IS A REFUSAL BY A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT, GIVEN OUT LOUD AT ABOUT HALF PAST THREE IN THE AFTERNOON IN A ROOM WITH ABOUT TWENTY PEOPLE IN IT, AND HER REASON IS THAT A FIGURE READ OUT IN A ROOM IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF FIGURE FROM A FIGURE ON A BOARD, AND IT WAS ENTERED IN THE SAME HAND AND THE SAME SIZE AS EVERY OTHER LINE ON THAT PAGE WITH HER NAME AND THE HOUR AGAINST IT, AND IT WAS READ OUT, AND SHE WAS NOT THANKED IN THAT ROOM.**

**AND THE ENTRY THAT IS WRONG ON ITS OWN FACE IS THE TWENTY-SECOND, ENTERED ON THE EIGHTEENTH DAY OF JUNE PAST, BEING A PANEL OF WORKED GLASS ABOUT ELEVEN INCHES BY EIGHT OUT OF A HULL LANDED AT THE THIRD LAY ON THE FOURTH DAY OF JUNE, STANDING ON SHELF FOUR IN A STORE ON THE SECOND LAY WHERE NO KEEPER IS PAID. IT CARRIES THREE LINES AND THE THIRD OF THE THREE ENDS IN A DASH. THE FOURTH LINE, WHICH THE HEAD OF THAT VOLUME SAYS IS WHAT THE THING DOES NOT SHOW, IS NOT UNDER IT. THE HEAD-NOTE THE MAN WAS WORKING FROM IS A NOTE OF FOUR LINES PINNED TO THE LID OF THE BOX SINCE THE FOURTH OF JUNE, SIGNED WITH A NAME AND NOT AN OFFICE, AND IT SAYS THAT THE GLASS IS SOUND AT THE JOIN, THAT THE JOIN WILL TAKE A MEND AND IT WILL TAKE A BACKING, AND WHERE IT CAME FROM, AND IT DOES NOT SAY WHAT THE PANEL IS NOT FIT FOR. A PERSON ABOUT FOUR INCHES HIGH, WITH A SHOULDER AND A HIP AND A HAND, STANDING A LITTLE WAY INSIDE A DOOR, IS IN THAT PANEL, AND THREE PEOPLE SAW IT ON MONDAY THE SIXTH OF SEPTEMBER STANDING UP AND WITHOUT ITS BEING TAKEN OUT OF THE BOX.**

**AND THE FINDING, AS IT STANDS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 420: A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE, CALLED ARTHUR SENNETT, WHO WRITES FIGURES ON A SLATE FOR A BUYER AT A FISH STALL AND HAS DONE FOR NINE YEARS, COUNTED THE HEADS OF THAT VOLUME ON THE BACK OF HIS OWN LEFT HAND WITH A STUB OF PENCIL AND FOUND THAT OF THIRTY-ONE HEADS THIRTY CARRY FOUR LINES UNDER THE HEAD AND ONE CARRIES THREE, AND THAT THE HEAD OF THAT VOLUME SAYS FOUR, AND THAT THE ONE IS THE TWENTY-SECOND. HE WROTE IT IN FOUR LINES IN PENCIL ON THE INSIDE OF THE BACK COVER OF THAT VOLUME WITH HIS OWN NAME AND THE DATE. HE SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE WAS NOT IN THE ROOM ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF JUNE AND IS NOT GOING TO SAY WHO WAS, AND FOUR PEOPLE STOOD IN THAT ROOM WHILE HE SAID IT AND NOT ONE OF THE FOUR PUT THE QUESTION TO HIM. HE IS NOT A CONSERVATOR, NOT AN OFFICER, NOT A MEMBER OF ANYTHING, NOT A WITNESS, NOT A SYMBOL AND NOT A COURIER, HE WAS NOT SENT FOR, NOBODY SPOKE TO HIM, HE CAME UP A STAIR ON THE SATURDAY BECAUSE THE DOOR WAS OFF THE LATCH AND HE CAME UP A STAIR ON THE SUNDAY BECAUSE HE WAS GOING OUT, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT WAS STANDING IN A STREET ACROSS FROM THAT DOOR FROM A QUARTER PAST FOUR ON THE AFTERNOON AND WENT IN AFTER THE FINDING WAS MADE. THE FINDING COSTS NOTHING TO MAKE AND IT CANNOT BE UN-MADE.**

### 6. The people, and the two men who may not be moved

**ALDEN MARR: THE MAN ON THE FAR BENCH. THE FAR BENCH WAS OCCUPIED FROM ABOUT TEN IN THE MORNING UNTIL ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON ON ALL TEN OF THE TEN DAYS, WHICH IS TEN OCCUPIED DAYS. IT WAS NOT APPROACHED ON ANY OF THEM, THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM ON ANY OF THEM, NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT ON ANY OF THEM, THE ONE SHOE BESIDE HIM THAT IS NOT HIS IS ON EVERY ONE OF THEM AND HAS BEEN THERE SINCE THE THIRD OF MAY PAST, AND NEITHER BROTHER WENT NEAR THE OTHER AT ANY HOUR OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. THE COUNT OF THE NAME *ALDEN* IN THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, AND THE MAN IS ENTERED AS A BENCH AND A DAILY BLOCK AND NOTHING ELSE. RULED HELD ON ALL THREE CLAUSES.**

**TOBIAS WREN: THE COUNT OF *SIXTY-ONE* IN THE TEN CHAPTERS IS TEN AND EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DAILY BLOCKS CARRIES IT. THE COUNT OF *ELEVEN PIECES* IS TEN AND THE AGE OF THAT BOAT IS UNSTATED ON EVERY ONE OF THE TEN PAGES. HE IS NOT SENT FOR, NOT ASKED, NOT THANKED, NOT A TEACHER, NOT A DOOR AND NOT A SACRIFICE, AND HE IS NOT ALDEN MARR. **HE SAYS NOTHING AT ALL IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND THAT IS THE CORRECT USE OF HIM ONCE MORE.****

**ORS KEST: THE COUNT OF HIS NAME IN THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO AND HE IS ASKED NOTHING IN ANY OF THEM.**

**NELL CARROW, THE ROPEMAKER, AND WHAT THE TEN DAYS DID AND DID NOT DO WITH HER, RULED HERE SO THAT LATER MOVEMENTS CANNOT IMPROVE IT. SHE IS ABOUT SIXTY-ONE, OF THE THIRD LAY, WITH A BAD KNEE, A STICK, A ROOM SHE HAS HAD FOR ELEVEN YEARS AT NINE MARKS A YEAR, BEING ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, PAID OUT OF ROPE IN EVERY ONE OF THOSE ELEVEN YEARS, WITH A ROPE WALK ABOUT FORTY FEET LONG IN THE BACK OF IT THAT DOES NOT RUN. SHE ASKED ONE QUESTION AT THE END OF A TABLE ON SUNDAY THE FIFTH, IN HER OWN MOUTH, AND WAS ANSWED IN ONE SENTENCE. SHE WAS ASKED ONE THING, ONCE, ON THURSDAY THE NINTH, BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX, AND SHE ASKED HIM ONE BACK, AND NEITHER OF THEM ASKED THE OTHER A SECOND THING, AND THAT IS THE COUNT. SHE BROUGHT A BOX UP TWO FLIGHTS OF STAIRS BETWEEN ONE O'CLOCK AND HALF PAST TWO ON SUNDAY THE TWELFTH, ON HER OWN BACK AND HER OWN SHOULDERS, AND PUT A PANEL OF ABOUT ELEVEN INCHES BY EIGHT ON THE TABLE HERSELF, AND STOOD AT THE BACK OF THAT ROOM AGAINST THE WALL WITH HER STICK IN FRONT OF HER AND DID NOT LOOK AT IT AGAIN FOR THE REST OF THAT AFTERNOON. SHE SAID OUT LOUD THAT SHE IS NOT GOING TO BE THANKED AT THE TOP OF THAT STAIR OR AT THE BOTTOM OF IT, AND THAT IF ANYBODY IN THAT ROOM SAYS A KIND THING TO HER SHE WILL WALK OUT, AND THE MAN WHO READS THAT BOOK TOLD ABOUT TWENTY PEOPLE ON THE THURSDAY THAT SHE HAD SAID SO ON A THURSDAY AND WOULD NOT SOFTEN IT. SHE WAS NOT THANKED BY ANYBODY, NOBODY WAS CHARGED, NOBODY WAS MADE WHOLE, HER ROOM ON THE THIRD LAY IS STILL HERS, AND NO FIGURE IN THAT YARD'S OWN LEAF STANDS AGAINST HER, HER BOX, HER BAD KNEE OR THE TWO FLIGHTS OF STAIRS. THE VOLUME DOES NOT ASK HER ANYTHING TWICE AND IS NOT TO DO SO.**

**AND THE OTHERS, EACH ON A PAGE AND ON A DAY, NONE OF THEM A WITNESS: Hobb Lee, of about forty-six, who mends nets on the third lay and has done since he was nine, and who was on the wrong side of a paper he could not read at nine years old in that harbor and has thirty-seven years of not knowing, forty-six less nine; Tom Barlas, of about thirty-four, who lets a room out on a Sunday and takes the money in a bowl and has never written one of the people who came up that stair down; Ned Vaile, of about fifty-five, who marks at a fish quay and keeps the marks of a public book and is not paid for it and is not a conservator; Arthur Sennett, of about thirty-one, who writes figures on a slate for a buyer and has done for nine years; Walter Dunn, of about forty-one, who is the night man at the fish market steps and has been for eleven years; Simeon Gale, of about thirty-four, who has the keys to two stores on the second lay; Joel Harrow, of about twenty-six, who stacks empties at the quay; a woman of about fifty-eight with an end stall and a slate; a copyist of about fifty-nine with twenty-two years at a counter; a man of about forty-one who was in that room on the twelfth and could not tell in which order he had come down a flight of stairs; a man of about sixty-two who has sat on the same bollard at the head of a slip since June; a woman of about thirty-one with a barrow of fish; a man of about thirty-three with a tin can; and the men on the far bench.**

### 7. The cost, and the bodies, at the last page of the ten

**THE COST OF MOVEMENT 2 IS PAID IN SIX THINGS AND IN NOTHING ELSE. AN HOUR OF A WORKING MAN'S SUNDAY, given up twice on two Sundays, being about two hours and twenty minutes a Sunday of reading, a shilling not earned, and a bowl on a step that a man has to make whether anybody is in the room or not, and the whole of it his own. ELEVEN CONVERSATIONS IN DAYLIGHT ON A WEDNESDAY, in a street and in eleven doors, and eleven of them the same conversation and four of them longer than a minute and the shortest about forty seconds. TWO FLIGHTS OF STAIRS, twice, once up with a barrow and a box and once down with a box and a bad knee. WHAT CAME OFF A PANEL, being a cold in the teeth and a taste of iron like a nail and a man's own body not knowing which of two doors he came out of, in a room of about twenty people of whom eleven could not read, told out of a mouth. A HUNDRED AND FORTY MINUTES ON A JOINER'S TABLE ON A SATURDAY, by a man nobody knew was in the room, reading a book nobody asked him to read, which is where the finding came from and which cost him a Saturday he was not paid for. AND A HARBOR THAT IS POORER ON THE TWELFTH DAY OF SEPTEMBER THAN ON THE SECOND OF IT, WITH NO FLOUR IN THAT MARKET AND NO OIL IN THAT HARBOR SINCE THE TWENTY-NINTH DAY OF AUGUST AND A LIGHT OUT OF A MOLE HEAD.**

**NO MAN DIED, NO BODY IS NAMED, NO CASUALTY FIGURE IS PRINTED ON ANY PAGE, AND THE COUNT OF THE WORD *THOUSAND* IN A MOUTH IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, THE ONE OCCURRENCE BEING A GLOSS OF NINE MARKS A YEAR. NOTHING IN THE HARBOR IS BETTER AT THE LAST PAGE THAN AT THE FIRST.**

**AND THE STANDING LIST, ALL UNPAID AND ALL UNMOVED, AND NONE OF IT ENTERED IN FULL IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS, BECAUSE THE STANDING INVENTORY IS ENTERED IN FULL ONCE IN THIS VOLUME AND ONCE ONLY AND IT IS NOT THIS BATCH'S TO PRINT:** three marks to a man of Ashtide, whose anchor date of the eighth of August past is a legacy of an earlier entry and is ruled not repaired and may not be re-dated, advanced, reduced or paid; seven pence to that yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright, unargued, chest shut, not asked in one hundred and twenty days; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure; forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid; forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two. And standing with those six: a page of six names on a mole with a boat as a price and no figure; a municipal claim on one of the three things in the circuit custody room; a box in an office on the west basin that is no longer empty and another box on the other paper that is and that a man of about fifty wants left empty; a nine-line sheet with a seal on it in the front street, answered by nobody; and a slip of paper with a figure on it and no name on it in a drawer, not looked at, not priced, not headed.

### 8. What was done, in one paragraph, and what this batch may not be used for

**WHAT MOVEMENT 2 DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH: A ROOM OVER A JOINER'S SHOP AT THE TOP OF FISH STREET WAS FOUND TO HAVE A BOOK ON A TABLE IN IT, AND THE BOOK WAS READ THROUGH FROM THE FIRST PAGE TO THE LAST BY FOUR PEOPLE, AND ITS HEAD WAS READ OUT, AND THE SECOND LINE OF THAT HEAD HAS BEEN RUBBED AT THE END FOR ABOUT FORTY YEARS; A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX WHO MENDS NETS AND HAS DONE SINCE HE WAS NINE SAID HE WOULD READ EVERY HEAD-NOTE IN THAT BOOK OUT LOUD ON A SUNDAY AND WRITE HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR UNDER EACH ONE IN HIS OWN HAND ON THE DAY, AND HE DID IT TWICE IN TEN DAYS; FOUR LINES WERE PUT ON THE DOOR OF THAT ROOM BY A NIGHT MAN WHO FOUND A LAMP BURNING IN IT ON THE NINETEENTH OF AUGUST, AND THE FOUR LINES NAME ELEVEN PEOPLE ASKED ONE AT A TIME AND ONE OF THE ELEVEN WAS IN THAT ROOM AND THE FINDER WILL NOT SAY WHICH; ELEVEN PEOPLE IN THAT HARBOR WERE COUNTED, SIX BY A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT IN HER OWN TRADE AND FIVE BY A MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-SIX ON A QUAY, AND SIX AND FIVE IS ELEVEN, AND A WEEK LATER A MAN WALKED ROUND THAT HARBOR ON HIS OWN TWO FEET AND TOLD ALL ELEVEN, ONE AT A TIME, IN DAYLIGHT, THAT THERE WAS A PAPER ON THAT DOOR, AND TOLD NONE OF THEM WHAT WAS ON IT; A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT REFUSED OUT LOUD IN THAT ROOM TO HAVE THE FIGURE OF LAMP OIL ENTERED IN THAT BOOK AND HER NO WENT ON THE PAGE AT THE SAME SIZE AS EVERY OTHER LINE WITH HER NAME AND THE HOUR AGAINST IT; A PANEL OUT OF A HULL LANDED AT THE THIRD LAY ON THE FOURTH OF JUNE WAS FOUND TO HAVE A PERSON IN IT AND THREE LINES UNDER ITS HEAD WHERE THE HEAD OF THAT BOOK SAYS FOUR, AND A MAN WHO ENTERED IT ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF JUNE SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE ASKED ONE QUESTION IN THAT ROOM AND WAS GIVEN NOTHING AND PUT A DASH; A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY ASKED AT THE END OF THAT TABLE WHETHER THAT BOOK HOLDS A THING A PERSON MADE THEMSELVES, WAS TOLD IT DOES NOT, BROUGHT HERS UP TWO FLIGHTS OF STAIRS SEVEN DAYS LATER, PUT IT ON THE TABLE HERSELF AND LOOKED AT IT; A ROOM EMPTIED; A BOX WENT DOWN THOSE STAIRS ON A BAD KNEE AND NOBODY THANKED HER; THE BOOK WAS SHUT AND SQUARED TO THE EDGE OF A TABLE; AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE WHO WRITES FIGURES ON A SLATE FOR A LIVING COUNTED THE HEADS ON THE BACK OF HIS OWN HAND AND FOUND THAT ONE OF THIRTY-ONE CARRIES THREE LINES WHERE THE HEAD OF THAT BOOK SAYS FOUR, AND WROTE IT IN PENCIL ON THE INSIDE OF THE BACK COVER, AND WAS NOT ASKED BY ANYBODY WHO PUT IT THERE.**

**WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NOT BE USED FOR: it may not be used to say that the omission has been repaired, because it has not been, and a dash is a hole and not a falsehood and the hole is still there; it may not be used to say that anybody has been told who left the dash, because nobody has, and the man who counted says he was not in that room on the eighteenth of June and that is the whole of the answer he has; it may not be used to say that the eleven have been told what is on the paper on that door, because they have not and are not going to be, and every one of them will read it on that door with his own eyes in his own time; it may not be used to say that a woman of about sixty-one was thanked, made whole, put back in her room, given a figure, put on a sheet, asked a second thing or charged with anything, because none of those happened and none of them is going to; it may not be used to say that what came off that panel is a disease, a fever, a complaint, glass, an illness or a contagion, because it is a cold in the teeth and a taste of iron and a body not knowing which of two doors it came out of, and it is told out of a mouth; it may not be used to say that anybody is going to pay the six hundred and forty pence, or the twenty-two lines of a wage column, or the eight marks and a day of a boat, or the three marks to a man of Ashtide, because nothing in this volume moves any of them; it may not be used to date the second entry into the room on the hill, which is the fifth of October and is the climax's; and it may not be used to put the count of three hundred and ninety-one on a wall, or into the book in Fish Street, or into a mouth.**

THE COUNT OF *SIXTY-ONE* ON THE TEN DAILY BLOCKS IS THE COUNT OF THE AGE OF THE MAN ON THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE AND IT IS NOT THE COUNT OF ANYBODY ELSE, AND THE CHAPTERS THAT GIVE THE ROPEMAKER OF THE THIRD LAY THE SAME AGE GIVE HER IT IN WORDS AND NEVER IN A FIGURE, AND THE AUDIT RULES THAT THE TWO ARE NOT TO BE RUN TOGETHER AND THAT A READER WHO RUNS THEM TOGETHER IS READING A COINCIDENCE AND NOT A FIGURE.**

### 13. The hand-over to Batch 0003, eight items and no more

1. **THE BOOK, THE ROOM, THE HEAD-RULE, THE FOUR LINES, AND THE THIRTY-ONE HEADS AND WHAT IS ON THEM, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX WHO READS THEM AND THE HOUR HE PUT UNDER EACH, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR WHO LETS THE ROOM OUT AND HAS NEVER WRITTEN ONE PERSON DOWN.** Thirty heads on the third of September and thirty-one on the twelfth; thirty carrying four lines and one carrying three; the twenty-second being the panel out of the hull landed at the third lay on the fourth of June, with a person in it and a dash at the end of its third line. **NO LATER MOVEMENT MAY REPAIR THE TWENTY-SECOND, MAY REMOVE THE DASH, MAY SAY WHO LEFT IT, MAY PUT IT ON A WALL, OR MAY PUT THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES, ITS FOUR COLUMNS OR ITS METHOD ONTO THAT PAGE OR ONTO ANY WALL IN MORROW QUAY.**
2. **THE PAPER OF FOUR LINES AT THE TOP LEFT OF THAT DOOR, PUT UP ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF AUGUST PAST BY A NIGHT MAN WITH A DRAWING-PIN UNDER A FOLD OF OILLED PAPER, WHICH NAMES ELEVEN PEOPLE ASKED ONE AT A TIME AND SAYS THAT ONE OF THE ELEVEN WAS IN THAT ROOM ON THE NIGHT OF THE NINETEENTH OF AUGUST, AND THAT THE FINDER WILL NOT SAY WHICH, AND THAT ANYBODY IN THAT LIST IS TO BE OFF OUT OF THIS HARBOR BEFORE THE TWENTIETH DAY OF SEPTEMBER NEXT; THE ELEVEN ARE COUNTED, UNNAMED, AND HAVE BEEN TOLD ONLY THAT THE PAPER IS THERE; AND IT HAS BEEN ANSWERED BY NOBODY AND IS NOT TO BE ANSWERED BY ANYBODY IN THIS VOLUME.**

### 6. The people, and the two men who may not be moved

**ALDEN MARR: THE MAN ON THE FAR BENCH. THE FAR BENCH WAS OCCUPIED FROM ABOUT TEN IN THE MORNING UNTIL ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON ON ALL TEN OF THE TEN DAYS, WHICH IS TEN OCCUPIED DAYS. IT WAS NOT APPROACHED ON ANY OF THEM, THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM ON ANY OF THEM, NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT ON ANY OF THEM, THE ONE SHOE BESIDE HIM THAT IS NOT HIS IS ON EVERY ONE OF THEM AND HAS BEEN THERE SINCE THE THIRD OF MAY PAST, AND NEITHER BROTHER WENT NEAR THE OTHER AT ANY HOUR OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. THE COUNT OF THE NAME *ALDEN* IN THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, AND THE MAN IS ENTERED AS A BENCH AND A DAILY BLOCK AND NOTHING ELSE. RULED HELD ON ALL THREE CLAUSES.**

**TOBIAS WREN: THE COUNT OF *SIXTY-ONE* IN THE TEN CHAPTERS IS TEN AND EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DAILY BLOCKS CARRIES IT. THE COUNT OF *ELEVEN PIECES* IS TEN AND THE AGE OF THAT BOAT IS UNSTATED ON EVERY ONE OF THE TEN PAGES. HE IS NOT SENT FOR, NOT ASKED, NOT THANKED, NOT A TEACHER, NOT A DOOR AND NOT A SACRIFICE, AND HE IS NOT ALDEN MARR. **HE SAYS NOTHING AT ALL IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND THAT IS THE CORRECT USE OF HIM ONCE MORE, AND HE IS THE ONLY PERSON IN THE TEN WHO CHANGED WHAT HE WAS DOING ON THE LAST DAY OF THE TEN, BEING THAT HE GOT UP OFF THE NINTH PIECE AT ABOUT HALF PAST THREE IN THE AFTERNOON AND WENT HOME, WHICH HE HAS NOT DONE ON ANY OF THE THIRTY DAYS.**

**ORS KEST: THE COUNT OF HIS NAME IN THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO AND HE IS ASKED NOTHING IN ANY OF THEM.**

**NELL CARROW, THE ROPEMAKER, AND WHAT THE TEN DAYS DID TO HER, RULED HERE SO THAT LATER MOVEMENTS CANNOT IMPROVE IT. SHE IS ABOUT SIXTY-ONE, OF THE THIRD LAY, WITH A BAD KNEE, A STICK, A ROOM SHE HAS HAD FOR ELEVEN YEARS AT NINE MARKS A YEAR, BEING ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, PAID OUT OF ROPE IN EVERY ONE OF THOSE ELEVEN YEARS, WITH A ROPE WALK ABOUT FORTY FEET LONG AND ABOUT FIVE FEET WIDE IN THE BACK OF IT THAT DOES NOT RUN. SHE ASKED ONE QUESTION AT THE END OF A TABLE ON SUNDAY THE FIFTH OF SEPTEMBER PAST, IN HER OWN MOUTH, AND WAS ANSWERED IN ONE SENTENCE. SHE WAS ASKED ONE THING, ONCE, ON THURSDAY THE NINTH OF SEPTEMBER PAST, BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX, AND SHE ASKED HIM ONE BACK, AND NEITHER OF THEM ASKED THE OTHER A SECOND THING, AND THAT IS THE COUNT. ON SUNDAY THE NINETEENTH OF SEPTEMBER, AT ABOUT ELEVEN IN THE MORNING, A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT WHO TAKES THE RENTS IN TWO HOUSES ON THAT SLIP TOLD HER THAT THE ROOM WAS NOT HERS AFTER THE END OF THE QUARTER, AND HE ASKED HER NOTHING, AND SAID IN HIS OWN MOUTH THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO ASK HER ANYTHING BECAUSE AN ANSWER GIVEN IN A STREET STAYS IN THE HEAD OF THE MAN WHO ASKED FOR IT AND HE WOULD RATHER HAVE ASKED NOTHING AND BE WRONG THAN HAVE ASKED AND BE RIGHT. SHE ASKED ONE QUESTION, WHICH WAS WHEN, AND WAS TOLD, AND SAID NOTHING ELSE. SHE CUT THE ROPE OFF HER BOX AT ABOUT ONE O'CLOCK, TOOK THE PANEL OUT AND PUT IT BACK IN AND KNOTED THE ROPE THE WAY SHE KNOTS IT, AND CARRIED THE BOX DOWN THE SLIP ON HER OWN BAD KNEE BACKWARDS WITH THE WHEEL OF THE BARROW AGAINST THE STEP ABOVE HER BETWEEN ONE O'CLOCK AND HALF PAST TWO, AND NOBODY ON THAT LAY CARRIED ANYTHING FOR HER AND NOBODY OFFERED. NOBODY WAS CHARGED, NOBODY WAS MADE WHOLE, NO FIGURE IN THAT YARD'S OWN LEAF STANDS AGAINST THAT ROOM OR THAT ROPE WALK OR THOSE ELEVEN YEARS OR THAT BOX OR THAT KNEE, NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR WAS TOLD THAT ANYTHING WAS DONE FOR HER, AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS THANKED HER. SHE IS NOT A SYMBOL, NOT AN ALLY, NOT A QUESTION THE VOLUME IS ASKING, AND SHE DOES NOT GET THAT ROOM BACK AT ANY PAGE OF THIS VOLUME. THE VOLUME DOES NOT ASK HER ANYTHING TWICE AND IS NOT TO DO SO.**

**AND THE OTHERS, EACH ON A PAGE AND ON A DAY, NONE OF THEM A WITNESS: Hobb Lee, of about forty-six, who mends nets on the third lay and reads in a market on a Thursday; Tom Barlas, of about thirty-four, who lets the room out on a Sunday; Ned Vaile, of about fifty-five, who keeps the marks of a public book; Arthur Sennett, of about thirty-one, who writes figures on a slate for a buyer; Walter Dunn, of about forty-one, whose paper of four lines ended its fourth line on the twentieth; a woman of about fifty-eight with an end stall and a slate; a copyist of about fifty-nine with twenty-two years at a counter; a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers; a man of about thirty-one of that lay with a chart in a bag; a man of about twenty-six who stacks empties at a quay; a man of about twenty-nine who owns a boat of about eleven tons; a boy of about fifteen on a pump; a man of about forty-four off the water with two fingers of his left hand stiff; a chandler of about fifty with a wife who keeps the count; a man of about fifty who works at a table with two papers on it; and the men on the far bench.**

### 7. The cost, and the bodies, at the last page of the ten

**THE COST OF MOVEMENT 3 IS PAID IN EIGHT THINGS AND IN NOTHING ELSE. A HALF-AN-HOUR OF A BOY'S MORNING AND A PAPER, being a boy of about seventeen who carried a message in a slip at ten o'clock on the fourteenth and stood on a step for twenty-five minutes at the head of the third lay with no reason in his hand to say what he was doing, and the man he was going to did not send it again, and nobody has asked that boy where he was. THREE HOURS ON A HARD, being a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers put round to the back of a slip from about seven until about ten on the eighteenth with about four other boats and a cup of tea off a stove belonging to somebody else. EIGHT FATHOMS OF TARRED ROPE AT FOUR SHILLINGS, BEING FORTY-EIGHT PENCE, refused at a counter to a man of about forty-four who carried a piece of worked glass out of a boat's hold in June and was not asked why. A DAY'S WORK AND A MARKET, being a man of about thirty of about nine tons who did not take his boat out on the Saturday, on the Monday, on the Tuesday or on the Wednesday, and lost a word off a sheet he cannot read. A ROOM OF ELEVEN YEARS AT NINE MARKS A YEAR, being one thousand four hundred and forty pence paid out of rope, put out on the nineteenth by a man who asked her nothing. A COLD IN THE TEETH, A TASTE OF IRON LIKE A NAIL AND A MAN'S OWN BODY NOT KNOWING WHICH OF TWO HATCHES HE CAME UP OUT OF, off a bell at about eleven foot beside a crate of three pieces of worked glass, given to two men on a berth and to two people in a shed and to nobody in a market. A READING OF SIX LINES IN THE MIDDLE OF A MARKET, about two hours and forty minutes of a net-mender's working day given up on a Thursday, and a reading of nine heads in a room on the Sunday, and neither of them paid for. AND A HARBOR THAT IS POORER ON THE TWENTY-SECOND DAY OF SEPTEMBER THAN ON THE THIRTEENTH, WITH NO FLOUR IN THAT MARKET, NO BARREL OF LAMP OIL SINCE THE TWENTY-NINTH DAY OF AUGUST, A FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE ON A BOARD THAT WAS NOT CLEARED AND A SHEET PUT UP ON THE OUTSIDE OF IT, A LIGHT OUT OF A MOLE HEAD, A BERTH HELD, A COUNTER SHUT, A WINDOW HELD ON A MAN WHO CANNOT READ IT, AND FORTY-EIGHT WEEKS FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE AGAINST ANY OF THEM.**

**NO MAN DIED, NO BODY IS NAMED, NO CASUALTY FIGURE IS PRINTED ON ANY PAGE, AND THE COUNT OF THE WORD *THOUSAND* IN A MOUTH IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, THE ONE OCCURRENCE BEING A GLOSS OF NINE MARKS A YEAR. NOTHING IN THE HARBOR IS BETTER AT THE LAST PAGE THAN AT THE FIRST, AND THE BAG IS HIGHER BY A HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FOUR PENCE AND THE HARBOR IS NOT.**

### 8. What was done, in one paragraph, and what this batch may not be used for

**WHAT MOVEMENT 3 DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH: A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY OF THAT THIRD LAY WHO CANNOT READ CAME UP A SLIP ON THE THIRTEENTH AND ASKED WHETHER THERE WAS A PAPER AGAINST HIM AND WAS TOLD THAT THERE WAS ONE AT A COUNTER IN AN OFFICE OFF THE WEST BASON, THAT NOBODY IN THAT SHED HAD SEEN IT, THAT IT COULD NOT BE READ TO HIM THERE BECAUSE HE WOULD HAVE THE READER'S HEAD AND NOT THE PAPER, AND THAT NOBODY KNEW WHETHER IT WAS AGAINST HIS BOAT; A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OFF A SCREW-STEAM PACKET OUT OF BRAMBLE STRAIT LANDED A SACK OF PRINTED SHEETS AND SAID HE HAD BEEN GIVEN THE LOT AT THE TOP OF A GANGWAY BY A MAN BEHIND A COUNTER WITH A BOOK OPEN WHO DID NOT ASK HIS NAME; TWENTY-FOUR SHEETS WENT THROUGH A COPYIST'S COUNTER ON THE FOURTEENTH AT A PENNY A SHEET AND THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-NINE DID NOT ASK; A BOY OF ABOUT SEVENTEEN HAD A MESSAGE TAKEN OUT OF HIS HAND IN A STREET ON THE FOURTEENTH BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR OFF THE WATER AND DID NOT GET IT BACK AND LOST THE HOUR HE WAS GOING TO BE SOMEWHERE ELSE IN; ON THE FIFTEENTH A SHEET OF SIX LINES WITH A DATE AT THE HEAD AND A CHARGE AT THE FOOT WENT UP ON A WALL AT THE BACK OF AN END STALL ON THE OUTSIDE OF A FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE THAT WAS NOT TAKEN DOWN FIRST AND CANNOT BE TAKEN OFF AGAIN, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR SAID THAT HE COULD NOT SAY IT WAS A LIE, AND ABOUT THIRTY PEOPLE STOOD IN FRONT OF IT BY NOON AND A CAREFUL MAN TRIED IT AND COULD NOT KNOCK IT DOWN; ON THE SIXTEENTH THAT SHEET WAS READ ALOUD IN THAT MARKET AT ELEVEN BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX WITH HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR AGAINST IT, FOUR MEN SAID OUT LOUD THEY HAD BEEN IN THE ROOM ON THE TWELFTH, AND THE SAME MAN SAID HE WOULD NOT READ A CLAIM OUT AT THAT TABLE AS A CLAIM; ON THE SEVENTEENTH A CHANDLER'S COUNTER SHUT TO A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR AND A PAPER WENT UP ON A COUNTER IN AN OFFICE OFF THE WEST BASON WITH A HAND ON IT AND NO NAME ON IT; ON THE EIGHTEENTH A BERTH WAS HELD ON A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WITH A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS HELD AND A CLAIM WINDOW WAS TOLD TO A MAN WHO CANNOT READ THE PAPER ON IT; ON THE NINETEENTH A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-ONE WAS PUT OUT OF A ROOM SHE HAS HAD FOR ELEVEN YEARS BY A MAN WHO ASKED HER NOTHING; ON THE TWENTIETH THE FOURTH LINE OF A PAPER ON A DOOR IN FISH STREET ENDED AND WAS ANSWERED BY NOBODY AND A MAN WENT DOWN IN A BELL AND CAME UP WITH A COLD IN HIS TEETH; ON THE TWENTY-FIRST A BOY TOLD THAT MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY SOMETHING HE HAD BEEN TOLD IN TURN AND HE WENT HOME AND DID NOT TAKE HIS BOAT OUT; AND ON THE TWENTY-SECOND THE LEAF WAS READ BACK AT THE MOLE HEAD WITH BOTH DEFINITIONS ON THE FACE OF IT, AND THE BAG WAS FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PENCE, AND THERE IS NO FLOUR AND NO OIL AND A LIGHT OUT AND A FIGURE ON A BOARD THAT DID NOT COME DOWN.**

**WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NOT BE USED FOR: it may not be used to say that the sheet on that wall is false, because no character in this harbor has said that and the sheet's first line is true and it was said out loud in a market and about thirty people heard it and four of them were in the room; it may not be used to say that the residue comes off a room and not off a piece of glass, because that has not been said out loud by anybody either and a woman who was in the room said in the market on the fifteenth that she was not going to say a thing she did not know; it may not be used to say that the two halves of the reversal are the answer to each other, because neither is on the page as an answer; it may not be used to say that the date at the head of that sheet has been compared with anything, because it has not, by anybody, out loud, on any page of these ten chapters; it may not be used to say that the eleven dates and the eighth of May have been put together, in a room or in a conversation or in a head that anybody printed; it may not be used to say that a woman of about sixty-one was thanked, made whole, put back in her room, given a figure, put on a sheet, asked a second thing or charged with anything, because none of those happened and none of them is going to; it may not be used to date the second entry into the room on the hill, which is the fifth of October and is the climax's; and it may not be used to say that anybody is going to pay the six hundred and forty pence, or the twenty-two lines of a wage column, or the eight marks and a day of a boat, or the three marks to a man of Ashtide, because nothing in this volume moves any of them.**

### 13. The hand-over to Batch 0004, eight items and no more

1. **THE SIX-LINE SHEET ON THE WALL AT THE BACK OF THAT END STALL, AND THE SLATE IT IS PUT UP ON THE OUTSIDE OF, AND WHO PUT IT UP AND WHAT HE SAID.** A printed sheet of six lines with a date at the head and a charge at the foot at one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, naming no person and no town and no office; put up at about ten in the morning on the fifteenth day of September past by a man of about thirty-four off a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait, on the outside of and about four inches to the left of a slate that carries four hundred and fifty pence with the first of June against it and three hundred and seventy-eight pence standing visible above it with the first of February against it, **and that figure was not taken down first and cannot be taken off again.** He said he did not write it, that it was given to him at the top of a gangway by a man behind a counter with a book open who did not ask his name and did not ask what it was for, that he read the first four lines four hundred miles from that harbor and cannot put them down, that he could not say it was a lie, and that he was not going to be asked a second time. The rest of the lot is standing against the back boards of the woman of about fifty-eight's stall with a stone on it and is not opened. **A later movement may not knock that sheet down, may not take it off that wall, may not name the man who printed it, may not print the sixth of May out loud beside anything, and may not move the oil figure.**
2. **THE FOUR MEN WHO SAID OUT LOUD THEY HAD BEEN IN THE ROOM ON THE TWELFTH, THE THIRTY-ONE-YEAR-OLD AND THE FORTY-ONE-YEAR-OLD AND THE AFTERTASTE, AND WHAT IS SETTLED AND WHAT IS NOT.** A cold in the teeth and a taste of iron like a nail and a man's own body not knowing which of two doors he came out of; a cold in the teeth, a taste of iron and a man not knowing which of two hatches he came up out of, off a bell at eleven foot beside a crate of three pieces of worked glass. **THE FIRST HALF IS TRUE AND ON THE PAGE AND NOBODY HAS EXPLAINED IT, AND THE SECOND HALF — THAT THE GLASS ITSELF IS CONTAGIOUS — IS ON A WALL AND HAS NEVER BEEN KNOCKED DOWN, AND NOBODY IN THIS HARBOR HAS SAID THE ONE ANSWERS THE OTHER, AND NEITHER HALF CANCELS THE OTHER, AND NEITHER OF THOSE TWO SENTENCES MAY BE SAID OUT LOUD BY A CHARACTER IN THIS VOLUME.**
3. **THE FIVE COSTS, ALL PAID TO REAL PEOPLE, NONE GIVEN BACK, NONE OF THEM A SCENE ABOUT ANYBODY'S PERCEPTION.** A berth held on the eighteenth. A chandler's counter shut to a man on the seventeenth. A claim window held on a man of about thirty who cannot read the paper on it and who was told *off* at a counter on the eighteenth and *stopped and hand in a third of anything landed* by a boy on the twenty-first, and who did not take his boat out on the Saturday, the Monday, the Tuesday or the Wednesday. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON SATURDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH, LEAVING FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON SUNDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH, BEING TWO BAULKS OF OAK PLANED, LEAVING THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON MONDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH, LEAVING FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH FOR THE PERSON ON THE WATER, LEAVING THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON THE SAME DAY FOR THE BELLWRIGHT'S DAY, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON THE SAME DAY, LEAVING THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-NINTH, BEING IRON CLAMPS AND A PLANK OF WHITE OAK FOUR INCHES BY NINE AND ELEVEN FEET LONG AND ROVES AND COPPER, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON THURSDAY THE THIRTIETH, LEAVING THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON FRIDAY THE FIRST DAY OF OCTOBER, BEING CANVAS AND TAR AND A SPARE BIGHT OF LINE AND COPPER, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON SATURDAY THE SECOND DAY OF OCTOBER AT ABOUT TEN IN THE MORNING, LEAVING THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON THE SAME DAY AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON IN COIN ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE TO A CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE AT THAT SAME FIGURE, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX, BEING ONE MARK AND THREE SHILLINGS.**

**AND THE TOTAL, WHICH IS THE CHAPTERS' OWN ARITHMETIC AND IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 440'S OWN OPENING BLOCK AND ITS OWN FIRST COLUMN: ONE THOUSAND AND EIGHT PENCE, BEING SIX MARKS FOUR SHILLINGS, CAME IN ON SIX DAYS AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT A DAY, AND ONE THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-FOUR PENCE, BEING EIGHT MARKS FIVE SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, WENT OUT IN EIGHT PAYMENTS ON SEVEN DAYS AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT A PAYMENT, AND FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PLUS ONE THOUSAND AND EIGHT MINUS ONE THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-FOUR IS ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX, WHICH IS THE BAG. THE PRINTED EQUATION EVALUATES: 6 × 168 = 1008, 8 × 168 = 1344, 532 + 1008 − 1344 = 196.**

**AND THE FIGURE SHORT OF THAT WAGE, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHT PENCE, BEING NINE SHILLINGS, ON EVERY DAY OF THE TEN THAT THE BAG STOOD AT FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO, BEING THE TWENTY-THIRD, THE TWENTY-FIFTH, THE TWENTY-SEVENTH AND THE TWENTY-EIGHTH AFTER ITS SECOND PAYMENT; TWO HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-SIX PENCE, BEING ONE MARK NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, ON EVERY DAY AND EVERY HOUR THE BAG STOOD AT THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR; AND FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY-FOUR PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, ON EVERY DAY AND EVERY HOUR THE BAG STOOD AT ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX. IT IS NEVER ZERO ON ANY DAY OF THE TEN AND NOBODY IS TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER IT SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO PAY IT. THE BAG WAS NEVER ABOVE FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO ON ANY HOUR OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NEVER REACHED THE WAGE. NOTHING HAS BEEN IN A TIN IN THAT SHED SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF APRIL PAST.**

**AND EVERY FIGURE OF MONEY IN THE TEN CHAPTERS WAS RUN ONCE IN THIS PASS IN THE HOUSE'S OWN ARITHMETIC ON EVERY GLOSSED FIGURE. TWELVE DISTINCT FIGURES WERE RESOLVED BY HAND AND ALL TWELVE RESOLVE: 168 AS ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE; 532 AS THREE MARKS FOUR SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 364 AS TWO MARKS THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE; 196 AS ONE MARK AND THREE SHILLINGS; 108 AS NINE SHILLINGS; 276 AS ONE MARK NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE; 444 AS TWO MARKS TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 284 AS ONE MARK TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 1,008 AS SIX MARKS FOUR SHILLINGS; 1,344 AS EIGHT MARKS FIVE SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 60 AS FIVE SHILLINGS; AND 378 AS THIRTY-ONE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, WITH 450 AS THIRTY-SEVEN SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE AND 640 AS FOUR MARKS.** THE ONLY OTHER FIGURES THAT LEFT ANYBODY'S HAND IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS ARE FOUR PENCE AND EIGHTEEN PENCE, BEING ONE SHILLING AND SIXPENCE, FOR BISCUITS AND A COIL OF NEW MANILA OUT OF A MAN'S OWN COAT; FOUR PENCE FOR TOBACCO OUT OF THE SAME COAT; A PENNY FOR A SHEET OF GOOD PAPER FROM A COPYIST'S COUNTER OUT OF THE SAME COAT; FIVE SHILLINGS, BEING SIXTY PENCE, WHICH IS A BELLWRIGHT'S OWN RATE AND WHICH SHE NAMES AND WHICH SHE IS NOT PAID; AND A YOUNG MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE'S OWN PAY AT EIGHT O'CLOCK ON A SATURDAY OUT OF HIS OWN STEAM TENDER. **NOT ONE PENNY OF THAT BAG CAME OUT OF THE OWNER OF ANY BOAT, OUT OF THE MAN WITH TWO PAPERS, OR OUT OF THE CROWN, AND THAT IS THE CONDITION ON WHICH THE STAGE WAS TAKEN AND IT IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 439.**

**AND THE HANDLERS OF FIGURES THAT MAY NOT BE RE-DERIVED ARE BOTH RULED ON: THE BAG IS FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PENCE AT THE OPEN AND ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX AT THE CLOSE AND IS NOT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE AND NOT ONE MARK, WHICH WAS THE OUTLINE'S PLANNING FIGURE AND WHICH THIS VOLUME'S CHAPTERS SUPERSEDED; AND THE SIX-LINE SHEET IS SIX LINES IN EVERY MOUTH, EVERY SUBTITLE, EVERY LEDGER COLUMN AND EVERY CLOSING BLOCK, AND THE NINE-LINE SHEET WITH A SEAL IS NINE LINES, IS ON A DIFFERENT WALL IN A DIFFERENT STREET, AND THE TWO WERE PUT IN ONE CLAUSE ONLY IN CHAPTER 440'S OWN CLOSING BLOCK AND WERE KEPT APART IN IT.**

### 3. The four-column leaf, and its four columns at the close of Chapter 440

**AT THE HOUR OF THE READ-BACK ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT THAT MOLE HEAD AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING ON SATURDAY THE SECOND DAY OF OCTOBER: ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-TWO / SEVEN HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE. AT THE CLOSE OF THAT DAY: ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-THREE / SEVEN HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE.** Both sets of figures are on the face of Chapter 440's own reading and both definitions are printed there in the ship's own mouth, as they were on the face of Chapters 350, 360, 370, 380, 390, 400, 410, 420 and 430, and the read-back is the batch's and is on its own face.

**THE WHOLE FORTY-DAY RUN ACROSS THE FOUR BATCHES, RE-DERIVED HERE OFF THE FACE OF FORTY CHAPTERS AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANY OTHER FILE: the first column's base is ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE at the close of Chapter 400 and it takes one entry against each of the forty days, no day in two of them, being ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-THREE at the close and ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-TWO at the hour of the last read-back, the fortieth day's own entry going in after the reading. The second column's base is FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE at the close of Chapter 400 and it takes five a day, three before the hour of that day's reading and two after it, being SEVEN HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE at the close and SEVEN HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN at the hour of the read-back, the arithmetic being five hundred and eighty-nine plus fifty and six hundred and eighty-seven plus fifty, AND BOTH OF THOSE ARE PRINTED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 440.**

**AND THE FOURTH COLUMN IS RULED HERE AND PRINTED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 440'S OWN READING: IT STANDS AT ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE, IT HAS TAKEN NO LINE IN ANY OF THESE FORTY DAYS NOR IN ANY DAY OF THE FORTY BEFORE THEM, THERE IS NO HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SIXTH LINE IN IT, IT IS NOT A CLOSURE AND IT IS NOT A STRIKE-OUT, AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD HAS CLOSED IT. THE COUNT OF THE ITALIC FOURTH-COLUMN LINE — THE LINE THAT BEGINS *What it is not* — ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT AND NOT A COINCIDENCE. THE REASON WAS ENTERED ONCE, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, IN THE YARD'S OWN MOUTH, AT ABOUT TEN PAST NINE IN THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF AUGUST, AND IS ENTERED AGAIN NOWHERE. EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DAILY BLOCKS CARRIES THE FACT AND NONE OF THEM ENTERS IT A SECOND TIME, AND CHAPTER 439'S SECOND COLUMN SAYS OUT LOUD THAT A YARD WHICH PUTS A REASON IN TWICE HAS TWO OF THEM.**

**THE THIRD COLUMN IS NONE ON FORTY CONSECUTIVE DAYS AND NOBODY HAS BEEN APPOINTED TO IT, THE BOY'S HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT, WHICH HAS BEEN THERE SINCE THE FOURTH OF APRIL PAST, WAS NOT SCRATCHED OUT, THE NAME BESIDE IT WAS SAID ONCE ON THE THIRTEENTH OF MAY PAST AND NOT SAID AGAIN, AND HIS SURNAME IS ON NO PAGE OF THE FORTY. THE THREE NOTS STANDING AGAINST THE EIGHTH OF JUNE PAST WERE NOT ASKED ABOUT ON ANY OF THE FORTY DAYS AND ARE A TWELFTH WEEK UNASKED.**

### 4. The wreck, the convoy, the rota and the bellwright, and the figures that are new to the book in these ten days

**THE WRECK IS NEW AND IT IS THE ONLY NEW HULL IN THIS BATCH.** The *Alewife*, of about nineteen tons, of the third lay, a warp round a bollard parted at about two o'clock in the morning of the twenty-second and she went up the foul off the south end with nobody in her and lay in about five foot of water with her port bilge up, her mast up, her garboard open about two foot forward of the keel. Nine men landed the mast in about fifty minutes, the wheel went into a boat, both anchors were let go and left in nine foot on a foul nobody has surveyed, and the holder of that writ packed the garboard from the inside and said out loud that it would hold until the flood. The flood came at about twenty past six in the evening, put her port rail against the mole's footing stones for about an hour and ten minutes, and at about half past seven she came off and took the ground on a bank about four hundred yards down that foul in about nine foot. **THERE IS NINE FOOT ON THAT BANK AT THE TOP OF THE WATER AND ABOUT SEVEN FOOT AND A HALF AT THE BOTTOM OF IT. THAT FOOT AND A HALF IS THE MOVEMENT'S ARGUMENT ON ONE FIGURE AND IT IS PRINTED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 436.**

**THE CONVOY IS SEVEN BOATS AND ABOUT THIRTY MEN AND THE CONSENT WAS ASKED OF ELEVEN MASTERS ONE AT A TIME IN THE SAME ELEVEN SENTENCES.** Ten said yes and one said no with a reason in his own mouth and was not asked again on any of the six days after it, was not given another job and was not thanked, and the fact that he was at his own bench in the front room of a shop in the second lay from about eight until about six on each of those six days is what the chapter prints instead of saying that nobody thanked him. **THE PAGE OF ELEVEN LINES CARRIES A NAME, AN HOUR, A BOAT AND A YES OR A NO AND THERE IS NO WORD AT THE HEAD OF IT ABOVE THE ELEVEN SENTENCES, AND NOBODY ASKED FOR ONE IN THAT SHED BETWEEN ABOUT NINE IN THE MORNING AND ABOUT HALF PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING.**

**THE ROTA IS FOUR DAYS AND ONE FIGURE AND IT IS ON A SHEET OF GOOD PAPER.** The twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth and thirtieth days of September and the first day of October, one person on the water in company from about seven in the morning until the last of the ebb, one hundred and sixty-eight pence out of that yard's own figures, not out of any boat and not out of any owner of a boat, and a person may refuse and will not be asked again. **The sheet cost a penny at a copyist's counter and the penny came out of the holder of that writ's own coat and not out of that bag.**

**THE NAMED TENDER IS HALVARD NESS, OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE, SECOND HAND ON A SMALL STEAM TENDER OF ABOUT FORTY TONS LYING AT THE HEAD OF THAT THIRD LAY.** He is not a cruiser and carries nothing that says so and does not call anybody sir. **THE CUTOFF IS FIFTEEN FATHOMS OF CHAIN WITH A SWIVEL IN IT, MADE UP FROM HIS TENDER'S QUARTER CLEAT TO THE WORKING BOAT'S BITT, ROUND A SPURLE AND BACK WITH A WEIGHT ON THE TAIL OF IT, SO THAT WHEN THE WEIGHT COMES UP THE WORKING STOPS.** He said out loud that he would not ask anybody's leave to pull it and that nobody in that boat had any standing to tell him not to, and that the only reason he can do that is that he is not being paid by any of them. **THE WEIGHT CAME OVER THE RAIL FOUR TIMES AND EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR HAS AN HOUR AND A WRITTEN REASON: TWENTY-TWO MINUTES PAST TWO IN THE AFTERNOON ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH, ABOUT TWENTY-ONE MINUTES TO TWO ON THE TWENTY-NINTH, ABOUT NINE MINUTES TO THREE ON THE THIRTIETH, AND ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES TO TWO ON THE FIRST DAY OF OCTOBER. HIS OWN HOURS RAN FROM ABOUT SEVEN UNTIL ABOUT FIVE AND HIS OWN RATE IS HIS TENDER'S AND IS PAID AT EIGHT O'CLOCK ON A SATURDAY OUT OF THAT TENDER AND THERE IS NO FIGURE OF IT ON ANY SHEET IN THAT HARBOR.**

**THE BELLWRIGHT IS MINA KETT, OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR, OF TIDEWATCH ON THE WESTERN REEF LINE.** She came down on the twenty-sixth with her own tools in a box and her own bag and paid her own passage out of her own hand. **HER OWN RATE IS FIVE SHILLINGS, BEING SIXTY PENCE, AND SHE NAMED IT ONCE OUT LOUD AND WAS PAID ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE, AND THE FIGURE SHE IS UNDER BY IS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE LESS SIXTY PENCE, BEING ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHT PENCE, BEING NINE SHILLINGS, A DAY FOR AS LONG AS SHE IS HERE, AND THAT SUM IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 439'S SECOND COLUMN UNDER HER OWN LINE, WHICH NAMES HER OWN FIGURE OF FIVE SHILLINGS, BEING SIXTY PENCE, AGAINST THE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE SHE IS PAID, AND IT IS IN NO OTHER PLACE IN THAT YARD'S BOOK.** She took eleven battens off a keel on a hard in about two hours and ten minutes and numbered the ends in pencil with her own marks and not with figures, and she said out loud that the new piece is a guess with a curve in it and not a drawing, and that she had told them so before she made it. **SHE WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION ABOUT THAT HARBOR'S OWN BELLWRIGHT AND DID NOT ASK HIM ONE EITHER, HIS HUNDRED AND FORTIETH DAY RAN, AND NO DIGIT OF ANYTHING HE EVER SAID IS ON A PAGE.**

**TIDEWATCH AND LOWFEN WERE BOTH ENTERED AND BOTH AS WORK.** Tidewatch is a nail in a workshop door frame with about forty small pieces of lead on it, cut in different shapes, about half of them notched on one arm with a hole through the head, and a woman of about sixty-one there who copies a cut onto a paper for a penny to anybody who walks in, and nobody refused at that door in twenty-six years, and the cuts that came down in the lid of that box are not for this coast and are not to go on a wall. Lowfen is a double post with the top one white, a raft of sticks a man's length across that a man of about sixty puts out every spring and takes down in the autumn for nothing, and a bell on a frame at the low end that is rung by whoever wants to come through, and a mould kept in a head and not in a book because the reeds put the ground out and pull it back. **NO FINAL ROUTE IS NAMED, THE WORD *NETWORK* IS IN NO MOUTH, AND THE NAME TIDEWATCH IS A PLACE AND NOT AN INSTITUTION AND NOT A DELEGATE AND NOT A FACE.**

### 5. The stage, and the thirty-five headed locks, verified one at a time, with a count beside its name

1. **L1, THE CALENDAR. HELD.** Ten consecutive days, one day to a chapter, no day missing and no day in two chapters, taken off Chapter 430 and not off an almanac. No year on any of the ten. The two-calendar fault is inherited, is not noticed, and no chapter explains a calendar and puts a character in a room who explains one to another.
2. **L2, THE MONEY. HELD.** A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve. The wage is four marks, being six hundred and forty pence. The figure that bag is short of it is one hundred and eight pence at the top of the chain, two hundred and seventy-six pence at the middle and four hundred and forty-four pence at the bottom, **and it is never zero on any of the ten days and no word is written under it.** One wage Tuesday fell and the column did not move on it.
3. **L3, THE CHANDLER'S THREE STATIC COUNTS. HELD.** Twenty-two, thirteen and eleven and the mark figure thirty-one, none advanced, the note not re-written. The counter shut to a man in the last batch is not shut again and no figure moved.
4. **L4, THE DELAYED NOTE. HELD.** Eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them, unmeasured, the call not named, the answer reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint. **THE COUNT OF *DELAYED* ACROSS THE TEN IS ONE AND IT IS THE STANDING SENTENCE IN CHAPTER 440.**
5. **L5, THE FISCAL ARITHMETIC. HELD.** Every figure of money is written in pence and then in marks, shillings and pence. Twelve distinct figures were resolved by hand in this pass and all twelve resolve; three figures that were unglossed on a first pass were repaired and are named at § 12.

HELD AND PAID.** One entry against each of the ten days in the first column, five a day in the second, none in the third and nobody appointed to it, and no line in the fourth and no hundred and twenty-sixth line. **THE THIRD COST OF THE STAGE IS PAID ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 439: FOUR REQUESTS TO STRIKE A LINE OUT OF ANY COLUMN AND ONE NINE-WORD REFUSAL USED THE SAME FOUR TIMES, AND THE NINE WORDS ARE ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 439 IN A MOUTH AND IN ITS FIRST COLUMN AND IN ITS LEDGER.** The boy's hand is at the head of the third column and his surname is on no page.
7. **L7, THE MONEY CHAIN. HELD.** Every entry carries a name and a day and the balance is printed at the end of every entry, and a stranger can take it again without adding anything. Not one penny of the whole of it came out of the owner of any boat, out of the man with two papers, or out of the Crown.
8. **L8, THE PLATE AT THE FIFTH SEAM. HELD AND NOT ADVANCED.** **THE COUNT OF THE WORD *PLATE* ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO.**
9. **L9, THE BELL. HELD.** The bell reads nothing, settles nothing and says no word. The eight marks and a day of a boat may not be paid out of that yard's own book and were not. The bellwright of that harbor is not asked and no digit of anything he ever said is on a page; his hundredth day was not passed and his hundred and fortieth day runs. **THE BELLWRIGHT WHO CAME DOWN OFF THE WESTERN REEF LINE IS A DIFFERENT PERSON IN A DIFFERENT PLACE, IS PAID OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES AT HER OWN RATE, IS UNDERPAID BY IT, SAID SO OUT LOUD ONCE, AND WAS NOT ASKED ANYTHING ABOUT THAT HARBOR'S OWN BELLWRIGHT AND DID NOT ASK HIM ANYTHING EITHER. THE COUNT OF *BELLWRIGHT* ACROSS THE TEN IS ELEVEN AND EVERY ONE IS A TRADE OR THE STANDING CLAUSE.**

HELD AND NOT ENTERED.** **THE ROOM WAS NOT ENTERED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, NO DIGIT OF ANY OF ITS THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE, THE THIRD OF THE THREE WAS NOT LOOKED AT AND WAS NOT NAMED, ITS MUNICIPAL CLAIM WAS NOT WITHDRAWN AND NO REQUEST FOR IT WAS MADE BY ANYBODY, THE SEAL LINE ON THE FIRST PAPER WAS DESCRIBED AND NOT READ OUT IN A MOUTH, AND THE OFFICE AT THE END OF IT IS NOT NAMED IN A MOUTH.** The second paper names ten in the morning on Tuesday the fifth day of October and your ten days ended four days before it and the room is not entered again until the last movement and not by the holder of that writ.

HELD.** A face of an office is a name, a seal and an office, and the office at the foot of the seal line on the paper on that custody-room door is not named in a mouth in these ten days. Soren Vey is in no room, on no mole and in no market, Ors Kest is asked nothing, a face of the Navy is a working man and not an officer. **A YOUNG MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE OFF A SMALL STEAM TENDER IS A WORKING MAN AND NOT A CRUISER AND NOT AN OFFICER. THE COUNT OF *SOREN VEY*, OF *ORS KEST*, OF *VEYRA HOLT*, OF *HALVEN ROOK*, OF *ILYA SERR* AND OF *MOTT* ACROSS THE TEN IS ZERO.**

THE TWO SIX-LINE AND NINE-LINE PAPERS ARE NEVER PUT IN ONE CLAUSE, ONE COLUMN OR ONE ROOM EXCEPT IN CHAPTER 440'S OWN CLOSING BLOCK, WHICH KEEPS THEM APART IN ONE SENTENCE.**

HELD AND NOT PAID, AND CARRIED TO THE LAST MOVEMENT BY NAME.** The far bench was occupied from ten until four on all ten days and was not approached and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of them and nothing was put on that bench and read as a gift and neither brother went near the other at any hour of any of the ten days and they did not speak across that shed in ten days. **NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY AND NO CONFESSION IS IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS, THE ORIGINAL REPAIR LOG IS NOT PRODUCED AND NOT NAMED, AND THE CONFESSION IS OWED TO CHAPTERS 441 TO 450.**
19. **L19, THE FIRST ECHO'S WITNESS. HELD.** **THE COUNT OF *ECHO* ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO.**
20. **L20, SERA MOTT. HELD.** Not asked and not on any page.
21. **L21, LABOUR STAYS VISIBLE. HELD AND IT IS THE SPINE OF THIS BATCH.** Nine men on a deck for fifty minutes and not paid for it; two men on a rope and a boy of fifteen on a pump for a hundred and five minutes; a man of about twenty-six holding a lamp over the side of somebody else's boat for two hours and forty minutes in the dark and not paid for it; a caulker's day asked for by name and paid on the flat of the bench stone; a bellwright's two hours and ten minutes with a drawknife; about thirty men on four days; a sweep out of a room who swept out the same room on the Sunday and went down in a bell on the Friday and could tell nothing at all. **NO ITEM OF THE VOLUME'S COST LIST IS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS.**
22. **L22, THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION AND THE TITLE. HELD.** The question was not asked and is not answered. **THE TITLE `outline/series.md:254` HAS NAMED IS IN NO MOUTH ON ANY PAGE OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND THE COUNT OF *ASSEMBLY*, OF *COMMITTEE*, OF *CHORUS* AND OF *FLEET* ACROSS THEM IS ZERO, AND A CHARACTER WHO MIGHT HAVE PROPOSED A BODY WAS REFUSED THE WORD HE ASKED FOR ON THE THIRTIETH IN DAYLIGHT.**
23. **L23, THE MANIFEST. HELD AND NOT USED.** The custody copy of the harbor authority's Gannet salvage report is entered in this batch's inventory as unreached.
24. **L24, THE MARKET WALL. HELD.** A sheet that goes up goes up on the outside of whatever is there. **THIS YARD'S OWN FOURTH RETURN AND THIS YARD'S OWN FOUR COLUMNS AND THIS YARD'S OWN METHOD ARE ON NO WALL IN MORROW QUAY AND ON NO PAGE OF THE ROOM OVER THE JOINER'S SHOP IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS. THE SIX-LINE SHEET WENT UP ON THE FIFTEENTH OF SEPTEMBER PAST ON THE OUTSIDE OF A FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE THAT WAS NOT TAKEN DOWN FIRST AND WAS NOT KNOCKED DOWN, NOT TAKEN OFF, NOT ANSWERED, NOT REPRINTED AND NOT MOVED IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR NAMED THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR WHO PUT IT UP OR THE MAN BEHIND THE COUNTER WHO GAVE IT TO HIM. THE NINE-LINE SHEET OF THE FOURTEENTH OF AUGUST PAST IS ON THAT WALL AND IS ANSWERED BY NOBODY. THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY IS ON ITS OWN WALL AND WAS NOT TOUCHED.**
25. **L25, THE INTERFACE DISCIPLINE. HELD.** No panels, no stat blocks, no status messages, no floating text, no second person in narration and no prompt text in the prose. **THE SECOND-PERSON SWEEP, RUN AFTER STRIPPING EVERY QUOTED AND EVERY ITALIC SPAN BY SCANNING RATHER THAN BY REGULAR EXPRESSION, RETURNS ZERO ON ALL TEN FILES. THE HOUSE'S OWN BAN ON REAL SOFTWARE VOCABULARY IS IN FORCE AND NONE OF ITS TERMS IS ON ANY PAGE. THE CONSENT'S ELEVEN SENTENCES ARE PRINTED AS A DOCUMENT AND ARE THE SAME ELEVEN SENTENCES THAT WERE READ OUT OF THE PAGE, SO A DOCUMENT IN THIS BOOK IS NEVER SHOWN TO A PERSON WHO HAS NEVER SEEN ONE.**
26. **L26, POWER. HELD, AND THE STAGE IS TAKEN.** **THE KEELWRIGHT STAGE IS TAKEN IN CHAPTERS 437 TO 440, ON THE WATER, IN COMPANY, AT A WAGE OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES, UNDER A CONSENT ASKED FOR ONE MAN AT A TIME, WITH A NAMED TENDER AND A CUTOFF THAT CAN BE PULLED WITHOUT ASKING. IT IS TAKEN AS A TRADE AND NOT AS A POWER, IT SETTLES NOTHING, IT PRICES NOTHING, IT DOES NOT SOLVE A PROBLEM OF PRICE, AND IT IS NOT A THING ANYBODY IS A MEMBER OF. THE WORD *KEELWRIGHT* IS IN FOUR PLACES ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS AND ALL FOUR ARE IN CHAPTER 439, AND IT IS NOT TAKEN BY BEING NAMED. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, IMPROVED OR RENAMED AND THE COUNT OF *FAULTREADER* IS ZERO. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE WAS NOT TAKEN AGAIN. THE CHORUS DIVER STAGE IS NOT ENTERED AND THE COUNT OF *CHORUS* IS ZERO, AND THE THREE MEN PUT IN THAT BELL ONE AT A TIME ARE NOT THAT STAGE AND ARE NOT A REHEARSAL OF IT. NO CHAPTER SURFACED A PRACTICE TRACE AND NO CHAPTER ENTERED AN ECHO OR ENTERED A VESSEL.**

HELD.** He is twenty-two, is owed forty marks of claim standing whole, is owed none of it, is off the stone since the fifteenth of May and is not replaced. ### 6. The people, and the two men who may not be moved

**THE PEOPLE WHO ARE ON A PAGE IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS.** Jos Lund, of about forty-four, master of the *Alewife*, of about nineteen tons. Ormond Kettle, of about forty-four, master of the *Sorrel*, of about nineteen tons, on that hard since June with her heel off. Ham Birt, of about fifty, master of a boat of about twenty-two tons of the second lay, whose boat struck the baulk. Silas Pride, of about fifty-two, of the first lay, boat of about nine tons. Alban Pree, of about sixty, of the first lay, forty-one years on that water. Sedge Rundle, of about forty-six, out of Lowfen, master of a boat of about fourteen tons. Jens Ower, of about twenty-nine, of no lay, a lighter of about eleven tons. Elias Voke, fifty-one, of the *Anna Ray*. Iver Sallow, of about thirty-one, of the *Ashtide Rose*. Rowan Teel, of about fifty-one, of the second lay, right forearm set out of his own hand, **who said no and was not asked again and was not given another job and was not thanked**. **Nessa Pike, of that second lay, master of a boat of about thirteen tons of her own, one of the seven, whose hours are in that day and whose table the bill comes to.** Hobb Lee, of about forty-six, who mends nets on the third lay and can read and reads the head-notes out loud with his own name and the hour under each. Ollum Trevask, of about thirty-four, of the second lay, who keeps the whole fouling ladder in that harbor in his own book and has never shown it to anybody and who said he has never been to Lowfen in his life. **Halvard Ness, of about twenty-three, second hand on a small steam tender of about forty tons, the named tender, with fifteen fathoms of chain and a cutoff and his own hours and his own rate.** **Mina Kett, of about thirty-four, a bellwright of Tidewatch on the western reef line.** Isaac Fell, of about twenty-three, a caulker of the third lay, of no boat, of no crew and of no office. Tam Sparre, of about twenty-nine, of the third lay, who put his hand flat on a plank in the dark. A man of about fifty-eight who sweeps out the room over a joiner's shop and who went down in that bell and could tell nothing at all. A man of about fifty who owns the boat of about twenty-two tons that struck the baulk. A woman of about fifty-eight with an end stall and a slate. A woman of about fifty-nine at a copyist's counter. A man of about thirty-four off the second lay who is not the other man of about thirty-four in that harbor. A man of about forty-one with a sheet of about twenty-six holding a lamp over a boat's side in the dark and not paid for it. A man of about twenty-six with a plane. A man of about forty-four who has been planing forty-one years. A man of about nineteen who said good morning in a street and did not stop. A woman of about sixty-one at Tidewatch who copies a lead cut for a penny and was not met and is not on a page. A man of about sixty at Lowfen who puts a bundle of hazel out on the point of a shoal every spring. A woman called Nera Sedge at Lowfen who put a post up in the year her husband died and owns it.

**AND THE TWO MEN WHO MAY NOT BE MOVED.** **ALDEN, SIXTY-ONE AT A FAR BENCH, OCCUPIED FROM TEN UNTIL FOUR ON ALL TEN DAYS, NOT APPROACHED, NOT GIVEN ANYTHING, NO CONFESSION, NO LOG, NO FIFTH SENTENCE.** **BEVIN, TWENTY-TWO, OFF THE STONE SINCE THE FIFTEENTH OF MAY, FORTY MARKS WHOLE AND OWED NONE OF IT, THE THIRD COLUMN EMPTY AND UNAPPOINTED, HIS HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT, HIS SURNAME ON NO PAGE, THE THREE NOTS A TWELFTH WEEK UNASKED, AND NOBODY IN THAT CREW ASKED HIM ONE WORD ABOUT ANYTHING IN THESE TEN DAYS.**

### 7. The cost, and the bodies, at the last page of the ten

**THE THREE COSTS OF THE STAGE, EACH ON THE FACE OF A PAGE AND NONE OF THEM SUMMED.**
- **SHARED LIABILITY.** A boat of about twenty-two tons of the second lay struck a baulk of oak about six feet long that that yard's own hands had laid down at about half past eight in the morning on the twenty-eighth of September with about nine inches of it out of the water in a sea and no light on it and no flag and nothing on it at all, and opened about nine foot of her garboard forward and put a hole in her lee rail about the size of two hands, and about thirty men got a line to her in about four minutes and she was under about two feet by the time she was fast and nobody was hurt. The owner said out loud that the baulk was that yard's and that the baulk was that yard's to mark and that nobody marked it. **THE BILL OF IRON CLAMPS AND A PLANK OF WHITE OAK FOUR INCHES BY NINE AND ELEVEN FEET LONG AND ROVES AND COPPER WENT OUT OF THAT YARD AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE AND IT IS NOT CHARGED TO THE OWNER OF ANY OF THE SEVEN BOATS, WHO WAS NOT ASKED TO PAY IT AND DID NOT OFFER, AND THE OWNER SAID HE IS GOING TO HOLD THAT BAULK NEXT TIME AND THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN DOWN WITH THE HOUR AGAINST IT.**
- **MATERIAL EXPENSE.** The whole of the material and wages of ten days came out of a bag that stood at five hundred and thirty-two pence at the open and stands at one hundred and ninety-six pence at the close, being one mark and three shillings, being six hundred and forty pence less four hundred and forty-four pence, being two marks ten shillings and fourpence. **One thousand and eight pence in on six days and one thousand three hundred and forty-four pence out in eight payments on seven days, and the bag's own arithmetic printed, and the figure it is short of the wage is never zero on any of the ten days and nobody is going to write one word under it.**
- **NO RIGHT TO ERASE.** Four people asked inside these ten days for a line to be struck out of a record: a man of about forty-four at about eleven in the morning on the first of October against a line carrying his name and an hour and eleven minutes of lateness; a bellwright of about thirty-four at about half past eleven against a line carrying her name and an hour and the figure in chalk on a slate at an end stall; and two men off the first lay at about two in the afternoon against a line in the first column of that yard's own leaf carrying about nine foot of garboard and a hole in a lee rail. **THE REFUSAL WAS THE SAME NINE WORDS IN ALL FOUR CASES, BEING THAT THAT LINE STAYS, THAT NOTHING COMES OUT OF THAT BOOK ONCE IT IS IN, FOR ANY REASON, TO ANYBODY, AND THERE IS NO COLUMN IN THAT BOOK FOR WHICH THOSE NINE WORDS ARE ANY DIFFERENT FROM ANY OTHER. THE BELLWRIGHT WAS ASKED FOR A SECOND LINE UNDER HERS AND GOT ONE, AND IT STANDS WHERE HER FIRST LINE STANDS, AND IT NAMES HER OWN FIGURE OF FIVE SHILLINGS, BEING SIXTY PENCE, AND HER OWN FIGURE OF FIVE SHILLINGS, BEING SIXTY PENCE, AGAINST THE ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE SHE IS PAID, WHICH IS A HUNDRED AND EIGHT PENCE, BEING NINE SHILLINGS, A DAY.**

**AND THE COSTS THIS VOLUME MAY NOT WAIVE, ALL PAID TO REAL PEOPLE AND NONE GIVEN BACK AND NONE IMPROVED:** nine men on a deck for fifty minutes and unpaid; about two hours and forty minutes of a man's own legs holding a lamp in the dark for other people's boat; fifty minutes of fresh water over the side on a pump; a woman's own five shillings against a yard's one mark and eightpence; a boat of about twenty-two tons opened nine foot and holed in the lee rail at one in the afternoon on a Tuesday and holed still.

**NO MAN DIED, NO BODY IS NAMED, NO CASUALTY FIGURE IS PRINTED ON ANY PAGE, AND NO PERSON IN THIS BATCH IS LOST TO PROVE ANYBODY'S GROWTH, AND A DAMAGED BOAT IN COMPANY WAS NOT MADE INTO AN INJURY.**

### 8. What was done, in one paragraph, and what this batch may not be used for

**WHAT MOVEMENT 4 DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH: A BOAT OF ABOUT NINETEEN TONS WENT UP A FOUL IN THE NIGHT WITH NOBODY IN HER AND WAS PUT DOWN ON HER PORT BILGE AND HER MAST WAS LANDED BY NINE MEN IN FIFTY MINUTES WHO WERE NOT PAID, AND SHE TOOK THE GROUND ON A BANK IN NINE FOOT WITH A GARBOARD OPEN ABOUT TWO FOOT AND ABOUT NINE FEET OF SOFT PLANK NINE FEET AFT OF IT; THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT WENT DOWN IN A BELL AT A QUARTER TO FOUR IN THE MORNING AND SHORE HER WITH TWO BAULKS AND FOUND THE SOFT PLANK WITH HIS THUMB AND SAID OUT LOUD THAT A SHORE DOES NOT STOP SOFT PLANK; A WOMAN WHO PRICES THINGS SAID SHE HAD NO FIGURE FOR A MAN IN THE WATER AT FOUR IN THE MORNING AND WOULD NOT MAKE ONE UP, AND A PACKET WENT FOUR HUNDRED MILES DOWN A COAST TO ASK FOR A PERSON WHO SETS OUT TO A PITCH; ELEVEN MASTERS WERE ASKED ONE AT A TIME IN THE SAME ELEVEN SENTENCES WITH A NAME AND AN HOUR AGAINST EVERY LINE, TEN SAID YES AND ONE SAID NO WITH A REASON IN HIS OWN MOUTH AND WAS NOT ASKED AGAIN ON ANY OF THE SIX DAYS AFTER IT; A BELLWRIGHT OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR CAME DOWN OFF THE WESTERN REEF LINE WITH HER OWN TOOLS, TOOK ELEVEN BATTENS OFF A KEEL IN TWO HOURS AND TEN MINUTES, WAS PAID ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE AGAINST HER OWN FIVE SHILLINGS, SAID THAT ONCE OUT LOUD AND NOT AGAIN, AND BROUGHT FORTY PIECES OF LEAD FROM A NAIL IN A WORKSHOP DOOR AT TIDEWATCH AND SAID THEY ARE NOT FOR THIS COAST AND ARE NOT TO GO ON A WALL; A YOUNG MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE OFF A STEAM TENDER MADE A CHAIN CUTOFF THAT A MAN WHO IS NOT BEING PAID BY ANYBODY IN THE BOAT IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO CAN PULL, AND PULLED IT FOUR TIMES WITH AN HOUR AND A REASON AGAINST EACH; SEVEN BOATS AND ABOUT THIRTY MEN PUT A NEW PIECE ON A KEEL IN COMPANY ACROSS A FOOT AND A HALF OF WATER, AND IT DID NOT FIT THE FIRST TIME; A BOAT OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE TONS OPENED NINE FOOT BY STRIKING THAT YARD'S OWN BAULK, AND THE BILL CAME TO THAT YARD; THREE MEN WERE PUT IN THAT BELL ONE AT A TIME WITH A REASON WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE EACH OF THEM WENT DOWN, AND THREE ACCOUNTS OF ABOUT TWO FOOT OF PLANK DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER AND NONE OF THEM HAS BEEN SETTLED; FOUR PEOPLE ASKED FOR A LINE TO BE STRUCK OUT AND WERE REFUSED IN THE SAME NINE WORDS; AND ON THE LAST DAY THE LEAF WAS READ BACK AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE WITH BOTH DEFINITIONS ON THE FACE OF IT, AND THE BAG WAS ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX PENCE, AND THERE IS NO FLOUR AND NO OIL AND A LIGHT OUT AND A FIGURE ON A BOARD THAT DID NOT COME DOWN.**

**WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NOT BE USED FOR: it may not be used to say that a keelwright is a thing a person can be, or a rank, or a licence, or a membership, or an improvement on anybody, because it is none of those on any of the ten pages; it may not be used to say that three men agreed about a plank in a hull, because they did not and the three accounts stand against each other; it may not be used to say that the twelve battens made the new piece fit, because it did not fit the first time and a sixteenth of an inch came off the whole length; it may not be used to say that Lowfen was visited or that Tidewatch was visited, because neither place was entered by anybody and both were entered as work and both were entered out of other men's mouths; it may not be used to say that the bellwright was asked about this harbor's own bellwright, because she was not and she did not ask; it may not be used to say that the wage of six hundred and forty pence, or the twenty-two lines of a wage column, or the eight marks and a day of a boat, or the three marks to a man of Ashtide, or the forty marks first after food, or the forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two, or the three hundred and thirty-six pence that came into this yard on two days in the last batch, was paid or reduced or advanced or is going to be paid; it may not be used to say that the chain cutoff is a rule or an office or a thing anybody enforces, because it is a chain and a weight and a man of twenty-three who is paid by a different owner from every person in that boat; it may not be used to date the second entry into the room on the hill, which is the fifth of October and is the climax's; and it may not be used to say that a thing on a wall in the front street was answered, because it stood on that wall for seventeen more days and it was not answered and no man on that bank stopped at it.**
