ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON SATURDAY THE NINTH, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX, AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON THE SAME DAY AT ABOUT ELEVEN IN THE MORNING FOR CORDAGE AND A SWIVEL, LEAVING TWENTY-EIGHT. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON SUNDAY THE TENTH, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX, AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON THE SAME DAY AT ABOUT HALF PAST ELEVEN IN THE MORNING FOR CANVAS AND NAILS, LEAVING TWENTY-EIGHT. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON MONDAY THE ELEVENTH, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX, AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON THE SAME DAY AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON FOR A COIL OF MARLINE, CANVAS AND NAILS, LEAVING TWENTY-EIGHT. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT IN ON TUESDAY THE TWELFTH AT ABOUT TEN IN THE MORNING, LEAVING ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX, AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT OUT ON THE SAME DAY IN COIN ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON TO A BELLWRIGHT OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OFF THE WESTERN REEF LINE AT THAT FIGURE, LEAVING TWENTY-EIGHT.**

**AND THE TOTAL, WHICH IS THE CHAPTERS' OWN ARITHMETIC AND IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 450'S OWN OPENING BLOCK AND ITS OWN FIRST COLUMN: ONE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY PENCE, BEING TEN MARKS SIX SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, CAME IN ON TEN DAYS AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT A DAY, AND ONE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED AND FORTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ELEVEN MARKS SEVEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, WENT OUT IN ELEVEN PAYMENTS ON TEN DAYS AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT A PAYMENT, AND ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX PLUS ONE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY MINUS ONE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED AND FORTY-EIGHT IS TWENTY-EIGHT, WHICH IS THE BAG. THE PRINTED EQUATION EVALUATES: 10 × 168 = 1,680, 11 × 168 = 1,848, 196 + 1,680 − 1,848 = 28.**

**AND THE FIGURE SHORT OF THAT WAGE, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY-FOUR PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, ON THE SAID SUNDAY THE THIRD, BEING TWO HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-SIX PENCE, BEING ONE MARK NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, BETWEEN THE HOUR OF TEN AND THE HOUR OF FOUR ON THAT DAY, AND SIX HUNDRED AND TWELVE PENCE, BEING THREE MARKS ELEVEN SHILLINGS, ON EVERY HOUR OF EVERY ONE OF THE NINE DAYS FROM MONDAY THE FOURTH TO TUESDAY THE TWELFTH. IT IS NEVER ZERO ON ANY HOUR OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NOBODY IS TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER IT SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO PAY IT. THE BAG WAS NEVER ABOVE THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOUR PENCE ON ANY HOUR OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NEVER REACHED THE WAGE. NOTHING HAS BEEN IN A TIN IN THAT SHED SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF APRIL PAST.**

**AND EVERY FIGURE OF MONEY IN THE TEN CHAPTERS WAS RUN ONCE IN THIS PASS IN THE HOUSE'S OWN ARITHMETIC ON EVERY GLOSSED FIGURE. FOURTEEN DISTINCT FIGURES WERE RESOLVED BY HAND AND ALL FOURTEEN RESOLVE: 168 AS ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE; 196 AS ONE MARK AND THREE SHILLINGS; 28 AS TWO SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 364 AS TWO MARKS THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE; 444 AS TWO MARKS TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 612 AS THREE MARKS ELEVEN SHILLINGS; 276 AS ONE MARK NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE; 640 AS FOUR MARKS; 1,680 AS TEN MARKS SIX SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE; 1,848 AS ELEVEN MARKS SEVEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE; 450 AS THIRTY-SEVEN SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE; 378 AS THIRTY-ONE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE; 60 AS FIVE SHILLINGS; 108 AS NINE SHILLINGS; AND 14 AS ONE SHILLING AND TWOPENCE. THE ONLY OTHER FIGURES THAT LEFT ANYBODY'S HAND IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS ARE FOUR PENCE FOR A SHEET OF GOOD PAPER FROM A COPYIST'S COUNTER OUT OF A MAN'S OWN COAT, TWENTY-EVEN PENCE, BEING TWO SHILLINGS AND THREEPENCE, FOR TWO SHEETS FROM THE SAME COUNTER ON THE SUNDAY THE TENTH, AND TWO MARKS NINE SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, BEING FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PENCE, WHICH A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE SAID HE HAD IN HIS POCKET AT TERNWATCH ON THE NINTH OF OCTOBER AND WHICH IS A FIGURE OF A PAST DAY AND NOT A FIGURE OF THIS HARBOR. NOT ONE PENNY OF THAT BAG CAME OUT OF THE OWNER OF ANY BOAT, OUT OF THE MAN WITH TWO PAPERS, OR OUT OF THE CROWN, AND THAT IS THE CONDITION ON WHICH THE STAGE WAS TAKEN AND IT IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 439.**

**AND THE HANDLERS OF FIGURES THAT MAY NOT BE RE-DERIVED ARE BOTH RULED ON: THE BAG IS ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX PENCE AT THE OPEN, TWENTY-EIGHT PENCE AT THE CLOSE, AND IS NOT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE AND NOT ONE MARK, WHICH WAS THE OUTLINE'S PLANNING FIGURE AND WHICH THIS VOLUME'S CHAPTERS SUPERSEDED ON THE FOURTH OF APRIL PAST; AND THE SIX-LINE SHEET IS SIX LINES IN EVERY MOUTH, EVERY SUBTITLE, EVERY LEDGER COLUMN AND EVERY CLOSING BLOCK, AND THE NINE-LINE SHEET WITH A SEAL IS NINE LINES, IS ON A DIFFERENT WALL IN A DIFFERENT STREET, AND THE TWO ARE KEPT APART ON EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DAYS AND WERE PUT IN ONE CLAUSE ON NO PAGE OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS.**

### 3. The four-column leaf, and its four columns at the close of Chapter 450

**AT THE HOUR OF THE READ-BACK ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT THAT MOLE HEAD AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING ON TUESDAY THE TWELFTH DAY OF OCTOBER: ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-TWO / SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-SEVEN / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE. AT THE CLOSE OF THAT DAY: ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-THREE / SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-NINE / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE.** Both sets of figures are on the face of Chapter 450's own reading and both definitions are printed there in the ship's own mouth, as they were on the face of Chapters 350, 360, 370, 380, 390, 400, 410, 420, 430 and 440, and the read-back is the batch's and is on its own face.

**THE WHOLE FIFTY-DAY RUN ACROSS THE FIVE BATCHES, RE-DERIVED HERE OFF THE FACE OF FIFTY CHAPTERS AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANY OTHER FILE: the first column's base is ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE at the close of Chapter 400 and it takes one entry against each of the fifty days, no day in two of them, being ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-THREE at the close and ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-TWO at the hour of the last read-back, the fiftieth day's own entry going in after the reading. The second column's base is FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE at the close of Chapter 400 and it takes five a day, three before the hour of that day's reading and two after it, being SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-NINE at the close and SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-SEVEN at the hour, the arithmetic being five hundred and eighty-nine plus one hundred and ninety at the close of Chapter 440 and seven hundred and thirty-nine plus fifty, and seven hundred and thirty-seven plus fifty, AND BOTH OF THOSE ARE PRINTED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 450.**

**AND THE FOURTH COLUMN IS RULED HERE AND PRINTED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 450'S OWN READING: IT STANDS AT ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE, IT HAS TAKEN NO LINE IN ANY OF THE FIFTY DAYS, THERE IS NO HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SIXTH LINE IN IT, IT IS NOT A CLOSURE AND IT IS NOT A STRIKE-OUT, AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD HAS CLOSED IT. THE COUNT OF THE ITALIC FOURTH-COLUMN LINE — THE LINE THAT BEGINS *What it is not* — ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT AND NOT A COINCIDENCE. THE REASON WAS ENTERED ONCE, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, IN THE YARD'S OWN MOUTH, AT ABOUT TEN PAST NINE IN THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF AUGUST, AND IS ENTERED AGAIN NOWHERE. EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DAILY BLOCKS AND BOTH CLOSING BLOCKS OF CHAPTER 450 CARRY THE FACT AND NONE OF THEM ENTERS IT A SECOND TIME.**

**THE THIRD COLUMN IS NONE ON FIFTY CONSECUTIVE DAYS AND NOBODY HAS BEEN APPOINTED TO IT, THE BOY'S HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT, WHICH HAS BEEN THERE SINCE THE FOURTH OF APRIL PAST, WAS NOT SCRATCHED OUT, THE NAME BESIDE IT WAS SAID ONCE ON THE THIRTEENTH OF MAY PAST AND NOT SAID AGAIN, AND HIS SURNAME IS ON NO PAGE OF THE FIFTY. THE THREE NOTS STANDING AGAINST THE EIGHTH OF JUNE PAST WERE NOT ASKED ABOUT ON ANY OF THE FIFTY DAYS AND ARE A FOURTEENTH WEEK UNASKED.**

### 4. The five elements of the climax, and the figures that are new to the book in these ten days

1. **THE WORK. A BOAT OF ABOUT NINETEEN TONS NAMED THE *ALEWIFE* CAME OFF A BANK ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED YARDS DOWN THAT FOUL AT ABOUT HALF PAST TWO IN THE AFTERNOON ON MONDAY THE FOURTH DAY OF OCTOBER WITH ABOUT ELEVEN FEET OF CAULKED JOINT IN HER THAT HAD BEEN WET TWICE AND DRY ONCE, AND WENT ALONGSIDE THE STONE AT THE HEAD OF THE THIRD LAY, AND A CHAIN WEIGHT CAME OVER A RAIL AT ABOUT TEN PAST THREE WITH AN HOUR AND A REASON AGAINST IT, AND A CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE CAME OUT AND LOOKED AT THAT JOINT AND WAS NOT PAID FOR LOOKING AT IT, AND NINE MEN GOT A MAST IN ON HER IN ABOUT FORTY MINUTES AND WERE NOT PAID FOR THAT EITHER. A BAULK OF OAK ABOUT SIX FEET LONG WENT DOWN ON THE SAME RUN OF HARD WATER ON THE SAME MORNING AND A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY HELD THE END OF IT IN SIX INCHES OF WATER FOR ABOUT AN HOUR AND TEN MINUTES, HAVING UNDERTAKEN TO ON THE FRIDAY BEFORE, AND WAS NOT THANKED AND DID NOT ASK. AND THEN SMALL SUPERVISED DIVES IN WHICH TWO OTHER WITNESSES ENTER A LINE CARRIED ON PAPER AND GIVE ACCOUNTS OF THE SAME STONE IN ABOUT FOUR AND A HALF FATHOMS AT THE FIFTH OF NINE SOUNDINGS THAT DO NOT AGREE WITH HIS AND ARE KEPT AND ARE NOT SETTLED, AND IN WHICH HE WENT DOWN ONCE, SUPERVISED, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE HE WENT DOWN.**
2. **THE COPY. MADE IN THE CUSTODY ROOM AT THE BACK OF A CORRIDOR IN AN OFFICE ON THAT HILL, AT TEN IN THE MORNING ON TUESDAY THE FIFTH DAY OF OCTOBER, UNDER THE SECOND PAPER ON THAT DOOR, WITH A COPYING CLERK OF THAT OFFICE IN IT THE WHOLE HOUR, AT ONE THING OUT OF THREE. IT IS A PIECE OF WORKED LEAD ABOUT THE SIZE OF A MAN'S PALM WITH A LINE ABOUT FOUR INCHES LONG AND NINE NOTCHES CUT INTO IT, THREE OF THE NINE DEEPER THAN THE OTHER SIX, AND AN OFFICE'S MARK AND A HAND AND THE CUTTER'S OWN MARK CUT SMALL AND OFF TO ONE SIDE, AND A PLACE ABOUT THE SIZE OF A THUMB LEFT OUT OF THE LINE ON PURPOSE, AND NO FIGURE AND NO NUMBER OF ANY KIND ON IT. IT IS A MADE THING AND NOT A TRANSCRIPT, IT IS STABLE, IT CARRIES A ROUTE AND NOT A SCENE, AND IT DID NOT COME DOWN THAT HILL AND DID NOT GO OUT OF THAT ROOM IN ANY HAND. THE THIRD OF THE THREE WAS NOT LOOKED AT AND WAS NOT NAMED, ITS MUNICIPAL CLAIM WAS NOT WITHDRAWN AND NO REQUEST FOR ITS WITHDRAWAL WAS MADE BY ANYBODY, THE ORIGINAL WENT BACK ON ITS SHELF UNDER THE SAME NUMBER, AND NO DIGIT OF ANY OF THE THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE OF THE FIFTY. THERE WERE FOUR PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM WHEN THE PAPER ON THE DOOR NAMES THREE, AND THE CLERK PUT A FOURTH STOOL AT THAT BENCH AND DID NOT WRITE THE FOURTH ONE IN HIS BOOK.**
3. **THE ACCOUNT. A SHEET OF ABOUT FOUR FEET WITH A HEAD-RULE, NINE BOUNDARIES PRINTED ON ITS OWN FACE, THREE NAMES AGAINST THE HEAD OF CUSTODY OF WHICH TWO DID NOT ASK TO BE ON IT, FOUR MORE UNDER A LINE THAT SAYS THEY ASKED FOR A TURN OF FOUR WEEKS AND ARE NOT AN OFFICE AND ARE NOT A DEPUT, AND A RULE THAT ANY PERSON IN THAT HARBOR MAY PUT HIS OWN WORDS AGAINST ANY LINE IN THE ROOM WHERE IT IS READ OUT WITH HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR UNDER IT, AND THAT THE PERSON WHO ENTERED IT DOES NOT GET TO STRIKE HIS. IT IS IN A CONTEXTUALIZED PUBLIC RECORD AND IS NOT A PRIVATE PROOF, IT IS NOT THE PUBLIC VOLUME IN FISH STREET AND A LINE IN IT IS NOT A LINE IN THAT VOLUME, AND IT SETTLES NO CONTESTED CLAIM. ITS SEVENTH BOUNDARY NAMES A PERSON WHO IS ALIVE AND IS NOT NAMED. ITS EIGHTH NAMES TWO HOLDS THAT STAND AGAINST TWO MEN AND ARE NOT GIVEN BACK BY ANYTHING ON IT. ITS NINTH IS THE CHARGE OF ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE, AT THE FOOT OF THE SIX-LINE SHEET. THE REFUSALS ARE ON IT AT THE SAME SIZE AS THE REST OF IT. A CHALLENGE WAS ENTERED AGAINST ITS FIFTH LINE ON FRIDAY THE EIGHTH BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR WHO PUT HIS OWN WORDS UNDER IT WITH HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR, AND THE ACCOUNT WAS NOT CHANGED, AND BOTH WERE READ OUT ALOUD AGAIN IN THE SAME ROOM AT THE SAME STATED HOUR ON MONDAY THE ELEVENTH.**
4. **THE CHARTER. A SHEET OF ABOUT THREE FEET, BOUGHT BLANK AT A COUNTER IN A ROOM OFF THAT MARKET FOR A PENNY OUT OF A MAN'S OWN COAT, WRITTEN IN A ROOM OVER A FISH MARKET ON SUNDAY THE TENTH DAY OF OCTOBER, WITH FOUR RULE-HEADS, BEING CLAIMS, REFUSALS, RESTRICTED RECORDS AND PUBLIC CORRECTION, FOUR STANDING LINES, BEING THAT NO ROUTE, PANEL OR ACCOUNT IS REPRESENTED BY ANYBODY WHO HAS NOT ASKED TO BE REPRESENTED, THAT THE REFUSALS ARE ON IT AND ARE NOT SMALLER THAN THE REST, THAT A COMMUNITY MAY WITHDRAW FROM A ROUTE, AND THAT THE COUNCIL TURNS, A CLAIM AGAINST THE COPY CARRIED ON IT AT THE SIZE OF THE FOUR HEADS AND NOT DISCHARGED BY IT, AND FOUR LINES SAYING WHAT IT IS NOT. IT HAS NO JURISDICTION WHATEVER, IT BINDS NOBODY WHO HAS NOT SIGNED IT, IT DECIDES NO CONTESTED CLAIM, IT SETTLES NOTHING, IT IS NOT A BODY WITH A HEAD AND NOT A COURT, THERE IS NO SEAT, NO ROLL AND NO SEAL, AND ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE WHO WENT INTO THAT ROOM DID NOT SIGN IT AND LOST NOTHING AND GAINED NOTHING. THE TITLE `outline/series.md:254` HAS NAMED WAS SAID ONCE, BY A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY AT ABOUT TEN PAST ELEVEN IN THE MORNING ON THE DAY THE SHEET WAS WRITTEN, AND HE WROTE IT AT THE HEAD OF THAT SHEET HIMSELF, AND NOBODY SAID IT AFTER HIM. THE FIRST MEETING IN THAT ROOM WAS A MEETING AND NOT A BODY WITH A HEAD.**
5. **THE COST, WHICH IS FIVE THINGS AND IS NOT A VICTORY, SET DOWN ONE UNDER ANOTHER IN CHAPTER 449'S OWN BODY AND NOT ON A WALL.** THE COPY AND THE ORIGINAL BOTH STAY IN THE BUILDING ON THAT HILL. THE PUBLIC READING IS AT A STATED HOUR, THE SEVENTH AND THE ELEVENTH, IN A ROOM ON THE PREMISES OF THAT OFFICE WITH A CUSTODIAN OF THAT OFFICE IN A CHAIR AT THE DOOR AND A LIST OF NAMES AND HOURS ON A BOARD, AND ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM COULD NOT READ BOTH TIMES AND HEARD THE WHOLE OF IT BOTH TIMES. AN OFFICE REGISTERS A CLAIM AGAINST THE COPY ON THE SEVENTH AND THE CHARTER CARRIES IT AND DOES NOT DISCHARGE IT. A PERSON OF NO OFFICE'S NAME IS ON A PUBLIC SHEET AND ON A SHEET OF FOUR HEADS, DID NOT ASK TO BE ON EITHER, NOBODY TOOK IT OFF EITHER, NOBODY THANKED HER AND NOBODY OFFERED, AND FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD STANDS WHOLE AGAINST HER. A DIVER ENTERED THE LINE ONCE, SUPERVISED, CAME UP WITH A COLD IN HIS TEETH AND A TASTE OF IRON LIKE A NAIL AND WITH A LOSS OF PERSONAL CERTAINTY ABOUT ONE AFTERNOON HE CAN PUT A NAME TO, THE TWENTY-NINTH OF JUNE, AND CANNOT PUT A NAME TO WHAT WAS IN THE BOAT WITH HIM, AND THAT AFTERNOON IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE AND NO NAME AGAINST IT. THE ROPEMAKER OF ABOUT SIXTY-ONE IS NOT PUT BACK IN HER ROOM, NOBODY IS MADE WHOLE AND NOBODY IS CHARGED. THE FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE IS STILL ON THE BOARD IN THE FRONT STREET AND DID NOT COME DOWN.

**THE FIGURES THAT ARE NEW TO THE BOOK IN THESE TEN DAYS AND NO OTHERS: NINE SOUNDINGS AND THREE OF THEM SHALLOW; A PIECE OF WORKED LEAD ABOUT THE SIZE OF A MAN'S PALM; A PLACE ABOUT THE SIZE OF A THUMB LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE; A FIGURE OF SEVEN AT A DOOR; A FIGURE OF NINE BOUNDARIES; FOUR NAMES AND FOUR HOURS ON A ROTATION; FOUR HEADS AND FOUR STANDING LINES AND FOUR LINES SAYING WHAT A THING IS NOT; ELEVEN NAMES AT THE FOOT OF A SHEET AND ELEVEN PEOPLE WHO DID NOT SIGN; FOUR ACCOUNTS OF ONE STONE IN ABOUT FOUR AND A HALF FATHOMS THAT DO NOT AGREE; SIX ACCOUNTS IN THAT LEAF THAT DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER; FIVE ACCOUNTS OF ABOUT TWO FOOT OF PLANK THAT DO NOT AGREE; A CAULKER'S DAY PAID ON THE SIXTH DAY OF OCTOBER; A BELLWRIGHT'S DAY PAID ON THE TWELFTH; AND ONE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY PENCE IN AND ONE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED AND FORTY-EIGHT PENCE OUT. THE COUNT OF THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE WAS CARRIED, UNUSED, NOT RE-COUNTED, AND IS ON NO WALL, ON NO PAGE OF THE FISH STREET ROOM AND IN NO MOUTH IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS.**

### 5. The stage, and the thirty-five headed locks, verified one at a time, with a count beside its name

1. **L1, THE CALENDAR. HELD.** Ten consecutive days, one day to a chapter, no day missing and no day in two chapters, taken off Chapter 430's own line and not off an almanac. No year on any of the ten. The two-calendar fault is inherited, is not noticed, and no chapter explains a calendar and puts a character in a room who explains one to another. **THE WEEK TURNED TWICE, ON A SUNDAY, IN THESE TEN DAYS, AND A WEEK COUNTER DID NOT MOVE ON A DAY THAT IS NOT A WEEK.**
2. **L2, THE MONEY. HELD.** A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve. The wage is four marks, being six hundred and forty pence. The figure that bag is short of it is four hundred and forty-four pence on the first day, two hundred and seventy-six pence between ten and four on the first day, and six hundred and twelve pence on every hour of the other nine days, **and it is never zero on any of the ten days and no word is written under it.** Two wage Tuesdays fell and the column did not move on either.
3. **L3, THE CHANDLER'S THREE STATIC COUNTS. HELD.** Twenty-two, thirteen and eleven and the mark figure thirty-one, none advanced, the note not re-written. The counter that shut to a man in Movement 3 is named in the account's fourth standing line and is not shut again and no figure moved.
4. **L4, THE DELAYED NOTE. HELD.** Eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them, unmeasured, the call not named, the answer reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint. **THE COUNT OF *DELAYED* ACROSS THE TEN IS ONE AND IT IS THE STANDING SENTENCE IN CHAPTER 450.**
5. **L5, THE FISCAL ARITHMETIC. HELD.** Every figure of money is written in pence and then in marks, shillings and pence. Fourteen distinct figures were resolved by hand in this pass and all fourteen resolve; three figures that were unglossed on a first pass were repaired and are named at § 12.
6. **L6, THE FOUR-COLUMN LEAF. HELD AND PAID.** One entry against each of the ten days in the first column, five a day in the second, none in the third and nobody appointed to it, and no line in the fourth and no hundred and twenty-sixth line. **THE THIRD COST OF THE STAGE WAS PAID IN MOVEMENT 4 AND IS CARRIED, AND A TWELFTH LINE IN THAT VOLUME'S OWN BOOK — FOUR WORDS UNDER THE FIFTH LINE OF A PUBLIC ACCOUNT — IS THE SAME RULE WORKED ON SOMETHING ELSE AND IS ON THE FACE OF CHAPTERS 446 AND 449.** The boy's hand is at the head of the third column and his surname is on no page.
7. **L7, THE MONEY CHAIN. HELD.** Every entry carries a name and a day and the balance is printed at the end of every entry, and a stranger can take it again without adding anything. Not one penny of the whole of it came out of the owner of any boat, out of the man with two papers, or out of the Crown.
8. **L8, THE PLATE AT THE FIFTH SEAM. HELD AND NOT ADVANCED.** **THE COUNT OF THE WORD *PLATE* ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO AFTER THE REPAIRS AT § 12, AND WAS TWO BEFORE THEM.**
9. **L9, THE BELL. HELD.** The bell reads nothing, settles nothing and says no word. The eight marks and a day of a boat may not be paid out of that yard's own book and were not. The bellwright of that harbor is not asked and no digit of anything he ever said is on a page; his hundred and fortieth day fell inside the last batch and **his hundred and fiftieth day falls on the twelfth day of October**. **THE BELLWRIGHT WHO CAME DOWN OFF THE WESTERN REEF LINE IS A DIFFERENT PERSON IN A DIFFERENT PLACE, IS PAID OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES AT HER OWN RATE, IS UNDERPAID BY IT, SAID SO OUT LOUD ONCE ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH DAY OF SEPTEMBER PAST AND DID NOT SAY IT AGAIN ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, AND WAS ASKED ONE QUESTION IN THAT BUILDING ON THE HILL AND IT WAS WHETHER SHE COULD CUT A LEAD. THE COUNT OF *BELLWRIGHT* ACROSS THE TEN IS FORTY-FIVE AND EVERY ONE IS A TRADE, A RATE, OR LOCK L9'S OWN STANDING CLAUSE.**
10. **L10, THE LEAD PLUG. HELD AND NOT ON ANY PAGE.** The chest is not opened and is not brought down the hill and its number is in no book in that harbor. **THE LEAD IN THIS VOLUME IS A PIECE OF WORKED LEAD ABOUT THE SIZE OF A MAN'S PALM AND IS NOT THE LEAD PLUG, AND THE TWO ARE NEVER NAMED IN ONE CLAUSE.**
11. **L11, THE GLASS STORM. HELD.** No cause is named for it on any of the ten chapters. The panic of this volume is not a glass storm and does not become one, and the six-line sheet is not read in full again and nobody compares it with anything.
12. **L12, THE COAST ROAD AND THE REFUSED WORD. HELD.** **THE WORD *NETWORK* IS IN NO MOUTH AND THE COUNT IS ZERO ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS. THE NINE FINAL ROUTES ARE NAMED NOWHERE, AND THE COUNT OF *ROUTE* ACROSS THE TEN IS THIRTEEN, ALL THIRTEEN BEING THE LINE OF NINE SOUNDINGS, THE RIGHT OF A COMMUNITY TO WITHDRAW FROM A ROUTE, AND THE WORDS *NOT ROUTES* IN THE ACCOUNT'S OWN HEAD-RULE.**
13. **L13, WHAT IS UNDER THIS TOWN. HELD.** Never explained, never named, never pursued. The compartment is spent and is not restated. The three Gannet documents stay three. **THE COUNT OF *COMPARTMENT* AND OF *MANIFEST* AND OF *GANNET* ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO AFTER THE REPAIRS AT § 12, AND WAS FOUR BEFORE THEM.**
14. **L14, THE CUSTODY ROOM. HELD, ENTERED ONCE, AND NOT ENTERED AGAIN.** **THE ROOM WAS ENTERED ONCE IN THESE TEN DAYS AND ONCE ONLY, AT TEN IN THE MORNING ON TUESDAY THE FIFTH DAY OF OCTOBER, UNDER THE SECOND PAPER ON THAT DOOR, WITH A COPYING CLERK OF THAT OFFICE IN IT THE WHOLE HOUR, AT ONE THING OUT OF THREE. NO DIGIT OF ANY OF ITS THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE, THE THIRD OF THE THREE WAS NOT LOOKED AT AND WAS NOT NAMED, ITS MUNICIPAL CLAIM WAS NOT WITHDRAWN AND NO REQUEST FOR IT WAS MADE BY ANYBODY, THE ORIGINAL WENT BACK ON ITS SHELF UNDER THE SAME NUMBER, NOTHING WENT OUT OF THAT ROOM IN ANY HAND, THE SEAL LINE ON THE FIRST PAPER WAS DESCRIBED IN CHAPTER 443 AND NOT REPRODUCED, AND IT WAS READ OUT ALOUD ONCE IN THE WHOLE VOLUME, ON THE SEVENTH OF OCTOBER, IN A ROOM, BY A WORKING MAN. THE OFFICE AT THE END OF IT IS NAMED IN A MOUTH ONCE ONLY, IN THAT SAME READING.**
15. **L15, THE CONCEALMENT. HELD.** The Oren mark is in no record and is not told, described, counted or put in the holder's writ's mouth in this batch. The count of *oren* across the ten is zero. **THE CUT CARRIES A LINE AND NINE SOUNDINGS AND THE MARK IS NOT IN IT, AND THE PLACE WHERE THE PRESSURE CHANGED IS NOT IN IT EITHER, AND THE REASON IS IN THE BELLWRIGHT'S OWN MOUTH ON THE FIFTH OF OCTOBER.**
16. **L16, WHO MAY APPEAR AND HOW. HELD.** A face of an office is a name, a seal and an office, and the office at the foot of the seal line on the paper on that custody-room door is not named in a mouth until the seventh of October. Soren Vey is in no room, on no mole and in a market, Ors Kest is asked nothing, a face of the Navy is a working man and not an officer. **THE COUNT OF *SOREN VEY*, OF *ORS KEST*, OF *VEYRA HOLT*, OF *HALVEN ROOK*, OF *MOTT* AND OF *CORVIN SARN* ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO. A COPYING CLERK, A MAN IN A COAT OF AN OFFICE IN A CITY, A BELLWRIGHT, A NET-MENDER, A LIGHTINGER, A MASTER, A CAULKER, A SHOPKEEPER AND A WOMAN WITH A SLATE ARE ALL WORKING PEOPLE ON A DAY AND AN HOUR.**
17. **L17, THE NINE-LINE MARK. HELD.** **THE NINE-LINE SHEET WITH A SEAL ON IT IN THAT FRONT STREET IS A DIFFERENT THING FROM THE MARK, IS A DOCUMENT, IS NINE LINES, NAMES NO PERSON AND NO HARBOR, PUTS NO FIGURE ON IT, IS ON THAT WALL FOR THE FIFTY-NINTH DAY, IS ANSWERED BY NOBODY AND WAS TOUCHED BY NOBODY IN THESE TEN DAYS. THE SIX-LINE SHEET IS SIX LINES ON EVERY PAGE OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND THE TWO WERE NEVER PUT IN ONE CLAUSE, ONE COLUMN OR ONE ROOM IN ANY OF THE TEN.**
18. **L18, THE ONE PARTIAL CONFESSION. HELD AND PAID, ONCE, ON THE NINTH DAY OF OCTOBER, AND THERE IS NO SECOND ONE.** A man of sixty-one came down that slip at about two o'clock in the afternoon, went into that shed where two people were and no more, and said four sentences out loud in his own mouth, and there was no fifth. **They were the fact of his own signature at Ternwatch on the twenty-second of November, the harbor and the yard and the hour, the weather and two marks nine shillings and fourpence in his pocket and a day's pay in front of him, and what he said to his wife that night and what he has said in that house every day for twenty-two years. ### 8. What was done, in one paragraph, and what this batch may not be used for

**WHAT MOVEMENT 5 DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH: SIX THINGS AN ACCOUNT HAS TO CARRY WERE SAID OUT LOUD ON A BENCH STONE IN A SHED SO THAT THEY COULD NOT BE CHANGED AFTERWARDS, AND A MAN TOLD A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE ON THE THIRD DAY OF OCTOBER, IN A SHED, BEFORE AND NOT AFTER, THAT HER NAME WAS GOING ON A PUBLIC SHEET, AND SHE SAID SHE HAD NOT ASKED FOR IT AND WAS NOT GOING TO ASK FOR IT TO BE TAKEN OFF; A BOAT OF ABOUT NINETEEN TONS CAME OFF A BANK IN NINE FOOT OF WATER ON THE FOURTH AND A MAN HELD THAT YARD'S OWN BAULK FOR AN HOUR AND TEN MINUTES AND WAS NOT THANKED; THE CUSTODY ROOM ON A HILL WAS ENTERED AT TEN IN THE MORNING ON THE FIFTH FOR ONE HOUR UNDER A PAPER ON ITS DOOR WITH A CLERK IN IT THE WHOLE TIME, AND FOUR PEOPLE WERE IN IT, AND A BELLWRIGHT CUT A LINE OF NINE SOUNDINGS IN LEAD IN ABOUT THIRTY-FIVE MINUTES WITH A THUMB-SIZED PLACE LEFT OUT OF IT ON PURPOSE AND NO FIGURE ON IT, AND THE ORIGINAL WENT BACK UNDER THE SAME NUMBER AND NOTHING WENT OUT IN ANY HAND; AN ACCOUNT OF ABOUT FOUR FEET WAS DRAWN UP ON THE SIXTH WITH NINE BOUNDARIES ON ITS FACE, FOUR OF WHICH NAME A THING THAT IS NOT GOING TO BE GIVEN BACK, AND A SHEET OF FOUR REFUSALS WENT INTO A BOX THAT A MAN AT A TABLE HAD ASKED TO BE LEFT EMPTY, AGAINST HIS WORD, WITH THE PAGE SAYING WHO PUT IT THERE AND WHY; THE ACCOUNT WAS READ ALOUD AT A STATED HOUR ON THE SEVENTH IN A ROOM ON THAT HILL WITH A CUSTODIAN AT THE DOOR AND THE OFFICE AT THE FOOT OF IT WENT INTO A WORKING MAN'S MOUTH ONCE; A LINE OF NINE SOUNDINGS WENT OUT OF THAT HARBOR ON PAPER ON THE EIGHTH AND THREE MEN GAVE THREE ACCOUNTS OF ONE STONE THAT DO NOT AGREE, AND ONE OF THEM PUT HIS WORDS AGAINST A LINE OF THE ACCOUNT, AND A DIVER WENT DOWN ONCE AND CAME UP WITH AN AFTERTASTE AND WITH ONE AFTERNOON IN JUNE HE CAN PUT A NAME TO AND NOTHING ELSE; A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE CAME DOWN A SLIP ON THE NINTH AND SAID FOUR SENTENCES IN HIS OWN MOUTH IN A SHED AND THERE WAS NO FIFTH; A SHEET OF ABOUT THREE FEET WITH FOUR HEADS ON IT AND NO JURISDICTION ON IT WAS WRITTEN ON THE TENTH IN A ROOM OVER A FISH MARKET, A WORKING MAN SAID THE NAME OF THAT THING ONCE AND WROTE IT AT THE HEAD OF IT HIMSELF, A QUESTION WAS ASKED AFTERWARDS AND WAS NOT ANSWERED AND IS IN A MINUTE, AND A SECOND QUESTION WAS ASKED AND NO RULE WAS WRITTEN ABOUT IT; AND ON THE ELEVENTH AND THE TWELFTH THE COSTS WERE SET DOWN ONE UNDER ANOTHER OFF A SLATE AND THE LEAF WAS READ BACK AT TEN PAST FIVE WITH BOTH DEFINITIONS ON ITS FACE AND A FOURTH COLUMN STANDING WHERE IT HAD STOOD, AND A LINE WAS RULED UNDER A HEAD IN A BOOK IN A ROOM AND LEFT EMPTY.**

**WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NOT BE USED FOR: it may not be used to say that a charter is a body, a court, a head, a fleet or an office, because it is none of those on any of the ten pages and eleven people who went into that room did not sign it; it may not be used to say that the cut of lead is a copy of the thing, because a stranger with a pencil can hold it up and see that it carries a line and nine soundings and a thumb-sized hole and no figure; it may not be used to say that the copy came to Morrow Quay, because it did not come down that hill and does not come down it; it may not be used to say that a bellwright was thanked or that her rate was improved or that she said her figure again, because she did none of those; it may not be used to say that three men agreed about a stone, or about about two foot of plank, because six accounts in that leaf do not agree with each other and not one has been settled; it may not be used to say that a man of sixty-one was forgiven, or that anything was written down, because nothing was; it may not be used to say that a name went on a sheet and a person was restored, because she was not restored and forty marks first after food stands whole; it may not be used to date any third entry into the room on the hill, because the room was entered once in these ten days and once only and the third is not a thing anybody in that harbor is going to be given; it may not be used to say that a thing on a wall in a front street was answered, because it stood there twenty-seven more days and it was not answered and one man read it aloud to two men who cannot read and could not say it was a lie and did not say it was not.**

### 13. The hand-over to the Volume 09 close, eight items and no more

1. **THE COPY, THE ACCOUNT AND THE CHARTER, AND WHAT EACH OF THEM IS.** A piece of worked lead about the size of a man's palm is in a drawer in a building on that hill with a line of nine soundings in it and an office's mark and a hand and a person's own mark and a thumb-sized place left out on purpose and no figure on it. An account of about four feet is on a desk at a door in that building with nine boundaries on its face and four words under its fifth line. A sheet of about three feet with four heads and four standing lines and a claim against the copy on it is on the wall of a room over a fish market with eleven names at the foot of it. **A later phase may not put any of the three on a wall in Morrow Quay, may not put the yard's own four columns on any of them, may not strike a line out of any of them, and may not say that any of them is a court, a body with a head, an office or a fleet.**
2. **THE FOUR QUESTIONS, ASKED ONCE EACH AND ANSWERED NOWHERE.** Whether a thing like that can speak for people who cannot speak safely and for people whose own account of what happened to them is being held under a lie, asked at about twenty past twelve in the afternoon on the tenth of October in a room over a fish market, naming no person, by a woman of no office, and not answered, and recorded in a minute as asked. Who is it that gets into the big Crown wrecks, asked at about half past twelve in the afternoon on the same day by a man of about forty-four, and no rule written about it, no office made for it, no seal line cut for it. **AND THE TWO OF VOLUME 08, WHICH ARE NOT RE-ASKED ANYWHERE IN THE FIFTY CHAPTERS. A later phase may not answer any of the four and may not re-ask any of them and may not let a character say the word *singular* of a person.**
3. **THE TITLE, AND WHERE IT IS AND IS NOT.** Said once, by a man of about fifty, in a room over a fish market, at about ten past eleven in the morning on the tenth day of October, on the day the sheet was written, and written by him at the head of that sheet in a hand that is not a clerk's. **THE COUNT ACROSS THE FIFTY CHAPTERS IS ONE AND IT IS IN THAT MOUTH, AND NOBODY PROPOSED A BODY BEFORE THAT DAY AND NOBODY PROPOSED ONE AFTER IT EITHER, AND THE THING THAT FORMS HAS NO JURISDICTION, BINDS NOBODY WHO DID NOT SIGN IT, DECIDES NO CONTESTED CLAIM, SETTLES NOTHING, HAS NO HEAD, AND IS NOT THE BEGINNING OF A FLEET.**
4. **THE SIX ACCOUNTS IN THAT LEAF THAT DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER.** Five of about two foot of plank in a boat of about nineteen tons, entered in the order they were said in the last movement, and three of one stone in about four and a half fathoms entered in the order they were said on the eighth of October, and **NOT ONE OF THE SIX HAS BEEN SETTLED AND A LATER PHASE MAY NOT SETTLE ANY OF THEM, MAY NOT ADD A SEVENTH THAT AGREES WITH ONE OF THE SIX, AND MAY NOT REMOVE ANY OF THE SIX.** The three baulks, the soft plank, the new piece of keel that did not fit the first time, the baulk with nothing on it, the eleven-line consent page with its one no, and the nine words that refused four requests and are not going to be softened or lengthed.
5. **THE FIVE COSTS OF THE CLIMAX AND THE STANDING CONDITION BEHIND THEM.** The copy and the original in the building; a stated hour and a custodian at a door; a claim in a book that is not withdrawn; a name on a public sheet that nobody took off and nobody thanked; a diver's afternoon of the twenty-ninth of June that he can put a name to and nothing else, in the second column with the reason against the line; a ropemaker not in her room; and a figure of four hundred and fifty pence on a board that did not come down. **NONE OF THEM MAY BE SUMMED INTO A VICTORY AND NONE MAY BE PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED, AND THE HARBOR IS POORER ON THE TWELFTH DAY OF OCTOBER THAN ON THE THIRD.**
6. **THE FOUR COLUMNS, THE BAG, THE MONEY CHAIN AND THE DAY-COUNTS AT THE LAST PAGE.** One hundred and eighty-three, seven hundred and eighty-nine, none, and one hundred and twenty-five, and one hundred and eighty-two and seven hundred and eighty-seven at the hour of the last reading; the bag at twenty-eight pence, being two shillings and fourpence, short of the wage by six hundred and twelve pence, being three marks eleven shillings; one thousand six hundred and eighty pence in on ten days and one thousand eight hundred and forty-eight pence out in eleven payments on ten days; the third column empty and unappointed with the boy's hand at the head of it and his surname on no page; and the day-counts as printed at § 1, running on to a hundred and forty-eight, a hundred and fifty, four hundred and eighty-eight, two hundred and fifty-four, seventy-two, ninety, twenty-seven, forty-two and fifty-nine.

NOT TO BE RE-OPENED, RE-STRUCK, RE-SUMMED OR SOFTENED: the custody room, which is entered twice in this volume and twice only; the third of the three and the claim on it; the bellwright of that harbor and his eight marks and a day of a boat; the twenty-second head of the Fish Street volume and its dash; the six-line sheet and the nine-line sheet and the four-line paper in Fish Street and the notice of the seventeenth of May; the plate in eleven feet; the compartment; the manifest; the three nots; the ninety; the count of three hundred and ninety-one; the first echo's witness; and the plate, the compartment and the manifest as words, the count of each of which across the last ten chapters is zero and each of which was two before the repair pass and is not going to be back.**

1. **THE MACHINE ON THAT FLOOR, AND WHAT IT IS FOR.** Fifteen frames in rows, nine fittings in each about three weeks old, a worn cup in the channel between every two frames, a hammer-and-square-and-chisel mark and six hundred and eleven on every frame, a cut that cannot be undone with the old hole open under it, and forty racks on the swept part that were not struck off any page. **Three people said one thing about it and do not agree, and no fourth voice is needed and no later chapter may settle the three.** A later chapter may look at the machine again and may not explain it again in a fourth chapter of the movement that opened it.

3. **THE PUMP HAND OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR WHO CAME UP SHORTER ON THE SEVENTH.** He said out loud what was gone and in what order it was not, was not asked why, was not asked to say it again, was not asked to write it down, was not thanked, is not a casualty and carries no figure. **He was not asked about his compressor hours before Movement 4 and the standing rule from the last batch's opening thread is still in force.**
4. **THE HOLE IN THE RULE, SAID OUT LOUD ON A DECK ON THE SIXTH.** Nine men decide a thing with their mouths and the best of the nine wins, and the holder of that writ told nine men that there is no rule for a machine on a floor and that when this boat is in a harbor there will be a room with about eleven people in it who cannot read and he is going to stand in that room and be told no. **That room is owed to a later movement and is not owed to this volume's close, and nobody in this batch was in it.**
5. **THE OLDEST THING ON THAT SHELF, AND THE FIVE THINGS SAID ABOUT IT.** Nine short lines joined at one point, cut with a graver on a plank in a hall, with no figure, no year and no name beside it; and the five things a woman of thirty said out loud before anybody could say them about her, being that it is a builder's mark, that it was cut before any claim was laid over that ground, that it is not a seal, that it is not a limit of anybody's consent, and that it is not proof that anybody agreed to anything. **Nobody in that boat compared it with the drawing of a mark in a book in a shed two days' sail off, because a drawing is not a mark, and that remains true.**

### 5. What the ten chapters paid, and the four things Movement 5 may not unpay

**PAID: THE CACHE, AND IT IS A CACHE AND NOT A FINDING.** Fifteen frames, forty racks, a swept floor, and now a second opening in a wall at the far end of that floor about four foot wide and five foot high, past the last of the frames, and a room behind it that was dry and had been dry a very long time, with four racks against the back wall and one long one down the side, every shelf of all five with a raised lip about two inches deep along the back of it, and racks full of brown folded paper that has been standing in a dry room in the dark. **THE THREE COMMITMENTS CHAPTER 480 LANDED ARE ALL PAID AND NONE OF THEM IS SETTLED: the master's declaration of the eleventh stands where he put it and his boat is not put to sea in this movement and no date is asked for or given; a man of about thirty-six named Corwin Tace set more marks on the fifteenth and was off that floor by the middle of that day and was not on that floor on the twenty-second and his tool roll is not on that deck; and the woman of thirty of no office wrote the page she promised on the fifteenth, in her own hand, with an hour against it, in the first column, and nobody asked her what that floor is and nobody thanked her.**

**AND THE FOUR A LATER MOVEMENT MAY NOT UNPAY: the record, which is a thing somebody wrote and which does not consent and cannot be asked anything and does not testify, and which went into the second column and not the first because a stranger with a pencil can check what a page looks like and cannot check what it was meant to do; the three one-thing accounts of the seventeenth, which do not agree and which settled nothing and which no stranger with a pencil can check in any part; the man of about thirty-eight who came up on the nineteenth with something in him that is not his and is keeping it, and is not hurt, is not a casualty, is not thanked, carries no figure, was not asked why, and went on working the day after and the day after that; and the deficit of thirteen thousand nine hundred and seventy-six pence, which is against that yard's own book and was said out loud in that yard's own mouth and was not answered.**

2. **ONE PAGE IS NOT IN THAT CRATE.** Brown for about three inches across the whole width of the bottom edge, gone into the fibres, will not sit flat and will not fold, was not cut, lies flat under a weight on that tarpaulin, and is **written on no sheet of any kind in that boat and on no sheet in that harbor.** The woman of thirty of no office named it out loud once, on the eighteenth, as the third thing off the second shelf of the rack against the back wall on the north side of that room, and said that the only way anybody will know where it is is if somebody on that boat remembers it. **A later phase may not put it in a crate whole and may not cut it and may not put it on a sheet.**
3. **THE THREE ONE-THING ACCOUNTS OF THE SEVENTEENTH.** A sound, a movement, and what was in the air, given one at a time, not in front of each other, each consented to out loud, each on a tether, each given up when it had been said, each into the second column in the order it was said, and none asked to give it better. **The three do not agree** — a shut room with a knocking from outside it, a room that is not shut because a sweetness came and went four times, and a back wall thin enough that something behind it came down about a foot. **Put together they have a clock of four things inside about two minutes and not one of the three knew the other two were carrying the other two parts of it. A later phase may not re-ask any of the three, may not settle them, and may not check any part of them with a pencil, because every part of them is a thing one man heard with his own ears or felt in his own body.**
4. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO CAME UP ON THE NINETEENTH WITH SOMETHING IN HIM THAT IS NOT HIS.** He said one thing about it, once, on that deck, in front of all nine of them, and it is in the second column with the hour against it and not in the first and not on any sheet that carries money. He is keeping it, nobody is to ask him for it, it cannot be given back because it was never taken, he is not hurt, is not a casualty, is not thanked, carries no figure, was not asked why, was not made an example, and went on working the twentieth and the twenty-first. **THIS IS NOT THE PUMP HAND OF THE SEVENTH OF NOVEMBER AND MAY NOT BE REPEATED, IMPROVED ON, RE-ASKED OR TREATED AS A WOUND LEFT STANDING OPEN. ### The shipyard, and what it is and is not

**THE BUILDING, ON THE PAGE AND IN NO OTHER ORDER: a roof of forty fathoms of three-inch fir and the boarding dressed to it; a bench; a stock of sawn fir; and a set of hours. NOTHING ELSE IS ON THE PAGE AND THE ORDER IS GIVEN OUT LOUD BY THE PERSON WHOSE YARD IT IS, WHO SAYS SHE IS GIVING THAT ACCOUNT IN THAT ORDER ON PURPOSE.** What was in it that was not the building was a glue pot, a set of saws, eleven years of shavings and two ash benches, and **a boat that was in that building on Monday morning and was not in it on Wednesday, because it went out on Saturday on a cart hired off the west basin and paid for out of the owner's own pocket, is on no sheet and is not going to be, and is at the north quay that evening with her bilge blocks under her.** The first person to see it is a woman of about fifty-two who keeps a fish stall at the head of that quay, from her own step at about ten, and what she gives is the shape of it and not what she thought it was: the smoke came off the west end and not the east, it went along the west wall toward the door and did not go out through the roof, and she wants that in whatever anybody is going to write. She is not asked a second question and is not thanked. About twenty people stand on that quay at about eleven at a distance the slater afterwards said was about the right distance and did not say why. What is left standing is the wall the flue runs in at the east end, the door frame and about nine feet of the north wall, and the iron in the bench frames did not go.

**NOTHING IS SAID ABOUT WHO DID IT. NO NAME OF ANY MAN IS SAID OUT LOUD ON THAT QUAY THAT DAY, NO ORDER IS GIVEN, NO MOTIVE IS ATTRIBUTED, NO FACE IS GIVEN, AND NO FIGURE IS SET AGAINST ANYBODY. A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE ASKS WHO DID IT AT ABOUT A QUARTER PAST ELEVEN AND AGAIN AT ABOUT HALF PAST AND IS ANSWERED NEITHER TIME AND DOES NOT ASK A THIRD TIME; TWENTY MINUTES LATER HE GIVES HIMSELF ONE REASON, BEING THAT TWO HULLS CAME IN PAST THE WEST QUAY ON MONDAY NIGHT AND WENT OUT ON THE TOP OF IT AND HE WAS AWAKE, AND HE SAYS THAT HE HAS NOT GOT A NAME AND IS NOT GOING TO GET ONE BY ASKING A WOMAN WITH A TRAY OF FISH IN HER HAND. THE CLOSE-SEA OFFICER OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH.**

**THE CHOICE IS PAID IN PENCE AND IN DAYS AND THE PAYING IS ON THE SHEET WITH THE DAYS ON IT.** At about a quarter to twelve on the Wednesday the man of about thirty-two says one thing out loud on that quay, once: **he is not going to walk up that coast road and ask anybody anything, because he has four men on a wage and a bench to make and a sheet anybody with a leaf and a pencil can check, and a man who goes looking is a man who is not making the bench, and a question is going to be under nobody's feet at all.** On the Thursday the person whose yard it is says eleven words out loud, once, in about fourteen people, and is asked to say them again louder for the people at the end of that quay and refuses in about nine words: **IT IS A BILL AND NOT A WOUND. SAY IT THAT WAY ROUND. NOBODY IS GOING TO FEEL BETTER AND I AM NOT ASKING ANYBODY TO FEEL BETTER.** **SHE IS NOT THANKED. NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR IS THANKED FOR THE SHIPYARD OR FOR THE CHOICE. ### Ternwatch, and the listening station, and the man of about twenty-nine

**TERNWATCH IS ENTERED IN CHAPTER 536 AND IN NO OTHER CHAPTER OF THIS VOLUME. IT IS A LISTENING STATION ON A COAST THAT IS BEING CLOSED AND IT IS A HUT OF TARRED BOARD ABOUT NINE FEET BY ELEVEN WITH A BENCH INSIDE AND A BELL UNDER A BOARD ON FOUR STICKS ON A LOW SHOULDER ABOUT THREE QUARTERS OF A MILE ABOVE A STREET OF ABOUT FORTY HOUSES WHERE NOBODY HAS BEEN OUT ON THE WATER SINCE THE AUTUMN. IT HAS STOOD THERE NINETEEN YEARS. THE BOARD ON THE POST WAS TAKEN DOWN IN THE AUTUMN AND HAS NOT GONE BACK UP.** A man of about fifty-two who ran it for nineteen years with a second man beside him comes up that shoulder once, on the Thursday, at about four in the afternoon, and **stands in the doorway and does not go in**, and says about forty words: I took nineteen years in that hut and I had a man beside me the whole of it and that is the only reason it was worth anything, and there is one man in there now and that is not a listening station, it is a man sitting in a box; you have got no book and no second pair of ears and nobody to say no to you at three in the morning, and if you write down what you think you heard you will be two men and one of them is not there; I am not going to be the second man in it. He goes down the shoulder and is not argued with, is not asked to come back and is not thanked.

**A MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-NINE SAT IN THAT HUT FROM ABOUT EIGHT IN THE EVENING UNTIL ABOUT THREE IN THE MORNING ON THE THURSDAY AND ON THE FRIDAY, WROTE DOWN WHAT HE COULD HEAR ON THE BACK OF A SHEET OUT OF A BOOK, AND GAVE HIS ACCOUNT OF IT IN ABOUT SIXTY WORDS: A PUMP AT THE THIRD HOUSE UP THAT ROAD THAT GOES AT ABOUT ELEVEN AND STOPS AT ABOUT TWELVE, WHICH HE HAS NEVER WALKED UP TO LOOK AT; A BELL ABOUT TWO IN THE MORNING OUT OVER THE WATER TO THE SOUTH THAT HE KNOWS IS A BELL AND NOT A GUN AND WHOSE OWNER HE CANNOT NAME AND WILL NOT WALK OUT TO FIND; AND HIMSELF, WHICH IS THAT HE CAN HEAR HIMSELF BREATHING ON THAT SIDE MORE CLEARLY THAN HE CAN HEAR A MAN STANDING IN A DOORWAY, AND HE DOES NOT KNOW WHAT THAT IS AND HAS NOT WRITTEN IT DOWN.** He is asked ONE question, being whether he can tell a pump from the water in a pipe, and answers **no** in three words, and that is the end of it. **NOBODY REMARKED ON ANYTHING HE SAID IN A WAY THAT IMPROVED HIM, NO FIGURE WAS SET AGAINST HIM, NO FIGURE IN THAT HARBOR OR ON THAT SHEET IS SET AGAINST HIM AND THERE IS NOT GOING TO BE ONE, IT IS NOT A MOTIVE IN ANYTHING HE DID, IT IS NOT A GIFT, HE IS NOT A MEMBER OF ANYTHING, HE IS NOT MADE TO BE MORE THAN HE IS, HE ASKED NOBODY FOR ANYTHING, HE WAS NOT THANKED, AND ON THE MONDAY HE ASKED FOR A DAY ASKED FOR BY NAME AND WAS GIVEN ONE AT THE FIGURE IN CHALK AND SAT IN THAT SHED FROM ONE UNTIL FOUR SAYING NOTHING AND WAS SAID NOTHING TO.** It has been twenty-nine days on the second and thirty-four on the seventh and thirty-eight on the eleventh, and the fourth of December is not mentioned on any page and no figure is set against it.

### The checks, run after the writing and recorded as counts and not as assertions

THE FIVE OUT-LINES WERE ADDED AND EVERY FIGURE PRINTED ON THE TEN PAGES WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT AND EVALUATED ON ONE MARK TO ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY PENCE.** 1,040 + 960 + 2,016 + 672 + 13,304 = **20,992 pence**, and 58,498 + 20,992 = 76,490 and 76,490 − 10,640 = 65,850. **FIFTY-EIGHT DISTINCT FIGURE-OF-MONEY-AND-GLOSS PAIRS WERE EXTRACTED FROM THE TEN PAGES AND ALL FIFTY-EIGHT EVALUATE.** The figures most likely to fail and their working: 59,538 = 372 × 160 + 18, so eighteen pence over the mark is one shilling and sixpence and is printed as such; 76,490 = 478 × 160 + 10, so the last figure carries **ten pence and no shillings** and is printed as *four hundred and seventy-eight marks and tenpence*; 65,850 = 411 × 160 + 90 and ninety pence is seven shillings and sixpence; 52,546 = 328 × 160 + 66 and sixty-six pence is five shillings and sixpence; 51,874 = 324 × 160 + 34 and thirty-four pence is two shillings and tenpence; 13,304 = 83 × 160 + 24, being eighty-three marks and two shillings; 15,320 = 95 × 160 + 120, being ninety-five marks and ten shillings; 2,016 = 12 × 160 + 96, being twelve marks and eight shillings; 504 = 3 × 160 + 24, being three marks and two shillings; 672 = 4 × 160 + 32, being four marks, two shillings and eightpence; 320 = 2 × 160 exactly; 960 = 6 × 160 exactly; 720 = 4 × 160 + 80, being four marks, six shillings and eightpence. The running out and the shortfall were derived by adding from the base of Chapter 530 and compared with the figure printed on the face of each of the ten pages, and **ten of ten agree**. The figure in on that sheet, ten thousand six hundred and forty pence, being sixty-six marks, six shillings and eightpence, was checked on all ten.

**CLOCKS. EVERY CLOCK ON THE TEN PAGES WAS RUN AGAINST ITSELF.** The cistern is charged at about eight on the second (not charged), the third, the sixth and the tenth and on no other day, and those are the hundred and thirteenth, hundred and fourteenth and hundred and fifteenth charges, and the figure of that hundred is never said out loud a second time. The wall comes down bare at about half past ten on the second and on the ninth, the eighty-seventh and eighty-eighth times, and goes up at the angle it has been at since the twelfth. The shipyard goes up between about ten and about half past eleven — about an hour, as stated — and the smoke had stopped coming off it by about half past eleven. The wagons are turned about at about ten and are on that quay at about half past four, which is four and a half hours on a road they were nine miles out on. The yard is priced at about half past eleven on the fourth; the four men are hired at about ten on the sixth for the sixth, the seventh and the eighth; the roof is up at about four on the eighth. A week's room at five shillings and fourpence a day for seven days is 96 × 7 = **672**. Forty fathoms at two hundred and forty a fathom is 9,600; sixteen fathoms of two-inch at two hundred a fathom is 3,200; three days of one man's hours at one hundred and sixty-eight a day is 504; three days apiece to four men at one hundred and sixty-eight a day is 4 × 3 × 168 = 2,016; and the four sum to 15,320, which is the figure on the slate on Tuesday and the sum on the sheet on Saturday. The bag is 28 + 168 − 168 = 28 on each of the ten days and 28 + 1,680 − 1,680 = 28 across the ten.

**COUNTED DOCUMENTS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM PASSES.** The paper read out in Chapter 540 carries five lines of rule and five lines are read aloud. Chapter 533's price is four figures and a sum. Chapter 537 puts three lines on the sheet and the three days across them are the sixth, the seventh and the eighth, with two of them on the face of one line. About nine people in the room over that market on the eleventh say one sentence each. About eleven people in that room cannot read.

**THE DUPLICATION SWEEP WAS RUN OVER THE APPARATUS AND NOT OVER THE SCENE PROSE, AND ITS NEGATIVE RESULT IS ONLY AS WIDE AS WHAT IT READ.** It was run across all forty-five pairs of the ten second columns and across all three hundred pairs between the ten and the second columns of Chapters 501 to 530, with the house's own apparatus entry formula and the attribution formula stripped out of both ends of every pair. **THE LONGEST SUBSTANTIVE RUN INSIDE THE BATCH AND AGAINST CHAPTERS 501 TO 530 IS EIGHT WORDS, AND EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN EIGHT-WORD RUNS THAT REMAIN IS ONE OF THE TWO EXEMPTIONS: EIGHT ARE THE HOUSE'S OWN PHRASE *ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM WHO CANNOT READ*, WHICH THE BATCH PROMPT SAYS IS NOT A FAULT, AND THREE ARE THE HOUSE'S OWN STANDING PHRASE *A DAY ASKED FOR BY NAME*, WHICH HAS BEEN CARRIED SINCE THE FIRST MOVEMENT. NO REASON ENTERED IN A SECOND COLUMN IS RESTATED IN ANY OTHER, AND THE TEN CLOSING PHRASES OF THE TEN SECOND COLUMNS ARE ALL DIFFERENT. IT IS NOT A CLAIM ABOUT THE WHOLE OF THE TEN FILES.** The first columns were NOT in that sweep and are the house's own ledger entry formula, which by design carries the day's money, the bag arithmetic, the cistern line and the rota board in the same words on every day of a movement, and that repetition is the form and not a defect. **THE TEN SETS OF WORDS CARRYING THE REQUIRED FACT — THAT NOTHING STANDING WAS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED, IMPROVED, STRIKED OR CLOSED ON THAT DAY — ARE IN TEN DIFFERENT CLAUSES AND A READER CAN TELL WHICH DAY EACH WAS WRITTEN ON.**

**SIX RE-WORDINGS WERE MADE BY THAT SWEEP IN THIS PHASE'S OWN WRITING PASS AND ALL SIX ARE IN THE TEN PAGES AS THEY STAND.** One, Chapter 531's reason for the berth fund's Sunday was near-verbatim of Chapter 524's and is now about an office with a slate in it. Two, the ten first columns and second columns both carried *and that nothing went onto that sheet in any hand in any line on that day* in identical words across four days of this batch, which is the house's own ledger formula and is out of the sweep's scope. Three, Chapters 532 and 533 and 539 carried *nothing was read out in the room over that market on that* in the same words and the three are now three different clauses. Four, Chapters 533, 538 and 539 all carried *was said out loud at half past five* against each other and are now three different phrases. Five, Chapters 536 and 538 carried *and is that a man who has said* and *and is that a man who has said* and are now *a man who says no to a thing he did for nineteen years* and *a man who says he will come back in the spring*. Six, Chapters 534 and 540 each carried *four crews that wrote no name in December and nobody has asked them since* in the same words and Chapter 540's is now *four crews on this coast put no name down in December and have not been asked about it since*.

**THE COUNTS THAT CAME BACK ZERO AND ARE RECORDED AS COUNTS.** A four-digit year, **ZERO**. *Gannet, manifest, compartment, fifth seam, orison, network, fleet, committee, chorus, singular, keelwright, the sea below, this chapter, this volume, this book, this series, in nine volumes, two volumes, volumes back, an earlier volume*, **ZERO**. *Cache, four feet, echo, damp brown, chamber, stove, twenty-two fathoms*, **ZERO**. The forbidden panel constructions, *not a lie, not a silence, not a refusal, not anybody's shame*, **ZERO INCLUDING IN THE NEGATIVE**. *Iven Sallow, Corwin Tace, Ilya Serr, Ors Kest, Veyra Holt, Halven Rook, Soren Vey, Mina Kett, Tarek Sol, Ashootide, Ashtide, Lowfen, Tidewatch, Saltmarch, Cinder Bay, Veyr, Bramble Strait, Court of Wreck Claims, assembly, minister*, **ZERO**. The second person in the narration and in the apparatus, **ZERO** on all ten, INCLUDING THE FIVE NUMBERED LINES OF THE PAPER READ ALOUD IN CHAPTER 540 AND THE THREE QUOTED PASSAGES IN CHAPTER 533 AND CHAPTER 537. **QUOTE PARITY IS EVEN ON ALL TEN FILES AT 14, 12, 20, 14, 18, 14, 16, 10, 10 AND 16 WITH ZERO UNPAIRED MARKS.** The word *plate* is on one page, being a fish plate in Chapter 540, which is one of the four permitted uses. The count of *Ternwatch* before Chapter 536 across the volume is **ZERO**.

**THREE CHAPTERS RUN ABOVE THE HOUSE GUIDELINE OF THREE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED WORDS AND THE REASON IS RECORDED RATHER THAN THE CHAPTER CUT.** Chapter 534 is 4,091 words and carries a destruction, four figures, a first witness who is given the shape of a thing and not its cause, a question asked twice and answered never, a refusal to look, and two days of pay. Chapter 535 is 3,960 and carries the eleven words, the refusal of a second reading, the days of the work said out loud in the open, and a line hired in advance. Chapter 540 is 5,187 and carries the arrival of a paper, a five-line document read aloud with a name not read, two confrontations, and nine one-sentence declarations in a room. **CUTTING ANY OF THEM REMOVES A BEAT AND NOT A WORD.**

### What this movement leaves, and what a later phase may not do with it

1. **MAY NOT KILL ANYBODY, MAY NOT NAME A BODY, MAY NOT PRINT A CASUALTY FIGURE, AND MAY NOT WRITE THE LOSS OF THAT SHIPYARD AS THE LOSS OF A PERSON.** It is a roof, a bench, a stock of sawn fir and a set of hours, and the boat that was in it is at the north quay with her bilge blocks under her.
2. **MAY NOT NAME A MAN FOR THE BURNING, MAY NOT GIVE HIM A FACE, AN ORDER, A MOTIVE, A FIGURE OR A TRIAL, AND MAY NOT PUT THE CLOSE-SEA OFFICER OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR ON A PAGE.** Two hulls came in past the west quay on the Monday night and went out on the top of it, on one man's word, and that is all that is on the page.
3. **MAY NOT RE-USE THE FIFTEEN THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY PENCE.** It is paid. It is in the slate in the drawer under that bench stone and in three lines on that sheet with the sixth, the seventh and the eighth of January against them. **Movement 5's reconstruction is a second payment of it and must be printed as a second payment, with its own figure and its own days, and must not be the same figure.**
4. **MAY NOT THANK ANYBODY FOR THE SHIPYARD OR FOR THE CHOICE, AND MAY NOT ASK THIS HARBOR FOR ANY PART OF IT.** The fortnight offered at two hundred and forty pence a day was refused in nine words and has not been offered again.
5. **MAY NOT READ THE NAME UNDER THE SEAL OUT ALOUD IN A ROOM, AND MAY NOT PUT THE MAN WHOSE NAME IT IS IN A ROOM.** The count of that name in any mouth across the fifty is zero.
6. **MAY NOT ENTER TERNWATCH BEFORE CHAPTER 536 OR MAKE IT A FISHER COMMONWEALTH THAT BROUGHT THE CONDITION.** The commonwealth is the one at the hard answered in Movement 2 and is eleven miles up that coast; its condition is not settled and is not agreeable; and the four lines with an hour under each are still on the face of that record.
7. **MAY NOT IMPROVE THE MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-NINE'S HEARING, MAY NOT SET A FIGURE AGAINST IT, MAY NOT MAKE IT A MOTIVE IN ANYTHING HE DOES, AND MAY NOT MAKE HIM A LISTENING STATION'S SUCCESS.** A station with one man in it is a man sitting in a box and that is what the man of about fifty-two said out loud on that shoulder.
8. **MAY NOT ENTER THE CHORUS DIVER STAGE AGAIN, MAY NOT NAME IT, MAY NOT IMPROVE IT, AND MAY NOT HAVE ANYBODY GO DOWN IN ABOUT FOUR FATHOMS OFF THAT THIRD LAY.** Nobody went into any water on any of the ten days of this movement.
9. **MAY NOT ASK THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO WHICH OF THE THREE ACCOUNTS OF THE THIRTIETH WAS HIS OWN, MAY NOT LIFT THE AFTERTASTE, MAY NOT SETTLE WHETHER THAT FLOAT WAS HELD OR LOOSE, AND MAY NOT ASK THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO SAID NO ON THE TWENTY-FIRST WHY HE SAID NO.**
10. **MAY NOT SAY THAT A LINE OF BOATS HAS BEEN TAKEN AWAY OR HAS EASED BEFORE CHAPTER 550.** There were still nine hulls about two sea miles off the head of that mole on the eleventh of January.
11. **MAY NOT FILL THE THIRD COLUMN, APPOINT ANYBODY TO IT, SCRATCH THE BOY'S HAND OUT OF THE HEAD OF IT, PUT HIS SURNAME ON A PAGE, OR PUT HIM ON THE WATER.** It took no line on any of the ten days.
12. **MAY NOT PAY, ADVANCE, REDUCE, RE-DATE, IMPROVE, STRIKE OR CLOSE ANYTHING STANDING.** Two wage Tuesdays went past in this movement with the column at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, twenty envelopes shut in a chest, and a further week fallen due at the close of each, being the sixty-third and the sixty-fourth. The lamp oil board is still at four hundred and fifty pence with the first of June above it. There is still no flour in that market.
13. **MAY NOT READ THE FITTING-OUT SHEET OUT IN THE ROOM OVER THAT MARKET, AND MAY NOT PUT IT AND THE FOUR HEADS IN ONE CLAUSE, ONE COLUMN, ONE ROOM OR ONE MOUTH WITHOUT BOTH BEING NAMED OUT LOUD.** They were named separately and out loud in that room on the eleventh.
14. **MAY NOT READ THE PROOF OUT AGAIN, MAY NOT GET AN ANSWER OUT OF IT, MAY NOT OPEN THE DRAWER ON THE HILL, MAY NOT PUT A DIGIT OF ANY OF THE THREE NUMBERS IN THAT ROOM ON A PAGE, AND MAY NOT USE THE SHEET OF ABOUT FOUR FEET TO DECIDE WHERE A BOAT GOES.**
15. **MAY NOT ASK THE QUESTION OF CHAPTER 550 BEFORE CHAPTER 550, MAY NOT RE-ASK THE QUESTION OF THE SECOND OF DECEMBER, AND MAY NOT SAY *SINGULAR* OF A PERSON.** All three counts are zero across the ten.

### Still open, and unchanged

The cache is on the bottom in the racks in about twenty-two fathoms two days' sail away and is on no page of this movement. The one damp brown page is flat under a weight in a room over that market and is on no page of this movement. **The proof is in a locked case on a long table in that room and was not read out on any of the ten days and no chapter of this movement got an answer out of it.** The three accounts of the floor of October past are not settled. The rail is not identified. The question a man of about thirty-four asked is still open. The third column is empty and the boy's hand is not scratched out. **The fourth column stands at one hundred and twenty-five with no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it.** The man of about thirty-four's Tuesday is still a hole. The man of about thirty-eight's kept thing is not asked about. **The man of about fifty-one out of a coast town four days down has said nothing to anybody about a page of six names for a hundred and eighty days and was not sent for.** The man of about twenty-nine can hear out of the left side of his head and it has been thirty-eight days and nothing anybody has done has made it into a thing he is better at. **The bellwright of that harbor was not asked for a figure on any of the ten days and gave none, his chest is shut, and the eight marks and a day of a boat are unargued.** A man of about sixty-one who repairs boats sat on the crown of that mole on the Wednesday and looked at what was burning for about a minute and went up it again and said nothing and was not thanked. **A SLATER OF ABOUT FORTY STOOD IN THAT DOORWAY ON THE SUNDAY AND SAID THERE IS NOT ONE SILL UNDER THAT ROOF AND THAT HE WILL LOOK AT IT IN THE SPRING, AND NO FIGURE WAS ASKED OF HIM AND HE GAVE NONE.** Nobody was thanked for anything on any of these ten days, and the volume is forty chapters old of fifty and is not closed.
